issues.title: Cross-domain: profile recursive cross-organizational Mission delegation
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
## Problem

[`draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01) identifies a deployment class the Mission family does not currently cover: an agent in one organization delegates a narrower part of its authority to an agent in another organization, which can delegate again, while the relying party verifies the complete narrowing chain without calling the origin for each request.

The family has the necessary pieces, but their current boundaries leave a deliberate hole:

- [Cross-Domain Projection](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/cb06c89699aae0a134f01e438f55614de940a2b1/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.md) is a single-hop projection from the Mission Issuer to a Resource AS. It rejects delegate-carried authority and resets local delegation depth; multi-domain chaining is future work.
- [Child Delegation](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/cb06c89699aae0a134f01e438f55614de940a2b1/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation.md) requires the child and parent Mission to have the same issuer.
- [Offline Attenuation](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/cb06c89699aae0a134f01e438f55614de940a2b1/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-attenuation.md) already carries the complete parent chain and verifies signature, capability, audience, expiry, depth, PoP, and an unchanged Mission binding, but it is not profiled across organizational trust domains.

Trying to stretch the current cross-domain grant into recursive delegation would conflate two different verbs: **Project** makes Mission authority consumable in a resource domain; **Delegate** gives a different actor a narrowed slice it may exercise or further narrow. The protocol needs to compose those verbs, not merge them.

## Recommendation

Define an **experimental Cross-Organizational Delegation companion** as a profile of Mission Offline Attenuation. The attenuation chain is the portable authority proof; Cross-Domain Projection remains the adapter by which a destination Resource AS validates the chain, applies local policy, and issues a local access token.

Do not add fields to `mission_intent`, do not turn `authority_hash` into an inclusion proof, and do not add a collection of delegation parameters to PAR or Token Exchange. A chain is presented as one typed `subject_token`; its signed hops carry the semantics.

This is an experimental companion until the underlying attenuating-agent-token substrate is stable. An issuer-mediated chain can be documented as a future standards-track alternative, but maintaining two wire formats in the first revision would make interoperability worse.

## Proposed protocol

### 1. Roles and artifact

Define a **Cross-Organizational Mission Delegation Chain** as the existing Mission-bound attenuation root plus zero or more attenuation children, presented in root-to-leaf order using the attenuation substrate's chain serialization and token-type identifier.

No new free-form envelope is introduced. Each hop continues to carry the substrate and Mission fields already needed for verification:

- the signed hop envelope (`iss`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`, explicit `typ`);
- `authorization_details` containing the authority at that hop;
- `aud`;
- `cnf`, binding the next presenter to its own key;
- the substrate's parent commitment and global depth members (`par_hash`, `del_depth`, `del_max_depth`);
- the unchanged `mission` claim (`id`, `issuer`, `authority_hash`, plus any members required by the principal-semantics issue); and
- the RFC 8693 `act` chain specified by #433. `act` carries identity lineage only; it MUST NOT be treated as proof that authority narrowed.

`authority_hash` remains a commitment to the complete approved Authority Set and an audit correlator. It does not prove that a narrowed entry was a member of that set. The signed root and the verified per-hop subset chain provide that proof.

### 2. Root issuance

The originating Mission Issuer MAY issue a cross-organizational attenuation root only when:

1. the Mission is active;
2. every carried `authorization_details` entry is within the Mission Authority Set;
3. every carried authorization-details type and constraint has standardized, deterministic subset semantics usable by downstream verifiers;
4. every entry is delegable and the root depth does not exceed its approved `delegation.max_depth`;
5. the root audience is an approved destination or audience envelope;
6. the root is sender-constrained to the approved agent's workload key; and
7. deployment policy permits the relevant authority and subject class to cross the named trust boundary.

An entry with a deployment-private action, constraint, matcher, or resource identifier whose meaning cannot be resolved by the destination MUST be omitted. It MUST NOT cross under a promise that the destination will interpret prose or issuer-local policy.

### 3. Per-hop derivation

A holder creates a child exactly as Offline Attenuation specifies, with these additional profile rules:

1. sign the child with the key bound by the parent's `cnf`;
2. bind the child to the exact parent through the substrate parent commitment;
3. narrow or preserve every `authorization_details` entry under the registered type and constraint subset rules;
4. keep `aud` equal to or narrower than the parent audience;
5. set `exp` no later than the parent and no later than the destination trust policy permits;
6. increment `del_depth` without resetting it at an organizational boundary, and preserve `del_max_depth`;
7. preserve the `mission` claim byte-for-byte for the members this profile makes invariant;
8. extend, never replace or truncate, the `act` identity chain per #433; and
9. bind the new leaf to the recipient workload's own PoP key.

The recipient proves possession of the leaf key at redemption or direct resource access. An organization change is not a new root and does not reset depth.

### 4. Destination verification and projection

A Resource AS or chain-verifying Resource Server MUST perform the following in order:

1. resolve the origin Mission Issuer to an accepted trust domain and verification key through deployment/federation policy; never trust an issuer merely because the chain names it;
2. validate the root type, signature, time bounds, and Mission-Issuer equality;
3. validate every parent commitment and child signature through the leaf;
4. verify that `mission` invariants are unchanged across all hops;
5. verify monotonic `del_depth`, the global maximum, nested audience and expiry, and every authorization-details subset relation;
6. reject an unknown authorization-details type, action, constraint, comparison rule, or actor-binding profile;
7. validate the RFC 8693 actor lineage and the leaf workload's PoP; identity verification does not replace the authority-chain checks;
8. establish that the Mission is active from a locally available state source within the deployment's declared freshness bound; and
9. intersect the verified delegated authority with current local principal entitlement and resource policy before permitting or minting a local token.

For offline enforcement, issuer metadata, verification keys, key status, and Mission state MAY be cached or distributed as signed state. Their maximum age and the consequence of stale or unavailable state MUST be declared. Missing or stale required state fails closed. This meets “no callback to the origin on the request path”; it does not claim instantaneous revocation.

When a Resource AS mints a conventional local token, it MUST:

- carry only the locally permitted subset;
- preserve the Mission reference and actor/principal invariants required by the companion profiles;
- bind the token to the local presenter;
- cap its expiry by the leaf and local policy; and
- record the chain digest, leaf `jti`, input authority, output authority, actor lineage, and policy version in the derivation evidence.

A local access token is not itself a new portable delegation root. Recursive cross-organizational delegation continues from the verified attenuation chain, not from a locally projected token that has lost the parent proof.

### 5. Trust model

“No interaction-specific bilateral agreement” does not mean “trust any issuer.” A conforming deployment MUST have a federation or administrative policy that maps:

- WIMSE trust-domain identifiers to accepted workload-identity trust anchors;
- Mission Issuers to accepted signing keys and key-status sources;
- resource identifiers to the Resource AS/RS authorized to consume them;
- authorization-details types and constraint registries to supported versions; and
- freshness ceilings for issuer metadata, key status, and Mission state.

The secure mapping from a trust-domain name to anchors is an explicit deployment dependency; the WIMSE architecture currently leaves that mapping out of scope.

## Conformance and tests

Add a capability declaration for `cross_org_delegation` and require both positive and negative vectors. At minimum:

- valid A → B → C chain across three trust domains;
- action, resource, amount, audience, or expiry widening at either hop;
- constraint removal, including removal of `requires_action_approval: true`;
- parent-hash substitution, reordered/missing hop, changed Mission binding, and untrusted root;
- depth reset at an organization boundary and depth overflow;
- wrong leaf PoP key, actor-chain truncation, and actor/leaf-key mismatch;
- unknown RAR type, action, constraint, or subset algorithm;
- revoked/expired Mission, compromised signing key, stale state, and unavailable state;
- a local projected token incorrectly offered as the parent of a new cross-org hop; and
- valid delegated authority denied by local entitlement or local policy.

The conformance statement MUST distinguish:

- **chain-verifying consumption**, where the RP receives and verifies the complete proof; and
- **AS-mediated consumption**, where an RS trusts its Resource AS's locally issued token and does not claim that it independently verified the cross-organizational chain.

## Dependencies and coordination

- Depends on #433 for one actor-chain convention. This issue does not redefine `act`.
- Depends on #539 for the invariant origin principal and dual-axis local authorization.
- Coordinates with #285, but does not resolve its PoP/lifetime pricing questions.
- Reuses the Common Constraints subset registry; it must not invent local comparison rules.
- Requires a cross-reference from Cross-Domain Projection's current “delegate-carries-its-own-authority” future-work text and from Offline Attenuation's deployment boundary.

## Tradeoffs

**Why profile Offline Attenuation:** it already supplies the proof property the Reece draft needs: the verifier receives the parent chain and can recompute every attenuation. It also preserves a single global depth. This is less machinery than inventing a second recursive-grant format.

**Cost:** the attenuation substrate is experimental; chains grow with delegation depth; verification cost is linear in hops; holders gain an offline minting capability; the origin cannot observe fan-out; and whole-Mission revocation does not selectively revoke a branch. Conservative depth/lifetime limits and optional leaf/key deny lists remain necessary.

**Why not recursively reuse the current cross-domain grant:** that grant is origin-issued, one-time, Resource-AS-audienced projection. Allowing each downstream AS to reinterpret it as a delegable root would erase the distinction between projection and delegation, reset policy/depth at boundaries, and still not give the final RP a proof of every subset relation.

**Why not rely on `authority_hash`:** a commitment to the complete Authority Set is not an inclusion proof for a narrowed subset. Supplying the full root and signed attenuation chain is larger, but it proves the property being claimed.

**Offline versus revocation:** locally cached signed state removes a synchronous origin dependency but necessarily accepts bounded staleness. The profile must publish that bound and fail closed after it; it cannot promise both fully disconnected operation and immediate revocation.

## Non-goals

- No change to Mission Intent or admission evidence.
- No new approval/governance event and no new Child Mission.
- No portable semantics for issuer-private resources, actions, or constraints.
- No claim that `act` proves authority or that `authority_hash` proves subset membership.
- No global, instantaneous branch revocation mechanism in the first version.

## Deliverables / acceptance criteria

1. A companion draft defining the profile and trust/freshness declarations above.
2. Cross-references and scope corrections in Cross-Domain Projection and Offline Attenuation.
3. A registered capability declaration and a full conformance matrix.
4. At least one three-domain reference flow and negative vectors for every failure class listed above.
5. Security and privacy text covering compromised delegation keys, chain correlation, origin-principal disclosure, state staleness, chain-size exhaustion, and branch revocation.


## Analysis and recommendation

(Architect review, 2026-08-13. Claims verified against the drafts at HEAD.)

**Verdict: sound; build after #433 and #539 land.** The two load-bearing decisions are correct and verified against the current texts:

- The Project-versus-Delegate verb separation matches the actual boundaries: Cross-Domain Projection is single-hop by design with multi-domain chaining explicitly future work; Child Delegation requires the child issuer to equal `parent.issuer`; Offline Attenuation already carries `par_hash`/`del_depth`/`del_max_depth` with the full parent chain and the unchanged Mission binding. Profiling attenuation, rather than stretching the cross-domain grant or inventing a second recursive format, is the smallest correct move.
- "A local projected token is never a new portable delegation root" is the credential-plane twin of the Work Products rule (information may propagate, authority may not). Keep it prominent: it is the sentence that prevents projection from silently becoming delegation.

### Corrections before build

1. **Invariance wording.** State the mission-claim invariant the way the substrate does: value equality of the named members (the root's `id`, `issuer`, `authority_hash`, plus `subject` once #539 lands), not byte preservation. Each hop is a freshly signed JWT and serializers differ; the substrate's own convention is member-value equality ("every token in the chain carries the same `id`, `issuer`, and `authority_hash` as the root").
2. **Freshness contract.** Where destination verification and the trust model declare maximum age and fail-closed behavior for cached issuer metadata, key status, and Mission state, cite the substrate's Bounded Reliance floor rather than defining a parallel staleness model. One floor, referenced, not restated.
3. **Capability registry host.** "Add a capability declaration for `cross_org_delegation`" must name the owning document and registry (the runtime capability-declaration surface versus the substrate's capability table). Pin it in the deliverables so the declaration has exactly one home.
4. **Depth-rule cross-reference.** The chain rule (never reset `del_depth` at an organizational boundary) will read as contradicting Cross-Domain Projection's local-depth reset unless the scope correction states the split explicitly: chain depth is global and monotonic across hops; projection-local delegation depth is local policy that begins only after chain verification; and a projected token cannot re-enter the chain (per the local-token-not-a-root rule).

### Sequencing

Depends on #433 (actor-chain convention) and #539 (origin-principal invariant). #433 was deferred pending a consumer; with #538/#539/#540 it now has three, so it should graduate to ready-and-blocking and be ruled first. Recommended order: #433, then #539, then this profile in parallel with #540.

### Endorsed as-is

The root-issuance rule that deployment-private entries MUST be omitted rather than crossing under interpretive promises (mirrors the projection discipline); the chain-verifying versus AS-mediated conformance distinction; the honest revocation posture (declared bounded staleness, fail closed, no instant-branch-revocation claim); experimental status while the attenuation substrate is experimental; the negative-vector list, which maps cleanly onto the #245 suite conventions.


## Build plan (analysis round 2, 2026-08-14, post-D80/D81/D82)

**Status: fully unblocked.** Everything this issue was waiting on has landed: the #433 architectural ruling is recorded (PR #544: authorization continuity; per-hop actor model; root actor issuer-attested; identity-to-`cnf` binding trust rule; no nested-history duplication; reconstruction at consuming boundaries; Actor Receipts held to the issuer-mediated lane), the Origin Principal profile is merged (PR #545: `mission.subject`, value-equality invariance, ID-JAG composition, dual-axis, `principal_mapping` evidence, `origin_principal` introspection privilege), and the authenticated introspection principal model those disclosure rules compose with is merged (PR #541). The reference implementation already has both halves of the chain machinery to extend: the AS-side root mint (`src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/attenuation.ts`) and an RS-side chain verifier (`src/services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts`, `@spec attenuation#mission-binding-check`), with `attenuation.test.ts` fixtures.

### Reconciliation: where the landed rulings supersede this issue's own protocol text

This issue predates the rulings; six points of its Proposed Protocol are superseded and the companion must follow the ruled versions:

1. **Per-hop actor, never a nested chain.** The hop-field list ("the RFC 8693 `act` chain") and per-hop rule 8 ("extend, never replace or truncate") are replaced: each chain artifact carries `act` holding exactly ONE profile-conformant actor object (`iss` REQUIRED, `sub`, `sub_profile`), naming only that hop's actor. The ordered history IS the validated root-to-leaf chain; a verifier reconstructs it and rejects conflicting or duplicated representations; the nested RFC 8693 projection is materialized once at a consuming boundary (PDP, introspection, destination AS), never carried per artifact.
2. **The root carries an issuer-attested actor.** Root issuance gains rule 8: the Mission Issuer places the approved agent as the root's `act` (issuer-asserted, bound to the root presenter `cnf`), so approved-agent identity travels with the chain instead of resting on a Mission Record the verifier may not hold. `client_id` and a bare `cnf` are not actor identity.
3. **Holder-asserted identities need the binding rule.** A named actor on a holder-created hop counts only when `(act.iss, act.sub)` is independently bound to that hop's `cnf` through a validated workload credential or attestation resolved via the federation mapping this issue's Trust Model already requires. Absent that binding the hop is key-only: its asserted identity is informational at most, MUST NOT satisfy `allowed_delegates`/`sub_profile` or influence authorization, and where policy requires a named actor, verification fails closed. (Recorded as binding constraints in attenuation's `{#actor-attribution}`; this companion supplies the wire member and verification semantics, generalized into the substrate afterward per the #433 sequencing answer.)
4. **The invariant member set now includes the principal.** "The unchanged `mission` claim (id, issuer, authority_hash, plus any members required by the principal-semantics issue)" is now concrete: `mission.subject` (closed `{iss, sub}`, VALUE equality per the merged convention) is REQUIRED on every artifact of a conforming chain, root-attested and invariance-verified; the multi-tenant unambiguity bar and pseudonym-at-record-creation rules apply as merged.
5. **AS-mediated provenance is not Actor Receipts.** For the AS-mediated consumption class, the bridge is one of: the validated chain carried alongside the local token; the chain exposed through introspection or evidence resolution (the destination AS recorded the chain digest and actor lineage in derivation evidence, plus `principal_mapping`); or a destination-AS **chain-verification attestation** committing to the complete chain and verification result. A destination AS never manufactures issuer receipts for holder-created hops.
6. **Freshness cites the Bounded Reliance floor.** Cached issuer metadata, key status, and Mission state declare maximum age and fail closed under the substrate's existing floor, referenced, not restated; Mission state at the verifier comes from the Status List / Mission Status surfaces.

### Recommendation

Build as **two PRs**, spec first:

- **PR A (spec):** the experimental companion `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-org-delegation` + the cross-domain scope corrections + the attenuation generalization hook. ~M.
- **PR B (implementation):** extend the existing root mint and chain verifier, add the destination-AS consumption path, land the conformance vectors. ~M-L.

Capability declaration: follow the family's existing pattern (no new registry, no new metadata member): the companion defines the `cross_org_delegation` **conformance claim** with two named consumption classes, advertised through existing surfaces exactly as Cross-Domain advertises its capability; the runtime/consumer sweep rule (MUST-declare consumption) applies as elsewhere.

### PR A: companion section map (with the details that matter)

1. **Status:** Experimental; profiles Mission Offline Attenuation; one wire format (holder-mediated); the issuer-mediated alternative and its actor-suite evidence layer (Receipts/Proofs/Bounds) documented as related work, with the Authority Bounds caution (every basis-reset or widening mechanism, including `domain_transition`, prohibited within a Mission; widening is Expansion).
2. **Roles and artifact:** the Delegation Chain = attenuation root + children in root-to-leaf order, substrate serialization and token type; Project-vs-Delegate framing; a projected local token is never a delegation root.
3. **Hop members:** the substrate's envelope (`iss`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`, explicit `typ`), `authorization_details`, `aud`, `cnf`, `par_hash`/`del_depth`/`del_max_depth`; plus this profile's `act` (ONE profile-conformant actor object per hop, REQUIRED) and the invariant `mission` claim (`id`, `issuer`, `authority_hash`, `subject`).
4. **Root issuance:** this issue's rules 1-7 as written, plus rule 8 (issuer-attested root actor = the approved agent, bound to root `cnf`) and the omission rule for deployment-private entries verbatim.
5. **Per-hop derivation:** this issue's rules minus act-nesting: sign with the parent's `cnf` key; bind via `par_hash`; narrow/preserve every entry under registered subset semantics; `aud` equal-or-narrower; `exp` no later; increment `del_depth` with no boundary reset; `mission` value-invariant including `subject`; set THIS hop's `act`; bind the leaf to the recipient's PoP key.
6. **Trust model:** the federation mapping from this issue verbatim, extended with one row: actor-identity attestation sources (trust-domain to workload-credential anchors for the `(act.iss, act.sub)`-to-`cnf` binding).
7. **Destination verification (the merged ordered algorithm):** (1) resolve the origin Mission Issuer through deployment/federation policy, never from the chain; (2) validate the root: type, signature, time, Mission-Issuer equality, issuer-attested root actor, `mission.subject` present and equal to the root record commitment; (3) validate every `par_hash` link and child signature through the leaf; (4) verify `mission` invariants (value equality, including `subject`) across all hops; (5) verify monotonic `del_depth`, the global maximum, nested `aud`/`exp`, and every subset relation; rejecting any unknown type, action, constraint, comparison rule, or actor-binding profile; (6) classify each hop's actor: named (binding validated) or key-only (asserted identity inert); fail closed where policy requires a named actor; (7) reconstruct the ordered actor history from the validated artifacts; reject conflicting or duplicated representations; (8) verify the leaf presenter's PoP; identity verification never substitutes for the authority-chain checks; (9) establish Mission state from a local state source within the declared freshness bound (Status List / Mission Status; Bounded Reliance floor; fail closed on stale or missing state); (10) authorize dual-axis per the Origin Principal profile: verified delegated authority ∩ current entitlement of the mapped origin principal ∩ local policy, with the ID-JAG-composition and `principal_mapping` rules where a local token is minted.
8. **Local projection:** this issue's mint rules verbatim, plus: local `act` restarts at the local delegate (D80); `mission.subject` unchanged; derivation evidence records the chain digest, leaf `jti`, input and output authority, reconstructed actor lineage, policy version, and `principal_mapping`.
9. **AS-mediated provenance bridge:** the three options above; the chain-verification attestation defined minimally (explicit `typ`; members: chain digest, leaf `jti`, verification result, verifying-AS policy version, verified-at) as an AS attestation about verification, OPTIONAL in v1.
10. **Conformance:** two classes (chain-verifying / AS-mediated, worded per this issue) with the full negative-vector list from this issue plus four rows the rulings added: root missing the issuer-attested actor; named-actor hop without a validated binding influencing authorization (must not); duplicated/conflicting actor representation (nested history smuggled onto a hop); `mission.subject` removed or substituted at a hop.
11. **Security/Privacy:** this issue's list, plus actor-identifier correlation (issuer-qualified identifiers are correlation handles; pairwise guidance as for `mission.subject`) and chain-size/DoS bounds (max hops, max artifact size, verification-cost ceiling, declared).

**Cross-domain corrections in the same PR:** the future-work sentences (~L549-557) repoint to the companion; the depth split stated (chain `del_depth` is global; projection-local delegation depth starts after chain verification; a projected token cannot re-enter a chain); the delegate-crossing exclusion narrowed to "except via the companion's verified chain."

**Attenuation hook:** one sentence under `{#actor-attribution}` naming the companion as the profile that defines the member (the generalization into the substrate itself remains the later step, per the #433 sequencing answer).

### PR B: implementation plan

- `kernel/attenuation.ts` (root mint): add the issuer-attested root `act` (from the Mission record's approved client + its `sub_profile`) and `mission.subject`; refuse roots for entries without registered subset semantics (already structural) and where policy forbids the boundary crossing.
- Chain derivation helper (holder-side, test/demo): per-hop `act`, `par_hash`, narrowing; used by fixtures to build A→B→C chains across three synthetic trust domains (three issuers/keys in config; federation mapping as a typed config surface, mirroring `introspection.json`).
- `mcp-payments/server.ts` verifier: extend `mission-binding-check` into the full ten-step algorithm (chain-verifying class); actor classification (named vs key-only) against a config-driven workload-attestation map; reconstruction + conflicting-representation rejection.
- Destination-AS path (`kernel/cross-domain.ts` + provider): accept a verified chain as the cross-org input, apply the Origin Principal mapping (AuthZEN check-10 semantics), mint the local token with restarted `act`, record derivation evidence + `principal_mapping` (AS-mediated class).
- Tests: the conformance matrix rows 1:1 (valid three-domain chain; widening at either hop; constraint and `requires_action_approval` removal; parent-hash substitution, reorder, missing hop, changed Mission binding incl. `subject`, untrusted root; depth reset and overflow; wrong leaf PoP; actor-binding absent where required, key-only hop identity inert; duplicated actor representation; unknown type/action/constraint/subset algorithm; revoked/expired Mission, stale/unavailable state; projected-token-as-parent refused; valid authority denied by local entitlement).
- Full gate as usual (typecheck, tests 0-skipped, lint).

### Open questions (blocking PR A only on the first)

1. **Companion name:** `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-org-delegation` (mirrors the cross-domain naming lane)?
2. **The chain-verification attestation:** define minimally in v1 (recommended: it is the only AS-mediated bridge that survives local-token expiry) or defer to a follow-on?
3. **Capability surface:** conformance claim + existing metadata (recommended, no new members) confirmed?

issues.title: Cross-domain identity: preserve the origin principal and require dual-axis authorization
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
## Problem

[`draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01) requires the original on-behalf-of principal to remain invariant across organizational delegation, while each relying party authorizes on two independent axes: the agent's delegated authority and that principal's entitlement to the target resource.

The Mission family currently has a sound two-namespace subject model inside one issuing domain:

- the Mission Record stores the external Subject as an immutable `{iss, sub}` pair;
- an AS maps that principal injectively to the access token's local `sub`; and
- delegated actors travel separately in the RFC 8693 `act` chain.

The [Cross-Domain Projection](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/cb06c89699aae0a134f01e438f55614de940a2b1/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.md) draft intentionally leaves cross-domain subject mapping to the underlying identity grant and local policy. A local token preserves the Mission reference but does not carry the Mission's external Subject. Consequently, a downstream RS that cannot query the origin can verify the token issuer and carried authority, but cannot independently establish that the same origin principal survived every mapping or apply principal entitlement against an issuer-qualified origin identity.

This is not solved by #433. The `act` chain identifies agents/delegates; it does not identify the human or service on whose behalf they act, and RFC 8693 explicitly separates delegation from impersonation.

## Recommendation

Profile one existing namespace instead of creating multiple top-level identity parameters:

- add a required `subject` member to the open `mission` claim **only for the cross-organizational profile**;
- use the Mission Record's existing closed `{iss, sub}` shape;
- carry it unchanged through the delegation chain and every local projection;
- keep standard token `sub` as the Resource AS's local subject and standard `client_id`/`act` as actor identity; and
- require authorization to be the intersection of delegated Mission authority, current principal entitlement, and local resource policy.

The resulting model has three deliberately separate identities:

| Identity | Wire location | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Origin principal | `mission.subject = {iss, sub}` | Immutable on-behalf-of principal approved by the Mission Issuer |
| Local subject | JWT `sub` with JWT `iss` | Destination-domain account/principal mapped from the origin principal |
| Acting workload(s) | `client_id`, `act`, and leaf `cnf` | The client and delegation lineage exercising authority |

Do not overload any one of these to mean another.

## Proposed specification

### 1. `mission.subject`

The cross-organizational profile defines this member in the existing open `mission` claim:

`subject`:
: REQUIRED for a credential or delegation chain claiming cross-organizational conformance. A closed object containing exactly:
  - `iss`: REQUIRED string identifying the Subject's home issuer; and
  - `sub`: REQUIRED string identifying the Subject within that issuer's namespace.

The value MUST equal the immutable `subject` object in the originating Mission Record. It MUST remain byte-for-byte unchanged in every delegation hop, cross-domain grant, projected local token, introspection projection used by this profile, and runtime decision context derived from them.

The member is identity provenance and a constraint input. It MUST NOT grant or widen authority. A generic Mission consumer may ignore it under the core open-object rule; a consumer claiming this profile MUST understand and verify it or fail closed.

No additional display name, email, organization name, role, group, entitlement, or assurance claim belongs in this object. Those values change independently and would turn the invariant into stale identity/authorization state.

### 2. Origin issuance

Before placing `mission.subject` on a credential, the Mission Issuer MUST:

1. take it from the approved immutable Mission Record, never from a token request parameter;
2. ensure the current local token `sub` is the injective AS-local mapping of that same Subject under the core approval rules;
3. disclose it only to audiences permitted by Mission policy and the deployment's privacy policy; and
4. use a pairwise or sector-specific subject identifier when the home issuer supports one and the receiving trust relationship does not require a globally correlatable identifier.

The Subject cannot be replaced by the current agent, approver, Mission owner, tenant, or a local account selected by the client.

### 3. Mapping at a destination Resource AS

A Resource AS consuming a conforming cross-organizational grant or delegation chain MUST establish a mapping:

```text
(mission.subject.iss, mission.subject.sub)
    -- local mapping policy/version -->
(local token iss, local token sub)
```

The mapping MUST be:

- based on authenticated issuer-qualified input, not a bare `sub`;
- injective within the mapping scope unless the deployment explicitly supports a governed many-to-one service account and treats the loss of individual attribution as a lower assurance class;
- established by the Resource AS or an identity service it trusts, not asserted by the agent;
- scoped to the destination audience/tenant;
- subject to current disablement, unlinking, and reassignment state; and
- recorded with a mapping-policy identifier/version and a digest of the issuer-qualified input and local output.

The local access token retains ordinary OAuth semantics:

- `iss` is the Resource AS;
- `sub` is the destination-local subject;
- `client_id` is the client requesting that token;
- `act` is the agent/delegate identity lineage under #433; and
- `mission.subject` is the unchanged origin principal.

The Resource AS signature attests to the mapping for the token's audience and lifetime. A separate subject-mapping assertion is not introduced in the base profile. A deployment that needs the mapping to be independently portable after the local token expires can register the existing derivation record with the audit profile; that is evidence, not authority.

### 4. Mapping continuity

Every downstream hop MUST compare `mission.subject` with the parent value before doing local mapping. Any removal, substitution, different issuer with the same `sub`, different `sub` under the same issuer, or type/shape change invalidates the complete chain.

Re-mapping is allowed at each Resource AS because local accounts are local facts. Replacing the origin principal is not. A downstream mapping does not make the destination-local `sub` the new origin for later hops.

If a mapping is missing, ambiguous, disabled, stale beyond the declared bound, or points to a principal not permitted for the requested tenant/audience, the Resource AS MUST refuse issuance or the RP MUST deny. It MUST NOT create an account or relationship merely because a valid delegation chain was presented unless a separate governed provisioning flow authorizes that state change.

### 5. Dual-axis authorization

At every point of use, the effective authority is:

```text
verified delegated authorization_details
  ∩ current entitlement of the mapped origin principal
  ∩ current resource/deployment policy
```

All three terms are required. In particular:

- valid delegated agent authority does not confer a missing customer/account/resource relationship on the principal;
- a principal entitlement does not authorize an agent action absent from the delegated Authority Set;
- an approval or mapping record does not bypass current policy; and
- a local role or relationship granted through an access-request workflow is governance state. The PDP observes it on a fresh decision; the workflow result is not a bearer bypass.

Each deployment MUST declare the source and maximum staleness of local principal entitlement. If current entitlement cannot be established within that bound, the decision fails closed. Mission-state freshness and entitlement freshness are separate declarations and MUST NOT be collapsed into one timestamp.

### 6. Runtime/AuthZEN carriage

Extend the AuthZEN binding's existing `context.mission` object with the same `subject` object for requests claiming the cross-organizational profile. Preserve the current roles:

- `subject.id` and `subject.properties.iss` describe the authenticated destination-local token subject;
- `context.actor` describes the acting client and RFC 8693 actor chain; and
- `context.mission.subject` describes the immutable origin principal.

The PEP MUST populate `context.mission.subject` only from a verified token/chain or trusted local token metadata. It MUST NOT copy an unverified request value. The PDP MUST compare it with the identity used for local-entitlement lookup and bind the permit and evidence to both origin and local subject identities.

To avoid exposing raw identifiers in retained evidence, Decision/Execution/derivation records SHOULD carry an issuer-qualified subject digest and mapping-policy version unless the raw identity is necessary for the stated audit purpose. The digest convention must be domain-separated and owned by the evidence profile; this issue does not create another generic evidence envelope.

### 7. Privacy and correlation

`mission.subject` makes an otherwise origin-local identity visible across audiences and can become a correlation handle. Therefore:

- origin issuers SHOULD use pairwise/pseudonymous subject identifiers where interoperability permits;
- tokens MUST be narrowed to one Resource AS/RS audience;
- Resource ASs MUST NOT copy the member into tokens for unrelated audiences;
- logs and evidence SHOULD retain digests/references instead of raw values where possible; and
- the trust agreement MUST state the purpose and retention period for the mapping.

The member MUST NOT contain human-readable PII.

## Conformance and tests

Add positive and negative tests for:

- one origin principal mapped to different valid local subjects in two resource domains while `mission.subject` stays unchanged;
- a valid three-hop chain whose `act` lineage changes while the principal does not;
- same `sub` under a different `iss`;
- changed or removed `mission.subject` at an intermediate hop;
- client-supplied subject substitution at token exchange;
- valid agent authority with no principal entitlement;
- valid principal entitlement with no delegated agent authority;
- stale, disabled, ambiguous, unlinked, or tenant-wrong mapping;
- local role/relationship grant followed by fresh re-evaluation;
- unknown cross-org subject semantics at a consumer claiming the profile; and
- privacy projection: origin subject absent from unrelated-audience tokens and raw subject absent from evidence where the declared profile uses digests.

The test oracle must evaluate the two authorization axes independently so an implementation cannot pass by treating the valid delegation chain as the principal entitlement.

## Dependencies and coordination

- #433 owns the RFC 8693 actor chain. This issue relies on it and MUST NOT invent `approved_client`, a second actor chain, or authority semantics for `act`.
- #538 requires this invariant before it can claim the Reece principal requirements.
- #540 binds per-action authorization to `mission.subject` and the acting key.
- Cross-Domain Projection, core Mission claim, AuthZEN, runtime evidence, audit, mandate/introspection projections, and the reference implementation must be updated coherently. A partial edit would create contradictory principal meanings.

## Tradeoffs

**One new nested member:** adding `mission.subject` is wire-visible and increases correlation risk, but it reuses the canonical Mission Subject shape and the existing `mission` namespace. Alternatives such as `origin_sub`, `obo`, `subject_issuer`, and mapping claims at the JWT top level multiply parameters and are easier to confuse with standard `sub`.

**Local mapping remains local:** the profile standardizes the input, invariants, and authorization rule, not a universal account-linking protocol. This preserves enterprise control and avoids turning Mission into identity provisioning, at the cost of deployment-specific mapping setup.

**No standalone mapping assertion by default:** the Resource AS's local token signature is sufficient on the enforcement path and avoids another credential. Durable third-party audit uses existing derivation evidence. A standalone mapping assertion may be useful later for mesh deployments, but should be added only after a consumer demonstrates that the local token/audit paths are insufficient.

**Dual-axis checks cost availability:** offline verification of the authority chain does not eliminate the need for current local entitlement. Cached entitlement permits bounded-disconnected operation but introduces a declared stale-entitlement window; immediate relationship revocation requires an online/local source.

**Privacy versus verifiability:** carrying an issuer-qualified principal lets an RP verify continuity without an origin callback, but reveals a stable identifier. Pairwise subject identifiers and audience-specific tokens reduce, not eliminate, this tradeoff.

## Non-goals

- No change to `mission_intent` or intent-admission provenance.
- No actor authority in the `act` claim.
- No roles, groups, entitlements, approval state, or PII inside `mission.subject`.
- No automatic local-account creation or relationship grant.
- No claim that subject mapping proves the delegated authority chain.

## Deliverables / acceptance criteria

1. Normative `mission.subject` definition in a cross-organizational companion, with core extensibility and privacy cross-references.
2. Cross-Domain, AuthZEN, runtime, evidence/audit, introspection/mandate, and implementation changes that preserve the three-identity separation.
3. A deployment declaration for subject-mapping and entitlement sources/freshness.
4. A conformance matrix covering mapping continuity, dual-axis authorization, and privacy projection.
5. Worked examples showing one origin principal, two local mappings, and a changing multi-hop `act` chain without identity conflation.


## Analysis and recommendation

(Architect review, 2026-08-13. Claims verified against the drafts at HEAD.)

**Verdict: correct foundation; two fixes and one placement decision before build.** Verified: the Mission Record stores the Subject as an immutable `{iss, sub}` pair and the core's injective mapping is an issuer-side approval-event rule; the `mission` claim is an open object whose unknown members generic consumers MUST ignore, so a profile-required nested member follows the established pattern (`containment_version` precedent); the AuthZEN binding already separates `subject` (local token subject), `context.actor` (acting lineage, never in `subject`), and `context.mission`; RFC 8693 act semantics are owned by #433. The three-identity table (origin principal / local subject / acting workloads) is the right decomposition and matches the family's continuity separation: identity, authorization, and evidence are different continuities, and this member is identity provenance used as a constraint input, never authority.

### Fixes

1. **Replace "byte-for-byte" with value equality of the closed `{iss, sub}` object.** The invariant must survive re-serialization: every attenuation hop is a freshly signed JWT, a projected local token is minted by a different AS's serializer, and an introspection response is dynamically serialized JSON. Byte equality is untestable on those surfaces; the attenuation substrate's own invariance convention is member-value equality. If a canonical form is ever needed for digests, use the family anchor idiom (JCS + typed digest), not raw bytes.
2. **Gate introspection disclosure with the introspection-principal model.** "Introspection projection used by this profile" must not carry the origin principal to every audience-authorized caller: `mission.subject` is exactly the correlation handle the authenticated-introspection surface (#526, PR #541) privilege-gates. Disclose it the way `proposal_hash` is disclosed: issuer-only is authority to assert, not authorization to disclose; a per-principal disclosure privilege governs carriage, composing with the pairwise-identifier guidance already in the privacy section.
3. **Decide the host document.** Deliverable 1 says "a cross-organizational companion" while #538 also proposes one, leaving it ambiguous whether the family gets one cross-org document or two. Recommendation: host `mission.subject` in the existing Cross-Domain Projection draft, profile-gated. The gap exists in today's single-hop grant too (this issue's own problem statement says so), and hosting there keeps a foundation invariant out of a document that depends on the experimental attenuation substrate. #538's companion then imports it. This also keeps the new-document count at two.

### Clarifications worth one sentence each

- Scope the dual-axis rule explicitly as this profile's conformance bar: deployments not claiming the profile keep the family's lifetime-bounded baseline, and runtime state evaluation stays a targeted overlay.
- When defining the destination-side mapping, cross-reference the core's issuer-side injective rule and state that these are different mappings, so the core rule is visibly untouched; the governed many-to-one service-account exception applies only to the destination mapping and correctly names its assurance downgrade.

### Sequencing

The foundation label is right. #433 first (the act convention now has three consumers), then this issue, then #538 and #540. The deliverable-2 blast radius (cross-domain, AuthZEN, runtime evidence, audit, introspection/mandate, implementation) is real; the introspection change should compose with PR #541's projection matrix rather than landing as a parallel edit.

**Session disposition (2026-08-23, architecture-review follow-through; verified against main @ 2d63119a):**

**Analysis**

Spec shipped on three surfaces, but implementation shipped on one and a half, not zero. `authorization-server/src/adapters/cross-org-grant.ts` (176-242) plus `kernel/cross-org-chain.ts` already do destination mapping: an issuer-qualified `mappingPolicy.entries` lookup, a minted local token with `mission.subject` preserved, and a `principal_mapping` evidence push (policy id/version, observed/valid timestamps). Its "dual axis" is `inputAuthority ∩ localCeiling`, a static ceiling, not current entitlement of the mapped principal: two of the spec's three required terms, not three. `mission-core/txn-authorization.ts` threads `origin_principal` through the approval binding at admission/completion (#616); the manifest's own notes on `txn-authorization.token.subject-namespace-mapping` and `.redemption.subject-mapping-revalidated` mark mapping revalidation and the foreign-issuer registry as unbuilt.

Two genuine zeros remain. `services/pdp/src/evaluate.ts`: `context.mission`'s type (line 84) has no `subject` member, `DenialReason` (94-112) has no `principal_mapping_failed`, and no entitlement lookup exists anywhere. Both todo AuthZEN rows (`origin-principal-mapping-required`, `context-mission.origin-principal-only-from-verified-source`) gate here. `services/ras/src/index.ts` `redeem()`: line 73's `mission` destructure omits `subject` (dropped on projection), and `.setSubject(String(payload.sub))` blind-copies with no co-resolution check, both direct violations of cross-domain#origin-principal-mapping. The 11-scenario list has no fixtures in `pdp/test` or `evals/fixtures`.

**Sketch**

PR A, PDP dual-axis primitive: add `subject?: {iss,sub}` to `context.mission`, add `principal_mapping_failed` to `DenialReason`, and add an `EvaluateOptions` entry beside `allowedFreshnessSources` (same fail-closed-on-unconfigured idiom) for entitlement resolution and its own staleness bound, kept separate from `stalenessBoundSeconds` per the profile's no-collapse rule. Implement rule 10's `mapped_subject` equality and entitlement check in `evaluateInner`.

PR B, RAS fix: type the mission destructure to include `subject`, add a mapping-policy lookup before minting, refuse `invalid_grant` on a missing/ambiguous mapping, carry `mission.subject` unchanged. Extend `cross-org-grant.ts`'s ceiling-only axis to also consult current entitlement so both surfaces share one contract.

PR C: the 11-scenario fixture suite, flipping the two todo rows and the txn-authorization partials.

**Recommendation**

PR A first (closes both todo rows, the surface the spec actually gates dual-axis on), then PR B, then PR C. PR B doesn't block PR A. #650 touches the same mint block in `ras/index.ts`; sequence it first since it's already `decide`-labeled with a direction and adds the registered-client plumbing PR B's mapping sits beside, but PR B isn't blocked by it: `client_id` is actor identity, `mission.subject` is principal identity, independent fields on one mint call.

**Tradeoffs**

Confirmed `policyViewId` (policy-view.ts:69-77) hashes a pinned field subset, not the whole view, so PR A's `context.mission` addition doesn't perturb existing pinned `policy_view_id` values. Keep `cross-org-grant.ts`'s static ceiling after PR A ships: it's a legitimate independent bound (resource/deployment policy), just not sufficient alone as "dual axis."
