comments.body:
Fresh review against `origin/main` at `2d63119a`: the PDP-first direction is reasonable, but the proposed PR A is not a complete vertical slice and would not close both AuthZEN rows.

`origin-principal-only-from-verified-source` is a PEP obligation as well as a PDP check. The token validators discard `mission.subject`; the PEP constructs neither `context.mission.subject` nor `subject.properties.iss`; and the current evaluation request cannot represent an issuer-qualified local subject. Yet the normative comparison is against `(subject.properties.iss, subject.id)` after mapping. PR A therefore needs the full verified-token → `TokenFacts` → AuthZEN-envelope path, an issuer-qualified local subject, and separate fail-closed mapping and current-entitlement resolver contracts. A generic entitlement resolver is insufficient unless it also returns mapping-policy identity/version, observation time/validity, and an independently freshness-bounded entitlement.

The existing Cross-Org adapter is less complete than the proposal assumes. Its static `.find` mapping cannot reject duplicate/ambiguous, disabled, stale, audience-wrong, or tenant-wrong mappings. `localCeiling` covers delegated authority intersected with local policy, not the current-entitlement term, and `valid_until` is assigned from token expiry without a mapping source proving that validity.

The RAS repair is required—it omits `mission.subject`, performs no destination mapping or identity-grant/Origin-Principal co-resolution, and blind-copies foreign `sub`—but Cross-Org must be repaired in the same implementation wave. Fixing only RAS leaves another profile entry point violating the same dual-axis requirements.

Revised sequence:

1. Shared mapping/entitlement contracts plus the complete PEP/PDP AuthZEN vertical slice.
2. Apply those contracts to both Cross-Org exchange and the ID-JAG RAS path.
3. Integration/privacy completion.

Tests and conformance-row updates should accompany each behavior PR, not wait for a later 11-scenario batch.

Evidence: [token validation](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/src/services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts#L238-L313), [PEP request](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/src/services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts#L553-L586), [AuthZEN rule 10](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md#L1045-L1077), [Cross-Org mapping](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/src/services/authorization-server/src/adapters/cross-org-grant.ts#L33-L65), and [RAS redemption](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/src/services/ras/src/index.ts#L73-L106).

Disposition: revise materially; build the end-to-end primitive and repair both entry paths before claiming either AuthZEN row closed.

issues.title: Runtime: profile portable cross-domain transaction authorization
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
## Problem

[`draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01) requires some delegated actions to remain subject to execution-time human authorization. The requirement is stronger than “MFA happened” or “a user once approved the Mission”: the authorization must be bound to the concrete action, parameters, resource, on-behalf-of principal, and authorized presenter; the designation must survive delegation; enforcement must work without a live callback to the approval authority; and the result must be usable at most once.

The Mission family already has the right policy model:

- the Common Constraint `requires_action_approval: true` is monotonic under subset and cannot be stripped by a child;
- [Mission Runtime](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/cb06c89699aae0a134f01e438f55614de940a2b1/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md) defines fresh action-bound approval, concrete-parameter binding, maximum age, fresh decision, TOCTOU checks, and atomic idempotency;
- [Mission AuthZEN](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/cb06c89699aae0a134f01e438f55614de940a2b1/draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md) correctly treats an ARAP approval as input to a fresh PDP decision, never as a bearer bypass; and
- the implementation has a de-risking transaction-challenge path, while #286 owns engagement with `draft-rosomakho-oauth-txn-challenge`.

What is missing is a profiled portable wire result for the cross-domain case. The runtime draft intentionally does not define that wire workflow. AuthZEN/ARAP normally assumes the PDP can resolve or verify approval state, and the current prototype carries a private `approval` object and a redundant `single_use` boolean. Neither is yet a composed interoperability contract for an RP that must enforce locally.

## Recommendation

Define a **Mission Transaction Authorization Profile** of `draft-rosomakho-oauth-txn-challenge`:

1. the protected resource signs a short-lived challenge for one normalized operation;
2. a trusted Transaction Authorization Server validates the challenge, Mission/delegation authority, presenter, and human/governance approval;
3. that server performs a fresh authorization decision with the approval as decision input; and
4. only after permit, it issues a sender-constrained, audience-restricted, single-use transaction access token that the resource can verify locally.

Keep the model small:

- retain `requires_action_approval` as the only Authority Set designation; do not add approval issuer, method, age, or UI parameters to RAR;
- use the standard JWT envelope, existing `authorization_details`, existing `mission` claim, existing `act` chain, existing `cnf`, and the runtime's existing `parameter_digest`;
- make single use semantic to the token `typ`; do not carry `single_use: true`;
- do not carry a generic `approval` object in the token; and
- keep Consent/Decision/Execution Evidence on the evidence and audit planes, correlated by transaction/token identifiers rather than embedded as a grab bag in every request.

The approval is not authority. The transaction token is authority because a trusted AS issued it after a fresh decision bounded by the Mission and the approved operation.

## Proposed protocol

### 1. Applicability

The profile is invoked when any of these requires action-bound approval:

- the matched Authority Set entry carries `constraints.requires_action_approval: true`;
- destination resource policy requires approval for the action/risk class; or
- a current local entitlement/governance rule requires it.

A delegated child MUST preserve `requires_action_approval: true` under the Common Constraints subset rule. `false` remains equivalent to omission and cannot override a `true` ancestor. This profile defines no second approval constraint.

Step-up authentication is not a substitute. A step-up obligation proves a stronger authentication context; it does not approve the transaction. A durable role/relationship grant produced by ARAP is also not an approval token: it becomes current governance state and the PDP re-evaluates it.

### 2. Resource challenge

After receiving an ordinary Mission-bound request, the PEP normalizes the operation under its Operation Profile and computes the runtime `parameter_digest`. If approval is required and no valid transaction token is present, the resource returns a signed transaction challenge.

The challenge is a JWT with an explicit `typ` registered/profiled for Mission transaction authorization. It contains:

- standard `iss`, `aud`, `iat`, `exp`, and `jti` claims, where `iss` is the protected resource and `aud` is the selected Transaction Authorization Server;
- `txn`, the resource-scoped transaction identifier;
- exactly one operation-scoped `authorization_details` entry or one compound-action detail whose registered semantics make it atomic;
- `parameter_digest`, computed exactly as Mission Runtime specifies;
- `mission`, copied from the verified credential/chain and including the invariant origin principal where the cross-organizational principal profile applies; and
- `cnf`, identifying the presenter key to which the resulting token must be bound.

The resource MUST derive these values from the request and verified credential. It MUST NOT accept client-supplied replacements. Raw action parameters SHOULD remain outside the challenge when the Transaction Authorization Server can authorize from the digest plus privacy-preserving attributes; where it needs raw values to render or decide, they travel through an authenticated/confidential request channel and are recomputed against the digest.

Challenge `exp` MUST be short and no later than the presented credential/chain, Mission expiry, and resource-declared challenge ceiling.

### 3. Challenge redemption and approval

The client presents the signed challenge, the current Mission-bound token or cross-organizational delegation chain, proof of the challenge's `cnf` key, and any separately authenticated attributes required by policy to the Transaction Authorization Server's endpoint.

The server MUST, in order:

1. authenticate the client/presenter and verify possession of the challenge-bound key;
2. resolve the challenge issuer to a registered resource and validate its exact `typ`, signature, audience, time, and `jti` replay state;
3. validate the Mission-bound token or complete delegation chain, including Mission state, origin principal, actor lineage, authority subset, audience, depth, expiry, and PoP;
4. require exact equality between the challenge Mission and the verified credential/chain Mission invariants;
5. establish that the requested `authorization_details` is within the verified delegated authority and applies to the challenge issuer/resource;
6. enforce `requires_action_approval` and destination policy;
7. obtain or resolve an ARAP-compatible governed approval from an acceptable independent approver/policy authority, bound to `txn`, operation identity, `parameter_digest`, resource, Mission, origin principal, and presenter key;
8. verify approval status, scope, grant time, maximum age, and `approved_until`; and
9. run a fresh PDP decision using the verified approval as context together with current Mission state, principal entitlement, resource policy, and the concrete parameter inputs/attributes.

Any denial ends the flow. Approval completion alone MUST NOT trigger token issuance and MUST NOT bypass step 9.

The set of acceptable Transaction Authorization Servers, resource challenge issuers, and approval authorities is deployment/federation policy. It is not taken from an untrusted request claim. The Transaction Authorization Server may be operated by the origin or destination domain; the resource trusts its signing key and policy role through pre-established federation metadata.

### 4. Transaction token

On permit, the server issues a JWT access token with an explicit `typ` whose registered semantics are “Mission transaction authorization, sender-constrained, single audience, single use.” It contains only:

- standard `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `iat`, `exp`, and `jti` access-token claims;
- ordinary `client_id` and `act` identity semantics where applicable;
- `txn`, copied from the verified challenge;
- the exact permitted `authorization_details`, never wider than the challenge, delegation chain, or current decision;
- `parameter_digest`, copied only after recomputation/verification;
- the unchanged `mission` claim; and
- `cnf`, bound to the verified presenter key.

The token MUST NOT carry:

- a generic `approval` object;
- a `single_use` boolean;
- raw rendered approval text or action parameters;
- roles/relationships conferred by an approval workflow; or
- evidence objects whose lifecycle and disclosure rules belong to the evidence/audit profiles.

The token's `exp` is no later than the earliest of challenge expiry, approval freshness/`approved_until`, current credential or delegation-chain expiry, Mission expiry, and deployment maximum. A short token lifetime limits stale policy and revocation exposure but does not replace point-of-use state checks required by the deployment's runtime claim.

### 5. Offline verification and execution

The protected resource verifies locally, without calling the Transaction Authorization Server on the request path:

1. exact token `typ`, trusted issuer/signature, intended `aud`, `iat`/`exp`, and token class;
2. `cnf` proof by the current presenter;
3. equality of `txn`, Mission invariants, operation `authorization_details`, and recomputed `parameter_digest` with the pending operation;
4. origin principal/local subject/actor consistency under the principal profile;
5. current local policy, principal entitlement, and any required Mission-state observation within their declared freshness bounds; and
6. atomic first use of `(iss, jti)` in the consumption domain.

Consumption MUST be linearizable across every replica capable of executing the same operation. The record is committed before the irreversible effect, or atomically with it where the operation store supports that transaction. If the consumption store is unavailable, enforcement fails closed for this profile.

`txn` identifies the resource transaction; `jti` identifies the issued authorization. The replay key is `(iss, jti)`. A retry after an ambiguous response uses the Operation Profile's idempotency key to retrieve or complete the same result; it never consumes the token to create a second effect. A genuinely new attempt requires a new challenge, approval decision, token, and idempotency key.

### 6. Evidence and audit

The approval service/AS records the Approval Governance/ARAP state and, where configured, Consent Evidence. The PDP emits Decision Evidence and the executor emits Execution Evidence under the existing profiles. They correlate using the Mission reference, `txn`, transaction-token `jti`, `parameter_digest`, and idempotency identity.

Those records do not ride in the transaction token. Where durable independent proof is required, the audit profile registers/receipts the relevant evidence and a Mission Receipt can summarize it. The enforcement token remains small and privacy-minimized; the evidence plane retains the richer account of who approved what and what executed.

The token issuer MUST be able to show that the fresh decision relied on a valid approval, but an RP's authorization decision rests on the trusted typed token plus current local checks, not on parsing an arbitrary evidence blob.

## Failure semantics

- No or expired action approval: deny; the workflow may return/request another approval.
- Approval granted but current policy/entitlement denies: deny; approval is not a bypass.
- Parameter, resource, Mission, principal, presenter, or audience mismatch: terminal refusal for that token/challenge.
- Stale/unavailable required state: fail closed; retry only according to the declared state-recovery policy.
- Consumed token: return the prior idempotent result when the Operation Profile allows it, otherwise `duplicate_suppressed`; never execute again.
- Challenge or token with unknown `typ` or authorization-details semantics: reject, not best-effort parse.

## Conformance and tests

Require positive and negative vectors for:

- valid cross-domain challenge → approval → fresh decision → one execution;
- delegated constraint preservation and attempted removal of `requires_action_approval`;
- MFA/step-up presented without transaction approval;
- valid approval for changed amount, recipient, resource, action, Mission, origin principal, actor, audience, or presenter key;
- approval complete but Authority Set, local entitlement, or resource policy denies;
- missing/changed `parameter_digest` and different canonicalization;
- challenge replay, token replay on one replica, and simultaneous replay across replicas;
- ambiguous first execution followed by an idempotent retry;
- expired challenge, approval, Mission, delegation leaf, or token;
- untrusted resource challenge issuer, transaction issuer, or approval authority;
- arbitrary signed JWT or ordinary Mission token presented as a transaction token;
- privacy projection showing that raw parameters and approval details are absent from the token; and
- evidence correlation from challenge and decision through exactly one execution or terminal refusal.

## Dependencies and coordination

- #286 owns upstream engagement with `draft-rosomakho-oauth-txn-challenge`, including the implementation-derived `parameter_digest` feedback. This issue consumes that work; it does not duplicate the outreach.
- Depends on #539 for cross-domain principal binding.
- Composes with #538; it does not define delegation.
- Reuses Runtime, AuthZEN/ARAP, Approval Governance, Consent Evidence, Runtime Evidence, and Audit. It must not introduce parallel approval/evidence schemas.
- The prototype in `src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/txn-challenge.ts` is a spike, not the specification. Its private `approval` and `single_use` members should be removed or confined to non-conforming demo code when this profile is implemented.

## Tradeoffs

**Transaction token versus portable raw approval:** a typed token lets the RP use normal OAuth validation and attests that an AS performed the fresh combined decision. Carrying raw approval state would expose approver information, force every RP to implement ARAP/governance verification, and tempt implementations to treat approval as a bypass. The cost is that the RP trusts the Transaction Authorization Server's decision rather than independently reconstructing the approval workflow.

**Offline enforcement versus online acquisition:** challenge redemption and human approval may be online and slow; only the final enforcement path is callback-free. This is the achievable boundary. Fully offline approval acquisition would require pre-issued standing authority and would no longer be fresh action authorization.

**At-most-once versus availability:** a linearizable consumed-token store is required across replicas. During partition, fail-closed sacrifices availability. A merely local cache cannot support the claimed at-most-once property.

**Digest privacy versus policy visibility:** `parameter_digest` avoids copying sensitive inputs into tokens, but a PDP/approver may still need authenticated raw or derived attributes to decide and render accurately. Digest-only processing is valid only when policy can evaluate it.

**Short lifetime versus user experience:** short challenge/token windows reduce stale-state and theft exposure but increase approval expiry and retry rates. The deployment must publish ceilings and instrument expirations rather than hide this tradeoff.

**Destination versus origin issuer:** allowing either deployment-selected issuer supports different trust models, but every resource must have an unambiguous accepted issuer set. A token cannot select its own trust authority.

## Non-goals

- No change to `mission_intent`.
- No new standing role, relationship, Mission expansion, or Child Mission.
- No conflation of obligation/step-up with governance approval.
- No generic `approval`, `evidence`, or `provenance` bag in the token.
- No guarantee of at-most-once without a shared atomic consumption domain.
- No claim that approval alone authorizes an action outside current Mission authority or resource policy.

## Deliverables / acceptance criteria

1. A Mission transaction-authorization companion/profile with the exact challenge, token, processing, trust, and failure rules above.
2. Runtime and AuthZEN composition text preserving approval-as-input and fresh PDP authority.
3. Resource/AS metadata for accepted challenge and transaction-token issuers, keys, algorithms, and lifetime ceilings, reusing upstream metadata where available.
4. A multi-replica reference implementation with atomic consumption and idempotent retry.
5. Conformance vectors for every binding, replay, trust, policy, expiry, and privacy failure above.
6. Evidence/audit correlation showing one decision maps to exactly one execution or a recorded refusal.


## Analysis and recommendation

(Architect review, 2026-08-13. Claims verified against the drafts and implementation at HEAD.)

**Verdict: cleanest of the three; build after #539, coordinated with #286.** Verified: `requires_action_approval` is registered with monotonic intersection semantics (logical OR), so a child cannot strip it; the runtime draft owns fresh action-bound approval, concrete-parameter binding, maximum age, TOCTOU, and atomic idempotency; the AuthZEN binding treats an ARAP approval as decision input, never a bearer bypass; and the spike really does carry the private `approval` object and `single_use: true` members this profile removes (`src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/txn-challenge.ts:92,104-106`). The profile preserves every existing invariant: typ-semantic single use, no approval/evidence/provenance bags in the token, step-up is not approval, `duplicate_suppressed` on consumed tokens, and approval never bypassing the fresh decision (step 9). Also done right and easy to miss: the challenge's `mission` claim is resource-copied, and redemption step 4 re-checks it for exact equality against the verified credential, which closes the resource-as-non-issuer gap.

### Corrections before build

1. **Reuse the metering linearizability contract.** The consumption-domain requirement (linearizable across every replica capable of the same operation, record committed before or atomically with the irreversible effect, fail closed when the store is unavailable) duplicates what the metering companion defines as the Exact-consistency topology profile. Cross-reference that profile's vocabulary for the consumption store instead of defining a second linearizability contract: one atomic-consumption vocabulary family-wide.
2. **Name the Mission-state source.** Offline verification step 5's "Mission-state observation within declared freshness bounds" should name the Status List / Mission Status companion as the intended freshness-bounded state source rather than leaving a new state channel implied. TTL-first: runtime state observation stays the targeted overlay it is everywhere else in the family.
3. **Invariance wording (same fix as #538/#539).** The "unchanged `mission` claim" in the transaction token is value equality of the profiled members, not byte preservation: the transaction token is a freshly signed JWT.

### Sequencing and coordination

Depends on #539 for the origin principal (and transitively on #433 for `act`). #286 owns the rosomakho upstream engagement, including the implementation-derived `parameter_digest` feedback; this profile consumes that work. The spike's `approval` and `single_use` members are removed (or confined to non-conforming demo code) in the implementing PR, per this issue's own coordination note.

### Endorsed as-is

The failure-semantics table; the at-most-once versus availability tradeoff stated honestly (fail closed under partition, no at-most-once claim without a shared atomic consumption domain); the privacy posture (digest in the token, raw parameters over authenticated channels only, no approver detail on the wire); the deployment-selected Transaction Authorization Server with pre-established federation metadata and no self-selected trust authority; evidence correlation by identifiers (`txn`, token `jti`, `parameter_digest`, idempotency identity) rather than embedding; the negative-vector list, which maps cleanly onto the #245 suite conventions.


## PR B build plan (implementation handoff, 2026-08-16)

Recorded so a fresh session can build PR B cold. Spec PRs #558 + #560 merged; **the implementation is pending and this issue stays open for it.** The authoritative contract is the MERGED draft on `main`: `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md` — read it in full first; do not edit any `draft-*.md`. This replaces a non-conforming spike; keep only the reusable signing, ARAP task-correlation, and transaction-engine pieces.

### Setup
Fetch main, `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/540b -b feat/540-txn-authz-impl origin/main`, work there. Push via `git -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization.git HEAD:refs/heads/feat/540-txn-authz-impl`.

### The contract (merged-spec sections; implement to these, do not restate/edit them)
- **Resource Challenge** `{#resource-challenge}`: signed JWT typ `txn-authz-challenge+jwt` (upstream), upstream claims (`iss, aud, iat, exp, jti, txn, authorization_details, reason`; optional `act, reason_uri`) PLUS this profile's REQUIRED `mission` (copied from the verified Mission-bound token incl. `mission.subject`), `parameter_digest` (runtime's), `cnf` (presenter key). The RS derives `mission`/`parameter_digest`/`cnf` from the request + verified token, never client-supplied. Operation Profile resolves from challenge `iss` + the RAR entry `type`.
- **Redemption** `{#challenge-redemption}`: endpoint `transaction_authorization_endpoint`; params = client auth (`client_id`), `transaction_challenge`, `subject_token` (the Mission-bound access token), `subject_token_type` = `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token`, + PoP (DPoP/mTLS) of the challenge `cnf`. TAS resolves the challenge issuer's keys from THAT resource's `txn_challenge_jwks_uri` (per-issuer, NOT one shared JWKS), then 7 ordered steps: (1) `subject_token` aud == challenge `iss` AND its `cnf` == request PoP; (2) challenge `mission` == `subject_token` mission invariants (value-equal); (3) challenge `authorization_details` ⊆ `subject_token` Authority Set and applies to challenge iss/resource; (4) enforce `requires_action_approval` + destination policy; (5) obtain governed ARAP approval bound to `txn`/operation/`parameter_digest`/resource/Mission/origin-principal/presenter-key; (6) verify approval status/scope/grant-time/max-age/`approved_until`; (7) **FRESH authorization decision** with the approval as context + current Mission state + `subject_token` validity + client/key binding + entitlement + policy + concrete params. **Step 6 alone MUST NOT issue and MUST NOT bypass step 7.**
- **Two-Phase Expiry** `{#two-phase-expiry}`: challenge `exp` = admission only (late challenge → new workflow, never revived); pending workflow (`transaction_authorization_id`) has its OWN deployment-declared lifetime (upstream `expires_in`); token `exp` bounded by fresh inputs + workflow-remaining, NEVER by the consumed challenge `exp`. Repeated initial submission of the same `(challenge issuer, challenge jti, client, cnf)` MUST return the existing workflow or fail deterministically — never a second workflow. Repeated polling returns the SAME token/result stably; the TAS MUST NOT mint a second token (different `jti`) for a `txn` whose workflow already produced one.
- **Transaction Token** `{#transaction-token}`: typ `mission-txn-token+jwt`. Claims: `iss, iat, exp, jti`; `aud` (singleton = challenge `iss`, never a list); `sub` (effective subject / origin principal, NEVER the Approver); `client_id`; `act` (REQUIRED when `subject_token`/challenge had actor context, else absent; attribution never authority); `txn`; `authorization_details` (exact permitted, ⊆ challenge/subject_token/decision); `parameter_digest` (top-level, recomputed then copied); `mission` (value-equal profiled members); `cnf`. MUST NOT carry `approval`, `single_use`, raw params, roles, or evidence; no refresh/delegation/token-exchange; not acceptable as a general Mission token.
- **Offline Verification** `{#offline-verification}`: RS verifies locally — typ + trusted issuer/sig + aud + iat/exp; `cnf` PoP; equality of `txn`, mission invariants, `authorization_details`, recomputed `parameter_digest` vs a RETAINED pending operation; principal/subject/actor consistency; state via the Status surface within freshness; atomic first use of resource-scoped `txn` (a second distinct token `jti` for an already-consumed `txn` is the SAME replay → refuse, `duplicate_suppressed`). Consumption LINEARIZABLE cross-replica (metering Exact enforcement profile), commit before the irreversible effect, **fail closed** if the store is unavailable.

### Six review findings (Karl, 2026-08-16) — each satisfied by conforming to the spec above; map one commit each
- **P0-1 fresh decision**: run step 7 on approval completion (re-evaluate subject-token, authority, entitlement, policy, params, approval freshness) — not just `gateDerivation()`.
- **P0-2 wire contract**: client auth + `transaction_challenge` + `subject_token`(+type) + PoP; validate `subject_token` aud == challenge `iss`; record authenticated `client_id`. (Not DPoP-in-Authorization + JSON `{challenge}`.)
- **P0-3 conforming token**: `mission-txn-token+jwt`, no `approval`/`single_use`, include `jti`/`sub`/`client_id`/`act`/top-level `parameter_digest`; RS reads NO embedded approval.
- **P1-1 challenge bindings + issuer-scoped keys**: challenge REQUIRES `mission`/`cnf`/`parameter_digest`; TAS resolves challenge-issuer keys per-resource `txn_challenge_jwks_uri` (one resource key MUST NOT claim another's `iss`).
- **P1-2 async lifetime + idempotency**: pending-handle own lifetime; `(issuer, challenge jti, client, cnf)` admission index; stable final poll response; separate challenge/workflow/token expiries.
- **P1-3 exact cross-replica consumption**: replace the in-memory `Set` with a linearizable store keyed by `txn`, fail closed on unavailability; verify token mission/`authorization_details`/`parameter_digest` vs a retained pending operation before consumption.

### Spike to replace (keep only reusable signing / ARAP correlation / transaction engine)
- `src/services/authorization-server/src/adapters/provider.ts` — the `/transaction` handler (`handleTransaction`, `txnTasks`, `TxnHandle`, ~1200-2200): wrong wire contract.
- `src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/txn-challenge.ts` — `issueTxnToken` carries forbidden `single_use:true` + `approval` and wrong typ `txn-token+jwt`.
- `src/services/mcp-payments/src/txn-challenge.ts` — `TxnReplayCache` is an in-memory `Set` (not cross-replica).
- `src/services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts` (~483) — RS extracts the embedded `approval` as authorization input; REMOVE.

### Conformance + gate
- `conformance-manifest.json` has **20 `txn-authorization.*` rows at `todo`** — turn them green. Read `scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` for the match rule (a test's file/name/level/surface must match the row; the row's `text` must appear verbatim in its cited spec anchor — don't edit specs). Add a covering test per row, set `tested`, populate `tests[]`; run `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` until OK.
- From `src/`: OpenFGA reachable (`curl -sk https://localhost:8080/healthz`), `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="$PWD/certs/openfga.crt"`; `pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` clean; `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=… pnpm test` all passing, 0 skipped (baseline 727). Integration tests: valid challenge→approval→fresh-decision→one execution; approval-complete-but-policy-denies; wrong subject_token audience; two tokens different `jti` same `txn` execute at most once; token refused as ordinary Mission token; cross-issuer key confusion refused; repeated poll returns same token; async approval completing after challenge `exp` still issues.

### Standing rules
No edits to `src/PLAN.md`, `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`, README, or any `draft-*.md`. Never merge / push-main / delete-branch. **Never `git add -A`** (a stray `.claude/settings.json` keeps getting swept in — stage explicit paths). Commit + push incrementally; open a **draft** PR (base main) "Mission Transaction Authorization: implementation (#540, PR B)" mapping the change set to the six findings + gate outputs + "Closes #540". After merge, PLAN.md gets a D-entry direct to main.

This issue stays open for PR B.

issues.title: Attenuation/actor-suite: profile Actor Chain Authority Bounds restrictions (no in-Mission basis reset)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Split from #433 per its 2026-08-14 review (P2), which found the proposed restriction incomplete: prohibiting only `reauthorized`/`bounds_events` does not preserve Mission monotonicity, because Actor Chain Authority Bounds also permits a `domain_transition` basis reset, and its audience behavior is not monotonically narrowing by default.

Any family profiling of Authority Bounds MUST prohibit every basis-reset or widening mechanism within one Mission, including `domain_transition`; cross-domain vocabulary translation needs an explicit verified subset/projection rule; and a new authority basis belongs in Expansion, successor creation, or another fresh approval boundary (the family's successor-or-refusal discipline, R19).

Bounds' monotonicity duplicates what the holder-mediated attenuation chain proves structurally, so any profiling belongs only on the issuer-mediated lane. Blocked on a real issuer-mediated consumer; the restriction rules above are the design record until then. Related: #433 (ruling), #538 (wire model).

issues.title: Family: migrate binding Statement tables to the supplied/activation claim format
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Follow-up from the #552 review (finding 3) and the #548 Statement-format upgrade.

#548 retired the `supported`/`conditional`/`not supported` claim states: a Mission Substrate Statement row is now `supplied` in a named scope when stated activation conditions hold, or `not supplied`, and every supplied row states activation conditions, temporal elements (freshness at use, decision/artifact lifetime, post-non-active residual, or express inheritance of the Bounded Reliance floor), and failure behavior.

Eight drafts still publish capability tables in the retired format:

- draft-mcguinness-mission-aauth.md (flagged in the #552 review: its State-Observable row is `conditional` on Mission Management, which publishes no Statement extension of its own)
- draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md
- draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md
- draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md
- draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md
- draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md
- draft-mcguinness-mission-uma.md
- draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md

Per the substrate's migrate-by-touch rule this is one mechanical-plus-audit sweep: each `conditional` row becomes `supplied` with its condition restated as the activation condition, and each supplied row gains (or expressly inherits) temporal and failure elements. The AAuth row already carries most of that content in prose; the audit is confirming per-row semantics, not inventing them. The #552 worked composition currently assumes a deployment-local Statement extension; once this sweep lands, that assumption can point at the bindings' own conforming rows.

Scope note: whether AAuth Mission Management publishes its own Statement extension (as the substrate's extension rule contemplates) or stays an activation condition of the base binding's row is a per-binding decision to make during the sweep.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against `origin/main` at `f1d65c8`: **the underlying drift is real, but I would not execute the proposed eight-document sweep as written. It mixes provider claims with consumer requirements and would reverse the meaning of five tables.**

## 1. Only three listed tables are binding Statements

The `supplied` / `not supplied` vocabulary is normative for a binding's Mission Substrate Statement. Substrate separately requires substrate-neutral profiles to declare capabilities they **consume** (`draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md:786-811`, `:842-916`).

The stale provider Statements that should migrate are:

- AAuth
- Mission Authority Server
- UMA

Harness, Runtime, Orchestration, Metering, and Containment instead publish capability-consumption tables. Those rows describe what the profile requires from a binding or adapter; converting them to `supplied` would incorrectly claim the consumer provides the capability. For example, Runtime conditionally consumes State-Observable—it does not supply a state source.

If the consumer vocabulary needs cleanup, do that separately with values such as `required`, `required when`, and `not consumed`, preserving the provider/consumer distinction.

## 2. All three stale Statements are missing the eighth capability

Substrate requires one row for every capability. AAuth, MAS, and UMA each have seven rows and omit **Authorized Context Correlation** (`aauth.md:799-874`, `authority-server.md:348-419`, `uma.md:895-970`). This is more important than mechanically replacing `conditional`.

Before adding those rows, resolve or explicitly explain the family's apparent semantic inconsistency:

- OAuth says native grant binding supplies Authorized Context Correlation.
- The substrate crosswalk says AAuth's native PS binding supplies it.
- GNAP says its Controller's native binding does **not** supply it because no cross-authority join exists.

Compare the capability definition at `substrate.md:730-745`, the OAuth row at `:1200-1208`, and the GNAP row at `gnap.md:1086-1098`. #554 should not silently make a different choice for every binding.

## 3. The three migrations need semantic audits, not mechanical conversion

Several current claims cannot simply become `supplied`:

- **MAS Monotonic Derivation** includes “PDP action evaluation.” Evaluation is not derivation. Limit the supplied scope to actual no-broader-than derivation points, such as native child creation.
- **UMA State-Observable** is not unconditional across both RPT modes. It is supplied when authenticated introspection, Mission Status, or another current-state surface is active. A self-contained RPT validated only until `exp` is not state observation.
- **AAuth Credential-Bound** applies only in PS-asserted/federated paths carrying and validating `mission_s256`; identity-based and resource-managed paths remain outside it.

Each supplied row needs precise activation, operational scope, temporal behavior, failure behavior, and limitations.

## 4. Keep the AAuth Management activation in the base Statement

The cleanest current shape is `State-Observable: supplied when AAuth Mission Management status is active`. A separate Statement extension in the management draft would add layering churn because that draft currently does not depend on Substrate or the AAuth binding.

The base AAuth draft already cites Management, however, while its `family-manifest.json` entry omits that dependency. Fix that manifest drift in the migration.

## 5. The #552 worked composition only partially collapses

After migration, the AAuth lifecycle claim and Management-conditioned state claim can point directly to the published AAuth Statement. The payment-policy adapter and gateway correlation join remain deployment-local provider claims. The example must not imply every provider claim becomes binding-owned.

## 6. Add a structural tripwire

The current validators allowed three binding Statements to retain retired vocabulary and omit an entire capability. Add validation that every `Mission Substrate Statement`:

- lists exactly the canonical eight capabilities;
- uses only `supplied` or `not supplied`;
- gives every supplied row an activation condition; and
- includes temporal and failure semantics.

## Recommended disposition

Keep #554 open, but rewrite its execution scope:

1. Resolve the Authorized Context Correlation native-binding rule.
2. Migrate only AAuth, MAS, and UMA provider Statements.
3. Add the missing correlation row to all three.
4. Audit each supplied claim semantically.
5. Update the #552 composition pointer and AAuth manifest dependency.
6. Add a Statement validator.
7. Handle the five consumer-table terminology changes separately, preserving consumer semantics.

**Verdict: good catch, but the present scope is not safe to implement mechanically.**

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: Executed as PR #621 under the review's seven-point disposition: the ACC native-binding rule resolved in the substrate definition (GNAP's reading; the OAuth Statement row and crosswalk corrected to match), only the three provider Statements migrated with the semantic audits applied and the eighth row added (MAS supplied, AAuth/UMA not supplied), Management kept as a base-Statement activation condition, the composition note's partial collapse recorded with the aauth→management manifest dep, the structural tripwire added (chained from check-family-manifest; the five consumer tables allowlisted pending #620), and the consumer-vocabulary work split to #620.

issues.title: Impl: wire Mission-Reference propagation through the gateway PEP path
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Follow-up from #283 (its review: "spec-only closure would leave the identified implementer gap present in the reference stack").

Wire the Mission Reference Propagation channel through the reference stack's gateway PEP path: parse the `Mission-Reference` Structured Fields Dictionary (and the MCP `_meta` key `com.karlmcguinness.mission/reference` where the gateway fronts MCP), feed the tuple into the Mission Join as the PEP-supplied reference, enforce the deny-on-conflict rules against any locally recorded binding, refuse governed work with missing/malformed carriage, and emit `mission_reference_conflict` on attribution conflicts. Conformance rows for the channel's refusal semantics ride the #245 suite once the wire behavior exists.

Refs: #283 (spec), #248 (assurance classes consume attachment provenance).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Part 1 merged (PR #635, `48b8b2ce`): both carriages (HTTP `Mission-Reference` Structured Fields Dictionary and MCP `_meta`), strict field-specific parsing, the credential-governs conflict rule with issuer authoritative end-to-end (strict claim parsing, view-issuer comparison, PDP contract), and the refusal contract (`mission_reference_conflict` as a coordinated pre-decision refusal, with the MAS and Runtime Evidence drafts naming the two surfacings). Conformance: `mas.reference.*` rows at their honest levels (conflict-deny tested with both arms; fail-closed-carriage partial; mcp-duplicate-keys recorded as boundary-blocked todo).

**Remaining scope keeping this open**: the MAS Join consumption path — a gateway PEP selecting a Mission for a credential that carries no `mission` claim, feeding the propagated tuple into the Join as rule 1's PEP-supplied reference. No Join substrate exists in src yet; that build is this issue's part 2.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**Session disposition (2026-08-23, architecture-review follow-through; verified against main @ 2d63119a):**

**Analysis**

Part 1 (PR #635) built parsing (`mission-reference.ts`: strict SFD plus MCP `_meta`) and `pep.ts`'s conflict check only for the credential-carries-mission case: `TokenFacts.mission` is a required field, `enforceInner` reads `token.mission.id` unconditionally (397, 417), and the propagated-reference check (428-433) only verifies agreement with the credential's own mission claim. Part 2 is the branch where an ordinary OAuth token carries no `mission` claim at all and the propagated reference is Join rule 1's PEP-supplied reference; nothing in src handles it.

The real blocker sits upstream of the PEP: `MissionView` (`services/pdp/src/policy-view.ts`, 39-67) carries no `subject` and no `client_id`, so Join rules 3 (subject join) and 4 (client join) have nothing to compare the authenticated token against. `loadView(missionId)` also takes no issuer, while reference-verification requires byte-equality on (issuer, id), so a same-id different-issuer collision isn't checked there. `DenialReason` (evaluate.ts, 94-112) has no `mission_mismatch`.

Zero conformance rows are anchored on the baseline join mechanism itself. The `mas.join.*`/`mas.enterprise.*` rows are all todo, but those gate the Join Assertion/Enterprise upgrade, a separate larger surface this issue shouldn't absorb.

**Sketch**

PR A: add `subject: {iss,sub}` and `client_id: string` to `MissionView`. Confirmed `policyViewId` hashes a pinned field subset, not the whole view, so this is safe against existing pinned hashes. Extend `loadView`'s contract to check the expected issuer alongside `mission_id`.

PR B: a baseline join resolver (mission-core or pdp) implementing rules 1, 3, 4, 6, 8: credential-carried reference governs when present, else the propagated tuple; resolve via `loadView`; compare authenticated subject/client_id against `view.subject.sub`/`view.client_id` (or an explicit delegate policy); deny `mission_mismatch` on failure; else the Mission's `authority_set` becomes the decision's authority source. Add `mission_mismatch` to `DenialReason`.

PR C: wire `pep.ts`. Branch at the top of `enforceInner` for a no-claim token: require a propagated reference for governed work or refuse; call PR B's resolver; on success evaluate against the resolved Mission instead of `token.mission`. Add the manifest rows (none exist today) and fixtures: matching subject/client permits under Mission authority; mismatch denies `mission_mismatch`; missing/malformed reference on governed MAS-mode work refuses (reuse the part-1 parser and `mission_reference_conflict`).

**Recommendation**

PR A first (small, unblocks everything, verified non-disruptive), then PR B (independently testable against `MissionView` fixtures), then PR C.

**Tradeoffs**

Branch in `enforceInner` rather than make `TokenFacts.mission` optional: risks the two paths drifting, but a separate joined entry-point would duplicate evidence/telemetry plumbing across 837 lines. Scope to the baseline mapping join only: a MAS-mode PEP without a Join Assertion stays at mapping-table equality, the spec's own accepted baseline risk; don't fold Join Assertion in here. Checking issuer inside `loadView` changes its signature for existing callers; a post-load check per call site is lower-risk but relies on call-site discipline, not an enforced contract.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against `origin/main` at `2d63119a`: the three-stage shape is right—join-capable view, independently tested baseline resolver, then gateway integration—but the sketch omits two load-bearing parts of the baseline join.

First, this cannot be only a branch at the top of `enforceInner`. `TokenFacts.mission` is required, both validators reject an ordinary OAuth token without a Mission claim, and enforcement/refusal evidence dereference `token.mission` outside that proposed branch. Introduce a discriminated ordinary/Mission-bound credential-facts model, or a dedicated MAS-mode entry point that resolves joined facts before entering the shared evaluation/evidence path. The ordinary-token arm must carry authenticated issuer-qualified subject, `client_id`, and its own authority/scope. Accepting a no-claim token must be enabled only for configured MAS-governed paths; the existing Mission-bound path should keep rejecting it.

Second, the resolver must implement all applicable baseline rules. Adding join fields to `MissionView`, keying `loadView` by canonical `(issuer,id)`, and adding `mission_mismatch` are necessary, but insufficient:

- If client matching admits a delegate, rule 5 requires narrowing to entries whose delegation policy authorizes that delegate and enforcing depth.
- Rule 8 requires intersecting the acting credential's authority, Mission authority, and Resource policy. Current `TokenFacts` has no ordinary-token authority, so the proposed resolver cannot enforce that bound.

Do not reuse the existing `mas.join.*` rows: those are Enterprise/Join-Assertion requirements. Add baseline rows for tuple resolution/freshness, subject join, client/delegate join and narrowing, no-fallback mismatch, Mission-authority sourcing, and the three-bound intersection. Land their tests with the resolver and gateway PRs.

Evidence: [current TokenFacts](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/src/services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts#L60-L75), [validator rejection](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/src/services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts#L238-L270), [baseline Join rules](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md#L1200-L1262), and [propagated-reference semantics](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md#L1381-L1415).

Disposition: approve the sequence only after adding the ordinary-token model, full delegate narrowing, three-bound intersection, and baseline-specific rows/tests.

issues.title: Family: thread Containment through harness resume, UMA composition, and Discovery
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-16 fresh architecture review.

Containment's own seams (discharge, expansion, attenuation) are stated on both sides, but three outer-ring documents have not absorbed the ratchet:

1. **Harness resume check.** `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md:578-581` patches the orchestration blind spot ("an unwind decision is not a Mission-state change") but containment has the identical shape: the Mission stays `active` while effective authority narrows. Resume-check sources 1 and 2 (Mission Status, Signals cache; `harness.md:524-527`) report lifecycle state only, so a harness resuming without a fresh runtime PDP decision can act on authority Containment already removed. `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment` is also absent from the harness entry's deps in `family-manifest.json`.

2. **UMA composition.** `draft-mcguinness-mission-uma.md:925-958` states composition consequences for child delegation, offline attenuation, cross-domain projection, and MAS, but never Containment, while declaring "Monotonic Derivation: supported" (`uma.md:912`). AAuth shows the coherent opposite: it declares non-support (`mission-aauth.md:828`), so its omission is stated. UMA's is unstated, and RPT issuance/upgrade is the natural containment-check point.

3. **Discovery cross-reference.** `containment.md:173` and `:478` name Discovery's tainted-session event as a containment trigger; `draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.md` never tells an implementer that its event has this consumer.

All three are one architectural gap: the newest cross-cutting overlay is enforced at the PDP but invisible to the surfaces that cache or poll.

Sketch and tradeoffs follow in a comment.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
## Sketch and tradeoffs

Citations check out against current line numbers: `harness.md:578-581` (the orchestration blind-spot patch), `harness.md:524-527` (resume-check sources 1 and 2), `uma.md:912` and `:925-958`, `mission-aauth.md:828`, and `containment.md:173` / `:478` all match verbatim. One terminology note, not a line correction: `containment.md`'s "tainted-session event of open-world discovery" names no literal event in `discovery.md`. The closest artifact is the routed-to-approval outcome under `{{injection-discovery}}` (`discovery.md:581-587`), carried as `tainted: true` in Discovery Evidence (`{{discovery-evidence}}`). The finding 3 sketch anchors there.

### 1. Harness resume check

`{{resume-checks}}` establishes `active` state only; a contain transition leaves the Mission `active` (`containment.md:458-460`), so it is invisible to that check, exactly the shape the orchestration paragraph already names. `{{cached-access}}` step 3 ("verify the action still passes runtime enforcement when the action is consequential") already closes this for a Runtime-Enforced deployment on consequential actions; nothing states that explicitly for the general resume path, and a Baseline-only deployment has no such backstop at all.

Sketch: add a subsection `## Interaction with Mission Containment {#containment-interaction}` after `{{orchestration-interaction}}`, mirroring its structure, plus one sentence in `{{resume-algorithm}}` beside the existing orchestration sentence. Add `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment` to `family-manifest.json`'s harness entry `deps` (between `child-delegation` and `expansion`, matching alphabetical order; it is already a dep of `mission-runtime.md` and absent from harness).

Normative sentence: "Where a deployment relies on Baseline containment only, a harness establishing state through `{{resume-checks}}` sources 1 or 2 MUST also read `containment_version` (or `authority_changed`) from the same response and MUST treat a value newer than its last-recorded one as narrowing the Mission's effective authority since that response was cached."

Options:
- **Defer to the PDP.** State that Runtime-Enforced deployments already close this through `{{cached-access}}` step 3; add no new harness duty, only the cross-reference. Cheapest, and consistent with keeping runtime enforcement a targeted overlay rather than a per-resource check.
- **Read `containment_version`/`authority_changed` off the existing status/cache response.** Costs nothing on the wire since Visibility already requires the field on both surfaces (`containment.md:653-660`). Closes the Baseline-only residual.
- **Rely on status-projection annotation alone.** Weakest: only helps a harness that materializes and re-reads an authority listing, not one gating purely on active/non-active.

Recommend the first two together, third noted as already-true background, not a sufficient sole fix.

Interaction with #562: the harness fix above keys on `containment_version` and the coarser `authority_changed`. #562 is litigating whether Effective Authority Set gets one defining home and whether discharge gets a counter to match containment's. Prefer `authority_changed` in the harness text since it already covers both containment and discharge per `signals.md:408-419`; revisit the exact field once #562 rules, rather than hardcoding `containment_version` now. Interaction with #287: independent. The harness read is on signals #287 doesn't touch (it only reshapes how discharge is committed, not the containment/discharge signal fields), so this fix does not need to wait.

### 2. UMA composition

`uma.md` declares Monotonic Derivation, Structured Authority, Lifecycle-Gated Authorization, and State-Observable all `supported` (lines 908-914), which is every capability containment's substrate table requires or conditions on (`containment.md:362-373`). UMA is positioned to claim both Baseline and Runtime-Enforced containment properties, more completely than any other binding, yet the composition list is silent. AAuth's silence is coherent (`Monotonic Derivation: not supported`, so it structurally cannot host containment); UMA's is not.

Sketch: add a bullet to the composition-consequences list (`{{mission-substrate}}`, after the FedAuthz bullet, before the Mission Assurance Levels bullet) stating that Containment composes at the token endpoint, anchored at `{{gating}}` and `{{subset}}`. Add one clause to `{{gating}}`'s existing active-check sentence gating a ticket exchange or upgrade against contained capability, and update `{{subset}}`'s "subset of the Mission's Authority Set" to "Effective Authority Set" conditional on Containment adoption. Add `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment` to `family-manifest.json`'s uma entry `deps` (between `attenuation` and `child-delegation`).

Normative sentence: "Where a deployment adopts Mission Containment, the authorization server MUST NOT complete a ticket exchange or upgrade an RPT for a permission that names only contained capability, and denies it `authority_contained` under the containment profile's denial reason."

Options:
- **Full gating clause in `{{gating}}` plus composition bullet.** Matches the "natural containment-check point" the issue names; small, localized edit.
- **Composition bullet only, no wire-level MUST.** Cheaper, but leaves the actual RPT issuance path unconstrained, undermining the claimed Monotonic Derivation support once containment runs.
- **Point to the runtime layer instead.** Argue the PDP already denies contained capability at action time (`{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen}}`), so UMA needs no token-endpoint change. Weaker: UMA's own Reliance Bound item (line 888) already makes the token endpoint a state-gated point in its own right, independent of the PDP; leaving it silent on containment is the same unstated-omission problem, just deferred.

Recommend the first: it is a small, localized addition consistent with the family's habit of gating at the credential-issuing surface, not only the PDP.

Interaction with #562: the `{{subset}}` rewrite from "Authority Set" to "Effective Authority Set" is exactly the term #562 flags as having no single home outside the experimental containment draft. Word the UMA clause as a cross-reference to `containment.md`'s definition rather than restating the computation, matching the disclaimer pattern #562 asks the family to use consistently.

### 3. Discovery cross-reference

`discovery.md` never states that its routed-to-approval-under-taint outcome, or the `tainted` member of Discovery Evidence, feeds Containment's protected-event policy. This is a one-line legibility gap, not a mechanism gap: containment.md already explicitly declines to define an interoperable event format or detection duty for discovery (`containment.md:279-286`), so the fix is attribution only, no new artifact.

Sketch: add a short paragraph after `{{injection-discovery}}`'s taint-gating rules, or beside `{{discovery-evidence}}`'s `tainted` member, naming Containment as a consumer.

Normative sentence: "A Containment deployment (`{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment}}`) MAY treat a routed-to-approval outcome of this section, or a Discovery Evidence record with `tainted` true, as its protected event; this document defines the event and its evidence, not the policy that consumes it."

Options:
- **Informative cross-reference sentence, as above.** Minimal, matches the family's existing one-directional-then-bidirectional pattern elsewhere.
- **Add a `containment`-aware field to Discovery Evidence.** Rejected: duplicates what `tainted` already carries and edges toward the dedicated event type containment.md explicitly defers.
- **Add discovery.md to containment.md's own `deps`, tighten containment's citation to the precise anchors.** Optional, secondary; would replace containment.md's generic document reference with `{{injection-discovery}}`/`{{discovery-evidence}}`, tightening the same seam from the citing side. Not required for this finding, worth a follow-up note.

Recommend the first only for this issue; flag the third as a nice-to-have companion tightening.

### Blast radius

Files touched: `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-uma.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.md`, `family-manifest.json`. No touch to `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`: all three findings are companion-to-companion cross-references and containment's existing informative mentions in core are unrelated to this gap. No core edit is proposed or needed here.

## Open questions

- Does the harness fix wait on #562's ruling for the exact field name (`containment_version` vs `authority_changed`), or land now with `authority_changed` and get revised later.
- Does the UMA `{{subset}}` wording change to "Effective Authority Set" now, ahead of #562's ruling on that term's defining home, or wait so it can cite the eventual home directly.
- Is the UMA token-endpoint gating clause worth adding at experimental maturity, or deferred until UMA leaves sketch status.
- Is the optional third option under finding 3 (tightening containment.md's own citation to precise discovery anchors) worth a companion issue, or folded into this one.
- Should `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment` be added to discovery.md's `deps` even without a normative citation, purely to reflect the informative relationship, or left as-is since discovery's deps track only what it cites.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against `main@883b497`: **the UMA seam is real and High, but I would revise the Harness and Discovery courses before implementation.**

The UMA rule must cover more than “a permission that names only contained capability.” An upgrade can carry forward a permission minted before containment, and UMA makes authenticated per-use introspection its native continued-reliance surface. The normative rule should therefore intersect the **entire resulting RPT**, including retained permissions, with the current Effective Authority Set; omit contained permissions from a mixed result; refuse an empty result with `authority_contained`; and apply the same filtering when introspecting a pre-transition RPT. Otherwise issuance closes while the principal Runtime-Enforced path remains open. Preserve the documented residual for self-contained RPTs with no live state check.

I would not add the proposed general Harness MUST. Containment explicitly defines Baseline as a new-derivation kill whose pre-transition credentials remain usable until their normal bound, while Runtime-Enforced provides the action-time kill. The Harness declares no authority-comparison role, and its consequential cached-access path already requires runtime enforcement. Making a Baseline Harness stop on any narrowing would silently strengthen the Containment property without enough information to know whether the resumed item uses the affected capability.

Add an informative Harness interaction subsection instead:

- Runtime-Enforced deployments close the path at the PDP;
- a Signals consumer that materializes authority follows Signals' existing `authority_changed` rematerialization rule; and
- Baseline retains the documented pre-transition residual.

The proposed carrier sentence also needs correction: `containment_version` can appear on Status and Signals, but `authority_changed` is a Signals event discriminator, not a Status response member. The Harness event cache is currently state-only. A new normative duty would expand the work into `MissionStatusLease`, Signals producer/receiver behavior, Harness code, and tests.

For Discovery, `tainted: true` and `routed_to_approval` should not themselves become protected events. Discovery emits evidence for every adjudication, and routing a tainted encounter to a human is the safety control succeeding. Containment deliberately leaves event-to-policy mapping deployment-defined. Tighten Containment's citation to the Discovery Evidence anchor and optionally add a reciprocal informative pointer saying deployment policy may consume that evidence; do not infer the protected event from either field alone.

Recommended scope: UMA normative gating plus introspection, Harness and Discovery informative composition text, manifest dependency updates, and conformance rows for mixed-result issuance/upgrade and pre-transition RPT introspection. No core edit is needed.

issues.title: Lifecycle: a single defining home for the Effective Authority Set; discharge change-visibility parity
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-16 fresh architecture review.

**1. The Effective Authority Set has no single defining home.** The only Terminology-grade definition lives in the Experimental containment draft (`containment.md:306-312`). `expansion.md:630-637` restates the identical computation inline, with no cross-reference and without the disclaimer pattern the core uses for deliberate restatements (`oauth-mission.md:2378-2381`). The term gates normative behavior in three places: `containment.md:500-540` (derivation gating), `expansion.md:619-622` (`nothing_to_expand`), and `child-delegation.md:1350-1358` (propagation to children). `template.md:627` uses "effective Authority Set" for what may be a third computation (unverified). Any future overlay added to the formula requires synchronized, uncross-referenced edits.

**2. Discharge is a second-class narrowing overlay for consumers.** Containment gets a dedicated `containment_version` plus omit-or-annotate (`containment.md:653-660`). Discharge gets omission only, with no counter (`status.md:1714-1723`). Signals gives both one shared `authority_changed` boolean (`signals.md:410-419`) but keys rematerialization guidance on `containment_version` alone (`signals.md:589-598`). A discharge-only consumer cannot distinguish "narrowed by discharge" from any other metadata-only commit without a fetch. Possibly intentional; no rationale is stated. Adjacent to #287 (state-plumbing simplification).

Sketch and tradeoffs follow in a comment.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
## Sketch and tradeoffs

### Sub-question: template.md:627

template.md:627 (`authorization_details`: "the instance's effective Authority Set") is the Dispatch success response for a Mission instance the same request commits (Dispatch step 7, template.md:475-476). At that instant no containment overlay and no discharge exist yet for the instance, so its effective set collapses to its just-derived approved set: containment.md's formula (approved minus contained minus discharged) and template.md's usage agree, trivially. It is not a third computation. The actual defect is different: template.md never cites the formula or a Terminology entry, so the agreement holds only because no overlay exists yet at instantiation, not because template.md pins it there. A future template.md change (an instance derived through some path that already reflects a parent's containment or discharge, for example) could diverge with nothing to catch it.

### Finding 1: single defining home

Options:

(a) Hoist the Terminology-grade definition into status.md, the lifecycle suite's root (Standards Track, already owns discharge and state version), and have containment/expansion/child-delegation/template cite it. This is a precedented pattern, not a new dependency shape: containment.md's own boilerplate already imports "state version" from status.md the same way (containment.md:292-295). containment.md keeps only its delta, the contained-capability term. expansion.md's inline restatement (630-637) collapses to a cross-reference. child-delegation.md's import sentence (317-319) gains one clause. template.md:627 gains a citation, closing the sub-question's gap.

(b) Keep the definition in containment.md and add the core's disclaimer pattern ("this section instantiates X; the two state the same rules", oauth-mission.md:2378-2381) at each restatement site. No relocation, but it leaves a maturity inversion standing: containment is Experimental while expansion and child-delegation cite the term normatively (both Standards Track), so two Standards Track documents' normative behavior keeps resting on an Experimental Terminology entry, footnoted rather than fixed. It also means four near-duplicate restatements stay in sync by hand instead of one.

(c) Define it in the core (oauth-mission.md). Rejected: core is a published editor's draft (edits need explicit go-ahead, no numbered revision), and the term's content, overlay subtraction, is companion machinery core does not otherwise host. This raises the edit bar for no gain over (a).

Recommend (a): it resolves the maturity inversion (status.md sits at or above every current consumer), reuses an existing import idiom, and does not touch core.

Sample definition sentence (status.md, Terminology):

> Effective Authority Set: the Mission's approved Authority Set as reduced by every narrowing overlay a deployment runs: entries this profile's completion machinery has discharged ({{completion}}), and capability the Mission Containment profile's overlay has contained ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment}}), where deployed. Where no narrowing overlay is deployed, the effective set is the approved set.

Sample cross-reference sentence (containment.md, replacing its own Terminology entry):

> This document uses Effective Authority Set from {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-status}}; this profile's delta is the contained-capability term its overlay contributes to that reduction, gated per {{derivation-gating}}.

### Finding 2: discharge change-visibility parity

Options:

(a) Add a dedicated `discharge_version` counter (status.md member, Signals discriminator and rematerialization guidance mirroring `containment_version`'s). Additive, containment.md untouched. But it makes a third version member alongside state version and `containment_version`, exactly the plumbing growth issue #287 ruled against when it adopted discharge in reduced form (a lifecycle operation, no new subsystem). It also sets a per-overlay-gets-its-own-counter precedent that does not scale: signals.md:417-419 already anticipates a future narrowing overlay.

(b) Generalize `containment_version` into one effective-authority version member that increments on either overlay's narrowing (broaden its definition in containment.md, carry the change through status.md's surfaces and signals.md's discriminator and rematerialization guidance). Nets to one counter instead of two or three, and closes the real gap: a discharge-only consumer gains a comparable value, not just a boolean, so it can skip a refetch when its held value is already current. Cost: this redefines an already-specified wire member's increment trigger. Per issue #535's framing (a wire-visible rename or semantic change is an adoption-time change needing compatibility analysis, not a silent edit), this needs a stated compatibility note for any consumer keying on `containment_version`'s narrower trigger. The bar is lower than #535's own case (containment.md is Experimental, not Standards Track), but not zero.

(c) Document the asymmetry as intentional in status.md, no new member. Cheapest, no wire change. Rejected as the recommendation: it does not restore the capability finding 2 names (compare-without-refetch), and asserting intentionality over a gap the review just surfaced is not the same as showing deployments do not need it.

Recommend (b), on the strength of #287's precedent (discharge adopted lean, no new subsystem) and the reduce-not-multiply direction: one shared counter serves both overlays, and any future one, rather than a growing family of near-identical per-overlay counters.

### Blast radius

Finding 1(a): status.md, containment.md, expansion.md, child-delegation.md, template.md. Core untouched. No wire change (Terminology and cross-reference edits only).

Finding 2(b): containment.md (member definition and Visibility section), status.md (surface requirement, Discharge Visibility), signals.md (discriminator and rematerialization guidance). expansion.md, child-delegation.md, and template.md are untouched; none reference `containment_version` directly. Core untouched. Wire change: yes, an already-specified Experimental member's semantics broaden; flag as adoption-affecting per #535's framing, with a compatibility note for existing `containment_version` consumers.

One citation correction: signals.md:410-419 lands one line into the `authority_changed` member; the member runs signals.md:408-422.

## Open questions

1. Does the hoisted definition go in status.md's existing Terminology section, or a new shared subsection near Discharge Visibility that both discharge and any future overlay cite symmetrically?
2. If (b) broadens `containment_version`, does the family rename it (and if so, to what) or keep the name and only widen its trigger, minimizing the diff at the cost of a name that no longer says what it covers?
3. Should the generalized counter be decided now, or sequenced after #287's still-open ask 1b (error-body convergence), since both touch status.md's surfaces in the same area?

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against `main@883b497`: **I agree with establishing one home for Effective Authority Set, but not with broadening `containment_version`.**

Status can own the term without making the stable document depend on Containment's experimental formula if the definition is abstract:

> **Effective Authority Set:** the approved Authority Set after applying every issuer-held, monotonic narrowing mechanism the deployment runs. This profile contributes discharged entries. Each other narrowing profile defines its own subtraction. No narrowing mechanism adds or restores authority.

Containment should cite that term and define its contained-capability contribution. Expansion should replace its inline duplicate with the shared citation while retaining its restoration consequence. Child Delegation should import the term. Template should say “derived” or “committed Authority Set”: at dispatch the instance was just created, so importing the overlay abstraction explains only a degenerate case.

I do not see a missing wire capability that justifies a shared counter today. `version` orders every lifecycle and metadata commit; `authority_changed` identifies the subset that narrowed effective authority; and Signals already requires rematerialization on that discriminator. Those values distinguish discharge from unrelated metadata changes. A further counter still cannot tell a stale consumer what changed, so it does not eliminate the required fetch.

The immediate gap is implementation of the existing contract. The Signals builder emits `containment_version` but not `authority_changed`; the receiver does not parse or act on either authority-change member; and the discharge/Signals conformance rows remain `todo`. Implement and negatively test that path before adding another wire member.

`containment_version` is also containment-specific implementation state: it snapshots deferred Expansion concurrency and appears throughout Containment Evidence, lifecycle commits, projections, PDP context, and tests. Broadening it would change behavior far beyond Status and Signals. Keeping the name would be misleading; renaming it would be an adoption-visible migration. If experience later establishes a genuine independent generation requirement, add an honestly named `effective_authority_version` rather than silently widening this one.

Recommended course:

- add the cycle-safe definition and citations;
- correct Template terminology;
- retain `version` as total commit order, `authority_changed` as the generic narrowing discriminator, and `containment_version` as containment-specific generation;
- implement/test the already-specified discriminator; and
- add a conformance invariant that every deployed issuer-held narrowing mechanism feeds the single effective-set computation used by every derivation and authority-reporting surface.

Add `family-manifest.json` and `conformance-manifest.json` to the scope. Core remains untouched.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: Follow-up candidates surfaced while implementing the spec PR, outside the ruling's stated blast radius and left untouched: `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md:488` attributes the term to "Mission Containment's Effective Authority Set", and `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md:1418` restates the formula inline attributing solely to Containment, without discharge or a status.md citation. Both now point below the term's new home; worth a small convergence pass if full alignment is wanted.

issues.title: Core/Architecture: reconcile capability vocabularies and pin the lockstep passages
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-16 fresh architecture review. Core is the published editor's draft; any core-touching change lands only as a reviewable PR on explicit go-ahead.

**1. Two capability vocabularies are never reconciled.** Core names three OPTIONAL capabilities: Delegation, Introspection, Cross-Domain (`oauth-mission.md:4085-4106`). The architecture document's Mission Substrate names seven capability claims (`mission-architecture.md:1192-1195`) and maps only three onto the Mission-bound token class (`:1290-1300`). No table anywhere equates the two namings, so the document whose job is the single structural view leaves its central binding with two vocabularies. #554 (Statement-table migration to the supplied/activation claim format) is the natural vehicle.

**2. Deliberate lockstep passages have no drift tripwires.** The self-containment copies are by design (#284 ruling), but nothing pins the pairs:

- Commitment construction: `oauth-mission.md:2326-2399` vs `substrate.md:390-428` (no shared test vectors).
- "Composition and the Effective Ceiling": `oauth-mission.md:4602-4625` vs `mission-architecture.md:834-847`.
- Work-product rule: `oauth-mission.md:4318-4358` vs `mission-architecture.md:826-832`.

**3. Architecture-doc internal nits.** The four-rung ladder appears under two names, with "Protocol core" missing its Baseline Issuance tag (`mission-architecture.md:524-554` vs `:2234-2392`). `:812-819` overstates core as naming three authorization bases when core fully defines only `direct` (`oauth-mission.md:2549-2557`).

Related but not filed here: the core MUST at `oauth-mission.md:2107-2120` whose checkable home is the schema-free Deployment Profile; raised as a question on parked #424 instead.

Sketch and tradeoffs follow in a comment.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
## Sketch and tradeoffs

Citations checked against the current text. All five oauth-mission.md ranges, all seven mission-architecture.md ranges, and the substrate.md range match the content described; no corrections needed.

### Finding 1: reconciling the two capability vocabularies

Core's three OPTIONAL capabilities are optional implementation surfaces (an implementation may or may not offer them). The substrate's eight capability claims are properties a binding supplies, and the OAuth binding supplies five of them unconditionally ("always" in its Mission Substrate Statement table). The two vocabularies answer different questions, so the mapping is uneven by design: an OPTIONAL surface can gate the activation of an otherwise-conditional claim, can exercise a transition point inside a claim that is already unconditionally true, or can fall outside the claim vocabulary entirely.

| Core OPTIONAL capability | Substrate capability claim(s) | Relationship |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Introspection | State-Observable | Core calls Introspection "one state-observable overlay on the lifecycle-gated baseline" (oauth-mission.md:3364). It is one of State-Observable's three named activation surfaces, Status, introspection, or Signals (substrate.md:1194). |
| Delegation | Monotonic Derivation, Credential-Bound | Both claims are supplied always, independent of Delegation. The `act` hop is one of the transition points ("derivation, delegation, and attenuation") Monotonic Derivation already covers (substrate.md:1196), and a delegated token still carries the `mission` claim, Credential-Bound (substrate.md:1197). Declaring Delegation names a channel; it does not gate either claim's truth. |
| Cross-Domain | None of the eight, distinctly | Preserves authority that "only narrows" (Monotonic Derivation), the mission reference and `authority_hash` (Credential-Bound), and gates on active state (Lifecycle-Gated Authorization), all already always-supplied. It is not Portable Evidence: that claim activates only when an Evidence, Mandate, or audit companion is active (substrate.md:1200), and the cross-domain companion is not among them. The vocabulary names no claim for a reference remaining meaningful under a different Controller; that is what Cross-Domain actually adds. |

Options for hosting this table:
