issues.title: Transaction authorization: Carrier Binding Floor and AAuth discharge via R3
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
## Problem

The transaction authorization profile is substrate-neutral on the kernel side and carrier-bound on the wire side. Its Mission Substrate section ({#mission-substrate}) declares kernel and capability consumption under the substrate rule ("defined against the Mission model rather than against OAuth 2.0 mechanics"), but every carrier obligation exists only as the OAuth discharge: `Accept-Txn-Challenge` and `transaction_authorization_required` for the signal, JOSE `typ`s for the artifact classes, `transaction_authorization_endpoint` with RFC 8693 `subject_token` carriage and DPoP/mTLS proof for redemption, `transaction_authorization_id`/`expires_in` and the RFC 8628-shaped poll vocabulary for the workflow, `txn_challenge_jwks_uri` for key discovery, `at+jwt` for the subject-credential class, and Authorization-header presentation for execution.

A binding author targeting AAuth, GNAP, or UMA therefore has to reverse-engineer the invariant list out of OAuth prose. That is exactly how a substrate grows a second canonicalization, a second error vocabulary, or a "single-use" result whose single use is a claim rather than a class property. Meanwhile the AAuth side has independently converged on nearly isomorphic mechanisms: the AAuth-Requirement challenge carrying a signed resource token (resource-authenticated challenge carrier), [draft-hardt-aauth-r3](https://dickhardt.github.io/AAuth/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.html) vocabulary-based authorization definitions (an operation-profile registry in all but name) and its content-addressed per-call proposal model (the parameter-binding half), and per-call auth tokens (the result class). The discharge is cheap now and gets more expensive as both sides drift.

## Recommendation

1. **Add a Carrier Binding Floor to the transaction authorization profile**: the dual of the existing consumption declaration. One section enumerating, carrier-neutrally, what any protocol binding MUST provide to host this profile, with each obligation carrying a one-line cross-reference to the OAuth discharge already specified in this document. No OAuth text moves or duplicates; the floor adds rigor, not length.
2. **The AAuth binding (draft-mcguinness-mission-aauth) gains a Transaction Authorization section** discharging every floor item with AAuth/R3 natives, and declaring the capability fail-closed where a native is missing. Deltas the discharge needs from upstream are filed against AAuth/R3 upstream-first (the established pattern), tracked under #286's composition-seams umbrella.
3. **Manifest**: the reserved `txn-authz.action` capability (declared, currently unused) gates the binding-facing conformance rows, activated when the AAuth discharge lands.
4. **GNAP and UMA discharge are out of scope here**, each getting one informative note: GNAP grant continuation is a native workflow handle (unusually good fit); the UMA binding follows its existing substrate-checklist method when taken up.

## Proposed floor (normative content sketch)

Each item is one obligation plus its OAuth discharge pointer.

- **F1 Challenge carrier.** The binding provides a resource-authenticated challenge artifact derived from the resource's authoritative state, committing to: operation identity, `parameter_digest`, the Mission invariants, and the presenter key. Client-supplied replacements are never accepted. Verifiers resolve a challenge issuer's keys from that issuer's published metadata and nowhere else; one issuer's key never verifies another's challenges. (OAuth discharge: {#resource-challenge}, `txn_challenge_jwks_uri`.)
- **F2 Operation identity.** Operation identity is (resource, versioned operation profile identifier). The profile validates the complete entry and yields a typed operation; human-readable text is never authorization input; a superseded profile version resolves only for workflows pinned to it. (OAuth discharge: RAR entry `type` + the Operation Profile rules of {#resource-challenge}.)
- **F3 One canonicalization.** A binding either adopts the runtime profile's `parameter_digest` into its native parameter commitment or defines a verifiable equivalence to it. It never defines a second digest. (OAuth discharge: {#resource-challenge}, "this document defines no second canonicalization".)
- **F4 Workflow handle and two-phase expiry.** Admission is bounded by challenge expiry only; the pending workflow has its own deployment-declared lifetime under a binding-native handle; repeated initial submission of the same (challenge issuer, challenge identifier, client, presenter key) returns the existing workflow or fails deterministically; at most one authorization result exists per (resource, `txn`), and repeated polls return it stably. (OAuth discharge: {#two-phase-expiry}, `transaction_authorization_id`/`expires_in`.)
- **F5 Approval binding and the fresh decision.** The governed approval is bound to the complete transaction: resource, `txn`, Mission invariants, operation identity and exact authorization details, `parameter_digest`, both identities, authenticated client, presenter key. Approval completion, step-up context, and durable governance grants never issue alone; issuance requires a fresh decision at completion, revalidated immediately before minting. (OAuth discharge: {#challenge-redemption} steps 4-7.)
- **F6 Result class.** The result artifact's class is distinguishable by every verifier from each general credential class of the substrate; single use is semantic to the class, never a member; the artifact is sender-constrained, single-audience, closed-content (no approval object, no evidence, no raw parameters), and never acceptable as a general Mission-bound credential. (OAuth discharge: {#transaction-token}, `mission-txn-token+jwt`.)
- **F7 Offline verification and consumption.** The resource verifies locally against the pending operation it retained, recomputing the digest from live state; consumption of the resource-scoped `txn` is atomic and linearizable across every replica capable of the operation, per the metering Exact enforcement profile; unavailable store fails closed; a second result identifier for a consumed `txn` is the same replay. (OAuth discharge: {#offline-verification}.)
- **F8 Identity projection.** The result's subject is the destination-local subject; the issuer-qualified origin principal travels alongside in the Mission invariants, never in place of it; actor context is attribution, never authority. (OAuth discharge: {#transaction-token}; coordinate with #588, whose correction the floor must state.)
- **F9 Possession.** The challenge commits to a presenter key; possession is proven at redemption and at execution; the execution proof binds to the presented artifact itself, not only to the key. (OAuth discharge: DPoP/mTLS `cnf`, `ath`.)
- **F10 Failure vocabulary.** Pending, denied, expired, and rate states map onto the substrate's native vocabulary; the binding defines no second vocabulary; refusals are typed so a probabilistic caller can re-plan without environment disclosure. (OAuth discharge: {#failure-semantics}.)

## AAuth discharge sketch

| Floor | AAuth native | Delta needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | AAuth-Requirement challenge with signed resource token | Carry Mission invariants + `parameter_digest` + presenter-key commitment in the resource token; per-issuer key resolution via AAuth resource metadata |
| F2 | R3 vocabulary-based authorization definitions (MCP tools, OpenAPI, gRPC, GraphQL) | Version/supersession semantics: superseded definitions resolve for pinned workflows only |
| F3 | R3 content-addressed per-call proposal document | Adopt the runtime `parameter_digest` into the document (preferred) or define verifiable equivalence; upstream conversation |
| F4 | R3 proposal-to-approval flow / grant negotiation handle | Name the workflow handle, its own lifetime, and the admission-idempotency tuple |
| F5 | PS/GS adjudication | State adjudication never issues: the per-call token requires the fresh decision; binding digest carried with the approval |
| F6 | R3 per-call auth token | Pin the class marker and the never-a-general-credential rule; single use semantic to the class |
| F7 | Resource-side enforcement (AAuth resources are first-class enforcers) | Restate retained-pending-operation matching + Exact consumption as binding obligations |
| F8 | AAuth person/agent identity model | Map local subject vs origin principal; attribution rules for the acting agent |
| F9 | AAuth proof-of-possession | Execution proof bound to the presented artifact (`ath` equivalent) |
| F10 | AAuth challenge/pending vocabulary | Mapping table only; no new members |

## Dependencies and coordination

- #286 owns upstream composition seams; the R3 deltas (F2 versioning, F3 digest adoption, F6 class marker) route through it or a sibling filed the same way as the earlier AAuth backlog (upstream-first, most items resolved without local forks).
- #588 must land (or land jointly) so F8 and the token section state the same subject rule.
- The UMA binding's substrate-checklist method is the validation precedent for the discharge section.
- The floor is the carrier-side dual of {#mission-substrate}; the substrate draft's contract is untouched.

## Tradeoffs

**Floor in the profile vs in the substrate draft:** the profile. These obligations are transaction-specific; the substrate stays the kernel contract. Commitment construction lives in the substrate because many documents share it; this floor is shared only by bindings of this one profile.

**Adopt the runtime digest into R3 vs equivalence mapping:** adoption is strongly preferred (one canonicalization family-wide). Equivalence is the fallback only if R3's content addressing is immovable upstream, and it must be verifiable, not attested.

**Activate the manifest capability now vs at discharge:** at discharge. The capability is already declared; gating rows on it before any binding discharges them would manufacture permanently-todo rows.

## Non-goals

- No change to this profile's OAuth carriers or claim sets.
- No second canonicalization, digest, or error vocabulary anywhere.
- No GNAP or UMA discharge in this issue.
- No new substrate kernel capability; {#mission-substrate} is unchanged except a cross-reference to the floor.
- No consolidation of binding documents.

## Deliverables / acceptance criteria

1. Carrier Binding Floor section in the transaction authorization profile: F1-F10, each with its OAuth-discharge cross-reference; no normative OAuth text moved or duplicated.
2. Transaction Authorization section in the AAuth binding discharging every floor item with substrate natives, or declaring the capability unsupported fail-closed.
3. Upstream delta list filed against AAuth/R3, coordinated under #286.
4. Binding-facing conformance rows gated on `txn-authz.action`; both manifest validators pass.
5. F8 and #588 state one subject rule.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against current main and AAuth/R3 -02: **support the factoring goal, but revise this issue before implementation.** The architecture debt is real; the proposed F1-F10 list is not yet a carrier floor, and the AAuth table currently overstates what R3 discharges.

### P1 — Separate transaction semantics, carrier requirements, and binding discharge

The current transaction draft already has the right ownership boundary in its introduction: Runtime owns parameter binding, freshness, the decision, and consumption; this draft is the OAuth wire workflow layered over them ([current text](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9346ed7e1e6e12db16e2c754acec6e1ffee5fc15/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md#L192-L209)). The proposed floor mixes three different things:

1. transaction invariants (complete operation binding, approval as input to a fresh decision, one effect);
2. carrier obligations (challenge, workflow handle, result artifact, presentation proof, native failures); and
3. OAuth-specific discharge (`parameter_digest`, `mission` invariants, `client_id`, singleton JWT `aud`, issuer metadata).

Use three explicit sections:

- **Transaction Authorization Invariants** — carrier-neutral requirements, normatively reusing Runtime rather than copying its rules;
- **Carrier Binding Requirements** — abstract slots a binding must fill: authenticated transaction proposal, stable workflow identity, authorization-result class, execution presentation, and failure mapping; and
- **OAuth Discharge** — cross-references to the existing OAuth sections.

Then put the AAuth/R3 discharge in the AAuth binding. Keep this out of the substrate draft as the issue proposes. This is transaction-profile composition, not another kernel capability.

### P1 — Several proposed “neutral” requirements are still OAuth-specific

- **F1/F3:** require a binding-defined, exact parameter commitment/equality procedure, not a member literally named `parameter_digest`. Likewise require the native Mission Reference and the identity/context needed by the decision, not the OAuth `mission` invariant object. Key trust must come from binding-defined authenticated metadata; “the issuer's published metadata and nowhere else” is an OAuth discharge, not the abstract rule.
- **F2:** `(resource, versioned operation profile identifier)` does not identify an operation. The invariant is `(resource identity, exact operation-semantics identity, operation identifier)`. OAuth can discharge that with versioned RAR `type` plus its action/operation. R3 discharges it with token `aud`, `vocabulary`, the vocabulary-specific operation, and `r3_s256`. Do not require a separate version member: R3 -02 deliberately removed one because the content hash pins the definition ([R3 operation scope](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L130-L134), [revision note](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L780-L788)). Require the pinned definition to remain resolvable for the workflow instead.
- **F5/F8:** name role slots, not “both identities”: effective subject, issuer-qualified origin principal when the binding has one, requesting actor/agent, authenticated presenter, and decision authority. F8's destination-local `sub` plus `mission.subject` rule is the correct **OAuth discharge** and should land with #588, but it is not a universal AAuth shape. AAuth carries the person namespace in `ps`, a directed `sub`, agent identity from the agent/subagent token, and key identity in `agent_jkt`/`cnf`; a binding must not invent a missing origin principal.
- **F6:** the neutral property is one execution domain, not necessarily a JWT “single audience.” Require a distinguishable, narrowly usable result class and a defined extension policy. AAuth auth tokens permit registered additional claims, so literal “closed-content” is not currently native.
- **F10:** a mapping necessarily crosses vocabularies. Require a total, deterministic mapping that preserves terminal/retryable/pending semantics and fails closed on an unmapped value. “No second vocabulary” should mean the binding does not expose a competing wire vocabulary. Remove the “probabilistic caller” rationale; typed retry behavior must not become an environment-disclosure requirement.

### P1 — F3 currently conflates three different commitments

Runtime `parameter_digest` is SHA-256 over the JCS serialization of the Operation Profile's normalized parameter object ([Runtime](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9346ed7e1e6e12db16e2c754acec6e1ffee5fc15/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L1944-L2021)). R3 -02 instead has:

- `r3_s256`, a content address over the exact proposal/document bytes, expressly with **no canonicalization** ([R3](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L464-L470));
- structural JSON equality for inline parameters; and
- per-parameter SHA-256 over exact bytes for a digested value ([per-call enforcement](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L637-L678)).

Those hashes commit different objects and can legitimately coexist. Replace “never defines a second digest” with:

> A binding MUST define one authoritative normalization/equality procedure covering every effect-influencing parameter. A content address over a distinct carrier artifact MAY coexist and MUST be domain-distinguished. If two commitments purport to bind the same semantic parameter set, the binding MUST define a deterministic verification relation and MUST refuse any mismatch.

For AAuth, prefer an explicit equivalence profile with test vectors over forcing the OAuth/JCS field into R3. Add `parameter_digest` upstream only if cross-carrier digest equality is itself an interoperability requirement.

### P1 — The floor omits the point-of-execution authorization gate

F7 mentions pending-operation matching and consumption, but omits the existing OAuth profile's most important non-bypass rule: immediately before execution, the resource checks identity consistency, current Resource policy and entitlement, and the Mission's current effective authority, including containment/discharge, within a declared freshness bound ([steps 4-6](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9346ed7e1e6e12db16e2c754acec6e1ffee5fc15/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md#L578-L624)). The result transports a bounded authorization; it does not freeze current authority.

Add a separate invariant:

> At execution, the resource MUST revalidate the result's resource, transaction, subject/actor/presenter, operation, and parameter bindings and every current lifecycle, authority, entitlement, and Resource-policy gate required by the claimed substrate/profile, within its declared freshness bounds, before atomically consuming the transaction.

This matters to AAuth: the current Mission AAuth binding declares State-Observable only conditionally and Structured Authority unsupported at baseline ([capability table](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9346ed7e1e6e12db16e2c754acec6e1ffee5fc15/draft-mcguinness-mission-aauth.md#L821-L832)). An AAuth/R3 transaction claim must identify exactly which native source supplies those execution-time gates; short token lifetime alone is not current-state observation.

### P1 — R3 -02 is a partial discharge, not a complete one

R3 has advanced beyond the issue's snapshot. It now natively provides resource-signed resource tokens, content-addressed per-call proposals, `401` retry and `202` held-invocation delivery, exact retry comparison, single-use language, and retained-result replay ([R3 flow](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L637-L678)). AAuth's required HTTP signature covers `signature-key`, so execution proof is already bound to the exact presented auth token, not just to a public key ([token use and verification](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol.md#L1973-L2031), [covered components](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol.md#L2667-L2705)). Mark those as native, not future deltas.

The remaining gaps are substantive:

1. **Transaction-instance binding.** `r3_s256` is a content hash, so two intentionally identical calls can share it. It is not a nonce or consumption identity. The resource-token `jti` identifies one challenge, but the resulting auth token does not bind that `jti`, and R3 does not prohibit a second per-call token for the same admitted transaction. Define one transaction instance identifier, echo it into the result, make issuance idempotent on it, and consume that identifier—not the proposal hash and not merely token `jti`.
2. **Fresh post-approval decision.** R3 currently says the AS evaluates the proposal and, “on approval,” issues the token ([flow step 2](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L673-L678)). It does not yet require approval to be only an input followed by immediate revalidation of Mission state, credential, identity/key binding, entitlement, and current Resource/AS policy.
3. **Distinct result class.** The per-call result is still ordinary `typ: aa-auth+jwt` with the approved operation moved into `r3_granted` ([token shape](https://github.com/dickhardt/AAuth/blob/932bc6cead9fca13fa60b085339038a548425d88/draft-hardt-aauth-r3.md#L553-L623)). A verifier cannot identify “single-use per-call result” from token class alone. Add a native class marker or a cryptographically bound transaction-purpose member and a rule forbidding general credential use.
4. **Concurrency and failure closure.** R3 says to mark the proposal consumed, but does not require a linearizable cross-replica transition, durable tombstone/idempotency horizon, or fail-closed behavior when the consumption store is unavailable.
5. **Stable workflow/result uniqueness.** AAuth supplies `Location` and pending lifetime, and -02 supplies retained results, but neither currently defines the complete admission-idempotency key nor “at most one authorization result per admitted transaction.”
6. **Complete approval and execution binding.** Specify how the approval and result bind the Mission Reference namespace, resource-token `jti`, person principal, agent identity, presenter key, exact R3 operation/proposal, and execution resource. Do not infer the agent identity where AAuth says it is unavailable.

Until all mandatory gaps have native or profiled rules, the AAuth binding MUST NOT claim `txn-authz.action`. “Unsupported fail-closed” is not a discharge: absence means the capability is unclaimed; fail-closed behavior applies after a deployment claims and invokes it.

### P2 — Keep conformance ownership compositional

`txn-authz.action` is reserved but unused ([manifest](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9346ed7e1e6e12db16e2c754acec6e1ffee5fc15/conformance-manifest.json#L106-L115)). Runtime already gates parameter, single-use, concurrency, and idempotency requirements on `runtime.transaction-assurance-tier`; do not duplicate those rows under a second capability. Define `txn-authz.action` as the portable carrier/workflow capability, state that claiming it depends on the Runtime transaction-assurance requirements (plus the binding's declared state/authority capabilities), and add only carrier/discharge rows under the new capability.

“Offline” should mean no request-path call to the authorization-result issuer. It must not prohibit authenticated, prefetched/cached current-state inputs the execution gate requires. Likewise, reuse the metering Exact transition semantics without making every transaction implementation claim the entire optional metering companion.

### Recommended issue decomposition and acceptance criteria

1. **This issue / floor:** add the two-layer invariant + carrier-requirement structure and the OAuth discharge cross-references; resolve the OAuth identity wording with #588. Do not duplicate Runtime's normative algorithms.
2. **AAuth/R3 discharge issue:** pin R3 -02, publish a MUST-by-MUST native/partial/missing matrix, file the six remaining upstream deltas under #286, and add the AAuth binding section only once every MUST is discharged. An informative gap matrix is fine before then; a capability claim is not.
3. **Manifest issue:** activate `txn-authz.action` only after the contract exists, reuse existing Runtime rows, add binding-specific positive/negative vectors, and encode/document the capability dependency.

Acceptance should include two identical-parameter calls remaining distinct, duplicate issuance for one admitted call being impossible, two replicas racing one result with exactly one execution, final policy/Mission state changing after approval but before minting/execution, wrong subject/agent/presenter/resource rejection, and proof over the exact result artifact. With those changes, the carrier-floor approach is the right architecture and AAuth/R3 remains the right first non-OAuth validation binding.

issues.title: impl: PDP evaluate() has two fail-open gaps (entry.type uninspected; freshness skipped when absent)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Found during #594 Wave 2 slice A (PDP refusal-test backlog), recorded in manifest notes but not fixed there since both are implementation hardening, not test work.

1. **`evaluateInner`'s entry match never inspects `entry.type`.** The authority-entry match (step 5) relies on the type being closed to one literal end-to-end at the AS admission layer. If that closure ever broke upstream (a new entry type admitted, a deserialization change), the PDP itself would not catch an unknown type: it would match on the remaining fields and potentially authorize under an entry whose semantics it does not understand. The runtime draft's unknown-authorization-details-type refusal expects the decision path to refuse what it does not recognize. Fix direction: assert the literal in evaluate() and deny (out_of_authority or the draft-specified classification) on any other value, fail-closed by construction.

2. **The freshness check is skipped entirely when `context.freshness` is absent.** A PEP that omits the freshness member gets zero staleness enforcement even for a high-consequence action: stale-state denial only triggers when the PEP volunteers the input. That inverts the fail-closed posture of runtime's compromise-resistant active-freshness condition (the PDP-side arm; the AS-side arm is a separate role). Fix direction: for actions whose class requires freshness, absence of the member is itself a denial (or the draft-specified refusal), not a bypass.

Both gaps have refusal-class ledger rows currently todo that would flip to tested once the code paths exist: runtime.decision-inputs.unknown-authorization-details-type-refusal and the PDP arm adjacent to runtime.compromise-resistant.active-freshness-condition. Acceptance: the two behaviors above implemented in services/pdp/src/evaluate.ts, unconditional stub-FGA tests, the corresponding manifest rows flipped honestly.

issues.title: impl: PEP fail-open gaps: list_invoices unbound material read; unrecognized decision-context members silently ignored
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Found during #594 Wave 2 slice B (PEP/RS refusal backlog, PR #609), recorded as manifest notes but not fixed there. Sibling of #608 (the PDP pair).

1. **`list_invoices` without `vendor_id` returns every invoice across every vendor, unbound.** A material read served with no binding to the Mission's authority scope, violating the runtime draft's read-binding floor (`runtime.read-binding.must-require-binding-for-material-reads` and `.floor-and-no-misclassification` are the todo ledger rows). Fix direction: require a binding parameter for material reads (or bind the result set to the Mission's authority entries) in `pep.ts`'s `TOOL_ACTIONS`, with a refusal test for the unbound form.

2. **`pep.ts` reads specific named `decision.context` members and silently ignores anything else.** The runtime draft's rule is the opposite polarity: an unrecognized condition on a permit makes the permit unusable (fail closed), never ignorable (`runtime.decision.conditions-and-obligations-enforceable` is the todo row). Fix direction: enumerate the recognized condition keys, treat any unrecognized member on a permit as a denial, and test with a synthetic unknown condition.

Acceptance: both behaviors implemented with unconditional tests, and the corresponding ledger rows flipped honestly.

issues.title: Family: consumer capability-table vocabulary (required / required when / not consumed)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Follow-up from the #554 review (item 1/7): Harness, Runtime, Orchestration, Metering, and Containment publish capability-CONSUMPTION tables that still use the retired provider vocabulary (`supported`/`conditional`/`not supported`). Converting them to `supplied` in the #554 sweep would have reversed their meaning (a consumer requiring State-Observable does not supply a state source), so they were excluded there.

Scope: migrate the five consumer tables to consumer vocabulary that preserves the provider/consumer distinction, per the review's suggestion: `required`, `required when <condition>`, `not consumed` (and `produced` where a profile genuinely produces, as the transaction-authorization consumption declaration already does). Keep each row's condition, scope, and limitation content; this is terminology plus audit, not re-derivation.

Files (current retired-vocabulary rows flagged by `scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs`): draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md, draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md, draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md, draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md, draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md.

Tripwire coupling: the validator added by #554's PR carries a temporary allowlist for exactly these five tables, annotated with this issue; landing this issue removes the allowlist, after which retired vocabulary anywhere fails CI.

Refs #554.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**Session disposition (2026-08-23, architecture-review follow-through; verified against main @ 2d63119a):**

**Analysis**

The five named tables (`Capability | Consumption | Scope of consumption`) hold 35 rows, 7 each; the checker's `CONSUMER_TABLE_ALLOWLIST_620` exempts exactly these. Auditing by the table's header rather than the retired-word regex (the checker's own method) turns up two more consumer tables neither named nor allowlisted: `draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.md` and the cited exemplar itself, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md`. Both avoid `supported/conditional/not supported` so never tripped the tripwire, but both use a bare `consumed` value absent from the issue's four-value target (`required` / `required when <condition>` / `not consumed` / `produced`). `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence.md`, an eighth consumer table, is already fully compliant, no edit needed.

Substrate's Composition-by-Capability section (the rule the exemplar cites) only obligates declaration; unlike Statements' `supplied`/`not supplied` (lines 943-945), it defines no consumer-claim vocabulary. The four-value target is the issue's own proposal, not yet normative anywhere; note this, don't block on it.

**Sketch (row inventory)**

| File | Rows | Needs conversion |
|---|---|---|
| harness | 7 | 2 `conditional`→required-when (Credential-Bound, Structured Authority); 1 produce-candidate (Portable Evidence) |
| runtime | 7 | 3 `conditional`→required-when (State-Observable, Monotonic Derivation, Credential-Bound) |
| orchestration | 7 | 1 `conditional`→required-when (Structured Authority); 1 produce-candidate (Portable Evidence) |
| metering | 7 | 1 `conditional`→required-when (Structured Authority, two-consumer text) |
| containment | 7 | 2 `conditional`→required-when (State-Observable, Credential-Bound); 1 produce-candidate (Portable Evidence) |
| mandate (not named) | 8 | 1 `consumed`→required-when (State-Observable) |
| transaction-authorization (exemplar) | 8 | 2 `consumed`→required (Structured Authority, State-Observable) |

Checker change: drop the allowlist; detect tables by the existing 3-column header, not filename, so future tables self-register; validate Consumption against `/^(required( and produced)?|required when .+|not consumed|produced)$/`; require non-empty Scope; check Capability names against the canonical eight without requiring completeness or order (unlike Statements, these tables legitimately omit untouched capabilities).

**Recommendation**

Write the generalized checker first and run it as the audit tool, not last: it enumerates every illegal cell (9 `conditional` plus 3 `consumed`) instead of only the ones assumed going in. One PR, widened to seven files: fold mandate.md and the exemplar's 3 cells in alongside the five named, since header-based detection makes them fail together; landing the checker without them just relocates the drift the allowlist currently hides.

**Tradeoffs**

Mechanical (9 rows): `conditional`→`required when <condition>`, condition drawn from existing Scope prose. Two are compound (harness and metering Structured Authority, multi-clause/two-consumer text) and need a distilled single condition, a judgment call, not extraction. Semantic (3 rows): harness/orchestration/containment Portable Evidence read `not consumed` but their Scope text says the profile produces its own evidence artifact; reclassifying to `produced` changes a claim, not a label, and the regex accepts either value, so it's human-verified only. The `consumed` cells split further: mandate's is conditional, the exemplar's two read unconditional; no single find-replace covers both.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against `origin/main` at `2d63119a`: widening to seven drafts and detecting consumer tables by their three-column header are correct. Two inventory corrections are needed.

First, there are 12 existing vocabulary cells to migrate, not nine: nine `conditional` cells across the five allowlisted drafts, plus `consumed` once in Mandate and twice in Transaction Authorization. Header discovery is exactly what exposes the latter three.

Second, do not reclassify the three `Portable Evidence` rows to bare `produced`. The substrate capability means evidence transferable across a stated administrative boundary and verifiable there, with canonicalization, integrity, ordering, retention, and disclosure properties. Producing an evidence-shaped object does not itself produce that capability:

- Harness Evidence becomes portable only when composed with registration and audit/signing-key machinery.
- Orchestration's evidence envelope is normally optional and has no registered media type.
- Containment defines canonical bytes and types but delegates cross-boundary registration to audit/transparency composition.

Keep those cells `not consumed` and retain output explanations in Scope. If Statements are intended to declare outputs as well as consumption, define that as a separate axis and support a conditional form such as “not consumed; produced when Audit is active.” Preserve `required and produced` for Transaction Authorization's Credential-Bound row because it consumes and mints the actual capability.

Evidence: [current checker allowlist](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs#L122-L149), [Mandate table](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.md#L279-L288), [Transaction Authorization table](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md#L926-L935), and [Portable Evidence definition](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md#L828-L847).

Disposition: generalized checker, seven drafts, and 12 mechanical conversions; reject the three semantic `produced` conversions absent a separate output-axis ruling.

issues.title: Core: controls taxonomy — three species in one bucket (acr, max_derivations, agent_deployment)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the validated tri-doc review (Aug 2026), P1 finding 2, the parts that are design decisions rather than corrections. `controls` currently mixes three species: an approval-ceremony authentication requirement (`acr`), an issuer-side minting ceiling (`max_derivations`), and an actor-instance/attestation binding (`agent_deployment`); metering adds consumption controls through the same seam.

Options the review puts on the table, each a ruling:
1. **`acr`**: prefer standard OAuth/OIDC `acr_values`/`max_age` (RFC 9470 composes them into authorization requests) for direct approval authentication, reserving `controls.acr` for the committed-in-intent form or retiring it. Family precedent favors typical OAuth patterns; the committed-vs-per-request semantic difference is the decision.
2. **`max_derivations`**: state explicitly that it is a *requested* ceiling with the effective ceiling min(request, issuer policy) — needs an implementation-behavior check before the sentence lands.
3. **`agent_deployment`**: relocate to the client-instance/attestation profile, leaving a pointer.
4. Optionally name the species in {{mission-intent}} so future controls declare which they are.

The correction half of the finding already landed (R3 rewrite; the closed-top-level rationale naming both extension seams) in the tri-doc review PR. Refs: reviewer analysis in the session record; PR for the correction half.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**2026-08-24 architecture-shape review, P1 finding 5 (scope extension proposed):** the review lands on this issue's three species and extends the ownership table to the whole Intent object:

| Concern | Proposed owner |
|---|---|
| Goal, purpose, success criteria, requested task expiry | Mission Intent |
| Requested resource and concrete authority | OAuth resource, scope, RAR |
| Approval strength and recency | RFC 9470 acr_values/max_age or AS policy |
| Derivation quota | AS policy or a Mission issuance-policy profile |
| Agent deployment binding | attestation/agent-deployment profile |
| Provenance/admission artifacts | submission evidence sibling |

Plus two renames: Intent's prose constraints -> task_bounds (or instructions) so it cannot be confused with enforced RAR constraints; and retire the controls extension bucket from core entirely (profiles add explicit parameters only with an interoperable producer and enforcer), which is a stronger form of this issue's option 4.

One pushback to weigh when ruling: Intent's resources member is the PROPOSAL side of the proposal-vs-grant separation (inert, pre-derivation), not a duplicate of the OAuth resource request; if it moves out, the Approver's rendered disclosure loses its requested-resources source. The rename fix (make its proposal-ness explicit) may serve better than relocation for that one member. Rule together with #706 (error/step-up reuse) so acr lands on RFC 9470 once.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against current `main` and the rest of the family: **revise, then accept the stronger “retire the bucket” direction.** The diagnosis is right, but the current options still move names before settling request/result ownership.

## P1 findings

1. **`acr_values` / `max_age` are not a drop-in replacement for `controls.acr`.** RFC 9470 uses those parameters after a protected resource challenges for the authentication event associated with the access token. Core's requirement is authentication of the **Approver**, who may be different from the token's Subject ([core explicitly permits that split](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L1987-L2003)). For the direct OAuth approval flow, standard `acr_values` and `max_age` are the right request carriage only if the profile states that they apply to the principal acting as Approver in that authorization interaction. The AS's risk-based approval floor remains authoritative and conjunctive; it is not client-controlled.

   Record the **achieved** approval context (`acr`, `amr`, `auth_time`) on the approval event / Consent Evidence, not as requested Intent. Also remove or tightly qualify core's permission to put approval `acr` / `auth_time` on a derived access token: [that text currently repurposes RFC 9068 claims](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2892-L2899), and is misleading when `approver != subject`. A JWT access-token authentication-context claim must keep its standard meaning; approval provenance belongs in the record/evidence surface.

2. **`max_derivations` currently has no effective-policy model.** The draft says the deployment sizes the cap from renewal cadence ([lines 915-931](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L915-L931)), but the implementation copies the client's value verbatim into the record, with omission meaning unbounded ([direct creation](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/kernel.ts#L300-L311), [child creation](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/child-delegation.ts#L492-L499)). There is no `min(request, issuer_policy)` clamp.

   More importantly, this is **not a swarm fan-out or concurrency limit**. It counts initial exchange, refresh, token exchange, and cross-domain grant issuance ([the normative counter definition](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L3281-L3301)); it does not count distinct instances and can be exhausted by one instance refreshing. Remove the architecture's fan-out claim. Model an AS-established effective issuance limit as record/operational policy. If a client is allowed to request a smaller ceiling, a dedicated issuance-policy profile should define both `requested_derivation_limit` and the immutable effective record value, approval rendering, omission semantics, and audit recomputation. A true instance/concurrency quota, if wanted, belongs to the instance/deployment profile and needs a distinct counter.

3. **Relocating `agent_deployment` requires preserving two different objects.** The approved class/version pin is committed approval context; an instance assertion or attestation is evidence that the current presenter belongs to that class. Moving both into “attestation” would lose the approved constraint, while leaving the pin in a generic Intent bucket leaves verification and identifier semantics deployment-defined ([current definition](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L933-L951)). A dedicated Agent Deployment Binding profile should own:

   - its PAR request member or typed submission-evidence input;
   - resolution to an AS-approved deployment identifier;
   - an immutable Mission-record extension and approval rendering;
   - the assertion/attestation format and presenter binding checked at every issuance; and
   - failure behavior when the profile is requested but the client cannot prove the binding.

   Core should point to that profile, not define a string whose identity, proof, and change semantics are all local policy.

4. **Retiring `controls` is a family migration, not a core-only edit.** Metering defines five runtime-enforced members through this exact seam; approval, expansion, child delegation, UMA, GNAP, MAS, security-model, architecture, shaping, examples, conformance rows, and code all refer to it. Do one coordinated breaking revision. Do not leave a deprecated open bag or silently dual-read aliases, because `intent_hash` makes differently shaped objects different commitments.

## P2 correction to the proposed ownership table

`intent.resources` is not presently inert proposal prose. Core requires every derived entry's resource to be one of those values ([lines 1384-1387](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L1384-L1387)). RFC 8707 `resource` selects the protected resource / token audience; RAR proposes concrete authorization; the Intent member also serves as a template-mode derivation ceiling and approval context. Either:

- keep it, preferably renamed `target_resources`, and state that it is a client-requested Intent ceiling rather than RFC 8707 carriage; or
- remove it only after defining one standard-parameter source of truth, coherence across multiple token audiences, template-mode lookup, approval rendering, and what commitment covers the values.

The proposed `constraints` -> `task_bounds` rename is good. Those strings are expressly non-machine-readable ([lines 850-856](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L850-L856)); the new name avoids collision with enforced RAR constraints.

## Recommended ruling / solution shape

Replace the bucket with an ownership table that, for every datum, fixes **producer, requested vs effective status, commitment, enforcer, and wire owner**:

| Datum | Owner and shape |
|---|---|
| Goal, task bounds, success criteria, requested task expiry, target-resource ceiling | Mission Intent |
| Concrete authority | `authorization_details`; `scope` / RFC 8707 `resource` where applicable |
| Direct-approval authentication request | `acr_values` / `max_age` in the OAuth request; AS policy floor remains authoritative |
| Achieved approval authentication | approval event / Consent Evidence, for the Approver |
| Effective issuance limit | AS policy, optionally a dedicated issuance-policy profile with requested/effective values |
| Approved deployment pin + instance proof | Agent Deployment Binding profile |
| Consumption bounds | Metering profile-owned explicit object/member plus its runtime enforcer |
| Provenance/admission artifacts | typed submission-evidence sibling |

Acceptance criteria should include: no generic `controls` extension seam; one explicit home for every old member; requested/effective derivation-limit tests (including omission, policy clamp, child/template/expansion, idempotent replay); removal of the false fan-out claim; approver-vs-subject authentication tests; profile dispatch and fail-closed behavior for deployment binding; regenerated hashes/vectors; and a full family/reference-implementation/conformance-manifest sweep.

**Tradeoff:** this is a larger breaking edit than merely naming three species, but it yields a composable profile boundary and prevents future parameters from collecting in a semantically unreviewable bag. Because these are Internet-Drafts and the object is already closed and hashed, this is the right point to make that break once.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**Session disposition on the review (2026-08-24): all findings adopted; the amended ruling below supersedes both the original options and the prior ownership-table comment.**

1. **Approver authentication, not token authentication.** acr_values/max_age become the request carriage for the direct flow ONLY with stated Approver semantics (core permits approver != subject); the AS's risk-based approval floor stays authoritative and conjunctive. Achieved context (acr, amr, auth_time) is recorded on the approval event / Consent Evidence, never as requested Intent. Core's permission to carry approval acr/auth_time on derived access tokens is removed or tightly qualified: RFC 9068 claims keep their standard token-authentication meaning; approval provenance lives in the record/evidence surface.

2. **max_derivations gets an effective-policy model, and the fan-out claim dies.** Verified state adopted: the implementation copies the client value verbatim with omission meaning unbounded and no min(request, issuer_policy) clamp; and the counter measures issuance events (initial, refresh, exchange, cross-domain), not instances: one instance refreshing can exhaust it. Ruling: remove the architecture's fan-out characterization; model an AS-established effective issuance limit as record/operational policy; if clients may request a smaller ceiling, a dedicated issuance-policy profile defines requested_derivation_limit vs the immutable effective value, rendering, omission semantics, and audit recomputation. A true instance/concurrency quota, if ever wanted, is a distinct counter in the instance/deployment profile.

3. **agent_deployment splits into two preserved objects** under a dedicated Agent Deployment Binding profile: the approved class/version pin (committed approval context, immutable record extension, approval rendering) and the instance assertion/attestation (presenter evidence checked at every issuance), plus the request member, resolution to an AS-approved identifier, and fail-closed behavior when requested but unprovable. Core points to the profile.

4. **Retirement of controls is one coordinated family migration**: metering's five members, approval/expansion/child/UMA/GNAP/MAS/security-model/architecture/shaping, examples, conformance rows, and code move in one breaking revision. No deprecated bag, no dual-read aliases: intent_hash makes differently shaped objects different commitments, so the break happens exactly once.

5. **P2 correction accepted**: intent.resources is a live derivation ceiling (every derived entry's resource must come from it), not inert proposal prose as the earlier comment suggested. Adopt the lighter path: keep it, renamed target_resources, stated as a client-requested Intent ceiling and template-mode lookup source, explicitly not RFC 8707 carriage. constraints -> task_bounds stands.

The review's producer / requested-vs-effective / commitment / enforcer / wire-owner table is the ruling's normative deliverable, and its acceptance criteria are adopted verbatim (including regenerated hashes/vectors and the family/implementation/manifest sweep).

Retiered decide -> coordinated: this executes as one cut, together with #706 (shared Approver-semantics interlock on RFC 9470 parameters). Awaiting go-ahead.

issues.title: Family: staged Mission Resource Access Profile split (plan of record)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the validated tri-doc review (Aug 2026), the downgraded-but-valid strategic finding: the OAuth binding couples the Mission governance kernel to one ambitious cross-resource authority profile — Mission Issuer conformance mandates `mission_resource_access`, its URI-prefix algebra, action families, delegation members, and the Common Constraints. RFC 9396 expressly permits a type to define its own members (no violation), and the review's measured blast radius (the type appears in ~20 of 41 drafts and ~77 TypeScript files; Common Constraints in ~11 drafts) makes this a staged plan, not an edit.

**Plan of record if executed** (the #207/#220 pattern):
1. **Mission OAuth Core**: approval, record, lifecycle, RAR carriage, type-owned narrowing, token binding.
2. **Mission Resource Access Profile**: `mission_resource_access`, Common Constraints, the generic subset algebra.

Rules when executed: relocation-only, MUST-inventory 1:1, discovery surfaces byte-identical where unaffected — and coordinate with #207 (the Mission Model split), whose Stage 1 relocation map already assigns the abstract Authority Set + subset + Common Constraints to the Model; executing #207 first may make this split its natural by-product rather than a separate operation.

**Triggers**: a WG adoption conversation raising the coupling; an adopter wanting Mission governance with a different (or no) generic authority type beyond what the MAS-first ramp and #220's RAR-free tier already answer; or #207 executing. Until then, deferred: today's single-type baseline is the interoperable floor.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**2026-08-24 architecture-shape review, P0 finding 1 (elevation proposed):** the review independently reaches this issue's conclusion and argues it now gates the core standardization proposal. Verified claim: the core defines mission_resource_access, generic resource matching, an action namespace with wildcard families, generic constraints, delegation policy, subset/intersection algebra, and a Common Constraints registry: a cross-resource authorization language carried by RAR, while RFC 9396 explicitly leaves authorization-detail semantics and comparison to the individual type. The architecture's "no new authority format" non-goal is therefore no longer true as stated.

Its recommendation matches this issue's plan of record: split mission_resource_access + Common Constraints + the subset algebra into the RAR profile; core keeps type-agnostic commitment of supported authorization_details types, the approved-set commitment, and derivation gating. Two additions from the review worth folding into the plan: (1) each RAR type must own its subset/enforcement semantics, which makes #645's per-type transformation capability map (narrow/delegate/project) a co-requisite rather than a nice-to-have, since delegation and expansion need to know a type's narrowing relation; (2) the architecture non-goal paragraph needs rewording in the same cut, or the family keeps making a claim the core contradicts.

Proposed retier: roadmap -> execute after the bundle-composition ruling (#704), since "what standardizes first" decides whether this split is a prerequisite or a fast-follow. Tradeoff stands as this issue recorded: the core stops being one self-contained document but stops claiming universal semantics for actions like invoices.read.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**Plan-of-record update (2026-08-24, owner-directed elevation): roadmap -> now.**

The first recorded trigger has fired: the 2026-08-24 shape review raised the coupling as its P0 finding, and #704's amended ruling names this split as the sequencing branch for the initial WG package (core + RAR profile presented separately, or lead monolithic and disclose). The owner has directed elevation.

**The recorded two-document plan stands unchanged**, including its execution rules: relocation-only, MUST-inventory 1:1, discovery surfaces byte-identical where unaffected.

**Corequisites added since the plan was recorded:**
- #645 becomes load-bearing, not optional: once core commits supported types generically, delegation, expansion, and containment need each type's narrowing relation declared somewhere machine-readable; the per-type transformation capability map (narrow / delegate / project) is that contract. Execute together or the split strands the subset consumers.
- Architecture non-goal reword rides the same cut: the "no new authority format" claim becomes true again the moment the profile ships, and the sentence should say the profile exists.
- #698 interlock: the lossless-or-omit scope-projection rule is per-type; core states the type-agnostic rule, the new profile carries mission_resource_access's concrete projection semantics.
- Reference-tier ripple: the subset/intersection algebra is normatively load-bearing for child-delegation, attenuation, expansion, and containment, which today receive it via core; post-split they cite the profile. Manifest typed edges, conformance rows quoting the type's text (re-anchored into the profile with a new source.specs entry), and the family wiring for a 42nd document all move in the same wave.

**One open sequencing sub-decision** (from the plan's own #207 coordination note): execute this standalone now, or run #207 Stage 1 first and take this as its by-product. The trigger that fired is the WG-conversation one, which argues standalone-now with the relocation kept compatible with #207's Stage 1 map (do not block the WG timeline on the larger Model split). Flagging rather than assuming; the execution PR will follow whichever the owner states.

Next step on go-ahead: the split lands as one reviewed PR wave (core is issue-first; this issue is that record), before the initial WG package is assembled per #704.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: **Sequencing resolved (2026-08-24, owner, via the #704 ruling):** standalone-now. The split executes before the initial WG package is assembled and does not wait for #207 Stage 1; the relocation stays compatible with #207's Stage 1 map. Ready for the execution PR wave on go-ahead.

issues.title: Signals: durable per-consumer delivery and outbox dispatcher (event-plane durability past the lifecycle hook)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the #640 review (round 5, findings 1–3, the event-plane half). The kernel's lifecycle_outbox now guarantees durable, replayable LOCAL finalization: persisted immutable commit payloads (stable event_id reused as the SET jti, original committed_at), drained at-least-once to the lifecycle hook, with startup drain. What it deliberately does NOT provide, and currently claims not to provide:

- **Per-consumer delivery durability**: the Signals emitter schedules async signing/delivery, returns immediately, and swallows failures — a crash after the hook but before SET signing/delivery loses the event past the hook boundary. The fix is per-consumer delivery jobs or persisted signed SETs, acknowledged only when delivery reaches the Signals profile's defined durable boundary (byte-identical redelivery, same jti).
- **Autonomous dispatch**: drains run at startup and on redemption/recovery polls; there is no recurring dispatcher. A worker plus claiming/lease semantics is required if more than one AS process can drain a shared database (out of scope for the D27 :memory: baseline, required for the file-backed escape hatch).
- **Cascade-under-replay fixture**: a child-bearing predecessor exercised through the crash-window replay.

Refs: #640 review round 5; kernel lifecycle_outbox; mission-signals MissionSignalEmitter; signals draft's same-jti redelivery rule.

issues.title: Machine-readable per-type transformation capability map (narrow / delegate / project)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Deferred design from the #644 review (finding 3). The core now declares each supported `authorization_details` type's transformation boundary (subset relation and delegation semantics understood, or carried-as-approved) as a deployment-documentation MUST at {#other-types}, explicitly NOT an interoperable discovery surface: RFC 9396's `authorization_details_types_supported` is an array of type strings, and the optional schema endpoint defines no field for the boundary, so a client without the documentation learns the boundary only by attempt.

The reviewer's alternative stands as the design option this issue tracks: a Mission-specific, machine-readable capability map with INDEPENDENT per-type properties (narrowing, delegation, projection are distinct capabilities — knowing how to narrow a type does not establish it can safely be delegated or projected). Candidate carriers, in family-preference order (no new endpoints/metadata members when existing surfaces can carry it): an entry in the type-metadata endpoint's per-type value (where advertised), a member of the AS's supported-type documentation with a registered JSON shape, or (last resort) a new AS metadata member.

Interlocks: the conformance row core.other-types.transformation-boundary-declared (deployment-documentation surface) would gain a machine-checkable observation; the AuthZEN policy-entry lane is the main consumer pressure; #424 (Deployment Profile schema) is the adjacent productization reservation and the two should not define competing capability vocabularies.

Not scheduled; recorded so the documentation-scoped MUST is understood as the deliberate floor, not the end state.

issues.title: Impl: authority_source record member and approval-time source verification (core #316 follow-through)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-22 reference-implementation family audit (pin-drift pass over `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`).

The #316 ruling landed in the core draft after the implementation's pin (`c2053e5`): the Mission Record now carries a REQUIRED `authority_source` object (`type`: `user_delegated` / `service_owned` / `organizational`, plus `policy` for organizational), and approval processing gains three MUSTs: establish the source from trusted configuration, verify the Approver may activate that source, and verify the derived Authority Set lies within the source ceiling. Rendering at approval is also normative.

The implementation has no trace of it: `MissionRecord` (`src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/types.ts`) has no `authority_source` member, and the approval flow in `kernel.ts` neither establishes nor verifies a source. `grep -rn authority_source src` returns nothing.

Direction: add the member to `MissionRecord` and the config-driven trusted source establishment at approval, with the two verification gates refusing before record creation. Demo config gives every seeded user/client an explicit source; the organizational path can ride the existing approver role in `config/identity.json`. The core row's pin bump stays deferred until this lands (D25/D41 convention).

issues.title: Impl: mission_expires_at response member and effective-expiry narrowing (family #525 follow-through)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-22 reference-implementation family audit (pin-drift pass over `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`).

The family-wide #525 change (core commit `18e0f3dd` and siblings) distinguishes requested from effective Mission expiry: the AS MAY narrow the requested `expires_at` by policy, and every Mission-creating success response MUST carry `mission_expires_at` (core token response, Expansion completion response, Child Mission creation response).

The implementation predates it on all three surfaces:

- `kernel.ts` assigns `expires_at: input.intent.expires_at` verbatim; no policy narrowing step exists.
- No response surface emits `mission_expires_at`: not the token response paths in `adapters/provider.ts`, not the expansion or child-creation exchange responses in `adapters/continuation-grant.ts`. `grep -rn mission_expires_at src` returns nothing.

Direction: one kernel narrowing hook (config-driven ceiling, effective = min(requested, policy)) plus the response member on each Mission-creating success body. Blocks the pin bumps for the core, expansion, and child-delegation rows.

issues.title: Impl: transaction-assurance idempotency claim states, idempotency_conflict, tombstones, active reconciliation (S-6 disposition stale)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-22 reference-implementation family audit (pin-drift pass over `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`).

`draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime` reworked the transaction-assurance tier after the row's pin (`02d53dd`, other runtime rows are current at `b5e35e2`):

1. Idempotency is now an explicit PDP-side atomic claim with a six-state resolution table (claimed / reserved / indeterminate / completed / failed / expired), a distinct terminal reason `idempotency_conflict` for a mismatched operation identity under the same key, and a mandatory tombstone horizon for high-consequence classes. The implementation has a binary redeem-once with a single `permit_consumed` reason (`services/mcp-payments/src/transaction.ts`) and a `duplicate_suppressed` path in the PEP; `idempotency_conflict`, claim states, and tombstones appear nowhere in `src/`.
2. Outcome reconciliation is now an active, deadline-driven process (owner and deadline, evidence determines the result, indeterminate converts to a tombstone). `services/mcp-payments/src/reconcile.ts` is a passive on-demand matcher with no deadline, no outcome recording, no tombstone conversion.

Spec-feedback note: D28 ruled the PDP a pure decision function with the PEP owning redemption state, and S-6 asked the companion to confirm the stateless-PDP contract. The new text moves the atomic claim to the PDP, the opposite direction, so S-6's disposition is stale. Worth an explicit ruling on where the claim store lives before implementing; the runtime transaction-assurance row's pin stays at `02d53dd` until then.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
**Session disposition (2026-08-23, architecture-review follow-through; verified against main @ 2d63119a):**

**Analysis**

S-6 is still literally open (PLAN.md:1296); what's stale is its candidate fix ("the PDP remains stateless, consumption tracking is a PEP duty"), which assumed D28's boundary was final. D28 (PLAN.md:113) drew that boundary only around redemption and lease state (PEP-owned) and deferred cumulative caps to the metering follow-on. Metering settled that deferred question with PDP-side operational state: its Exactness and Topology section (draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md#topology) names an Exact enforcement profile (a single serializing PDP, a shared linearizable store, or structurally-exact sub-budgets) and a Bounded-consistency profile (distributed PDPs, published overshoot), barring Bounded for `exclusive` since exclusivity can't degrade gracefully (metering:616-628).

The new idempotency claim (runtime.md#idempotency, 2118-2211) has the same shape (exactly-one-winner over an (idempotency scope, key) pair, durable tombstone for high-consequence classes) but cites none of this, reading as a second, uncoordinated stateful mechanism. It's also broader than the transaction-assurance tier: line 2131's "a keyed action" isn't qualified to the classes line 2128 scopes (irreversible/external-commitment/privileged-admin), so a core-tier reversible write using the idempotency-key control (line 2099) textually inherits the same PDP claim duty. That's a spec delta worth naming, not just an implementation gap.

**Sketch**

Cross-reference metering's Topology framework from runtime#idempotency instead of restating it. Pin the high-consequence claim and tombstone to Exact enforcement only (no Bounded fallback, matching `exclusive`); declare the claim domain per claim in the Enforcement Scope Statement, alongside the Mission state source and PDP identity bullets (runtime.md:630-678 has no claim-store bullet yet). Narrow line 2131 to the classes line 2128 already names, so a core-tier reversible write's idempotency-key control stays a lighter PEP/resource dedup key, not the atomic-claim machinery.

**Recommendation**

Option (a), scoped, not retired. D28's "pure decision function" is narrowed, not reversed: the PDP stays stateless by default; the transaction-assurance tier's idempotency claim (and metering's Exact-enforcement counters) are declared PDP-side operational state, named per claim in the Enforcement Scope Statement. Reject (b): a freshness-bounded state source tolerates staleness, while an exactly-one-winner claim needs a linearizable write, a different consistency class, though the store can still sit off the PDP process (the AS kernel's existing `creation-idempotency` store, src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/creation-idempotency.ts, is the template). Reject (c) as framed: metering already forbids a Bounded fallback for hard invariants; reuse that vocabulary rather than invent a looser one for idempotency.

**Tradeoffs**

No new mechanism: metering's Topology framework and the AS's creation-idempotency precedent already model this; the PDP (or its named store) gets an equivalent table. Conformance: re-pin SPEC_VERSIONS.md's transaction-assurance row (02d53dd) and check the authzen PDP-request row (f5977e0), since `duplicate_suppressed`/`idempotency_conflict` live there too; update CONFORMANCE.md:73 and the D28/S-6 entries in PLAN.md. Stateless-PDP deployments survive for core-tier, non-keyed actions; a deployment claiming the idempotency-key control or transaction-assurance for a high-consequence class accepts a declared Exact-enforcement domain, not a blanket stateful mandate.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review against `origin/main` at `2d63119a`: I agree with narrowing D28 rather than reversing it. D28 assigns redemption and lease state to the PEP and expressly deferred cumulative counters; Metering subsequently established that elected controls can require PDP-side operational state or a named linearizable store. Runtime idempotency can reuse that topology vocabulary.

Two refinements are needed:

- The idempotency claim is **Exact-only**, not a choice between Exact and Bounded. Its exactly-one-winner property has the same non-degradable shape as Metering's `exclusive` latch. The Enforcement Scope Statement should declare the Exact claim-domain/store topology per mediated action class or idempotency scope—not enumerate dynamic claims—and inability to reach that domain must fail closed.
- Narrowing "a keyed action" to the three high-consequence classes is safe only if the reversible-write branch remains complete. Runtime allows a reversible write to use a short permit window plus an idempotency key. If that case no longer uses the PDP claim, the Resource/PEP still needs an atomic reserve/deduplicate rule covering concurrent and completed duplicates; otherwise the narrowing weakens the existing guarantee.

The AS creation-idempotency store is useful precedent for atomic reservation and fingerprint conflict, but not a drop-in implementation: it has only `reserved/completed/failed` and frees expired tombstones, whereas Runtime requires the larger claim-state table and an indeterminate claim that never becomes reusable through time alone.

Evidence: [runtime claim semantics](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2118-L2211), [reversible-write branch](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2095-L2101), [reconciliation](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2385-L2416), and [Metering topology](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/2d63119a16c29baa80106d8e6cd4b6cae00dfd29/draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md#L551-L630).

Disposition: approve narrowed D28 with Exact-only topology and preserved reversible-write semantics.

issues.title: Impl: Decision Evidence evidence_envelope (REQUIRED) and Egress Evidence mission-reference shape
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-22 reference-implementation family audit (pin-drift pass over `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`).

Two evidence-shape conformance gaps, one latent and one from harness drift:

1. `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence` (row pinned CURRENT at `3694449`) makes `evidence_envelope` (integrity protection: `format` + `value`) REQUIRED on the Decision Evidence Object. The retained records built in `services/mcp-payments/src/evidence.ts` carry no `evidence_envelope` and are unsigned; only `packages/orchestration` implements the envelope convention (for compensation evidence). This is a gap against an already-current pin, not drift: the row claims `runtime-evidence#decision-evidence-object` while the REQUIRED member is absent.
2. `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness` gained a normative `#egress-evidence` section (Egress Evidence is an implemented surface, not a named deferral): the record's Mission reference is a REQUIRED nested `mission` object `{id, issuer, authority_hash?}` and the timestamp member is `occurred_at`. The implementation's `EgressEvidence` carries flat `mission_id` + `authority_hash`, has no `issuer` member anywhere in `EvidenceBase`, and names the timestamp `at`. The flat shape is a repo-wide `EvidenceBase` convention (decision/refusal/execution kinds share it), so this is a systemic reconcile: either restructure the base or record a documented deviation.

The harness row's pin bump waits on (2). Suggest deciding (2)'s direction first since it constrains how (1)'s envelope attaches.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: Audit addendum (same 2026-08-22 pass, containment verification): a third evidence-shape item belongs here. The containment draft's Protected Event Receipt has no dedicated realization: the ingestion/rejection record is folded into the generic flat `ingestion` evidence kind (services/mcp-payments/src/evidence.ts IngestionEvidence + kernel/issuer-evidence.ts) with no `receipt_id`, no nested `mission`/`event` objects, optional rather than REQUIRED `emitter`, and no dedicated media type or JCS canonical-bytes rule, while ContainmentEvidence (kernel/containment.ts) matches its object exactly. Whatever direction item 2's EvidenceBase reconcile takes should cover this record too. The new containment matrix row names this caveat.

issues.title: Impl: RAS local token must carry the redeeming client's client_id (S-12 precondition)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-22 reference-implementation family audit (pin-drift pass over `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`).

`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain` flipped the local-token rule at the Resource AS (commits `6792a153` / `91163100`): the token minted on ID-JAG redemption MUST set `client_id` to the redeeming client's own local registration and MUST NOT carry the Mission's approved agent identity (the old text allowed preserving the issuer's `client_id` as audit-only).

The demo RAS (`services/ras/src/index.ts`, `redeem()`) mints the local token with no `client_id` member at all, and the mint path has nowhere to source one: the RAS has no registered-client model. That is the already-accepted S-12 deviation (presenter binding via `cnf.jkt` instead of client authentication at the RAS token endpoint).

Direction: close S-12 first (register the redeeming client at the RAS, authenticate the redemption call), then stamp the authenticated client as `client_id` on the minted token. The cross-domain row's pin stays at `dc7a897` until this lands.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: **Ruled (2026-08-24, owner): S-12 resolved as a property-level MUST.** The destination-local credential MUST identify the redeeming destination client per the destination's own conventions (where RFC 9068-style JWT local tokens are used, that is client_id); the origin identity travels exclusively via the Origin Principal members and never as the local client identity. Execution: one sentence-level cross-domain spec addition stating the property-level requirement, then the RAS implementation change this issue tracks (same mint path as the #539 stage-B work; the fields are independent). Unblocked.

issues.title: Impl: async-delegation family-fallback mission claim drops predecessor/parent lineage
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
From the 2026-08-22 reference-implementation family audit (pin-drift pass over `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`).

Possible lineage-claim bug on the async-delegation refresh path. In `services/authorization-server/src/adapters/provider.ts`, `extraTokenClaims`'s delegation-family fallback returns bare `kernel.missionClaim(famRecord)`, while the main `gateDerivation` path correctly selects `childMissionClaim` / `successorMissionClaim` when the record carries `parent` / `predecessor`. If a per-delegation refresh-token family roots at a successor or Child Mission, its refreshed token's `mission` claim silently drops the REQUIRED lineage member (`expansion#predecessor-member`, `child-delegation#parent-member`).

Reachability unconfirmed: the audit verified the code branch but did not trace whether a delegation family can actually root at a successor or child record today. If it cannot, add the guard anyway (or an assertion) so the invariant is enforced rather than incidental; if it can, this is a live conformance bug with a straightforward fix (reuse the same claim selection as the main path) plus a regression test in `async-delegation.test.ts`.

issues.title: Impl: lifecycle discharge operation, terminal_when, nonce dedup (+ signals authority_hash member)
