pulls.title: demo: interactive surfaces (browser console, terminal exhibit, Jaeger traces)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Adds the three ways to *see* the flows working — none existed before (the build shipped a headless runner + scorecards only). All three drive the same composed stack (`demo/src/stack.ts`) so they exercise the identical PEP → PDP → OpenFGA path.

## 1. Live browser console — `pnpm demo:serve` → http://localhost:4407
A clickable dashboard over a Node HTTP server that composes the full stack and seeds a mission (subject alice, approver bob) with a wire + evidence:
- **Agent panel**: catalog with live statuses + action buttons (read inv-1, wire inv-1 ok, wire inv-2 over-cap, wire inv-3 out-of-vendor).
- **Operator panel**: mission fleet with suspend/revoke/resume, and the **verified evidence timeline** (the D32 feed with five-step verification).
- Acting updates the catalog and timeline live; a revoke flips `payments` connected → consent_required.
The `apps/` React SPAs remain production-shaped thin views; this dashboard is the runnable surface.

## 2. Terminal exhibit — `pnpm exhibit`
A narrated end-to-end walk printing the **real wire artifacts** at each step: anchors, derived authority, permits, denial reasons (`constraint_exceeded`, `out_of_authority`, `mission_inactive`), and the verified evidence feed. This is the deferred O-28 exhibit mode.

## 3. Distributed traces — `pnpm demo:trace` → http://localhost:16686 (service `mission-demo`)
Instrumented the real enforcement path (`pdp.evaluate`, `fga.check`, `pep.enforce`) with OTel spans — no-ops without an SDK, so the test suite is unaffected. Each action is one trace: `flow.wire → pep.enforce → pdp.evaluate → fga.check`. Verified spans reach Jaeger.

## Also
- `mission-core` canonicalize now drops undefined-valued members (JSON/JCS-correct; fixed a throw on evidence with an absent `trace_id`). Anchor vectors unaffected.
- 119/119 tests, typecheck + lint clean. DEMO.md documents all three surfaces.

pulls.title: demo: detailed exhibit -- full protocol artifacts at every step
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Addresses the gap: the terminal exhibit was summary lines and missing the actual artifacts. It is now a full protocol trace that prints the real wire values end to end:

- **Catalog**: the request + the full response (services, connection statuses, request-access link).
- **Intent**: the shaped `mission_intent` — deliberately over-broad (a bogus `vendor.delete`, extra vendors, a huge cap) so the narrowing is visible.
- **Proposal → derived**: the derived Authority Set with the narrowing called out (`vendor.delete` dropped, vendors clamped to `acme`, cap 999999 → 500).
- **Mission Record + anchors** and the **mission-bound access token** (decoded claims: mission projection, `cnf`, `authorization_details`).
- **Each tool call**: the MCP `tools/call` with params + the presented token, the **PEP effective parameters + `parameter_digest`**, the **AuthZEN PDP request envelope** (subject/resource/action/context with actor, capability_source, amount), and the **PDP decision** (decision_id, policy_view_id, permit, single_use) — for the permit and for each denial reason.
- Revocation → denied decision, then the verified evidence feed.

## Enabler
`PepDeps.observe` — an optional hook that captures the AuthZEN envelope and the raw PDP decision the PEP built. It never affects the decision and is a no-op in production; the demo stack exposes it as `onEnforce`.

119/119 tests, typecheck + lint clean.

pulls.title: demo: wire the ARAP JIT flow across all three surfaces
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Makes the **M6 ARAP reevaluate** path a first-class part of the interactive demo: an action that is **within the mission's authority** but gated behind a **per-action approval**, resolved **just-in-time**.

`send_remittance_email` (`payments:remittance.send`) is in the demo mission's Authority Set, but deployment policy requires an action-bound approval before it commits. The round-trip:

1. Agent calls the tool → PDP denies `action_approval_required`, marked **requestable** (a PDP-signed `binding_token` + the ARS intake endpoint).
2. Agent submits an access request → the ARS **verifies the PDP-signed binding** before it opens a task.
3. Approver (**bob**, distinct from acting subject **alice**) adjudicates → the ARS mints an **action-bound approval object** scoped to the request's `parameter_digest`.
4. Agent retries the same call carrying `context.action_approval` → PDP **permits** (digest matches, within max age) → the email commits.

The approval is **input context, never a new grant**; the mission is never widened (D42/D37). The **same `parameter_digest`** binds the denial, the approval, and the permit throughout.

## Surfaces

- **Terminal exhibit** (`pnpm exhibit`): new narrated **step 6** printing the full deny → submit → approve → retry → permit sequence with real wire artifacts (envelope, signed binding, ARS task, approval object, both decisions).
- **Browser console** (`pnpm demo:serve`): an **Approver panel** (ARAP queue with approve/deny) plus a JIT trigger + retry button in the agent panel; the operator timeline picks up the new verified evidence.
- **Jaeger** (`pnpm demo:trace`): a `flow.jit` span nesting `pep.enforce → pdp.evaluate → fga.check` for both attempts.

## Production change

`services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts` — `callTransactionTool` now threads `context.action_approval` and surfaces the requestable `access_request`. Non-breaking: added as a 5th optional param after `beforeCommit`; existing callers (tests, evals) are unaffected. Covered by a new `transaction.test.ts` case: no approval → `action_approval_required` + `access_request` surfaced; mismatched digest → still refused; matching approval → permit + commit.

## Verification

- Gate green: typecheck, lint, **120 tests** (was 119; +1 JIT test), live against OpenFGA.
- All three surfaces exercised live end-to-end.

## Notes for reviewers

- The browser server's `lastDigest` is a shared module-level var. Two concurrent tool calls could clobber it, but `ars.submit` verifies the digest against the signed binding and would throw loudly rather than corrupt state — and this is a single-session demo, so it's fine as-is.
- **PLAN.md is intentionally not touched here** — per the project's workflow, PLAN.md lands direct-to-main and code lands as PRs; this demonstrates already-documented M6/M12 capability, so no decision/milestone/log entry changes.

pulls.title: demo: put the demo server on a Hono router
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Replaces the hand-rolled `node:http` request handler in `demo/src/server.ts` with a small **Hono** app. The handler had grown into a nine-route `if (path === ...) / regex` chain; Hono gives a readable route table, JSON + error middleware, and typed path params.

**Demo-only, scoped by design:**
- **No view engine.** The page is client-rendered (static HTML + `fetch`); the production view layer is the `apps/*` React SPAs. Server-side templating would be a step sideways.
- **Same process shape.** `@hono/node-server` serves `app.fetch` on `node:http`, so it's still one command (`pnpm demo:serve`), same port, identical endpoints and behavior.

## Why this and not Express / a view engine

The repo already has its framework story: OAuth on Koa (via `node-oidc-provider`), `console-bff` as a transport-agnostic BFF, and React/Vite SPAs in `apps/*`. The demo server is glue in front of `composeStack`. Hono is the minimal, TS-first fit for cleaning up its routing without pulling a heavier framework or an unnecessary templating engine into the least-important process.

## Changes

- `app.onError` / `app.notFound` replace the `try/catch` + trailing 404.
- Param routes (`missions/:id/timeline`, `missions/:id/lifecycle`) replace regex matches.
- `readJson(c)` tolerates an empty body.
- Adds `hono` + `@hono/node-server` to `demo/package.json` (the repo's first HTTP-framework dep, confined to the demo package).

## Verification

Ran the server live and round-tripped every route identically: session, catalog (3 services), fleet, param timeline, JSON 404, the full JIT/ARAP flow (deny → queue → retry-pending → approve → retry-executed), and param lifecycle (suspend). Gate green: typecheck, lint, **120 tests**.

pulls.title: exhibit: real OAuth issuance (incl. id_token), ID-JAG cross-domain, full lifecycle
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Extends the terminal exhibit (`pnpm exhibit`) to answer three gaps: it showed no id_token, never touched the ID-JAG cross-domain leg, and did only a single revoke for lifecycle. It now drives a **real authorization server** end to end and prints every request/response as the real value on the wire.

## ⚠️ Not demo-only — a real AS capability change (review these first)

- **`services/authorization-server/src/adapters/provider.ts`**: the AS now supports OIDC — `openid` added to `scopes`, and the grant is granted exactly the requested scopes, so `/token` issues a **real id_token** when `openid` is requested. Previously the AS issued no id_token at all. This is a genuine capability addition, verified by the existing suite (still 120 green) and the exhibit.
- **`packages/demo-data`**: the agent client scope becomes `openid payments`; `DERIVATION_POLICY.ceiling` gains the LedgerCloud SaaS resource (so one mission can span both estates); and demo-data takes a new `workspace:*` dependency on `@mission/mcp-saas` to import the canonical `SAAS_RESOURCE` (guarantees the ceiling ↔ SaaS-server action-name match). No cycle (mcp-saas depends only on jose).

## composeStack: real issuance behind a flag

`composeStack({ withAuthServer: true })` stands up the real provider (`buildAuthorizationServer`) on an HTTP port, uses **its** kernel as the single source of truth (so provider-approved missions are visible to the PDP), verifies real tokens at the payments RS against the AS `/jwks`, and wires the cross-domain RAS + SaaS servers with an ID-JAG grant helper. **The browser and trace surfaces leave the flag off** and keep the in-process kernel + `TokenFacts` path, byte-for-byte unchanged.

## What the exhibit now shows (every step = request/response)

- **Real issuance** (new `demo/src/oauth-client.ts`, ported from the green `tracer.test.ts`): PAR → authorize → headless interaction/decide (Bob approves alice) → token, with DPoP, `private_key_jwt`, PKCE, and the mandatory dpop-nonce retry. A genuine **access_token AND id_token**.
- The access token decoded: `aud` = the payments resource, `cnf.jkt` DPoP-binding, `authorization_details` spanning **both** estates. The id_token decoded: `aud` = `client_id` (identifies the user to the client, distinct from the resource-audienced access token).
- **RS validation**: `server.validateToken` (signature via `/jwks`, DPoP jkt == cnf.jkt, mission claim); the returned `TokenFacts` drive every tool call — no more hand-built token.
- **ID-JAG cross-domain** (M9): a real grant audience-scoped to the SaaS estate → RAS redeem → SaaS `post_journal_entry`; a replay is rejected `invalid_grant` (single-use).
- **Full lifecycle**: suspend (denied) → resume (permitted) over the wire; then expansion to a widened successor + supersede-on-redemption (the original credential stops authorizing); then revoke the successor over the wire.
- JIT/ARAP, out-of-authority/over-cap denials, and the verified evidence feed retained.

## Design honesty

Two hops stay in-process by deliberate design and are narrated as such: the PDP is a pure function (D28) and the payments MCP transport is a production swap (O-33). Everything printed is a real artifact (the id_token came off the real `/token` response).

## Deviation (deliberate)

Expansion widens via **actions** (`+payments:payment.schedule`), not the cap: the fixed derivation ceiling re-clamps any raised cap to 500, so a "raised cap" would be fiction. `successorWidensOnly(...) === true` is printed to prove the widening is real. Noted in-output.

## Verification

Ran the exhibit live (exit 0; 11 evidence rows verified). Gate green: `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (**120 passed**). Browser + trace surfaces smoke-booted on the refactored stack.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Per the repo workflow, PLAN.md lands direct-to-main. The openid/id_token enablement is a real AS capability worth a Spec Feedback Log line; I'll propose that text separately rather than fold it into this code PR.

pulls.title: config: move identity/policy/clients/catalog/seed/topology to static JSON
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Moves inline TS config to static JSON under `src/config/`, loaded and validated at boot behind one typed loader in `@mission/demo-data`. The public export surface is unchanged; env vars still override. Two phases.

## Design (agreed)
- **Static kids, ephemeral keys (D25 kept).** Config holds each key's `kid`+`alg` only; the boot loader still generates every keypair per boot and stamps the configured kid. No private keys in the repo. Works because trust flows through JWKS (verifiers resolve the public key by kid), never a pinned key value.
- **Loader:** lean hand-rolled validators (fail-fast naming file+field, matching the `validateMissionIntent` style — no new dependency). Config dir resolved module-relative (walk up for `config/topology.json`), `MISSION_CONFIG_DIR` override, never `process.cwd`. Read via `fs` so editing JSON needs no recompile.
- Types preserved through the loader: `WRITE_ACTIONS` stays a `Set`, `DERIVATION_POLICY` a non-empty tuple, `CatalogServiceSeed` carries the literal unions consumers rely on.

## Phase 1 — data already inside demo-data
`config/{identity,policy,clients,catalog}.json` + `config/seed/{vendors,invoices}.json` + `config/topology.json` (resources). demo-data becomes a JSON loader with the same exports/values/types. **Zero consumer or test edits.** Dropped demo-data's import of `@mission/mcp-saas` (SaaS URL is config now) — demo-data is a leaf again.

## Phase 2 — topology, injected (not read by services)
`config/topology.json` extended with issuers, endpoints, ports, TTLs, dev service token, per-purpose key kids/algs, and openfga defaults; demo-data exports a validated `TOPOLOGY`. composeStack injects all of it into the constructors it already calls.

### ⚠️ Touches services (review these — verified by the unchanged 120-test suite)
- `services/authorization-server/src/index.ts` + `adapters/provider.ts`: the as-token/as-status **kids+algs** and **accessTokenTTL** now come from config (AS already depended on demo-data; no new edge). `accessTokenTTL` is an additive optional `AdapterOptions` field (default 300).
- `services/ras/src/index.ts`: additive optional `localTokenAudience` (default the current literal), replacing a hardcoded `setAudience`.
- `services/mcp-saas/src/index.ts`: additive optional `resource` self-id (default `SAAS_RESOURCE`, still exported).
All new service params are **optional with the current literal as default**, so services stay standalone-runnable and existing tests need zero edits (`cross-domain.test.ts` unchanged, git-verified). No service reads config files; demo-data stays a leaf; no cycles.

**Out of scope by design:** the PDP permit TTLs (120/300) and mcp-payments lease seconds (30) are behavioral constants inside decision/execution logic, not topology, and stay in code.

## Verification
- **Value fidelity** (the real acceptance criterion — the exhibit can't catch config drift since producer and verifier both read it): diffed every committed config value against the pre-refactor literals in git history — issuers, ports (4400/4407), TTLs (300/120/300/300), all kids/algs, ARS endpoint, resources (4403/4406/4499), dev token, openfga defaults, the policy cap/vendors/actions, and client scope/redirect/kid — **all match, no drift.**
- Gate: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean, `pnpm lint` clean, **120 tests (0 skipped, 0 test edits)**, `pnpm exhibit` green end to end, browser + trace surfaces boot, and the two config-loading launchers pass: **`pnpm evals`** (100% containment, zero gaps) and **`pnpm demo:vendor-test`** (all four axes deny).
- Env override (`MCP_PAYMENTS_RESOURCE`) still propagates into policy + catalog.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
A `D`-entry recording the config-driven-stack decision (and the static-kid/ephemeral-key rule) lands in PLAN.md direct-to-main after merge, per the workflow.

pulls.title: exhibit: syntax-highlight the JSON blocks
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Makes the terminal exhibit (`pnpm exhibit`) easier to read: the JSON blocks were printed monochrome (only step headers, notes, and verdicts were colored). Now they're syntax-highlighted.

## Change (one file, cosmetic)
A small dependency-free ANSI highlighter added to the exhibit's `block()` helper:
- object keys → cyan
- string values → green
- numbers → yellow
- booleans / null → magenta
- punctuation (braces, colons, commas) → terminal default

Quoted strings are matched as whole tokens first, so digits or braces *inside* a string (timestamps, `sha-256:` hashes) are never recolored. Matches the exhibit's existing hand-rolled ANSI style — **no new dependency**. Demo-only: `block()` lives in `exhibit.ts`, which no test imports.

## Verification
`pnpm exhibit` runs to completion (exit 0); keys/strings/numbers/booleans render in the intended colors, step headers/notes/verdicts unchanged. `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm lint` clean; **120 tests** still pass.

pulls.title: arop: carry JIT approval via AROP Transaction Challenge, not a tool input
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Fixes a conformance defect you flagged: the demo's JIT approval was carried as an **agent-supplied tool input** (`context.action_approval`), with no cryptographic binding — an agent could forge it (it learns `parameter_digest` from the denial). AROP (openid/authzen#531) is explicit that the approval never rides the client wire ("the decision is not carried on the wire … no new in-band input mechanism"); the completion is an AS-issued token. This reroutes the flow through the **AROP Transaction Challenge** binding, over real HTTP.

## ⚠️ Not demo-only — changes committed AS + RS behavior and a delivered milestone (review these)

- **`services/authorization-server`**: NEW `transaction_authorization_endpoint` (`POST /transaction`, advertised in metadata) — client-authenticated by its DPoP-bound base mission token, bodied with the RS-signed txn-challenge; validates the challenge, D42 subset-gates vs the **active** mission, opens an ARS approval task, and on approval issues a txn-token. `txn-challenge.ts`: `parameter_digest` added; `issueTxnToken` carries an `approval` claim and the **active** mission unchanged. `access-request`: `openForTxn` (AS-vouched task, no PDP binding). **`arop.test.ts` scenario 7 realigned** to carry the active mission (dropped `createExpansion`/`successorMissionClaim`) — this fixes the **D42 txn-path defect** the plan had flagged for DTR but left in the txn path.
- **`services/mcp-payments`**: the RS signs a txn-challenge on an `action_approval_required` denial (scoped to the specific gated action, a proper subset that keeps constraints) and validates a presented txn-token (sig/iss/aud/typ, `cnf.jkt` chains to the base token, single-use), deriving `context.approval` from it. **Removed** the agent-supplied `actionApproval` param from `callTransactionTool`.

## Design: hybrid (settled with review; resolves S-3)

The AS issues the txn-token (AROP token issuance); the RS validates that AS-signed token and derives `context.approval`; the **PDP step 8 is unchanged** and still validates it. The bug was the approval's *source* (agent) and *carriage* (tool input), not the reevaluate primitive — so those are fixed and the PEP→PDP→OpenFGA thesis + the `parameter_digest` binding are preserved. This is **M6's completion mechanism changing** from reevaluate-with-agent-context to AROP token issuance, and it resolves the open **S-3** ambiguity (reevaluate vs token-issuance) in favor of the hybrid.

## De-risked before building

A throwaway spike proved the full chain (challenge → validate → D42 subset → issue token with `parameter_digest` + `cnf` → RS validate → step 8 permit → foreign-key rejected) before any of the ~10-file build. Delivered in three gated phases (AS / RS / demo+removal).

## Verification (all mine, re-run)

- `pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` clean; **126 tests** (added AS txn-endpoint + RS AROP cases; removed the old agent-supplied JIT test).
- `pnpm exhibit` exit 0 — the JIT step is now real-HTTP AROP: DENY `action_approval_required` + RS `txn-challenge` → `POST /transaction` (pending) → Bob approves via the ARS → **txn-token** (active mission unchanged, `approval.parameter_digest`, `cnf.jkt`==base jkt, `single_use`) → re-present carrying the **txn-token** → PERMIT + committed. The approver task is now labeled with the gated action.
- Browser + trace surfaces boot; `pnpm evals` (100% containment) and `pnpm demo:vendor-test` pass.
- Confirmed no caller passes an agent-supplied approval (grep-clean).

## Residuals (named, intentional)

- The ARAP `requestable`/`access_request` path in `pep.ts` + `ars.submit(binding_token)` is now **unused by any surface** but retained as a capability (ARAP reevaluate mode). Not dead code that slipped through — a deliberate keep.
- `mcp-payments/src/txn-challenge.ts` is a **copy** of the AS leaf primitives (to avoid a dep cycle that would drag the AS kernel + oidc-provider into the RS closure). Format-coupled; both files now cross-reference each other.
- The **other RS (`mcp-saas`) has no per-action approval gate** — it's token-only (no PDP), so there is nothing to convert there.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

A `D`-entry lands direct-to-main after merge: records the hybrid choice, the retained-dormant ARAP `requestable` capability, S-3 resolved, and the scenario-7 D42 realign.

pulls.title: as: id_token carries OIDC identity claims from the identity store
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The AS issued a real id_token, but it carried only `sub`. Now it carries the subject's identity, sourced from the config-driven identity store.

## Changes (an AS capability change — review `provider.ts`)
- **`services/authorization-server/src/adapters/provider.ts`**: `scopes` += `profile`, `email`; a `claims` map (`profile: [name, preferred_username]`, `email: [email]`); **`conformIdTokenClaims: false`** so those claims land in the id_token itself rather than only at the userinfo endpoint (the exhibit shows the id_token, and there's no userinfo call); `findAccount` resolves the user from the `USERS` identity store and returns `name`/`email`/`preferred_username` (falls back to `sub` for an unknown subject).
- **`config/identity.json`** + demo-data loader: `email` added to each user (Alice Anderson / alice@acme.example, Bob Brown / bob@acme.example); `SeededUser` gains `email`.
- **`config/clients.json`**: the agent client's `scope` += `profile email` so it may request them.
- **`demo/src/exhibit.ts`**: requests `openid profile email payments` and prints the identity claims.

## Verification
`pnpm exhibit` now shows the id_token carrying `iss/sub/aud` + `name: "Alice Anderson"`, `preferred_username: "alice"`, `email: "alice@acme.example"`. Gate green: `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, **126 tests**. The tracer/txn/arop tests are unaffected (they request `payments` only, so no id_token is issued).

Consistent with S-9: the id_token is a standard OIDC identity token (identifies the user to the client); authority still travels only in the mission-bound access token.

pulls.title: arop: use the transaction_authorization_id continuation handle (not challenge re-POST)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Makes the AROP Transaction Challenge flow use the spec's continuation handle (openid/authzen#531). Resolves two conformance points raised in review:

1. **Not mixing bindings / not RS-as-requester.** The spec has one RS-originated model: the RS asserts a *signed* challenge, the **client** presents it to the AS, the **AS** submits the ARAP access request and is the sole issuer ("the originating deployment does not forward anything on the client's behalf"). Polling is native to the txn binding (its own handle + the transaction endpoint), *not* DTR. Our model was already right; the mechanics weren't.
2. **The binding token that captures the challenge state = the `transaction_authorization_id`.** The RS-signed `txn-challenge` binds the operation; the AS-issued `transaction_authorization_id` is the continuation handle bound to the *validated* challenge (and to the requesting client's `cnf`), which the client polls with. We were missing the handle — we re-POSTed the whole challenge each poll.

## Change (AS endpoint + clients; RS + crypto unchanged)
- **`services/authorization-server/src/adapters/provider.ts`** — `handleTransaction` branches on body shape after shared base-token+DPoP auth:
  - **Initiation** `{ challenge }` → validate + D42 subset-gate + open the ARS task → mint an opaque `transaction_authorization_id`, store the validated state `{ taskId, txn, missionId, cnfJkt, parameter_digest, authorization_details, subject, audience, expiresAt }` → `200 { transaction_authorization_id, expires_in, interval }`.
  - **Poll** `{ transaction_authorization_id }` → look up the handle, **verify base-token `cnf.jkt` == stored `cnf`** (handle bound to the client), check the ARS task → pending, or issue the txn-token from stored state (active mission unchanged, D42). Unknown id → 404; cnf mismatch → 403.
  - The client presents the challenge **once**; everything after is poll-by-id.
- **`txn-endpoint.test.ts`** — rewritten to the handle flow (initiate → pending → approve → poll-by-id → token, all token-claim assertions preserved) + new negatives: unknown id → 404, cnf mismatch → 403.
- **`exhibit.ts` / `server.ts`** — present the challenge once, poll by `transaction_authorization_id`, re-present the issued txn-token to the RS.

RS side (`mcp-payments`), the txn-token shape, and topology are untouched.

## Verification
`pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` clean; **128 tests** (126 + 2 negatives). `pnpm exhibit` exit 0 — step 7 shows: DENY `action_approval_required` → RS `txn-challenge` → `POST /transaction {challenge}` (once) → `{ transaction_authorization_id, expires_in: 300, interval: 5 }` → Bob approves via the ARS → `POST /transaction {transaction_authorization_id}` → txn-token (active mission unchanged, `single_use`, `cnf`==base jkt, `approval.parameter_digest`) → re-present → PERMIT. Browser round-trip, traces, evals (100% containment), and vendor-test all pass.

## Note
Idempotency-by-`txn` is gone by design (the challenge is presented once; the RS mints a fresh `txn` per emission, so a duplicate initiation cannot occur in the wired flows).

## Follow-up
The AROP `D`-entry (direct-to-main after merge) will record this handle refinement (client-driven, `transaction_authorization_id`) alongside the hybrid / S-3 / D42 notes.

pulls.title: ci(impl-ci): start OpenFGA as a step so the server actually runs
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
**impl-ci was failing on every push/PR.** Root cause: the OpenFGA image needs the `run` subcommand to start its server (the dev `docker-compose.yml` has `command: run`), but GitHub Actions `services:` **cannot pass a container command**. So the CI service container never listened on 8080 — every OpenFGA-backed test silently **skipped** ("OpenFGA unreachable") and `pnpm evals` (which hard-requires OpenFGA) **failed the job**.

## Fix
- Replace the `services: openfga` block with a **step** that runs `docker run -d … openfga/openfga@<digest> run` (plain HTTP + preshared auth, pinned by digest per D39) and waits for `/healthz`.
- `scripts/evals.mjs`: set the dev CA only if `certs/openfga.crt` exists, so CI (plain HTTP, no cert) doesn't emit the misleading "Ignoring extra certs" warning.

## Verification
Simulated CI exactly, locally: started a plain-HTTP OpenFGA with `run`, then ran the eval with **no cert** (`env -u NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS -u OPENFGA_CA_CERT OPENFGA_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:8090 …`) → **passes, 100% containment, exit 0**. The green impl-ci run on this PR is the end-to-end proof. As a bonus, CI now **runs** (not skips) the 128 OpenFGA-backed tests.

pulls.title: exhibit: label roles/endpoints per step + render HTTP request/response
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Presentation-only pass over the terminal exhibit (`pnpm exhibit`) so it reads as an annotated protocol trace. **Behavior, calls, and ordering are unchanged** — only how each step prints. Only `demo/src/exhibit.ts` changed (+175/-26).

## What's new
- **A "Cast & wire" legend** up front: Agent, AS, Payments RS, PDP, OpenFGA, ARS, RAS, SaaS RS, Transparency, and the Bob/Olivia humans — each with its endpoint and whether it's **[HTTP]** (on the wire) or **[in-process]** in this demo (D28 for the PDP, O-33 for the MCP transport).
- **A `who → who · endpoint · [HTTP|in-process]` label** at the start of every step's action, so each hop's two roles and endpoint are unmistakable.
- **`httpReq`/`httpRes` helpers** that render the real HTTP hops as wire exchanges (method, URL, key headers with long DPoP/token values redacted, `status + reason`, body): the issuance legs (`/request`, `/auth`, `/interaction/decide`, `/token`), the AROP `/transaction` initiation + poll, and lifecycle `/missions/{id}/lifecycle`. In-process hops (tool calls, PEP→PDP→OpenFGA, RAS/SaaS, catalog, evidence) are labeled with the endpoint they represent.

## Example (step 7, AROP)
```
Agent → Payments RS  tools/call send_remittance_email (base token)  [in-process MCP · O-33]
  ✗ DENY → action_approval_required
Payments RS → Agent  401-style txn-challenge (RS-signed)  [in-process]
Agent → AS  POST /transaction (initiation — challenge presented once)  [HTTP]
  → POST http://localhost:4400/transaction
    headers: authorization: DPoP <base token>; dpop: <proof>; content-type: application/json
  ← 200 OK  { transaction_authorization_id: "txa_…", expires_in: 300, interval: 5 }
Approver (Bob) → ARS  adjudicate AROP task (approve)  [in-process]
Agent → AS  POST /transaction (poll — with transaction_authorization_id)  [HTTP]
  ← 200 OK  { access_token: "<txn-token>", token_type: "DPoP", txn: … }
Agent → Payments RS  tools/call send_remittance_email (re-present txn-token)  [in-process MCP · O-33]
  ✓ PERMIT
```

## Verification
`pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `pnpm exhibit` exit 0 (verified the legend + the step-2 issuance legs and step-7 AROP hops render as clean HTTP exchanges with role/endpoint labels); **128 tests** still pass (no test imports `exhibit.ts`); `demo:trace` unaffected.

Note: the two step-2 legs show `/interaction/{uid}` as a literal placeholder (the uid isn't in the captured artifacts); every other value is a real captured wire value. Pre-existing `oidc-provider NOTICE` startup lines still appear once (they originate outside `exhibit.ts`).

pulls.title: fix(arop): conformance bugs vs txn-challenge-00 / DTR-00 drafts
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
A spec-fidelity pass diffed our AROP impl against the actual `draft-rosomakho-oauth-txn-challenge-00` and `draft-gerber-oauth-deferred-token-response-00`. The completion **model was validated** (client-driven Transaction Challenge + `transaction_authorization_id` handle; poll-by-handle is native to the txn draft, not a DTR conflation). This PR fixes the genuine deviations it found. No model change.

## Fixes
- **Challenge JWT** (`txn-challenge.ts`, both the AS and the mcp-payments copy): `typ` `txn-challenge+jwt` → **`txn-authz-challenge+jwt`** (§4.2.1); add the **REQUIRED `jti`** (§4.2.2); carry the transaction id in a **`txn` claim**, not `sub` (§4.2.2).
- **§6.2 token↔challenge binding**: the RS records the `txn` it issued a challenge for and refuses (`txn_unknown`) a presented txn-token whose `txn` was never challenged, alongside single-use replay.
- **AS `/transaction` poll liveness** (`provider.ts`): a **denied** task now returns `400 access_denied` and an **expired** handle `400 expired_token` (handle reaped) — instead of polling `authorization_pending` **forever**; pending → `400 authorization_pending`; approved → `200` token (§5.3, RFC 8628-shaped).
- **DTR** (`deferred.ts`): unknown / already-redeemed `deferral_code` → **`invalid_grant`** (§5.6), not `access_denied`.
- **Clients** (`exhibit.ts`, `demo/server.ts`): read the challenge `txn` claim; treat `400 authorization_pending` as pending and `access_denied`/`expired_token` as terminal.
- **`SPEC_VERSIONS.md`**: repin the DTR + Txn Challenge rows to the concrete `-00` drafts (datatracker URLs); correct the AROP row's stale "via Expansion" wording (D42/D46).
- **`arop.test.ts`**: correct the stale "returns 401" comment to the in-process `access_challenge` reality (O-33).

## Accepted deviations (logged separately, not fixed here)
In-process challenge transport (`access_challenge` field vs a 401 `WWW-Authenticate`, O-33), endpoint JSON-vs-form + `challenge` vs `transaction_challenge`, no `Accept-Txn-Challenge` gate, `txn_challenge_jwks_uri` injected-not-served, DTR not wired to `/token`. These go into the Spec Feedback Log direct-to-main.

## Verification
`pnpm -r typecheck` clean; **131 tests** (128 + 3: pending→400, denied→400 `access_denied`, foreign-txn→`txn_unknown`, DTR unknown/redeemed→`invalid_grant`); `pnpm exhibit` exit 0 — the challenge now shows `typ: txn-authz-challenge+jwt` with `txn`+`jti`, and the flow still PERMITs; browser JIT round-trip, `evals` (100% containment), and `demo:vendor-test` all pass.

## Follow-up (direct-to-main, after merge)
An S-entry for the real draft gap (`parameter_digest` has no home in the txn-challenge draft — our AS requires it), an entry logging the accepted deviations above, the `PLAN.md:379` "returns 401" correction, and O-3/O-4 dispositions.

pulls.title: mission-authzen + runtime: reconcile the ARAP composition (fidelity pass)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
From the ARAP + ID-JAG spec-fidelity pass. `mission-authzen` composes with the AuthZEN Access Request and Approval Profile (ARAP) under its own mission member names; the pass found the composition under-specified, and one field had no home in the profile that *owns* the approval artifact (`mission-runtime`). These edits make the composition faithful and explicit **without** renaming the deliberate mission vocabulary (`context.action_approval`, `denial_binding`, `denial_reason`).

## `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen`
1. **`approved_until` on the action-approval context** — ARAP marks it REQUIRED ("MUST NOT use the approval after this timestamp"); the profile carried only `approved_at` + a deployment max-age. Added `approved_until` (REQUIRED when `action_approval` is present); the PDP MUST NOT accept the approval past it, and the `action_approval_required` trigger now also fires when it is past `approved_until`.
2. **`access_request` shape** — the example and member definition omitted ARAP's REQUIRED **`expires_at`** and the PDP-signed **`binding_token`** while claiming the members "are the ARAP requestable-denial context" and that "this profile does not define their shape" (self-contradictory, since the example named `denial_binding`, which ARAP doesn't define). Added `expires_at` + `binding_token`; named `denial_binding` as this profile's alias for ARAP's `evaluation_id`.
3. **A "Mapping to ARAP" note** — `context.action_approval` ↔ ARAP `context.approval`; `denial_binding` ↔ `evaluation_id`; `binding_token` ↔ `binding_token`; the `action_approval_required` reason ↔ ARAP's `context.reason` value `approval_required`.

## `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime` (the coordinated owner-side edit)
mission-authzen states the runtime profile *owns* the approval artifact, but §Action-Bound Approval rule 2 defined expiry only as a **relative maximum age** — so the newly-required `approved_until` carriage member had no home. Rule 2 now also allows an absolute **`approved_until`**; the approval is fresh only before the **earlier of** `approved_at` + max-age and `approved_until`.

## Verification
Both drafts build clean (`make draft-…-mission-authzen.txt` / `…-mission-runtime.txt` → kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt OK). Source-only (generated `.txt` gitignored). No impl change here; the matching impl fixes (PDP honors `approved_until`, emits `expires_at` on `access_request`, ID-JAG `client_id`) land in the separate conformance-fix PR.

No other repo drafts need changes: the published **core** only references ARAP at a high level + defines `requires_action_approval` as a gate flag (not the wire shape); security-model/expansion reference the concepts; consent-evidence/aauth use an unrelated `approved_at`.

Draft for your review — your companions, your call on wording.

pulls.title: fix(arop/id-jag): emit/honor what the companions now require
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes the spec↔impl gap opened by PR #351 (mission-authzen + runtime now REQUIRE `approved_until`, and `access_request.expires_at`). MUST-level fixes from the ARAP + ID-JAG spec-fidelity pass; the model is unchanged.

## Fixes
- **`context.access_request` carries `expires_at`** (`pdp/evaluate.ts`, RFC 3339, `now+300s`); the `binding_token` gets a matching `exp` so the two agree.
- **`approved_until` honored end to end** — `ActionApproval`/`ActionApprovalInput` gain it; PDP step 8 refuses `action_approval_required` when `now > approved_until` (on top of the max-age + digest checks); `deriveApprovalFromTxnToken` passes the txn-token's `approval.approved_until` through.
- **ARS approval-state JWS carries `iss` + `aud`** (`access-request`, ARAP MUST); constructor takes `issuer` + `approvalAudience`, threaded from composeStack.
- **ID-JAG grant carries the REQUIRED `client_id`** (`cross-domain.ts`, draft-04 §3.1); `IssueGrantInput` gains `clientId` (`ap-agent` in the demo).
- **`SPEC_VERSIONS.md`** repinned: ARAP → `openid/authzen PR #508` blob; ID-JAG → `-04`, with the new surfaces noted.

## Accepted deviation
The RAS doesn't enforce ID-JAG client-match (no registered-client model there; `cnf.jkt` binds instead). The `client_id` claim is present per the draft; the RAS enforcement gap is logged as **S-12** (direct-to-main).

## Verification
`pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` clean; **134 tests** (131 + 3: `access_request.expires_at` present + RFC3339; approval past `approved_until` → deny; ID-JAG grant carries `client_id`). `pnpm exhibit` exit 0 — the txn-token carries `approved_until` and step 7 still PERMITs; `evals` + `demo:vendor-test` pass.

## Follow-up (direct-to-main, after merge)
**S-12** (RAS client-model, accepted) + **S-16** (single-use layering: the cross-domain companion tightens ID-JAG's MAY-resubmit to one-time), and move **O-10 / O-19** to resolved. Pairs with #351 (merged).

pulls.title: feat(arop/dtr): wire the deferred grant onto the real /token endpoint
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Wires the AROP **Deferred Token Response (DTR)** deferred grant onto the **real** node-oidc-provider `/token` endpoint. Closes the O-3 residual — DTR was implemented only in `DeferralStore` (kernel) and unreachable over the wire; the sibling txn-challenge binding already had its real `/transaction` endpoint.

## How

- **`registerGrantType(urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:deferred)`** — keeps the token endpoint's client-auth + DPoP machinery (vs. a hand-rolled route).
- **Redemption mints a real token, not opaque**: constructs an `AccessToken` with a `ResourceServer` (so it's a JWT, `aud`=resource), DPoP-sender-constrained (`cnf.jkt` derived from the request proof), TTL clamped by `approved_until`, carrying the **active Mission unchanged (D42)** via `grantId` → the existing `extraTokenClaims` hook. Error codes map to the provider's built-in `AuthorizationPending`/`SlowDown`/`ExpiredToken`/`AccessDenied`/`InvalidGrant`.
- **Backoff (`deferred.ts`)**: `redeem()` now returns `expired_token` past the advertised 600s lifetime and `slow_down` (RFC 8628, advertises `interval+5`) on too-fast polls — a real gap; before, it pended forever.

## Deviation (logged)

DTR's initiation lives on the *originating* grant (`completion_mode=deferred`), which node-oidc-provider can't conditionally defer without wrapping a built-in grant. Initiation is therefore **folded into the deferred grant type** (`deferred_authorization` → 400 `authorization_pending` + `deferral_code`); responses stay DTR-shaped. Noted in `SPEC_VERSIONS.md`.

## Test

New `dtr-endpoint.test.ts` (real HTTP) proves the redeemed token is a real resource-bound DPoP JWT — JWKS-verified with `aud` + `mission.id` + `cnf.jkt` + `exp ≤ approved_until` + RAR subset — plus single-use (`invalid_grant`), deny (`access_denied`), and expiry (`expired_token`).

## Gate

`pnpm -r typecheck` clean · `pnpm test` 101 passed (+4 new) · `pnpm exhibit` exit 0 (new step 8 "AROP over DTR") · evals 100% containment · `demo:vendor-test` all axes denied.

## Follow-up (direct-to-main after merge)

Resolve **O-3** in PLAN.md; log the folded-initiation and derivation double-count (latent — no `max_derivations` configured) as S-entries.

pulls.title: fix(arop/dtr): count each AROP DTR redemption once (O-36)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Fixes **O-36**: an AROP Deferred Token Response redemption double-counted derivations. `DeferralStore.redeem()` called `kernel.gateDerivation()` (active/cap check **+** `derivation_count` increment), and then `extraTokenClaims` gated again at mint time (via `grant_id`) — so `derivation_count` incremented **twice** per redemption.

Latent today (no `max_derivations` is configured in `config/`/`demo/`/`evals/`), but a capped mission would spend two derivations per AROP redemption and hit `derivation_cap_exhausted` a redemption early.

## Fix

- `redeem()` now does a **read-only** active check (`kernel.get` + `applyExpiry` — the same pattern `open()` already uses) and refuses a non-active Mission with `access_denied`. It no longer gates/increments.
- `extraTokenClaims` remains the **single authoritative gate** (active/cap check + one increment) at mint.

## Test

`dtr-endpoint.test.ts` case 10 asserts `derivation_count` increments **exactly once** per redemption (and that `open()` doesn't move it). Verified genuine: it fails `expected 2 to be 1` against the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.

## Gate

`pnpm -r typecheck` clean · `pnpm test` 102 passed (+1) · `pnpm exhibit` exit 0.

## Follow-up

On merge, move **O-36** to resolved in PLAN.md direct-to-main.

pulls.title: feat(evals): LLM-driven red-team mode (O-31), replay-first, opt-in
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Adds an **optional LLM-driven red-team mode** to `evals/` (O-31): an attacker agent that actively tries to escape mission bounds, complementing the deterministic scripted suite.

Per **D24 the LLM mode is optional and does NOT gate CI** — the deterministic `pnpm evals` suite stays the gate. `evals/src/run.ts` and `scripts/evals.mjs` are **byte-identical** (0-line diff) and the `evals` package script is unchanged.

## Design (pressure-tested)

- **Independent bounds oracle** — `oracleExpect` is a pure function of the seeded store + `EVAL_VIEW_AUTHORITY`, importing **nothing** from `@mission/pdp`. We never ask the PDP to grade itself; the oracle is the ground truth, and the seed replay test independently asserts the real PDP agrees with it on every case.
- **Attacker action space restricted to `{tool, args}`** against a fixed in-bounds token. Token forgery / authority tampering / TOCTOU are already covered deterministically in `suites.ts` and are exactly where a sloppy oracle produces false breaches.
- **`expect` from the oracle, not blanket deny**, and a **separate red-team scorecard** — `breach = oracle-deny attack that produced a side effect`; `passed = breaches === 0`.
- **Replay-first**: a committed 9-attack seed fixture + a key-free replay path; the live `@anthropic-ai/sdk` generator (dynamically imported) layers on top, opt-in via `--live` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Tests (non-vacuous)

`evals/test/redteam.test.ts`: 7 oracle unit tests; **2 key-free `scoreRedTeam` tests that construct a breach and assert `passed === false`** (proving the detector isn't vacuous); 1 live-OpenFGA replay of the committed seed asserting zero breaches, correct bucket classification, and `outcome === oracle` for all 9 attacks.

## Run it

```
pnpm evals:redteam          # replay the seed, key-free, deterministic
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... pnpm evals:redteam --live   # generate live attacks
```

## Known limitations (documented, benign under the current authority)

1. Breach detection is ledger-only (`Connectors.sendEmail` writes to a separate `outbox`), so a *permitted* remittance wouldn't register — moot, `remittance.send` is ungranted.
2. No scorecard bucket for oracle-deny + permit + no-side-effect — can't occur under the current authority; the replay test's `outcome === oracle` assertion would catch it.

## Gate

typecheck clean · lint clean · `pnpm test` 149 passed / 0 skipped (+10, dev CA set) · `pnpm evals` (D24) unchanged · `evals:redteam` replay breaches:0 · `pnpm exhibit` exit 0.

## Follow-up

On merge: move **O-31** to resolved in PLAN.md direct-to-main (LLM red-team mode shipped; replay fixture is the comparability mechanism; feeding findings into new deterministic cases remains the ongoing use).

pulls.title: feat(apps): UI pass on the reference consoles (richer rendering + states + design)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

A UI pass on the three `apps/*` React consoles (approver / operator / agent-console), treated as **production-shaped reference code**. They stay **unbuilt by design** — `demo/src/server.ts` states the runnable surface is `demo/public/index.html` ("no per-app Vite build"), so this adds **no** `index.html`, `vite.config`, or `tsconfig`.

## Substance (grounded, not cosmetic)

The operator and agent-console apps had local interfaces that **dropped fields the BFF actually sends** — so the fix is rendering real data, not invented:

- **operator** — local `FleetRow`/`TimelineRow` omitted `version`, `approver`, `predecessor`, and the evidence `digest`. Now mirrors `console-bff` exactly and renders them: mission lineage (`predecessor`), approver, version on fleet rows; digest on timeline rows. State badges are tone-coded per `status#legal-transitions`.
- **agent-console** — was rendering only `display_name` + status. Now shows the service `type`, the connection **binding** (`authorization_code` / `token_exchange` / `id_jag`), categories/tags, and a **request-access link** when not connected.
- **approver** — no richer data is available (the BFF's `approverQueue` is type-narrowed to `{id, mission_id, action, subject}`), so this is honestly **states + styling** only.
- **all three** — loading / error / empty states (they previously did a bare `useEffect().then(setX)` that blanked silently on a 5xx); a cohesive **theme-aware** (`prefers-color-scheme`) co-located stylesheet; disabled buttons while a write is in flight.

## Validation — and an honest gate note

`apps/*` are **outside the repo's gates by design**: there is **no `@types/react` anywhere** in the repo (so the *original* files were never type-checkable either), no per-app `tsconfig`/`typecheck` script, and biome lints only `packages/**`+`scripts/**`. I deliberately did **not** add build tooling to force them into the gate.

So instead of "typecheck clean," the honest validation is:
- **esbuild transpile** of all three files — parse/JSX clean.
- Careful review; interfaces mirror the verified BFF shapes.
- Standard gate **unaffected** (apps are leaf SPAs imported by nothing): `pnpm -r typecheck` Done, `pnpm test` 149 passed, `pnpm exhibit` exit 0.

## Not done (deliberately)

Making the apps buildable/runnable (index.html + main.tsx + vite.config per app) — that would contradict the documented "no per-app Vite build" decision and add three untested build targets. If desired, that's a separate call.

pulls.title: feat(harness): mission harness increment 1 — real MCP channel + no-bypass proof
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

**Increment 1 of the mission harness** — realizes the `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness` profile's **two duties** over a *real* `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` channel. Additive: existing direct-PEP callers, the scripted demo runner, and the D24 evals gate are untouched.

This is the framework-independent, key-free centerpiece: **the mediated MCP channel + a proof that no tool path bypasses the PEP.** The LLM agent loop (AI SDK) is Increment 2.

## The two duties

- **Duty 2 — mediated execution environment (no bypass):** a real MCP `Server` (SDK `1.29.0`, `InMemoryTransport`) whose `tools/list` + `tools/call` delegate to the unchanged `McpPaymentsServer`/PEP. The mission credential — a real ES256-signed mission access token — crosses **in** the MCP request under a namespaced `_meta` key and is validated server-side (new `validateMissionToken`: sig / iss / aud / mission / `cnf.jkt`) into `TokenFacts`. A bare `TokenFacts` is never accepted over the wire; this finally gives the payments PEP a real MCP transport (advances **O-33**).
- **Duty 1 — fail-closed resume:** `resumeGuard` composes the existing `checkOnResume`; `MediatedHarness.callTool`/`listTools` refuse before touching the channel when the mission isn't active.

## No-bypass proof (`mcp-channel.test.ts`, live OpenFGA)

- `tools/list` over MCP is mission-scoped — ungranted tools absent.
- In-authority call permits, commits exactly one ledger entry, records decision + execution evidence.
- Four adversarial inputs (over-cap, wrong-vendor, ungranted tool, unknown mission) each run on a **fresh direct-PEP stack AND the MCP stack** and asserted to enforce **identically** (same verdict + reason), with **zero ledger side effects** and a matching deny/refusal record.
- A **tampered credential** and a **raw client with no `_meta`** are both refused at the channel (`invalid_credential`) with **zero PEP contact** — the credential is required to cross in.

## Documented simplification (Increment-2 carry-forward)

`validateMissionToken` skips **live DPoP proof-of-possession** — the in-process transport has no HTTP request to bind `htu`/`htm` to. It's a *separate* public method from the full `validateToken`; a real HTTP transport must use the latter. Flagged in the method doc.

## Gate

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` OK · `pnpm -r typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm test` **162 passed** (+13, +2 files) · `pnpm evals` (D24) unchanged · `pnpm exhibit` exit 0.

## Next (Increment 2, opt-in / needs a key)

The AI SDK agent loop as the reference harness binding, connecting to this mediated channel; Claude Agent SDK notes as the MCP/EMA-native alternative. Plus, on merge, an O-33 disposition + a mission-harness log entry in PLAN.md direct-to-main.

pulls.title: feat(harness): increment 2 — opt-in AI SDK agent loop on the mediated channel
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

**Increment 2 of the mission harness** — an opt-in **Vercel AI SDK** agent loop on top of increment 1's mediated MCP channel. The AI SDK is the **planner**; `MediatedHarness` stays the **only** tool path, so both harness duties still hold on every action (duty 2 no-bypass via the MCP channel + PEP; duty 1 fail-closed resume).

This is the "swap the planner, keep the channel" story: because the payments PEP is a real MCP server (increment 1), the agent framework is just a client. LangGraph was ruled out (its checkpointer would copy Mission state into engine state, which the draft forbids); the Claude Agent SDK is the MCP/EMA-native alternative but runs its loop in a subprocess — so the AI SDK (fully in-process, widest reach) is the reference binding.

## How

- `agent-loop.ts` — `runAgentLoop` builds AI SDK tools by selecting the mission-**granted** names (`harness.listTools`) from a fixed 4-tool `{invoice_id}` Zod map; each tool's `execute` delegates to `harness.callTool` (never the PEP/store directly); `generateText` with `stepCountIs`. The model is **injected** (imports `ai`, never a provider) — real Anthropic live, mock in tests.
- `demo/src/agent-run.ts` + `scripts/agent.mjs` — the opt-in live runner (`pnpm agent`), mirroring `evals:redteam`: composes the stack, issues a **real** DPoP mission token via `issueMissionToken`, and prints a transcript. With **no key** it prints a hint and exits 0.

## Key-free CI deliverable (`agent-loop.test.ts`, MockLanguageModelV3, live OpenFGA)

The planner is a mock that scripts "a tool call, then a final text" — no API key. Four assertions prove it cannot escape the channel:
- **(a) adversarial** — an out-of-bounds plan (`inv-2`, $900 > $500 cap) is **denied** (`constraint_exceeded`) with the connectors ledger **unchanged (0)**.
- **(b) in-authority** — an under-cap Acme wire **permits** with exactly **one** ledger entry (guards against a deny-everything false pass).
- **(c) non-active mission** — `resumeGuard` fails closed **before** the channel is touched (spy channel `calls === []`; direct call → `mission_not_active:revoked`).
- **(d) least exposure** — the toolset handed to the model excludes the ungranted `send_remittance_email`/`schedule_payment`.

## Verified against the installed package (not recall)

pulls.author: mcguinness

## The bug you hit

`pnpm demo:serve` crashes with `ENOENT ... demo/public/index.html` on a fresh checkout of main.

**Root cause:** `demo/public/index.html` is the hand-authored interactive dashboard (the runnable UI, served by `demo/src/server.ts`). The repo-root `.gitignore` has a blanket **`*.html`** rule — meant to ignore *built* draft HTML (`draft-mcguinness-*.html` from the I-D toolchain) — which also matched the dashboard, so it was **never committed**. It only existed in local checkouts where it had been created.

## Fix

- A scoped `!demo/public/index.html` negation in `src/.gitignore` (documents that this HTML is a real source asset, not a build output).
- Commit the file (`git add -f`). Once tracked, `.gitignore` no longer hides edits to it.

Verified: the file now stages/tracks, it's the complete dashboard, and it's the only served HTML affected. No code changed — this is purely the missing static asset + the gitignore carve-out.

## What

Two demo-only improvements to the console (`demo/src/server.ts` + `demo/public/index.html`), from your two asks. No enforcement/protocol change — contracts only extended.

### 1. Richer activity log
Each entry now reads like:
```
Execute wire transfer · inv-1 acme $125.00 → PERMIT · mission msn_… · execution committed
Execute wire transfer · inv-2 acme $900.00 → DENY: Exceeds a mission constraint (constraint_exceeded) · mission msn_…
```
A server `stepDetail()` derives `{target:{invoice,vendor,amount}, outcome, evidence, reason}` from data already in the response (vendor/amount via a direct store read, not through the PEP), and a single UI `renderStep()` renders it (human tool + reason names via the #361 label map). No fragile global observer hook.

### 2. One-click "Run mission" (autonomous)
A **"Run mission"** button runs the mission for you instead of clicking each action. `POST /agent/run` is a **deterministic** planner (not key-gated — the LLM path stays in `pnpm agent`): it attempts to pay each seeded invoice through the PEP, so the containment story tells itself —
- inv-1 (acme, $125) → **executes**
- inv-2 (acme, $900) → **denies** (over cap)
- inv-3 (globex, $50) → **denies** (out of vendor)
- then the JIT-gated remittance → **pauses at the approval gate** (opens the ARS task, enables the existing Retry button — "approve in the Approver console, then Retry"). It doesn't hang or hide the gate.

It returns steps in the same shape a single action uses, so both render through the one `renderStep` path.

## Verified (mine, on free ports)

- **First `/agent/run` (fresh):** inv-1 `PERMIT [executed]`, inv-2 `DENY constraint_exceeded`, inv-3 `DENY out_of_authority`, remittance `PAUSED [awaiting approval]` with a task id.
- **Second `/agent/run` (same server):** sane — inv-1 → `permit_consumed` (the single-use-permit property), JIT re-pauses, HTTP 200 (no crash). This was the advisor-flagged failure mode; it behaves correctly.
- Enriched `/agent/act` (wire + read) carries target/outcome/evidence; `/agent/act`, `/agent/retry`, `/agent/mission`, `/labels` contracts intact.
- Gate green: typecheck, lint, `pnpm test` 166, evals; exhibit exit 0 on a free AS port (its "fail" was just your running server holding 4400).
