pulls.title: feat(demo): async mission approval on Approver tab + polling + rich context
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Reworks the demo approval flow (3 demo files) so mission issuance is an **async approval on the Approver tab**, both approvals **poll**, and the Approver tab has **real context**. No enforcement/protocol change.

### Async mission approval (no more headless auto-approve)
- `issueMissionToken` is split at its `decide` step: `submitMissionApproval` (PAR→authorize→uid, no decide) / `completeMissionApproval` (approve→token) / `denyMissionApproval` (decide-deny so the AS interaction settles).
- **Submit routes to approval**: `/agent/submit` parks a pending mission approval and returns `{pending, approvalId, derived}` — the mission is **not** issued and does **not** appear in the fleet until an approver approves it. The UI switches to the **Approver tab** on submit.
- Approving it there completes issuance and swaps it in as the agent's active mission.

### Polling (both, with stop conditions)
- **Mission**: polls `/agent/approval-status` until active / denied / timeout.
- **JIT**: polls `/agent/retry` until executed / denied / timeout instead of a manual click (Retry stays as a fallback). Both pollers clear their interval on every path; an in-flight JIT poll aborts if the active mission changed (server also `txnHandles.clear()`s on swap, so a stale retry can't execute against a new mission).

### Richer approver context
Each queue entry is `{id, type:"mission"|"jit", subject, context}` — a mission shows goal + derived authority; a JIT shows action (human label) · invoice · amount · vendor · parameter-digest · mission.

## Verified (mine, curl on free ports — the async flow no test covers)

- **submit → pending**, fleet **unchanged**, queue shows the mission with `goal` + narrowed `derived` (vendors → acme).
- **approve → status `active`** + missionId, mission **now in the fleet**.
- **Submit twice before approving** (the jar-keying failure mode): two distinct approvals → two distinct missions, each carrying **its own** intent's authority — `read-only → [invoice.read]`, `full → [invoice.read, payment.execute]`. No jar corruption.
- Deny settles the interaction (not left dangling; not in fleet). typecheck / lint / `pnpm test` 166 / evals / exhibit green; scope is the 3 demo files only.

## Still open (your call)

The **label** item — I didn't include a guess (the advisor's caution: a wrong label guess would ship inside this PR you merge on trust). Tell me which labels you meant (the terse "wire/read" **buttons** → human names, or something still raw = likely a stale server) and I'll fold it in.

## To see it
`git pull`, restart `pnpm demo:serve`, hard-refresh → Mission tab → **Submit for approval** → it jumps to the Approver tab; approve there and watch it go active (no clicking Retry).

pulls.title: feat(harness): increment 3 — real HTTP MCP transport with DPoP proof-of-possession
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

**Harness increment 3** — a real HTTP MCP transport for the payments RS with **DPoP proof-of-possession enforced**. This closes the one honest simplification I flagged shipping increments 1–2: the in-memory channel skips PoP (no HTTP request to bind `htu`/`htm` to), so "sender-constrained" was asserted, not enforced. Over HTTP, **the token alone no longer suffices — possession must be proven per request**.

Additive: the in-memory channel and its no-bypass test are **untouched** (two transports, one PEP); the demo/exhibit are **not** rewired (in-memory stays the demo default).

## How

- **Server** (`mcp-http-transport.ts`): hosts the SDK's `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` behind a **DPoP-auth middleware** that gates *every* HTTP request (initialize / tools/list / tools/call) — it reads `Authorization: DPoP <token>` + the `DPoP` proof, reconstructs the canonical `htu` (origin+pathname, query stripped) + `htm`, and runs the **existing** `validateToken` (full PoP: proof key thumbprint == token `cnf.jkt`, `htu`/`htm` bound) → `req.auth` → handlers call the same PEP methods. 401 before dispatch on any failure.
- **Client**: `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` with a custom `fetch` that stamps `Authorization: DPoP <token>` + a **fresh DPoP proof per request** (verified the SDK routes `initialize` and every send through it).

## The assertions that earn this increment

`mcp-http-channel.test.ts` (real HTTP, ephemeral port, live OpenFGA — 7 tests, all run):
- **Happy path succeeds** — a valid DPoP-bound in-authority call permits + one ledger entry + evidence (so the canonical `htu` isn't accidentally passing for the wrong reason).
- **Parity** with the direct PEP on adversarial calls; **tools/list** mission-scoped.
- **Discriminating (reject *before* the PEP):**
  - **token-without-proof / bearer** — a valid token with no `DPoP` proof (and the Bearer scheme) → **401**, the SDK bearer client can't even `initialize`, **zero evidence + zero ledger**; then a valid DPoP client on the *same* server permits (non-vacuous). In increment 1 the token alone sufficed via `_meta`; here it doesn't.
  - **mismatched key** — a well-formed proof signed by a key whose thumbprint ≠ `cnf.jkt` → **401** before the PEP, same non-vacuous check.

## Verified (mine)

HTTP test 7 passed (twice, stable); `pnpm test` **173 / 0 skipped** (new HTTP tests ran); typecheck / lint / evals / exhibit green. `validateToken` and the in-memory transport/test are unchanged.

## Deviation

Two `as unknown as Transport` casts at the SDK `connect()` boundaries — the SDK's transport classes declare `onclose`/`sessionId` as `T | undefined` against their own interface under this repo's `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. Variance-only, runtime-safe.

## After merge (direct-to-main)

O-33's disposition updated (PoP-over-transport now closed for the HTTP path) and D47's carry-forward clause amended.

pulls.title: feat(harness): scope statement + channel-class enumeration + status-continuity binding
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Completes the mission harness additively, on top of the already-shipped duty-1 (`checkOnResume`) and duty-2 (mediated MCP channel). Draft: `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness` (pin `dc7a897`).

## What lands

**Shared types — `packages/mission-core/src/binding.ts`** (owned in the service-dep-free core so Orchestration / Status List / Signals reuse ONE vocabulary rather than each redefining it):
- `StateSource` — the shared, string-open `state_source` value space (`status | signal | runtime_decision | harness | operator | ...`).
- `MissionStatusLease` — `{ state, status_checked_at, status_expires_at, version?, state_source }`: the one status shape the harness consumes and Status List / Signals produce.
- `StopPolicy` (`suppress | pause | terminate | handoff`) and `MissionBinding` (§mission-binding object; `stop_policy` REQUIRED). Only `suppress` is realized (the harness's no-dispatch behavior); the rest are declared-but-unimplemented.

**Execution-environment scope statement — `services/agent/src/harness-scope.ts`** (@spec `harness#mediated-egress`):
- Channel-class enum (DNS, log/error, shared stores, shared vector stores, spawned OS processes, provider model context, inference API, remote-ref rendering) with a per-class disposition (`mediated | excluded | outside_claim`).
- `buildScopeStatement(config)` gates completeness by claim level: a config that CLAIMS trifecta / agent-compromise-resistant containment MUST enumerate every channel class (and name >=1 mediated action class) or is rejected; a single-process (`in_memory` transport) config is downgraded to the honest "no mediation claim" form (`requested_containment_claim` records the downgrade). Completeness is a MUST only in the containment branch; SHOULD otherwise.
- `signScopeStatement` / `verifyScopeStatement` (JCS via `@mission/core` + `jose` ES256, mirroring the transparency evidence convention). NOTE: the draft says MUST *publish*, not MUST *sign* — signing only makes a published statement verifiable; SPEC_VERSIONS states this.

**Status-continuity binding** (@spec `harness#resume-algorithm`, step 5):
- `checkStatusContinuity(lease, now)` composes IN FRONT of `checkOnResume`: fails closed once `now > status_expires_at` EVEN IF the last state was `active` (the "22:00 checked / 22:05 expired, resume at 02:00 refused" example). Session continuity is not authority continuity.
- New `createStatusMediatedHarness(server, missionId, readStatus, now?)` factory / optional 4th `MediatedHarness` ctor arg re-checks lease freshness at EACH `callTool`/`listTools` submission (fresh-at-submission, not only at resume). Stale refusals carry `mission_status_stale:` vs the existing `mission_not_active:`.

## Tests
- `services/agent/test/harness-scope.test.ts` (new): full enumeration under a compromise-resistant claim; sign/verify round-trip + tampered-statement rejection; in-memory downgrade to the honest no-claim form; containment claim that omits a class / names no action class is rejected.
- `services/agent/test/mediated-harness.test.ts`: a NEW `describe` (stale-lease fail-closed even when active; within-window active proceeds; no-lease suppression). The existing duty-1 `describe` and `spyChannel` helper are byte-identical — that they stay green is the additivity proof.

## Deviations (all backward-compatible)
- **`MediatedHarness` gained an OPTIONAL 4th constructor arg** (`MediatedHarnessOptions`). The task said "signatures UNCHANGED"; every existing 3-arg call site (demo `createMediatedHarness`, the duty-1 tests) compiles and behaves identically — which is what the constraint protects. `checkOnResume` and `createMediatedHarness` are untouched.
- **`ResumeDecision` gained an optional `stale?: boolean`** field (exported interface). Backward-compatible; it keeps the existing `mission_not_active:revoked` string intact while giving the stale path its own reason.
- **`@mission/core` added to `services/agent`** deps + tsconfig references (mirrors `authorization-server`); `pnpm-lock.yaml` moved accordingly.
- Signing beyond the draft's publish MUST (see above), recorded in SPEC_VERSIONS Notes.

## Deferred (named, not built)
Signed Harness Evidence + transparency registration + harness key publication; session-taint / egress-downgrade (taint policy carried only as an opaque pass-through); discovery-bound channels entering the enumeration at binding; multi-entry per-mediated-action-class statements; queue-item/expiry; sub-agent stop propagation; the harness execution-state machine.

## Gate (all green)
`docker compose up -d`; `pnpm -r typecheck`; `pnpm lint`; `pnpm test` (181 passed, +8 new; existing duty-1 tests green unmodified); `pnpm evals` (100% containment, zero evidence gaps); `pnpm exhibit` (complete).

pulls.title: feat(status): Mission Status List (draft-ietf-oauth-status-list -21)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Profiles **draft-ietf-oauth-status-list -21** as constrained by `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-status` §status-list. First of the two-feature status pipeline; Mission Signals will subscribe to the `onLifecycleCommit` seam next.

## Wire shape — Status List Token (`kernel/status-list.ts`)
- **Header:** `{ typ: "statuslist+jwt", alg: "ES256", kid: <as-status> }`
- **Payload:** `{ iss, sub (== list uri), iat, exp, ttl, status_list: { bits: 2, lst } }`
- `lst` = 2-bit entries packed **LSB-first** within each byte, **ZLIB**-compressed (`zlib.deflateSync`, RFC 1950 framing — not `deflateRaw`), base64url.
- **state → bit:** `active` → `0x00` VALID; `suspended` → `0x02` SUSPENDED; every terminal state (`revoked`/`expired`/`completed`/`superseded`/`cascaded`, via `TERMINAL_STATES` so future terminals flow through) → `0x01` INVALID; `0x03` reserved/never emitted.
- **Consumer helpers:** `verifyStatusListToken(jws, jwks, {uri?, now?})` (sig, `typ`, `sub == uri`, `iat`/`exp`); `readStatus(token, idx, now?)` → `active` (VALID within `exp`) / `non-active` (anything else, unknown index, or expired list — never fabricates a specific terminal state). `readStatusBit` exposes the raw wire value.

## The shared commit seam (Mission Signals subscribes next)
`KernelOptions.onLifecycleCommit?(commit: LifecycleCommit): void`, where

```ts
LifecycleCommit = { id, issuer, prior_state?, state, version, committed_at, expires_at, successor? }
```

Fired **once per committed transition** from the three real commit funnels — `setState()` (covers `transition()` + `applyExpiry()`), `supersedeOnRedemption()` (the raw UPDATE that bypasses setState → emits `superseded` + `successor`), and `insertRecord()` (the activating event: `version:1`, no `prior_state`; shared by `approve()` and expansion). The provider `/lifecycle` idempotent no-op returns before setState, so it does not fire. Every commit is built from the **post-UPDATE persisted row** (re-`get(id)`), not the in-memory spread, because `transition()` discards `applyExpiry()`'s return and the spread `version` can be off by one. The Status List republisher (`StatusListPublisher`) subscribes by marking its cached token dirty (flag cleared before the async sign, so a transition committing mid-sign is not lost).

## Anti-oracle (draft §mission-status-anti-oracle)
`missions.status_list_idx INTEGER UNIQUE` (nullable; participants only). The index is **random**, drawn into a list sized well above the population (`1<<17`), persisted UNIQUE and retried on collision — never sequential, never derivable from `mission_id`. `allocateStatusIndex` is injected so tests are deterministic. Enrollment is restricted to **active** Missions, so a fresh participant's VALID bit matches the unallocated default and a list cached before enrollment still reads that index correctly (enrolling a non-active Mission would publish VALID for it until an unrelated transition republished — a fail-open). `status_list: { idx, uri }` rides `signedStatus` and `introspectionMission`. The whole-list route is **deliberately unauthenticated** (`GET /statuslist/:listId`, `Content-Type: application/statuslist+jwt`): the fetch covers every opaque index at once and reveals no per-mission interest.

## Two latent bug fixes
1. The status-list enumerator applies expiry **across the set** (raw `allMissions()` skips `applyExpiry`, so it would publish VALID for an already-expired Mission).
2. `supersedeOnRedemption` transitions are now reflected (via the hook; the enumerator re-reads rows).

## Test (`test/status-list.test.ts`, deterministic — drives `now` + `allocateStatusIndex`)
- Non-sequential injected allocator → distinct indices, **not** creation/sorted order (anti-oracle guard); `status_list` surfaces on introspection.
- Publish → `jwtVerify` against the as-status public JWK: `typ == statuslist+jwt`, `sub == mission uri`, `bits == 2`; inflate → every participant reads `0x00`.
- Revoke one, suspend one, **advance the clock past a third's expiry** → republish → bits `0x01`/`0x02`/`0x01` (the expiry case guards the applyExpiry-enumerator fix; still-active stay `0x00`).
- `readStatus` consult: VALID→active; INVALID/SUSPENDED/reserved `0x03`/unknown/expired→non-active.
- Active-only enrollment guard: `participateInStatusList` on a revoked Mission throws.

## Scope
Additive in `services/authorization-server` + the new test. Wiring the consult into live `pep.loadView`/PDP is **deferred** (helper + test prove the path). Signals (the SET push) is **not** implemented — only the clean `onLifecycleCommit` seam is left for it.

Notes for Signals / reviewers:
- Lazy expiry means a status read/publish can itself emit an `expired` commit (existing `applyExpiry`-on-read design), so subscribers should expect `expired` commits originating from a status-list fetch.
- Observed, out of scope: `transition()` discards `applyExpiry()`'s return, so on an already-expired Mission `setState`'s terminal check reads the stale in-memory state and can walk `expired` → `revoked`. Pre-existing, unrelated to the two fixes above; the commit hook is unaffected because it always re-reads the persisted row.

## Gate (all green)
`pnpm -r typecheck` ✓ · `pnpm lint` ✓ (exit 0) · `pnpm test` → **178 passed / 27 files, 0 skipped** (+1 file / +5 tests from this PR) · `pnpm evals` ✓ (exit 0, 100% containment) · `pnpm exhibit` ✓ (exit 0).

**Reproducing the live-test run:** all worktrees produce compose project name `src`, so they share one `src-openfga-1` container. It currently serves a cert generated by a different worktree, so a fresh `src/certs/openfga.crt` fails TLS (`DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT`) and the live suites skip / `pnpm evals` (which hard-sets `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=${cwd}/certs/openfga.crt`) errors. The green run above was taken after aligning `src/certs/openfga.crt` to the served cert (SHA1 `1A:4B:FF:FF:10:CB…`) and exporting `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`/`OPENFGA_CA_CERT` to it. If the live suites skip on re-run, that is the OpenFGA cert mismatch, not this change (the new status-list test is a pure kernel test and always runs).

pulls.title: feat(attenuation): offline AAT-chain mission attenuation
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Implements **draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-attenuation** (pin `eb568f5`): **holder-side, offline, macaroon-caveat-style narrowing** of an already-issued Mission-bound token via an **Attenuating Agent Token (AAT) JWS chain**. Not an AS re-issuance, not a new Mission. Three phases:

- **Root** (AS-minted): a Mission-bound JWT carrying an `attenuating_agent_token` RAR detail whose `tools` are **derived from the Mission Authority Set**; `iss == mission.issuer`, `del_depth: 0`, explicit `del_max_depth`, `cnf`, `aud`.
- **Child** (holder-minted, offline, no AS): narrower `tools`, `del_depth+1`, `par_hash = base64url(SHA-256(parent JWS Signing Input))`, `mission` carried unchanged, signed under the parent `cnf` key.
- **Consumer/PEP verify**: chain signatures + `par_hash` linkage + capability monotonicity + identical `mission` across the chain + root under AS keys + aud/exp nesting + PoP; the kill switch (Mission `active` on every presentation) is the **existing PEP→PDP state gate**, not reimplemented.

## The two subset relations

- **root ⊆ Authority Set** — `deriveAttenuationRoot` reverse-maps a requested narrowing to `AuthorityEntry[]` and reuses the issuance profile's `isSubsetSet` (read-only import; `derive.ts`/`types.ts` untouched).
- **child ⊆ parent** — `toolsSubset` in `@mission/core`, a `tools`-map comparator (NOT `isSubsetSet`): a child may drop a tool or tighten a constraint, never add a tool, loosen, or drop a parent constraint.

## The mapping layer (where correctness lives)

`kernel/attenuation.ts` `mapAuthorityToTools` / `mapToolsToAuthority`: tool-id ↔ `(resource, action)` via the shared `aatToolId`/`parseAatToolId` primitives; `max_amount` ↔ `amount_<ccy>` (range), `vendors` ↔ `vendor` (enum). **Currency is synthesized from the arg name** (`amount_usd` → `USD`) so `isSubsetEntry`'s currency hard-fail is meaningful on the reverse map. The mapping is **TOTAL and FAIL-CLOSED**: an unrecognized constraint or argument name is rejected, never silently dropped.

## Leaf-authority enforcement (reusing `out_of_authority`)

`validateAttenuationChain` (mcp-payments `server.ts`) verifies the chain and produces `TokenFacts` whose effective authority is the **leaf's** narrowed tools (`leafAuthority`). The PEP guard denies an action **inside the Mission but outside the leaf** by reusing the existing `out_of_authority` `DenialReason` — **no new union value, no `EvaluationRequest` change**. The guard precedes the PDP call, so this denial needs no OpenFGA (the PDP `out_of_authority` short-circuit is only reachable with FGA). Crypto hygiene: children are verified under the exact key the parent `cnf` commits to; a header `jwk` carrying private material is rejected; every `jwtVerify` pins `ES256`; `par_hash` is computed over the sliced wire bytes.

## Deferrals (recorded here, not in code)

- **Delegation gap.** `AuthorityEntry` has no `delegation` member, so §root-mapping bullet 3 (non-delegable-by-default → `del_max_depth: 0`) cannot be derived. Resolution for this PR: `del_max_depth` is an **explicit input** to `deriveAttenuationRoot`; `types.ts`/`derive.ts` are left untouched. The per-entry `delegation` policy + the `del_max_depth`-derivation rule are deferred (will log to PLAN §8 after merge).
- **Leaf constraint enforcement.** The PEP guard is **action-level**: if a leaf narrows `amount_usd` 500→200, a $300 call still passes because the PDP checks the Mission's 500. Leaf *constraint* enforcement at the PEP is deferred; the chain verifier already enforces constraint monotonicity along the chain.

## Out of scope

Unifying the AAT `par_hash` chain with the issuance profile's `act` (actor-chain) delegation chain — the AAT chain stays in `@mission/core`. No edits to `derive.ts` (read-only import), `actor-chain`, the PDP `EvaluationRequest`/`DenialReason`, or the demo. The `mission_attenuation_root` request param is declared in the draft but **not wired** through the token path here (metadata advertises `mission_attenuation_supported` only). The AAT substrate (`draft-niyikiza-oauth-attenuating-agent-tokens`) is external + in-progress; added to SPEC_VERSIONS "Adopted for planning" with no fabricated revision.

## Test assertions

- `packages/mission-core/test/attenuation-chain.test.ts` (**pure, keyless, always runs**): `toolsSubset` positives/negatives; a valid chain returns the leaf; **attenuate-WIDEN rejected by the verifier** (child raises the cap; grandchild re-adds a dropped tool); mission re-bind, `exp` > parent, `aud` widen, `par_hash` tamper, and depth-cap negatives.
- `services/mcp-payments/test/attenuation.test.ts` (mint smoke): §root-mapping round-trip (`isSubsetEntry` true, USD synthesized) + fail-closed throw; end-to-end mint (`deriveAttenuationRoot` → `mintChildOffline` → `validateAttenuationChain`) yields `leafAuthority = invoice.read`; **in-Mission-but-outside-leaf `schedule_payment` → `out_of_authority`** (always runs, no OpenFGA); in-leaf `get_invoice` → **PEP-permitted** (OpenFGA-gated).

## Gate

`pnpm install`, `pnpm -r typecheck` (19 projects), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (**30 files / 206 tests**), `pnpm evals` (100% containment, 0 evidence gaps, 0 over-block), `pnpm exhibit` — all green. OpenFGA was reachable, so the in-leaf permit case ran (did not skip).

pulls.title: feat(signals): Mission Signals — SET lifecycle events
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Implements `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-signals` (pin `4cc71d7`): the PUSH complement to the Status List's PULL. A Mission Issuer emits a signed `mission.lifecycle-change` Security Event Token (SET) when it commits a lifecycle transition, so consumers stop honoring a Mission promptly instead of waiting out token lifetimes.

## Deviation from the brief (read first)
The brief asked for `signalConsumers?` on `buildAuthorizationServer`. The monorepo typechecks with `tsc --build` composite **project references**, which forbid cycles. `@mission/signals` imports `LifecycleCommit` from `@mission/authorization-server`, so the AS importing `@mission/signals` back (to build the emitter) would form a reference cycle (TS6202). Instead:
- The AS gained a generic `onLifecycleCommit?: (commit) => void` subscriber, composed with the existing Status List republisher so **both** run per commit. The AS never imports `@mission/signals`.
- `signalConsumers` lives on the `MissionSignalEmitter` (in `@mission/signals`), whose `onCommit` is injected into the AS. `@mission/signals` is the DAG leaf (`signals → authorization-server, core`).

Empirically verified: full `pnpm -r typecheck` passes with `packages/mission-signals` referencing the AS and no cycle.

## The SET shape (`signLifecycleEvent`)
`typ: secevent+jwt`, ES256, `kid`. Envelope: `iss` (Mission Issuer), `aud` (consumer), `iat`, `jti`, `sub_id: {format:"opaque", id: mission_id}`. Body: `events["https://schemas.karlmcguinness.com/mission/lifecycle-change"] = { mission:{id,issuer}, state, prior_state?, version, committed_at, expires_at, successor? }`. Built with `jose` `SignJWT`, mirroring `services/transparency`.

## Subscribing to (not re-adding) the kernel hook
The kernel already fires `onLifecycleCommit(commit: LifecycleCommit)` from its three commit funnels (`setState`, `supersedeOnRedemption`, `insertRecord`, incl. the activating insert at version 1). No funnel hooks were added. At the AS construction site the existing `() => statusListPublisher?.markDirty()` became `(commit) => { statusListPublisher?.markDirty(); opts.onLifecycleCommit?.(commit); }`. The emitter's `onCommit` is synchronous (signing is scheduled off the commit path; `drain()` is a test/shutdown barrier).

## Receiver: version-idempotent, anti-revive (`MissionSignalReceiver`)
`verifyAndApply` runs the four `§set-protection` checks in order — signature (`jwtVerify` with `createLocalJWKSet`, `typ: secevent+jwt`), explicit `iss`, explicit `aud`, `jti` dedup — then applies by `version`: a `version` **at or below** the last applied never regresses state (an old `active` never overrides a newer `revoked`). First-seen `version > 1` and version-jumps are detected as gaps (marked not-honored; automatic Status refetch deferred). Received `state` is typed `string` and compared `=== "active"`, so any non-active value (incl. unrecognized) is non-deriving. `viewState` feeds a consumer's `loadView`; `lease()` returns the shared `MissionStatusLease` (`@mission/core`) tagged `state_source: "signal"`.

## Test — `packages/mission-signals/test/signals.test.ts` (in-process, no HTTP/OpenFGA)
A real `MissionKernel` → emitter → receiver, with a `loadView` that builds the PDP `MissionView` **from the receiver cache alone** (state/version from the signal, never `kernel.get()`), plus a stub `Fga`. Asserts:
- **Happy path:** evaluate before signal → permit; `transition(id,"revoke")` → SET emitted → applied → next evaluate denies **`mission_inactive`** (PDP step 2), not `stale_state`; lease reflects `revoked`/signal.
- **Anti-revive:** a stale lower-version `active` SET (fresh `jti`) → `status: "stale"`, no regression.
- **Verification:** wrong `aud` / wrong `iss` / bad signature each → `refused` with the matching reason, cache unchanged.
- **Redelivery:** same `jti` reapplied → `duplicate`, no error, no regression.

## Gate (all green)
`pnpm install`, `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint` (clean; 2 pre-existing biome-migrate infos), `pnpm test` (29 files / 192 tests; delta = +6 signals, zero regressions/skips), `pnpm evals` (100% containment), `pnpm exhibit` (complete). OpenFGA reachable via the aligned worktree cert, so the live tests ran rather than skipped.

## Scope / deferred (named)
Additive: new `packages/mission-signals`, the AS `onLifecycleCommit?` seam, `SPEC_VERSIONS.md` row. Untouched: PDP envelope / `DenialReason` union, transports, demo enforcement. Deferred: SSF transmitter/stream-config/add-subject endpoints + `mission_event_stream_endpoint` metadata; RFC 8935/8936 HTTP transports; heartbeat/liveness + staleness fallback; Status refetch on gap; `suspend_until`/`on_expiry`/`tenant` (no kernel model); demo-stack signal wiring (emitter is injectable at `buildAuthorizationServer`).

pulls.title: feat(orchestration): mission unwinding + compensation profile
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Mission Orchestration and Unwinding

Implements `draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md` (pin `3ce193c`, 2026-07-15) as a new deterministic package `packages/orchestration`.

**This is the saga / compensation "unwinding" profile** — how in-flight state is safely stopped and compensated when a Mission is halted. It is **not** parent→child sub-agent delegation (that is `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation`, out of scope here). It is a client/agent-side execution profile and **issues no credential**.

### The five deterministic pieces (`packages/orchestration/src/`)

- **`reversibility.ts`** — the five reversibility classes; `floorReversibility(runtimeActionClass)` per the draft's runtime-action-class → minimum table; raise-only `enforceReversibilityFloor` (MUST NOT lower); a `ClassSource` union so untrusted model output cannot be the sole authority for lowering class.
- **`unwind-plan.ts`** — `UnwindPlan` type; `unwindPlanHash(iss, plan)` = `computeAnchor("mission-unwind-plan", iss, plan)`; `validateUnwindPlan`; and the fail-closed `commitUnwindPlan` dispatch gate (durable commit strictly before dispatch; a failed write MUST NOT dispatch).
- **`state-change.ts`** — `onMissionStateChange({state, stale, steps})` encoding the 5-step sequence with the **staleness asymmetry**: an established non-active state runs items 1–5; **staleness alone runs items 1,2,3,5 and MUST NOT run post-completion (item 4)**. Established non-active takes precedence over staleness (a signed `revoked` overrides a stale `active` cache). A committed step under staleness carries **no** `orchestration_decision` (item 4 did not run), rather than a misleading `record_only`.
- **`in-flight.ts`** — `classifyOutcome` adapter over the D36 payments `OpState`: `reserved`→`not_dispatched`, `permit_consumed`→`dispatched_not_committed`, `connector_committed`/`evidence_emitted`/`reconciled`→`committed`, `abandoned`/unknown→`unknown` (routes to human review for high-risk classes).
- **`compensation.ts`** — `resolveCompensationAuthority`: only `resource_policy` or an active, scoped `separate_mission`; the terminated Mission's authority is refused; no basis → `human_review`; permits carry the `compensates_decision_id` binding. Plus reverse-dependency ordering and `compensation_incomplete` enumeration.
- **`evidence.ts`** — the Orchestration Evidence builder (faithful sibling of `mcp-payments/src/evidence.ts`); `state_source` imported from `@mission/core` (not redefined); JWS `evidence_envelope` REQUIRED (fail-closed) when compensating a high-risk class.

### Integrity anchor (no algorithm change)

The draft's worked unwind plan reproduces its published hash **byte-exact** under the existing `computeAnchor` envelope — `sha-256:jKxM47ygRiTXYVfKjrVE34VZx8nsxg1I9OPPeHnO-_c`. The only `mission-core` change is one added constant, `UNWIND_PLAN_TYP = "mission-unwind-plan"`, in `packages/mission-core/src/anchors.ts` (and its re-export). `computeAnchor` itself is untouched.

### Tests

`packages/orchestration/test/orchestration.test.ts` (16 cases, pure/deterministic, always run). Covers: the published-hash vector (byte-exact); fail-closed dispatch (commit strictly before dispatch); established-revoked → full 5-step with post-completion; staleness → items 1,2,3,5 only (no post-completion of any kind); compensation authority (terminated-Mission refused / no-basis → review / active `separate_mission` → permit with `authority_basis` + `compensates_decision_id` + high-risk `evidence_envelope` whose JWS header carries `alg`/`kid`/`typ`); and the full `OpState` → outcome mapping. Every behavior carries an `@spec` tag; a `SPEC_VERSIONS.md` row was added.

### Scope

Additive only. Services are imported **read-only** as type-only devDependencies (`OpState` from `@mission/mcp-payments`, `MissionState` from `@mission/agent`); **no service is modified.**

**Files touched beyond the new package (intentional, named):**
- `packages/mission-core/src/anchors.ts` + `index.ts` — the one `UNWIND_PLAN_TYP` constant and its re-export.
- root `src/tsconfig.json` — project reference to the new package.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` — the new workspace package.
- `SPEC_VERSIONS.md` — the traceability row.

**Known gap:** `privileged_administration` is a **new** runtime action class this profile introduces; it is not yet present in `services/pdp/src/policy.ts` (which floors unknown classes to the default 300s staleness bound). A deployment adopting it must extend that policy. Documented in `reversibility.ts`.

### Deferred (named, not implemented here)

- **Live trigger wiring**: Mission Status poll / Lifecycle Signals / PDP-denial feed / harness-stop feed → `onMissionStateChange`.
- **Agent-side orchestration driver** that consumes these decisions.
- **Human-review queue infrastructure** (queues, parked-item max-age expiry).
- **Compensation-chain caps** (loop escalation).
- **The execution ledger** (owned by the harness draft).

### Harness ↔ orchestrator precedence (§relationship) — noted, no live arbiter

The draft's stage-split rule is stated here but intentionally **not** implemented (no live arbiter):
- Both would stop a **dispatched/in-flight** step → the orchestrator's in-flight handling governs (only it can unwind committed work).
- Both would stop an **undispatched** item → the harness stop policy governs.
- One would stop and the other continue → the item stops; the harness honors an orchestrator cancel/hold per its resume algorithm.

### Gate

`pnpm install`, `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (29 files / 202 tests), `pnpm evals`, `pnpm exhibit` — all green.

pulls.title: feat(child-delegation): parent→child sub-missions with cascade
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Implements **Mission Child-Delegation** (O-38, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation` @ `8427e9b`) as an additive, kernel-level flow in `services/authorization-server`, mirroring `kernel/expansion.ts` / `kernel/cross-domain.ts` (kernel flow + cascade, unwired to endpoints — same posture as `attenuation.ts`).

A **Child Mission** is a NEW Mission (own `mission_id`, actor, lifecycle, `act` chain) whose authority is a strict subset of a **PARENT** — distinct from Attenuation (same-mission token narrowing) and Expansion (same-subject widening successor).

## What landed

**`kernel/child-delegation.ts` (new)**
- `createChildMission(kernel, input)` — resolve + active-check the parent (`applyExpiry` state check, mirroring `createExpansion`; child creation is not a derivation and does not consume the parent's derivation cap); the delegation on-switch is an explicit input (`delegationAllowed`, precedent: `deriveAttenuationRoot`'s `delMaxDepth` — see S-15 note below); a fresh actor hop built with `@mission/actor-chain` (`extendChain` restarting at the child actor, `client_id == child_actor.sub`); **strict-subset** (see next section); child `expires_at` **clamped ≤ parent's**; the child's **own** `authority_hash` over the child set; a `parent` lineage object (`{id, issuer, authority_hash, depth, cascade_mode, delegation_id?, created_at}`, `depth = (parent.parent?.depth ?? 0) + 1`); subject + human accountability inherited from the parent; the **`dlg_`-prefixed delegation event IS the child's approval event** (no separate human approval).
- `childMissionClaim` adds the `parent` member (mirrors `successorMissionClaim`).
- `ChildDelegationError` + `ChildDenialReason` (`parent_not_active | parent_mismatch | not_strict_subset | child_actor_not_allowed | fanout_exceeded | policy_denied`).

**`types.ts`** — `ParentRef` + `MissionRecord.parent?` (additive); `CascadeMode` (`immediate` only).

**`kernel.ts` (additive)** — `parent_id`/`parent_json` in `insertRecord`'s INSERT (immutable after creation, like `predecessor`); `rowToRecord` rebuilds `parent`; `findChildren`; **`cascadeChildren`** fired from the TERMINAL-commit path — a gate at the end of `setState` (covers `transition(revoke/complete)` and `applyExpiry`→expired) plus an explicit call in `supersedeOnRedemption` (which bypasses `setState`). Because each child transition flows `setState → onLifecycleCommit`, the **Status List republisher and Mission Signals propagate for free** (`stateToBit` already maps `cascaded` → INVALID). Transitivity rides the `setState` terminal gate (so `cascadeChildren` does not self-recurse); descendants not in `active`/`suspended` are skipped so an already-terminal grandchild can't abort the cascade via `LifecycleConflictError`.

## Strict-subset: derive-then-prove (a deliberate refinement)

The child Authority Set is derived under the **original derivation policy** (the child Intent is untrusted, like any Intent) and then **proven** a strict subset of the parent — the parent set is the ceiling, enforced by **refusal** (`not_strict_subset`), not silent clamping. This is what §strict-subset mandates ("the issuer MUST refuse child creation with `not_strict_subset`"): deriving *under* the parent ceiling would silently narrow an over-broad request and never refuse, making the guard dead code and the widening-rejection untestable. Consequence of reusing the core `isSubsetEntry`: a child that **omits** a constraint the parent narrowed (`max_amount`/`vendors`) is refused, so a child MUST restate constraints at or below the parent's.

## suspend is deliberately NOT cascaded

Per §cascade, `suspended` is the one **reversible** trigger: children are held non-active and restored on parent resume, and MUST NOT go terminal. Cascade here fires **only** for terminal parent transitions (`revoked`/`expired`/`completed`/`superseded`/`cascaded` → child `cascaded`). **Consequence of the deferral:** with a parent `suspended`, the child stays `active` and `gateDerivation(childId)` currently succeeds, which does not yet satisfy §child-state's ancestor-active requirement. Under `immediate` cascade the **terminal** ancestor case is satisfied by construction (a terminal ancestor drives the child to `cascaded`, so the child's own state check suffices — no ancestor walk needed); only the suspend case is the open gap.

## Depth cap

Small hard child-generation depth cap (reject `depth > 2`) → `fanout_exceeded`. The per-entry `max_child_depth` fan-out ceiling is deferred.

## Tests — `test/child-delegation.test.ts` (10, deterministic; kernel harness + `onLifecycleCommit` spy)

In-slice subset + `gateDerivation` succeeds; parent-but-outside-child not a subset (probe carries the child's constraints so the failure is action-attributable); widening → `not_strict_subset`; expiry clamp; **revoke → child `cascaded` → `gateDerivation` throws `mission_not_active`, and the `onLifecycleCommit` spy observed the child's `cascaded` commit (prior_state `active`, version 2) — proving Status List/Signals propagate**; transitive grandchild cascade; already-terminal grandchild does not abort; depth cap; `policy_denied`; `parent_not_active`.

## Gate (all green)

`pnpm install`, `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint` (services are outside the root biome scope by repo convention), `pnpm test` (33 files / 240 tests, incl. the 10 new), `pnpm evals` (100% containment, OpenFGA live), `pnpm exhibit` (complete, on the wire).

## Deferred (named)

PAR wire params (`parent` / `parent_token` / `child_actor`, front-channel carve-outs); the child-bound JWT authorization grant issuance (§child-client-identity); **suspend-projection + restore-on-resume** (§cascade reversible trigger — see gap above); fan-out accounting (`max_children`, `allowed_child_actors`, `max_child_depth`, per-entry `children`); the `AuthorityEntry.delegation` core extension (**S-15**, shared with Attenuation); child Decision Evidence; discovery metadata; cross-issuer; the consumer-verified cascade modes (`bounded_staleness`, `status_required`).

Scope: additive in `services/authorization-server` + the new test + `SPEC_VERSIONS.md`. `derive.ts` imported read-only; `attenuation.ts`/`expansion.ts`/`cross-domain.ts`, the PDP, and the demo are untouched. `PLAN.md` and root `draft-*.md` not edited.

pulls.title: feat(delegation): AuthorityEntry.delegation core extension + derive/subset semantics
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

PR1 of the sequenced child-delegation build: the **derivation / subset layer only**. Adds the `AuthorityEntry.delegation` core extension (the internal **S-15** gap) so authority derivation and the subset comparison understand per-entry delegation policy. This is foundational for later child-delegation fan-out.

Out of scope (later PRs): kernel fan-out, PAR wire params, provider changes, `child-delegation.ts`. The offline holder-side chain verifier (`packages/mission-core/src/attenuation-chain.ts`) is a **separate** `del_max_depth` surface and is untouched. The hand-built golden-vector fixtures are left delegation-free.

## Changes

- **`kernel/types.ts`** — optional `delegation` on `AuthorityEntry` (`max_depth`, `allowed_delegates`, plus an open JSON index so the companion `children` object rides unchanged). Written as an intersection type so the named members keep precise types under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (a plain index-signature form is rejected by the compiler). Adds a shared `DelegateMatcher`.
- **`kernel/derive.ts`**
  - `intersect()` carries + narrows `delegation` as an **inherit-by-default GRANT**. **Ceiling-absent → result has NO delegation** (a capability the ceiling never granted cannot be introduced by the untrusted proposal, the compromised-shaper property). This is the **deliberate opposite** of the `constraints` ceiling-absent branch (which takes the proposal's `vendors`), because `delegation` is a grant, not a restriction. Ceiling-present + proposal-omitted **inherits unchanged**. Both present → `max_depth` min; `allowed_delegates` intersect (a restriction *inside* a granted delegation, so it mirrors `vendors` exactly, ceiling-absent takes the proposal's, and a comment says so); the `children` grant gated the same way one level down; unrecognized companion members carried from the **ceiling**, never the proposal.
  - `isSubsetEntry()` treats `delegation` as a **narrowing dimension in the opposite direction** from constraints: candidate **omitting** delegation the grantor has → **PASS** (the child simply does not re-delegate); candidate **introducing** delegation the grantor lacks → **FAIL**; both present → `max_depth ≤`, `allowed_delegates ⊆`, `children` no broader.
- **`kernel/attenuation.ts`** — `deriveAttenuationRoot` now **DERIVES `del_max_depth`** (min `max_depth` across the delegable entries; non-delegable entries drop from a root whose depth `> 0`) instead of requiring the caller to supply it. Closes **S-15**. `delMaxDepth` remains an optional back-compat override that drops nothing (the one existing caller, `mcp-payments/test/attenuation.test.ts`, passes `delMaxDepth: 2` and still passes). A client-requested narrowing (`requestedTools`) is minted **non-delegating** (`del_max_depth 0`, fail-closed): deriving a depth over the *justifying* parent entries is fan-out accounting, deferred to the kernel PR.
- **`demo-data` + `config/policy.json`** — the payments (read-bearing) ceiling entry becomes delegable with a `children` object; the ledger `journal.write` entry stays delegation-free. `CeilingEntry` gains a `delegation` passthrough and `loadPolicy` carries it through (it was silently dropping unknown members).
- **`SPEC_VERSIONS.md`** — one bullet recording the extension.
- **Tests** — new `services/authorization-server/test/derivation-delegation.test.ts` (15 tests): intersect inherit + ceiling-absent flip + both-present narrow; subset narrowing direction (both directions of the presence flip, `max_depth` isolated); derived `del_max_depth` (min across delegable, non-delegable dropped) plus the `requestedTools` fail-closed and back-compat-override cases; a delegation-free regression (fully additive on both sides); and a wiring assertion that the demo ceiling actually carries delegation (guards against a vacuous green gate).

## Two things to know

- **`requestedTools` decision:** minted non-delegating (`del_max_depth 0`) rather than deriving a depth from the justifying parent entries. That justification mapping is fan-out accounting and belongs to a later PR; a non-delegating root is fail-closed and can never let a non-delegable requested tool ride a depth-`>0` root.
- **Demo divergence (stated plainly):** the delegable payments entry also carries `payment.schedule` / `payment.execute` / `remittance.send`, so the demo is not *purely* "delegable read, non-delegable write." This is structurally forced: `delegation` is per-entry while the demo ceiling entries are per-resource, and splitting an entry into read/write halves sharing a resource would break `deriveAuthoritySet`'s per-resource `find`. The non-delegable exemplar is the ledger `journal.write` entry.

## Gate

Run with OpenFGA up (`src-openfga-1`) and the CA cert exported:

```
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --build, clean
pnpm test        # vitest run — 34 files, 255 passed, 0 skipped
pnpm lint        # biome check . — exit 0
```

0 skipped: the demo-ceiling change did not regress child-delegation, arop, or the attenuation override caller.

Draft — do not merge.

pulls.title: feat(child-delegation): fan-out accounting + child evidence
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## PR2: Child-delegation fan-out accounting + Child Evidence (kernel READ-path)

Stacks on **PR1** (`feat/delegation-authority-extension`) — base of this PR is that branch, **not** `main`. PR1 added the `AuthorityEntry.delegation` core extension (the S-15 on-switch); this PR consumes it.

### What changed

**Drop the placeholder.** `delegationAllowed: boolean` is removed from `CreateChildInput`. The delegation decision is now **derived** from the parent's stored `authority_set` entries' `delegation.children` (which PR1's derivation carries/narrows as an inherit-by-default grant).

**Deterministic justifying-entry selection.** Each child Authority Set entry is attributed to the **first** parent entry, in Authority Set order, that it `isSubsetEntry` of (imported from `derive.js`). That child-entry -> parent-entry mapping is the accounting basis, per `@spec child-delegation#fanout-accounting`.

**Four fan-out controls enforced, each per justifying entry:**
- **on-switch** — every justifying parent entry must carry a `delegation.children` object, else refuse the **new** reason `delegation_not_permitted`. `policy_denied` stays in the union for a genuine `child_creation_policy` denial and is **not** reused for the on-switch.
- **`allowed_child_actors`** — the `childActor` must match at least one matcher (a matcher matches when every present `sub`/`sub_profile` equals the actor's), else `child_actor_not_allowed`.
- **`max_children`** — non-terminal existing children are counted via `kernel.findChildren` + `TERMINAL_STATES`, **bucketed by justifying parent entry**; creating a child that would push a bucket over its cap refuses `fanout_exceeded`. A slot frees after a child terminates. The count -> check -> `insertRecord` runs with no `await` between count and insert; on the single-threaded in-process kernel this is effectively atomic (commented in-code).
- **`max_child_depth`** (default **1**) — a per-entry, decrementing child-generation ceiling the child `depth` is measured against; it **augments** the hard `MAX_CHILD_DEPTH` (stricter wins). Kept distinct from `parent.depth`, which counts up.

**Child Evidence.** `createChildMission` returns a Child Evidence record on permit and attaches a **deny** record to the thrown `ChildDelegationError` on refusal. The prospective child `id`/`authority_hash` are computed **before** the gates so a deny record carries a real `child` member. Fields: `evidence_id` (`chd_`-prefixed), `parent`, `child`, `child_actor`, `attenuation.result`, `fanout` `{active_children, max_children}`, `cascade_mode`, `decision`, `denial_reason?`, `created_at`. Media type `application/mission-child-evidence+json`; canonical bytes via `childEvidenceBytes` (JCS, reusing `@mission/core`'s `canonicalize`).

**Labels.** `demo/src/labels.ts` `REASON_LABELS` gains human glosses for `parent_not_active`, `parent_mismatch`, `not_strict_subset`, `child_actor_not_allowed`, `fanout_exceeded`, `policy_denied`, and the new `delegation_not_permitted`.

### Divergence to confirm
- **`decision` values are `created` / `denied`** (the draft's `@spec child-delegation#child-evidence-object` enumeration), not the task note's shorthand "permit/deny". Chosen because the impl is `@spec`-anchored to the draft. Documented in `SPEC_VERSIONS.md`.
- Touched `services/authorization-server/src/index.ts` (2 lines) to export `childEvidenceBytes` and `CHILD_EVIDENCE_MEDIA_TYPE` for the tests, following the existing barrel convention. Not in the explicit MAY-change list but not forbidden.

### Types (minimal)
`types.ts` gains `ChildFanoutControls` (a typed reader for the `children` companion object) and `ChildEvidence`. `AuthorityEntry.delegation` is kept **byte-identical** (its open `JsonValue`-shaped index is what `derive.ts` relies on), so `derive.ts` and `kernel.ts` are untouched. `MissionRecord` is left to PR3.

### Tests
`services/authorization-server/test/child-delegation.test.ts`: updated for the `delegationAllowed` removal and the `delegation_not_permitted` rename, plus new coverage:
- (a) parent whose justifying entry has no `children` (demo ledger entry) -> `delegation_not_permitted`;
- (b) non-`ai_agent` actor -> `child_actor_not_allowed`;
- (c) the 6th concurrent child -> `fanout_exceeded`, then terminate one and a new creation succeeds;
- (d) a child subset of two parent entries counts against the first-in-order entry only (hand-built two-entry parent, cap 1 vs 5);
- (e) Child Evidence shape + stable JCS bytes on permit and deny.

### Gate
```
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --build, clean
pnpm test        # 34 files, 259 passed
pnpm lint        # biome check ., exit 0 (2 pre-existing config-version infos)
```

pulls.title: feat(child-delegation): suspend-projection + restore-on-resume + ancestor-active gate
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## PR3 — suspend-projection + restore-on-resume + ancestor-active gate

Stacked on **PR2** (base `feat/child-delegation-fanout`; chain PR1 <- PR2 <- PR3). Implements the one **reversible** cascade trigger from `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation` (§cascade, §child-state).

### What it does
- **Suspend projection.** A parent `suspend` projects its transitive **active** descendants to the reversible `suspended` hold, stamping `projected_from = "active"`. A descendant already suspended *independently* (not `active`) is skipped and gets no marker.
- **Restore on resume.** A parent `resume` restores only children that are still `suspended` **and** carry a `projected_from` marker, back to their pre-suspension state, then clears the marker.
- **Expiry precedence.** A child whose `expires_at` passed during suspension ends `expired` (terminal), never revived to `active`.
- **Ancestor-active gate.** `gateDerivation` walks the `parent` lineage and refuses (`mission_not_active`) if any ancestor is non-active (belt-and-suspenders with projection; the profile requires the explicit check).
- **Propagation for free.** Onset and lift both flow through `setState -> emitCommit`, so the Status List republisher and Mission Signals propagate; transitivity and generation order ride `setState`'s own re-entry.
- **Terminal wins.** A parent revoked/completed/expired *while suspended* still cascades descendants terminally (`cascaded`).

### Files
- `kernel/kernel.ts` — `projected_from` column; `projectSuspendedChildren` / `restoreProjectedChildren`; the `suspended`/`active` gates in `setState`; the ancestor walk in `gateDerivation`.
- `kernel/types.ts` — `MissionRecord.projected_from` (PR3's partition of this file).
- `SPEC_VERSIONS.md` — one bullet.
- `test/suspend-projection.test.ts` — (a) generation-order projection, (b) expiry precedence, (c) exact-state restore +version, (d) independent-suspend not restored, (f) revoke-while-suspended cascades terminally, (e/e') ancestor gate.
- `packages/mission-signals/test/suspend-lift.test.ts` — the `suspended`->`active` **lift** is accepted by the anti-revive receiver (version-based forward progress); Status List reads back the restored state.

### Gate
`pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm test` **267 passed / 0 skipped**; `pnpm lint` (biome) exit 0 (2 pre-existing config-version infos).

Do not merge; the chain merges in order after PR1 and PR2.

pulls.title: feat(child-delegation): PAR wire params + child-grant issuance + discovery
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## PR4: wire child creation onto the AS + child-grant issuance + discovery

Stacks on PR3 (`feat/child-delegation-suspend`). Base is PR3, not `main`. The kernel `createChildMission` (PR2) and the suspend-projection lifecycle (PR3) are already present; this PR wires child creation onto the real OAuth surface.

@spec `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation`: `#child-creation`, `#child-client-identity`, `#request-processing`, `#discovery`.

### What landed

**PAR wire params + front-channel guard.** `parent`, `parent_token`, and `child_actor` are registered `extraParams`, mirroring `mission_intent`. `parent_token` is a back-channel credential: the validator refuses it with `invalid_request` on any route other than PAR. Because `loadPushedAuthorizationRequest` rehydrates the pushed params before `checkExtraParams` re-runs on `/auth`, a `request_uri` resolved on the front channel trips this guard (tested end-to-end).

**Parent resolution (RESOLVE-ONLY).** The back-channel `POST /child-missions` reads the pushed request, then resolves the Parent Mission from `parent_token` via `RefreshToken.find` (non-consuming, `ignoreSessionBinding`). The `refresh_token` grant is never invoked, so there is no rotation and no replay registration. It cross-checks the resolved mission against the `parent` param (`parent_mismatch`).

**createChildMission wiring.** Steps 4-11 run through the PR2 kernel. `ChildDelegationError.reason` maps to layered OAuth errors carried in the `mission_denial_reason` member, set on `ctx` directly (status before body) so oidc-provider's `err_out` renderer does not strip it: `parent_not_active`/`parent_mismatch` -> `invalid_grant`; `delegation_not_permitted`/`child_actor_not_allowed`/`not_strict_subset`/`fanout_exceeded` -> `invalid_request`; `policy_denied` -> `access_denied`.

**Child-grant issuance.** On success the AS mints the child-bound RFC 7523 JWT authorization grant (`adapters/child-grant.ts`, ID-JAG-shaped): `aud` = the token endpoint, `sub` = the Mission subject (inherited from the parent), `client_id` = the child actor, and the `mission` claim carries the `parent` lineage and the CHILD `authority_hash`. It is the grant reference the parent conveys; it is redeemable only by the named child actor and is never a child token.

**Discovery.** `mission_child_delegation_supported = true` beside `mission_attenuation_supported`.

**Security.** The route is guarded by the dev-grade service token (the same guard `/missions/:id/lifecycle` and `/introspect` use) as the explicit authenticated request of `#request-processing` step 1, and binds the acting client from the PAR record (`pushed.iss`, PAR client-authenticated). The pushed request is destroyed after read, so `parent_token` does not sit at rest; it is never logged or echoed.

### Split: PR4b (in-scope, deferred)

Only the final leg is deferred: the child redeeming that assertion AS ITSELF at `/token` (RFC 7523 JWT-bearer) needs the child actor registered as an OAuth client so it can authenticate at the token endpoint. No path to that stays within this PR's allowed surface (it requires `config/clients.json` + demo-data). A production AS would run child creation on `/token` via `registerGrantType` (real `private_key_jwt`) instead of the service-token guard used here. A skipped placeholder marks the deferred redemption test.

### Files

- `services/authorization-server/src/adapters/provider.ts`: extraParams (`parent`/`parent_token`/`child_actor`) + front-channel guard; back-channel `POST /child-missions` handler (parent resolve, mismatch guard, createChildMission, denial mapping); discovery flag; `childGrant{Key,Kid,Alg}` options.
- `services/authorization-server/src/adapters/child-grant.ts` (new): `mintChildGrant` + the child-grant typ / RFC 7523 grant-type constants.
- `services/authorization-server/src/index.ts`: wire the child-grant signing key (AS token key) + export the new module.
- `services/authorization-server/test/child-delegation-endpoint.test.ts` (new): happy path, `parent_mismatch`, front-channel guard, no-rotation/no-replay, unauthenticated rejection, discovery, and a skipped PR4b redemption placeholder.
- `SPEC_VERSIONS.md`: table row + note bullet; states what is realized and names PR4b (does not claim fully-wired).

### Gate

`pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm lint` (OpenFGA up). typecheck clean; test 273 passed, 1 skipped (the PR4b placeholder); lint exit 0 (2 pre-existing biome-config infos only).

Draft; do not merge.

pulls.title: feat(child-delegation): child redeems grant assertion as itself at /token (RFC 7523)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Closes the functional gap left by PR4: a Child Mission's actor can now redeem its child-bound RFC 7523 JWT authorization grant AS ITSELF at `/token` and receive a DPoP-bound child access token. Two inseparable parts in one PR.

## Part A: child-actor client registration

- Append the `subagent-invoice-extractor` confidential client to `config/clients.json` (grant_types `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`, `private_key_jwt`, ES256), matching the draft worked example. `policy.json`'s `allowed_child_actors` matches on `sub_profile: ai_agent`, so child creation with this actor passes.
- `demo-data`: refactor `seedAgentClient` into a private `buildSeededClient(seed)` and add `seedChildClient()`, which resolves the seed by `client_id` (never by positional index, safe under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) and throws `ConfigError` if absent. `seedAgentClient()` still returns `CLIENTS[0]`.
- `index.ts`: minimal wiring only. Add the second client to the `clients` array, seed it, and expose `childClientJwk` on `BuiltAs`. `agentClientJwk` and its consumers are byte-identical.

## Part B: redemption handler (`handleChildJwtBearerGrant`)

Registered UNCONDITIONALLY next to the deferred grant (so the URN is in `configuration.grantTypes` before the child client validates lazily, and `assertion` is declared in the params set so the token endpoint does not strip it). Mirrors `mintDeferredToken` step for step:

1. Read `assertion`; missing -> `invalid_request`.
2. Verify the assertion on the AS public JWKS (`iss` = AS, `aud` = token endpoint, `typ` = child-grant typ); failure -> `invalid_grant`.
3. **Security gate:** `assertion.client_id` MUST equal the authenticated client, else `invalid_grant`.
4. Resolve the Child Mission record and cross-check its `client_id` + `authority_hash` against the assertion (record is authoritative).
5. DPoP jkt extraction (mirrors `mintDeferredToken`): `ctx.get("DPoP")`, decode header, thumbprint, verify `typ: dpop+jwt`, assert `htu`/`htm`. This jkt is the child's own key -> the token's `cnf.jkt`.
6. Lazy Grant binding: bind a new oidc `Grant` to the child on first redemption, reuse `record.grant_id` afterward.
7. Resource + TTL clamp to the child's `expires_at`.
8. Mint the resource-bound JWT access token (`gty` = jwt-bearer, `rar` = child authority set, `at.jkt`).
9. `200` with `token_type: DPoP`, `authorization_details`, `cache-control: no-store`.

## Security gate

The assertion names `client_id` as its only authorized redeemer; it MUST equal the authenticated client, else `invalid_grant` with a DISTINCT `error_description` ("child grant redeemer does not match the authenticated client"). oidc-provider's `invalid_grant` renderer replaces thrown descriptions with a generic "grant request is invalid", so the distinct description is emitted directly on `ctx` (the same technique `handleChildCreation` uses for `mission_denial_reason` and `handleDeferredGrant` initiation uses for `deferral_code`). This gate is what makes conveying the assertion through the parent safe.

## Lazy Grant binding + single-gate guarantee

On first redemption a new `Grant` is bound to the child, so `findByGrant(grantId)` resolves to the child inside `extraTokenClaims`, which attaches the child mission claim and gates the derivation. Subsequent redemptions reuse `record.grant_id` (no duplicate Grant). The handler deliberately does NOT call `gateDerivation`, so `extraTokenClaims` increments `derivation_count` exactly once per redemption. `extraTokenClaims` selects the claim shape by lineage: a Child Mission projects the `parent` lineage member (`childMissionClaim`), a root Mission the base claim.

## Note on the negative test

`ap-agent` cannot reach the client_id gate: oidc-provider rejects at the client `grant_types` allowlist first (`ap-agent` has no jwt-bearer grant type), which is the stronger real boundary and precisely why the parent can safely convey the assertion. Registering jwt-bearer on `ap-agent` to make a negative test hit the gate would make the parent redemption-capable, a posture regression, so it is deliberately not done. The client_id gate is therefore asserted via a foreign-actor assertion redeemed by the authenticated child client; the `ap-agent` attempt is also tested and asserted to fail at the grant-type allowlist. The security gate returns normally (sets `ctx`) rather than throwing; no code subscribes to `grant.success`/`grant.error`, so this is telemetry-neutral (the pre-existing deferred-initiation branch makes the same tradeoff).

## Tests

Replaces the PR4b `it.skip` placeholder with a real suite (dedicated parent to isolate fan-out):

- **Happy path:** child redeems -> 200; token asserts `token_type: DPoP`, `sub: alice`, `client_id: subagent-invoice-extractor`, `aud: CANONICAL_RESOURCE`, `cnf.jkt` = independently derived child DPoP thumbprint, `authorization_details` deep-equals the child authority set, `mission.id` = child, `mission.authority_hash` = child hash (differs from parent), `mission.parent.id`/`.depth`. Advisor check 1: mission claim asserted present before drill-through; `findByGrant(grantId)` resolves the child; `derivation_count` 0 -> 1.
- **Reuse branch:** the same assertion redeems twice; second goes through the `grant_id` reuse branch (grant_id unchanged, no duplicate Grant); `derivation_count` 1 -> 2 (one increment per redemption).
- **Security gate:** a foreign-actor assertion redeemed by the authenticated child client -> `invalid_grant` with the distinct `error_description`.
- **Parent cannot redeem:** `ap-agent` -> `invalid_request` "not allowed for this client".
- **Ancestor gate:** a revoked parent cascades the child -> redemption `invalid_grant`.

## Known-stale doc line (follow-up)

`adapters/child-grant.ts` line 17 still says redemption is "deferred to PR4b". It is on this PR's MUST-NOT-TOUCH list (the assertion it mints is already complete and verified), so it is left unedited; flag for a follow-up sweep.

## Gate

`pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm test` 278 passed, 0 skipped (the placeholder skip dropped to 0); `pnpm lint` exit 0.

pulls.title: feat(child-delegation): relocate child creation to /token grant; retire POST /child-missions
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

PR4c, the final child-delegation cleanup. Relocates Child Mission **creation** off the bespoke dev-guarded `POST /child-missions` route onto the OAuth **token endpoint** as a registered grant type, authenticated by the parent's real `private_key_jwt`. This satisfies the house rule "no new endpoints when an existing surface carries it" and the draft's `#request-processing` step 1 ("authenticate the client submitting the request").

Purely a relocation: the creation logic (PAR resolution, parent resolve-only lookup, `parent`/`parent_mismatch` cross-check, `createChildMission`, `mintChildGrant`, `mission_denial_reason` mapping) is unchanged. Only the entry point and its client authentication change.

Stacks on **PR4b** (`feat/child-delegation-redemption`); base is that branch, not `main`.

## Changes

- **New creation grant URN** `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:mission-child-creation` (exported `CHILD_CREATION_GRANT_TYPE`), distinct from the child jwt-bearer URN, registered with `request_uri` in its params set (or `stripGrantIrrelevantParams` drops it).
- **`handleChildCreation` becomes `handleChildCreationGrant`**, invoked by the grant. oidc-provider's client-auth middleware runs before the handler, so `ctx.oidc.client` is the authenticated parent. The handler now requires the PAR client (`pushed.iss`) to equal that authenticated client and rejects otherwise. This is the genuine authentication that replaces the `x-service-token` stand-in for this path. Success response is 200 (the token endpoint's success), body shape unchanged (`mission_id`, `parent`, `grant_type`, `assertion`); `grant_type` still names the grant the child redeems under.
- **`POST /child-missions` route deleted.** The shared `x-service-token`/`DEV_SERVICE_TOKEN` dev guard and its other consumers (interaction decide, status, statuslist, lifecycle, introspect, transaction) are untouched.
- **`config/clients.json`:** `ap-agent` gains the creation grant URN (1-insertion/1-deletion on its `grant_types` line only). The child client `subagent-invoice-extractor` is untouched.
- **`child-grant.ts` doc fix:** redemption is no longer "deferred to PR4b" (it shipped); creation relocated in PR4c. Comment only.
- **`SPEC_VERSIONS.md`:** appended one bullet noting PR4b (redemption) plus PR4c (creation on `/token`) close the child-delegation wiring, and swapped the stale route phrase in the table row; single-issuer fully wired.

## Tests

`child-delegation-endpoint.test.ts` now exercises the full lifecycle end-to-end on the OAuth surface, no bespoke route. Creation tests (happy path, `parent_mismatch`, resolve-only/no-replay, unauthenticated) hit `/token` with the creation grant as `ap-agent` via `private_key_jwt`. The unauthenticated negative confirms client auth rejects before the handler. The PR4b redemption tests and the front-channel `parent_token` guard test are unchanged and still pass.

Gate (Docker + OpenFGA up): `pnpm typecheck` clean, `pnpm test` 37 files / **278 passed / 0 skipped**, `pnpm lint` exit 0.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Discovery metadata:** `registerGrantType` adds the URN to `configuration.grantTypes`, so `/.well-known/openid-configuration` now advertises `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:mission-child-creation` in `grant_types_supported`. The child-delegation draft does not register a creation grant type (its IANA section registers only the PAR params, the discovery flag, and denial reasons); this URN is deliberately impl-local, consistent with the existing `:deferred` grant.
- **PAR destroy ordering (known choice):** the handler calls `parEntity.destroy()` before the `pushed.iss != client.clientId` rejection, so a wrong client presenting someone else's `request_uri` would burn that PAR before being refused. Not exploitable in the current config (only `ap-agent` holds the creation grant, so no second client reaches the handler), and the early destroy preserves the "parent_token never sits at rest" rationale. Left as-is rather than trading one property for the other.

Do not merge; draft.

pulls.title: feat(ica): foundations — actor-chain collapse, continuation-assertion validator, handle store
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## PR-A: ICA foundations

Three independent, additive foundation modules for Identity Continuation
Assertion support (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-id-continuation-assertion-00`). PR-A
wires nothing into the token endpoint; later PRs consume these.

### Module 1 — actor-chain consecutive-identical-actor collapse
Adds `extendChainCollapsing(newActor, inbound)` alongside the existing
`extendChain`. When `newActor.iss === inbound.iss && newActor.sub === inbound.sub`
(raw, case-sensitive, no canonicalization) the inbound chain is returned
unchanged, so a duplicate current-actor entry does not enter the `act` lineage;
otherwise it prepends exactly as `extendChain` does.

- Chose a **new function** rather than a `{ collapse: true }` option on
  `extendChain`, so `extendChain`'s existing behavior stays byte-identical for
  its two production callers (`delegation.ts`, `child-delegation.ts`) with no
  new branch introduced there.
- **Collapse-before-depth ordering:** the collapse happens in this function,
  before any downstream `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH` check (e.g. `validateActChain`), so a
  single actor taking several intra-domain hops keeps a depth-1 lineage and
  never trips the cap.
- On a collapse the returned chain is `inbound` verbatim, so non-identity
  members of `newActor` (including a rebound `cnf`) are discarded on that hop.
  This is intentional (the hop record persists elsewhere; this governs only the
  `act` lineage), and documented so a later PR that reads `act.cnf` reads the
  top-level `cnf` instead.

### Module 2 — ICA subject-token validator (`kernel/continuation-assertion.ts`)
`validateContinuationAssertion(assertion, { audience, issuers, presenterJkt, replay })`
mirrors `instance-assertion.ts` (unverified `iss` peek to select the trusted
Chain Authority issuer, then `jwtVerify`, then rechecks; shared
`newReplayCache`). Exports `IDENTITY_CONTINUATION_JWT_TYP`
(`oauth-identity-continuation+jwt`), `IDENTITY_CONTINUATION_TOKEN_TYPE`
(`urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:identity-continuation`),
`MAX_CONTINUATION_LIFETIME_S`, and `ContinuationAssertionError`.

Rejection set (in order):

1. Unknown issuer.
2. Signature / audience / issuer / `typ` / algorithm failure (audience is the
   **AS issuer identifier**, not `${issuer}/token`; asymmetric algs only).
3. Header `typ` recheck.
4. Lifetime: `exp - iat <= 300` **and** `exp > iat` (missing `iat`/`exp` rejected).
5. `cnf` MUST contain **exactly** `jkt` and `cnf.jkt` MUST equal `presenterJkt`.
6. `identity_continuation_handle`: string, 22-256 chars, base64url alphabet.
7. Any of these top-level claims present: `sub`, `auth_time`, `acr`, `amr`,
   `sid`, `scope`, `resource`, `authorization_details`, `audience`,
   `requested_token_type`.
8. `act`: a single-level object with non-empty string `iss`/`sub`; rejects a
   nested `act`, `exp`, `nbf`, `aud`, `scope`, or `cnf`.
9. `jti` present and not previously seen; recorded on success.

Returns `{ iss, aud, handle, act, cnf, iat, exp, jti }`.

### Module 3 — continuation handle store (`kernel/continuation-store.ts`)
`ContinuationStore` over SQLite (`openStore`), modeled on `DeferralStore`. Two
tables:

- `continuation_anchors` (`anchor_id` PK, `anchor_type` grant|session,
  `mission_id`, `session_id`, `auth_time`, `acr`, `amr` JSON, `state`
  active|terminal, `created_at`). The **root auth envelope lives here**, not on
  `MissionRecord`, so no kernel schema migration is needed.
- `continuation_handles` (`handle` PK, `anchor_id`, `mission_id`, `actor_iss`,
  `actor_sub`, `cnf_jkt`, `prior_handle`, `state`, `created_at`).

API: `rootGrantAnchor` (durable, `session_id` null), `rootSessionAnchor`,
`mint` (handle = `ich_` + 144 bits base64url, within the 22-256 ICA bounds),
`resolve` (recovers mission/anchor/actor/auth-envelope/cnf; undefined when
unknown or when the handle or its anchor is terminal), `onLifecycleCommit`, and
`terminateSession`.

- **Not single-use:** `resolve` never consumes the handle. A hop record
  persists across continuations, so the same handle resolves repeatedly.
- **`onLifecycleCommit(commit)`:** when `TERMINAL_STATES.has(commit.state)`,
  marks all anchors and handles for that Mission terminal. This method is
  **wired into the AS lifecycle-commit fan-out by a later PR** — implemented
  here, not wired into `index.ts` in this PR.
- **`terminateSession(sessionId)`:** terminates only session-anchored anchors
  and their handles; grant anchors (and their handles) survive.
- The store holds **no kernel reference** (a small, noted divergence from
  `DeferralStore`): none of its methods query the kernel and `onLifecycleCommit`
  receives its event by value, so the later-PR fan-out supplies the commit from

(`validateContinuationAssertion`, the constants, `ContinuationAssertionError`,

is already exported from `instance-assertion.ts`).
