pulls.title: feat(ica): extend issueCrossDomainGrant for continuation ID-JAGs (handle, audience-local sub, act, auth envelope)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Extends `issueCrossDomainGrant` so one code path can emit a **continuation ID-JAG**: a grant carrying a fresh `identity_continuation_handle`, an audience-local `sub`, a pre-built collapsed `act` lineage, and a carried (not refreshed) root auth envelope. Additive and opt-in: legacy callers pass none of the new fields and get a byte-identical grant.

Stacks on **PR-A (`feat/ica-foundations`)** — base is `feat/ica-foundations`, not `main`.

## The four optional `IssueGrantInput` fields

All optional; omitting every one reproduces today's exact behavior.

- `sub?: string` — audience-local subject. When present it replaces `record.subject.sub` as the ID-JAG `sub`. The deterministic resolver that computes it lives in the caller (a later PR); here the passed value is consumed verbatim.
- `identityContinuationHandle?: string` — emitted as a top-level `identity_continuation_handle` claim (the fresh new-hop handle, minted by the caller, never generated here).
- `act?: ActObject` (from `@mission/actor-chain`) — emitted verbatim as the `act` claim. It is a pre-built, already-collapsed lineage; this function does not build or collapse it (the caller uses PR-A's `extendChainCollapsing`).
- `authEnvelope?: { auth_time?: number; acr?: string; amr?: string[] }` — present sub-fields are emitted as top-level `auth_time`/`acr`/`amr`; absent sub-fields are omitted.

## Single code path + legacy-unchanged guarantee

The five legacy claims (`mission`, `authorization_details`, `cnf`, `sub`, `client_id`) are built in their existing insertion order; the continuation claims are appended afterward via conditional assignment. `sub` uses `input.sub !== undefined ? input.sub : record.subject.sub`, so a legacy call keeps the global subject and adds no new claims — an identical `JSON.stringify` payload, identical key order. Signing key/kid remain caller-supplied. No sibling emitter.

The RAS redeem path still reads `mission`/`authorization_details`/`cnf`/`sub`/`exp`/`jti`, all still present. Legacy callers (`src/demo/src/stack.ts`, `src/services/mcp-saas/test/cross-domain.test.ts`) are untouched and pass unchanged.

## Test

New self-contained AS-package test `test/cross-domain-continuation.test.ts`:

- **Extended path**: passes an audience-local `sub`, a handle, an `act` built with `extendChainCollapsing` (a realistic collapsed depth-1 lineage), and a full auth envelope; asserts `sub` is the audience-local value (not `record.subject.sub`), `identity_continuation_handle`/`act`/`auth_time`/`acr`/`amr` present and equal, and `cnf`/`mission`/`authorization_details`/`client_id` still present.
- **Partial envelope**: `authEnvelope: { auth_time: 123 }` alone emits `auth_time` and omits `acr`/`amr`.
- **Legacy negative**: no new fields keeps `sub = record.subject.sub` and asserts (via `not.toHaveProperty`) that none of the five continuation claims appear.
- **Key-order pin**: the legacy payload key order is exactly `mission, authorization_details, cnf, sub, client_id, iss, aud, iat, exp, jti`.

## Gate

`pnpm -C src typecheck`, `pnpm -C src test`, `pnpm -C src lint` all pass: 40 files / 316 tests passed, 0 skipped; lint exit 0.

Draft. Do not merge ahead of PR-A.

pulls.title: feat(ica): RFC 8693 token-exchange grant — ICA subject token to Mission-rooted continuation ID-JAG
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## RFC 8693 token-exchange grant: ICA subject token to Mission-rooted continuation ID-JAG

Stacks on `feat/ica-cross-domain` (PR-B). Base this PR on PR-B, not `main`.

Wires the token-exchange grant at `/token`: an Identity Continuation Assertion (ICA), presented as the RFC 8693 `subject_token`, is exchanged for a Mission-rooted continuation ID-JAG. This is the core end-to-end intra-domain continuation hop, with the full four-signal actor agreement and the RFC 8693 error taxonomy.

### Registration
`TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE = urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`, registered UNCONDITIONALLY next to the child grants (mirrors `CHILD_JWT_BEARER_GRANT_TYPE`): a client listing the URN must not fail client-metadata validation, and the handler validates its wiring lazily. `ap-agent` gains the URN in `clients.json`.

Params set: `subject_token`, `subject_token_type`, `actor_token`, `actor_token_type`, `audience`, `resource`, `requested_token_type`, `authorization_details`.

**`resource`/`scope` — pinned empirically.** With `resource` absent from the set the happy path failed with `resource required` (the token endpoint stripped it; the `resourceIndicators` machinery does NOT retain `resource` for a custom grant). So `resource` MUST be declared and is. `scope` is not read by the handler and is not declared.

### Handler steps
1. Require `requested_token_type` = id-jag and `subject_token_type` = identity-continuation (else `invalid_request`); require `subject_token`, `audience`, `resource`.
2. Signal #1 (client auth): the authenticated presenter -> current actor `(iss = AS issuer, sub = client_id)`. This is the contract the Chain Authority must mint the ICA `act` and the `actor_token` against.
3. Signal #4 (DPoP): derive `jkt` exactly as `mintDeferredToken` (htu = `${issuer}/token`, htm = POST); failure -> `invalid_dpop_proof`.
4. Validate the ICA (`validateContinuationAssertion`, audience = the AS issuer). Typed errors map to `invalid_request` with the specific message preserved (unlike `invalid_grant`, `invalid_request` is not re-rendered), so lifetime>300 / forbidden-claim / replay / presenter-key reasons stay visible.
5. Resolve handle -> Mission; unknown/terminal -> `invalid_continuation` (STORE path).
6. `invalid_target` when `resourceToAs(resource) != audience`.
7. Signal #2 (`actor_token`, required): verified against the confirmed DPoP key and required to carry `cnf.jkt == jkt`; extract `(iss, sub)`.
8. Four-signal agreement.
9. Mint the ID-JAG via `issueCrossDomainGrant` (PR-B optional fields).
10. RFC 8693 response `{ access_token, issued_token_type: id-jag, token_type: N_A, expires_in }`, `cache-control: no-store`, set on ctx directly.
11. No replay re-record (the validator already recorded the jti).

### Four-signal actor agreement
`{client-auth actor, actor_token (iss,sub), ICA act (iss,sub)}` must agree by raw case-sensitive `===`, and `actor_token cnf.jkt === ICA cnf.jkt === presenter jkt`. Each mismatch returns `invalid_grant` with a DISTINCT `error_description` set on `ctx` directly, so the `invalid_grant` renderer does not overwrite it.

### Single-gate / SignJWT guarantee
The ID-JAG is minted through `issueCrossDomainGrant`, which builds and signs the JWT with a direct `SignJWT` and runs `gateDerivation` EXACTLY ONCE. It is never routed through `provider.AccessToken`. The handler's own `kernel.get` (for the deterministic sub) is a non-gating read, so there is no double-gate. A `GateError` maps to `invalid_continuation` (gate path, distinct description from the store path); the bare "no audience-scoped authority" error maps to `invalid_target`.

### Deterministic audience-local sub
`subjectResolver(audience, record.subject)` replaces the global subject. The default is a stable digest over `(issuer, audience, subject.sub)` — a CONSTANT salt, so the same `(audience, subject)` yields the same sub across hops and across AS restarts. The test asserts equality across two ICAs and inequality with the global subject.

### Signing-key divergence (must-read)
The task said "sign with the AS token key so the ID-JAG verifies on jwks_uri." That is a task-instruction conflict, not a free choice: `issueCrossDomainGrant` hardcodes an ES256 protected header (`cross-domain.ts`), and the AS token key is RS256 (`topology.json` `asToken.alg`), so it cannot sign the ID-JAG. I satisfied the stated GOAL (verifies on jwks_uri) by signing with the ES256 `as-txn` key, which is already published on jwks_uri, via new `continuationGrantKey`/`continuationGrantKid` options wired in `index.ts`.

- Tension: this cuts against the D39 per-purpose-key note (`index.ts` comments that `as-txn` signs txn-bound approval tokens; it now also signs continuation ID-JAGs).
- Rejected alternative: a new dedicated per-purpose key would need a kid, and `topology.json` was outside the allowed files, which fights the config-driven-stack rule (kids live in config). Reusing the existing ES256 kid is the lowest-blast-radius choice; no test pins the `/jwks` key set.

### Lifecycle-commit fan-out
`index.ts` constructs the `ContinuationStore` and composes its `onLifecycleCommit` into the SAME fan-out as the Status List republisher and the injected Signals subscriber, so a terminal Mission terminates all of its continuation anchors and handles. Test (g) revokes a Mission and proves the presented handle then fails `invalid_continuation`.

### Notes / caveats
- **ICA is single-use from validation.** `validateContinuationAssertion` records the jti; a request that fails a LATER step (target/actor/gate) still consumes the ICA. Fail-safe, not retryable.
- **Coverage of the two `invalid_continuation` paths.** Test (g) pins the STORE path (fan-out terminalization). The `GateError` path is not separately exercised because, once the fan-out terminalizes handles, step 5 always short-circuits first; the two paths carry distinct descriptions.
- **`chainAuthorityIssuers` default is an unexercised placeholder.** It defaults to "the AS acting as its own Chain Authority" (its own jwks_uri keys), which would trust the AS's own status/token keys to mint ICAs — a confused-deputy surface. No caller invokes it (the test injects a dedicated CA; `stack.ts` is untouched). The demo wiring / PR-D should replace it with a dedicated Chain Authority issuer.

### Gate
`pnpm -C src typecheck` clean. `pnpm -C src test`: 41 files, 324 tests passed, 0 skipped. `pnpm -C src lint`: no errors (2 pre-existing biome config infos; the biome config scopes to `packages/**`+`scripts/**`, so `services/**` is covered by typecheck).

Draft; do not merge.

pulls.title: feat(ica): dedicated continuation signing key + RAS end-to-end redemption + discovery/RAS metadata
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## PR-D of Identity Continuation Assertion (ICA) support

Makes the continuation ID-JAG work end-to-end at the Resource AS and advertises
the feature. **Stacks on PR-C** (`feat/ica-token-exchange`); base of this PR is
`feat/ica-token-exchange`, not `main`.

### 1. Dedicated `as-continuation` signing key (D39 per-purpose)

PR-C minted the continuation ID-JAG with the ES256 `as-txn` key as a
**placeholder**: the AS token key is RS256 but `issueCrossDomainGrant` hardcodes
an ES256 header, so the token key could not sign it, and `as-txn` is the
transaction-assurance key (wrong purpose for an identity grant).

A continuation ID-JAG is an **identity** grant, so it now gets its own dedicated
key:

- `topology.json` adds `asContinuation` (`kid: as-continuation`, `alg: ES256`);
  the typed topology loader (`@mission/demo-data`) is extended for it.
- The AS generates it per boot and publishes its **public** JWK on the
  `jwks_uri` alongside `as-token`/`as-status`/`as-txn`, so the ID-JAG verifies
  there. Its **private** half is wired as the continuation-grant signer,
  replacing the `as-txn` placeholder.
- ES256 matches the header `issueCrossDomainGrant` hardcodes (unchanged), so no
  signing-path change was needed. `as-txn`, the RS256 AS token key, and all
  other consumers are untouched; the key addition is purely additive.

### 2. RAS trust + end-to-end redemption

- The demo stack (`demo/src/stack.ts`) adds the AS public `as-continuation` JWK
  (read from the AS `jwks_uri`) to the RAS `trustedIssuers` under the AS issuer,
  next to the existing cross-domain key. It throws at stack build time if that
  key is absent from the published set, so a wiring regression fails loudly.
  (`stack.ts` is not covered by the vitest gate, which globs
  `packages/*/test` and `services/*/test` only; this change is verified by
  inspection. The gated e2e test below exercises the same trust wiring against
  the same live `jwks_uri`.)
- New test in `continuation-grant.test.ts`: mint a continuation ID-JAG at
  `/token`, then `ras.redeem(idJag, jkt)` at a `ResourceAuthorizationServer`
  (`aud` = the RAS issuer). Asserts the local token surfaces the audience-local
  `sub`, `authorization_details`, the `cnf` sender-constraint, and the preserved
  mission anchors; a replay is refused (one-time `jti`).
- The happy-path test now asserts the ID-JAG header `kid` is `as-continuation`
  (`remoteJwks` resolves by kid, so this is what proves the rewire off the
  placeholder actually happened).

### 3. Discovery

The AS `.well-known/openid-configuration` advertises
`identity_continuation_supported = true`.

### 4. RAS metadata

`metadata()` advertises `authorization_grant_profiles_supported` for both the
`id-jag` and `id-jag-continuation` grant profiles.

### Note on the Chain Authority trust set

The AS acts as its own Chain Authority via its published `jwks` set, so
`as-continuation` also joins that set. This is consistent with
`as-token`/`as-status`/`as-txn` already being there, and the continuation-grant
tests inject their own Chain Authority key. The widening is deliberate.

### Divergence from the task text

- `continuationGrantAlg`: task item 1 named this option to set. No such plumbing
  exists (`AdapterOptions` has only `continuationGrantKey`/`continuationGrantKid`)
  and none is needed: `issueCrossDomainGrant` hardcodes `alg: ES256` in the
  protected header, and the new key is ES256, so it matches. No param added.
- Three files outside the stated MAY-change list were touched:
  - `packages/demo-data/src/index.ts`: the typed topology loader. Forced, not
    optional: `tsc --build` hard-failed on `TOPOLOGY.keys.asContinuation`
    without the interface field + `reqKey` line (config-driven-stack pattern).
  - `services/authorization-server/package.json`: added `@mission/ras` as a
    devDependency so the e2e test can import `ResourceAuthorizationServer`
    (no dependency cycle; `@mission/ras` exports source, no build step).
  - `pnpm-lock.yaml`: the resulting lockfile update.

### Gate

Docker + OpenFGA up (`/healthz` SERVING). Run in `src/`:

- `pnpm typecheck` (tsc --build): pass.
- `pnpm test` (vitest run): **326 passed, 0 skipped**, 41 files.
- `pnpm lint` (biome check): clean (2 pre-existing config-deprecation infos
  only, no errors).

Draft; do not merge.

pulls.title: feat(ica): grant-anchor rooting at Mission approval + lifecycle invariants (revocation, keeps-exp, session)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

PR-E (final code PR) of Identity Continuation Assertion (ICA) support. Rounds out "lifecycle": the durable grant-anchored continuation root becomes real (rooted when a Mission is approved, not test-only), and end-to-end lifecycle invariants are proven by tests.

**Stacks on PR-D (`feat/ica-ras-discovery`), not `main`.**

## Where rooting is hooked and why

Approval-time rooting is wired into the AS assembly's EXISTING lifecycle-commit fan-out (`src/services/authorization-server/src/index.ts`), on the ACTIVATING commit (`version === 1 && prior_state === undefined && state === "active"`). A new module-level `rootMissionContinuation(store, record)` roots a grant anchor (`rootGrantAnchor`) and mints an INITIAL handle bound to the Mission's actor.

- **No kernel change, no provider change.** The commit fan-out is the single funnel that already fires for `kernel.approve()` (and thus for both the provider approval interaction and direct-kernel test approvals). Hooking here keeps the kernel free of any store dependency, exactly as the existing `continuationStore.onLifecycleCommit` composition does.
- The fan-out only exists in `buildAuthorizationServer`, so bare-kernel unit tests are entirely unaffected.

## Blast radius: which Missions get a root

`insertRecord -> emitCommit` fires the activating commit for `approve()` (kernel.ts), expansion successors (`expansion.ts:75`), and Child Missions (`child-delegation.ts:425`). So **every activated Mission gets a durable grant anchor + initial handle**, including expansion successors and Child Missions. This is intentional and models "a Mission is the durable root." It is purely additive: the anchor/handle sit inert until a continuation is presented, so a Mission that never continues is unaffected. All 331 existing tests are unchanged.

## Auth-envelope provenance

The rooted envelope is the demo's ROOTING-EVENT envelope, not a real authentication event:
- `auth_time` = the approval timestamp (`record.created_at`, seconds)
- `acr` = `intent.controls.acr` when present
- `amr` = omitted

A real deployment supplies the root authentication event's envelope instead. The initial handle binds the Mission's actor as the agent CLIENT (`iss = AS issuer`, `sub = client_id`), matching the /token four-signal contract's `currentActor`. No `cnf` is bound (no DPoP key exists at approval); the four-signal check validates the PRESENTED key at /token, never the stored handle's cnf. `ContinuationStore.mint`'s `cnfJkt` is widened to optional for this (a type widening; every chained-hop caller still passes a string and gets an identical row).

## Idempotency guard

Idempotent re-approval emits NO commit (a duplicate `approval_event_id` throws inside `insertRecord` before `emitCommit`), so rooting never fires twice for the same approval. Belt-and-suspenders, `rootMissionContinuation` also skips when the Mission already carries a handle (`handlesForMission(id).length > 0`), so an anchor is never duplicated.

## Tests (lifecycle proof)

Added a `continuation lifecycle invariants` describe block to `continuation-grant.test.ts` (reuses the existing ICA/RAS/jwks harness; a new `approveLineage` helper approves WITHOUT manual rooting and reads the auto-rooted handle):

1. **Approval-time rooting** - an approved Mission's auto-rooted initial handle mints a continuation ID-JAG end to end; the approval envelope (`acr`, `auth_time`) reaches the issued ID-JAG.
2. **Revocation blocks NEW continuations** - revoke the Mission, present the handle at /token, get `invalid_continuation` (the `onLifecycleCommit` fan-out terminated the anchor/handle).
3. **Already-issued keeps its exp** - an ID-JAG minted before revoke still verifies against the AS jwks with its ORIGINAL `exp` and still redeems at a RAS after revoke (the RAS consults the AS signing key, not the continuation store); a NEW continuation over the same lineage is refused. Revocation is live and blocks fresh issuance only; it does not retroactively shorten issued tokens.
4. **Session anchoring** - a `rootSessionAnchor` + handle stops resolving after `terminateSession`, while the Mission's grant anchor is unaffected.
5. (bonus) **Idempotent approval does not double-root** - the same `approval_event_id` yields exactly one anchor/handle.

## Gate

- `pnpm -C src typecheck` - clean
- `pnpm -C src test` - 41 files, **331 passed, 0 skipped**
- `pnpm -C src lint` - clean (2 pre-existing biome config-deprecation infos). NB: the repo's biome config lints only `packages/**` and `scripts/**`; `services/**` changes are gated by `tsc`.

pulls.title: docs: oauth-mission-continuation authorization-continuity profile (outline) + architecture/README/cross-domain/AAuth reframe
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Architecture: Identity Continuation composed with Missions

Adds a first-class **Continue** verb to `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md`, documenting how the Identity Continuation Assertion (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-id-continuation-assertion`) composes with Missions.

- **Verb spine + `## Continue` subsection** (sibling to Project/Delegate): the question/boundary/owner treatment. A Mission is the durable, grant-anchored root a continuation chains from; the assertion carries no subject, so continuation preserves the Mission's subject and authority across an intra-domain hop rather than narrowing to a sub-actor (Delegate) or crossing a trust boundary (Project). Distinguishes continuation (mints a fresh grant, carries authority forward) from the harness's session continuity (never authority).
- **Document Map** entry under Lifecycle, next to cross-domain.
- **Informative references**: the ICA draft and RFC 8693.

Builds clean (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt OK; no undefined xrefs). Accompanies the ICA reference-implementation stack (#378 → #379 → #380 → #381 → #382), which wires the RFC 8693 token-exchange grant, the Mission-rooted continuation ID-JAG, discovery, and the RAS grant profile.

This is the "draft" half of the requested deliverable (code + draft). Independent of the code branches (doc-only); mergeable on its own.

pulls.title: feat(continuation): async-delegation foundations (DelegationFamilyStore + kernel.gateActive)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Foundations for an upcoming async-delegation continuation transport. Two additive modules plus unit tests. No provider/handler wiring, no continuation-grant changes: a later PR composes these into the AS.

### 1. `DelegationFamilyStore` (new)
`src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/delegation-family-store.ts` — a self-contained SQLite store (via `openStore`, mirroring `ContinuationStore`) that binds a grant to the Mission whose delegation lineage it belongs to.

- `record({ grantId, missionId })` — insert an `active` family row.
- `resolve(grantId)` → `{ missionId, state } | undefined` — undefined when the grant is unknown OR its family is terminal.
- `onLifecycleCommit(commit)` — on a terminal Mission commit, mark every family row for that Mission `terminal` (mirrors `ContinuationStore.onLifecycleCommit`).
- `familiesForMission(missionId)` → `string[]` — grant ids in ANY state, so a caller can drive revocation even after termination.

Re-exported additively from `src/services/authorization-server/src/index.ts` (nothing else there changed).

### 2. `kernel.gateActive(id)`
`src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/kernel.ts` — the SAME checks as `gateDerivation` (expiry clock, `active`-state requirement, ancestor-active lineage walk) WITHOUT the `max_derivations` cap check and WITHOUT the `derivation_count` increment. Throws `GateError` with the same reasons.

The three shared checks were factored into a private `gateActiveLineage` helper that both `gateDerivation` and `gateActive` call. `gateDerivation`'s observable behavior is unchanged (check ordering preserved: ancestor walk still runs before the cap check; increment still on success only).

## Tests
- `test/delegation-family-store.test.ts` — record/resolve, unknown → undefined, terminal commit stops `resolve` while the grant stays listed in `familiesForMission`, non-terminal commit does not terminate, only the named Mission is affected.
- `test/gate-active.test.ts` — active passes with `derivation_count` unchanged (asserted against the persisted row), suspended/expired throw, a non-active ancestor throws (`/non-active ancestor/`, via a raw UPDATE that bypasses the cascade so the child stays active and the lineage branch is what fires), and a cap-exhausted Mission still passes `gateActive` without incrementing.

## Validation
- `pnpm -C src typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm -C src test` — 43 files, 342 passed, 0 skipped
- `pnpm -C src lint` — exit 0. Note: biome's `includes` cover `packages/**` and `scripts/**` only, so the new `services/` files fall outside its scope; the run reports 2 pre-existing config deprecation infos. Typecheck + the 342 passing tests are the real validation for these files.

pulls.title: feat(continuation): async-delegation transport handler + provider wiring
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Async-delegation continuation transport

Completes the async-delegation continuation transport on the AS (provider wiring +
issuance handler + tests), on top of the foundations in PR #384
(`feat/async-delegation-foundations`: `DelegationFamilyStore` and
`kernel.gateActive`, consumed here, not modified).

An acting client presents a base mission ACCESS token (RFC 8693 `subject_token`,
`subject_token_type = access_token`) with `request_refresh_token=true` and receives
an initial DPoP-bound access token AND a rotated, sender-constrained refresh token
for a durable, disconnected delegation. Refresh redemption is ordinary native
`grant_type=refresh_token` (no custom refresh handler).

### The load-bearing decision

Both tokens are bound to a NEW per-delegation `Grant` (one Grant per issuance),
tracked in `DelegationFamilyStore` (grant_id -> mission_id). This is **never** the
Mission's approval grant: a consumed-async-RT reuse wipe (reuse detection revokes by
grantId) must not destroy the Mission grant and break child-delegation's
`parent_token`. The per-delegation grant also makes confinement structural: the
grant's `rar` IS the confined subset, so every refreshed access token re-projects
exactly that subset and stays audienced to the target.

### Changes

- `adapters/provider.ts`: `extraTokenClaims` family fallback (after the unchanged
  Mission-approval-grant branch: on a `familyStore` hit, attach the Mission claim
  after `gateActive` -- no derivation increment); `rotateRefreshToken` (force
  rotation for family grants, else the inlined oidc-provider default);
  `ttl.RefreshToken` (clamp a family RT to the Mission `expires_at`, else the 14-day
  default); `request_refresh_token` added to the token-exchange params Set;
  `delegated_refresh_token_profile_supported` discovery flag;
  `AdapterOptions.familyStore`; `resourceServerInfoFor`/`newResourceServer` exported.
- `index.ts`: construct `DelegationFamilyStore`; join its `onLifecycleCommit` and a
  provider-capturing terminal subscriber to the single lifecycle-commit fan-out;
  pass the store via `AdapterOptions`; expose it on `BuiltAs`. The terminal
  subscriber revokes + destroys every family grant of a terminal Mission via the
  static `RefreshToken.revokeByGrantId` + `Grant.destroy` (the hook has no ctx),
  covering ALL terminal paths (revoke/complete AND expiry/cascade/supersede, which
  all funnel through the one hook, keyed on `commit.id`).
- `adapters/continuation-grant.ts`: dispatch in `handleTokenExchangeGrant` (before
  the ICA hard-checks; the ICA path is byte-identical when the flag is absent) +
  `handleAsyncDelegationExchange` (DPoP-derive jkt; resolve the Mission from the
  base access token; require active + intra-domain target + confined subset;
  `gateDerivation` exactly once; new per-delegation Grant with `addResourceScope`
  and rar = confined subset; record the family; mint the initial access token and
  the sender-constrained refresh token).

### Guardrails (all tested in `test/async-delegation.test.ts`)

1. Per-delegation grant isolation -- after a family RT reuse wipe, the Mission's
   code-flow refresh token AND a child creation still succeed.
2. Single count -- `derivation_count` rises by exactly 1 across issuance + N
   refreshes; a code-flow refresh still increments (regression).
3. Refreshed access-token audience = target (refresh token carries `resource`).
4. `addResourceScope(target)` present (else refresh filters the scope empty).
5. `rt.jkt` set manually; a disconnected client sends a fresh DPoP proof per refresh;
   a wrong key fails jkt verification.
6. `request_refresh_token` survives token-endpoint param stripping.
7. Mandatory rotation -- a consumed-RT retry trips reuse detection, killing THIS
   family only.
   Plus absolute-lifetime clamping and family revocation on terminal paths.

### Gate

- `pnpm -C src typecheck` -- clean.
- `pnpm -C src test` (Docker + OpenFGA up, `OPENFGA_CA_CERT`/`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`

pulls.title: feat(continuation): record the continuation hop reference in execution-time evidence
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## What

Decision #2 of the Mission Continuation profile: thread the continuation hop
reference into execution-time evidence so an action taken under a continued
credential attributes to both its Mission and the specific hop that authorized
it. Additive and separable; no behavior change beyond the added evidence field.

## Changes

- `services/mcp-payments/src/evidence.ts`: add optional
  `hop_reference?: { jti; mission_id; continuation_handle? }` to `EvidenceBase`.
  It flows into every evidence kind (discriminated union preserved) and into
  `EvidenceInput` automatically.
- `services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts`: carry optional `jti` and
  `identityContinuationHandle` on `TokenFacts` (both token claims were dropped).
- `services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts`: copy `payload.jti` and
  `payload.identity_continuation_handle` into `TokenFacts` at the two
  access-token validation sites (`validateToken`, `validateMissionToken`), and
  populate `hop_reference` on the transaction `ExecutionEvidence`. Guarded on
  `jti`, so non-JWT / older tokens are unaffected.

## No transparency-code change

The Mission Receipt commits to evidence by hash: `signStatement` calls
`evidenceDigest`, which is `sha-256` over the JCS-canonical evidence bytes
(`canonicalize(evidence)`). Because `hop_reference` is an ordinary evidence
field, it enters the receipt digest automatically. The added transparency test
proves this: dropping `hop_reference` re-hashes to a different digest and fails
the five-step offline verification at step 5.

## Deliberately deferred

Mirroring `hop_reference` onto Decision Evidence / Refusal Records, and onto the
attenuation-chain validation path (`validateAttenuationChain` has two candidate
payloads, so "which jti is the hop" is an open design question). The transaction
`ExecutionEvidence` is the required insertion.

## Tests

- mcp-payments transaction test (OpenFGA-gated): execution under a continued
  credential records `hop_reference.{jti, mission_id, continuation_handle}`;
  jti-only omits `continuation_handle`; no-jti omits `hop_reference` entirely.
- mcp-payments mediated-channel test (OpenFGA-gated): end to end over the real
  MCP transport, a signed token carrying `jti` + `identity_continuation_handle`
  produces the expected `hop_reference` in Execution Evidence. This covers the
  `validateMissionToken` claim-copy (claim name -> `TokenFacts` -> evidence),
  which the hand-built `TokenFacts` cases could not, so a claim-name typo fails.
- transparency test (ungated): the receipt digest commits `hop_reference`
  (drop it -> five-step verification fails at step 5).

Full suite: 44 files, 359 passed, 0 skipped. typecheck + lint clean.

pulls.title: docs(containment): Mission Containment companion draft + architecture positioning
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

New companion Internet-Draft, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment` (Mission Containment for OAuth 2.0): event-triggered, monotonic, in-Mission narrowing of a live Mission's effective authority. The "oauth" name is per the Document Map naming rule: the profile extends Authorization Server surfaces.

Category `std`, optional layered extension, mirroring the expansion/status/child-delegation companions in front matter, section order, and voice.

## The model

- **Overlay, not mutation.** The approved Authority Set and its `intent_hash`/`authority_hash` anchors are immutable; containment is evaluated state held by the issuer (`containment_version` + contained `{resource, actions?}` set), by the same argument the Status profile uses to keep fired completion status out of the anchor. Removal-only in v1; constraint tightening is a named deferral so monotonicity stays trivially decidable.
- **Contain transition.** Union-only (MUST NOT revert), idempotent per `event_id`, legal from `active` and `suspended`, refused on terminal states; commits as a metadata-only state-version increment, so materialized policy views are detectably obsolete.
- **Protected events fail closed.** Indeterminate authenticity or applicability narrows anyway or withholds derivation, never ignores; event-source trust reuses the Status profile's signed event-source verification.
- **Derivation gating.** Tokens, Child Missions, cross-domain projections, and offline attenuation roots all derive from the Effective Authority Set; an all-contained request fails with `authority_contained` (approved-then-contained, distinct from `out_of_authority`, expansion-eligible); mixed requests omit the contained part.
- **Visibility and propagation.** `containment_version` on status/introspection surfaces; propagation rides existing machinery (state-version movement on the pull surface; the Signals metadata-only `mission.lifecycle-change` shape; a dedicated containment event type is deferred).
- **Restoration only by successor.** Containment does not propagate to an expansion successor, and the expansion consent MUST surface the predecessor's containment history (closes the laundering gap).
- **Containment Evidence.** JCS-canonical record, `application/mission-containment-evidence+json` used by local agreement pending registration, mirroring the child-delegation evidence conventions.

## Architecture draft (small edits)

- Capability kill row in the Containment Matrix (finer blast radius than Mission kill)
- Containment added to the Govern verb's owner list
- Document Map entry under Lifecycle
- Informative reference

## Validation

- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.txt`: kramdown-rfc OK, xml2rfc-txt OK
- `make draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.txt`: kramdown-rfc OK, xml2rfc-txt OK
- No unresolved references; no em-dashes; core draft untouched

## Note for review

One deliberate precision on propagation: a contain transition leaves an `active` Mission `active`, so its Status List bit is unchanged (the list carries reliance bits only; the state version stays on the authoritative surfaces, per the Status profile). The draft states that containment binds derivation at the issuer, so list-consumer staleness never widens what a contained Mission can issue, and consumers pick up the narrowed view on their next authoritative read within existing freshness rules.

pulls.title: feat(containment): kernel overlay, contain transition, effective-set derivation + propagation
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Mission Containment: kernel overlay + propagation

An issuer-held, versioned, MONOTONIC narrowing overlay on an active Mission's effective authority. The approved `authority_set` and `authority_hash` are immutable; containment is evaluated state. Removal-only in v1 (entries/actions; no constraint deltas); restore is only the existing Expansion successor path (unchanged).

### Kernel
- `kernel/types.ts`: `MissionContainment`, `ContainmentEventRecord`; `MissionRecord.containment?`; the commit-funnel doc comment now names four funnels.
- `kernel/kernel.ts`:
  - nullable `containment_json` column, read in `rowToRecord`, written only by `contain()` (a fresh mission has none);
  - `contain(id, { event, remove })`: terminal-state refusal (legal from `active`/`suspended`), idempotent by `event_id` (mirrors `approve()`: a repeat returns the current record, no version bump, no extra event row), monotonic UNION of contained entries, `isSubsetSet` belt-and-suspenders, atomic `containment_json` + `version + 1` in `withTransaction`, then `emitCommit(fresh, fresh.state)`: the metadata-only fourth commit funnel (`prior_state === state`), so the Status List and Mission Signals propagate with no new channels;
  - `effectiveAuthoritySet(record)`: approved set minus contained actions (an entry fully contained, or contained with no `actions` member, is dropped); FAST PATH: no containment returns the approved set as-is;
  - `GateError` gains `authority_contained`; `gateDerivation` refuses an empty effective set;
  - `signedStatus` scopes entries through the effective set and carries `containment_version`; `introspectionMission` carries it only when containment exists (absent-means-none).
- New `kernel/containment.ts`: `ContainmentEvidence`, `CONTAINMENT_EVIDENCE_MEDIA_TYPE`, `containmentEvidenceBytes` (JCS), `buildContainmentEvidence`; mirrors child-delegation evidence conventions.

### Effective-set funnels (all `authority_set` copy/ceiling sites)
- `adapters/provider.ts`: `decide()` grant rar + resource; child JWT-bearer redemption (lazy grant rar, AccessToken rar, response `authorization_details`, resource fallback); `mintDeferredToken` resource fallback; the txn subset gate.
- `adapters/continuation-grant.ts`: async-delegation confined-subset default + ceiling.
- `adapters/child-grant.ts`: the child-bound assertion's `authorization_details`.
- `kernel/cross-domain.ts`: audience-scoped ID-JAG projection.
- `kernel/child-delegation.ts`: the parent strict-subset ceiling (justifying-index attribution still over the approved set: subset-of-effective implies subset-of-approved).
- `kernel/attenuation.ts`: root mapping, requested-tools ceiling, `del_max_depth` derivation.
- `kernel/deferred.ts`: open + redeem subset ceilings (containment between approval and redemption refuses).

### Wire
- `POST /missions/:id/lifecycle` gains `operation: "contain"` carrying `{ event, remove }`, returning `{ id, state, version, containment_version }`; 409 on `LifecycleConflictError`; same dev service-token guard.

### Known scope boundary (follow-up PR)
The PERSISTED oidc grant rar (approval grant, async-delegation family grant) is copied at issuance time; a later contain does not rewrite the stored grant, so refresh-path `authorization_details` echo the issuance-time set until the PDP join enforces the effective set at the resource. All mint-time reads and delegation ceilings are live against the effective set, and a fully contained Mission refuses at `extraTokenClaims` via `gateDerivation`. PDP join + demo trigger land in the follow-up PR.

### Tests
- `services/authorization-server/test/containment.test.ts` (9 tests): union + idempotency; the metadata-only commit + Status List republish (bit unchanged); `authority_hash` byte-identical while `signedStatus`/introspection carry `containment_version`; mint omission; `authority_contained`; delegation surfaces (`not_strict_subset`, cross-domain, attenuation); terminal refused / suspended permitted; lifecycle endpoint end-to-end (401/400/200/idempotent/409).
- `packages/mission-signals/test/containment-commit.test.ts`: a wired `MissionSignalReceiver` APPLIES the metadata-only commit (version moves, state unchanged), mirroring the suspend-lift harness.

### Gate
`pnpm -C src typecheck` clean; `pnpm -C src test`: 46 files, 369 tests, 0 skipped (full suite incl. child-delegation, continuation, async, deferred, arop); `pnpm -C src lint` clean (2 pre-existing biome.json infos).

pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Realizes the harness draft's second mediation boundary: a default-deny egress gate in the agent's execution environment, keyed to the published execution-environment scope statement, so the demo agent has no unmediated egress path. The tool path stays MediatedHarness (unchanged; composed, not modified); the gate mediates the agent's other declared channel, the inference API. Stacked on #387 (base: feat/evidence-unification), consuming its EgressEvidence kind and emitter/scope_statement_digest base members.

## Code

- services/agent/src/harness-scope.ts: ChannelClassStatement gains optional destinations (origins), meaningful only for a mediated channel, so the published claim and the enforced allowlist are the same object. buildScopeStatement's honesty checks extend to reject destinations on a non-mediated channel. scopeDigest is now exported for evidence scope_statement_digest.
- services/agent/src/egress-gate.ts (new): EgressGate.
  - request(channel_class, destination), default-deny in order: (1) mission-state guard FIRST, fail closed, MediatedHarness.callTool's exact refusal styles (mission_not_active:state / mission_status_stale:state); (2) egress_undeclared:channel for a channel the statement does not mark mediated; (3) egress_destination_unlisted:origin for an origin outside the channel's declared set.
  - Every request (permitted AND refused) is recorded as EgressEvidence in the gate's own EvidenceStore (producer-retained, D32) with emitter role "egress" and the statement digest.
  - The constructor rejects a statement whose destinations sit on a non-mediated channel; state/status inputs mirror MediatedHarness exactly (readState, optional readStatus + now).
  - guardedFetch(inner) wraps fetch: each call is decided as an inference_api request and forwarded only on permit.
- demo/src/agent-run.ts: builds the honest single-process scope statement (inference_api mediated with destinations ["https://api.anthropic.com"]; other classes outside the claim; direct process network access named as the unmediated exclusion), constructs the gate, and creates the model via createAnthropic({ fetch: gate.guardedFetch() }). Prints permitted/refused egress counts. The key-free test path never loads this file.

This is an in-process reference realization: it mediates the egress API for a non-compromised agent and supports no containment claim (the existing in_memory -> containment_claim "none" downgrade encodes this).

## Draft (companion, builds green)

- mediated-egress: a harness MAY realize secondary-channel mediation as a harness-composed egress gate whose authoritative input is the published scope statement; a mediated channel MAY name its destination set; undeclared-channel or unlisted-destination egress MUST be refused and recorded, under the same fail-closed Mission-state rule as the resume checks; an in-process gate supports no containment claim; the gate is not the session-taint rule.
- Harness Evidence object: egress_refused joins the event_type enum; new egress member (channel_class, destination, disposition; REQUIRED for an egress_refused event), mirroring the taint member.
- SPEC_VERSIONS: harness row + notes record the gate as realized; session-taint / egress-downgrade stay deferred.

## Tests (services/agent/test/egress-gate.test.ts, key-free, no OpenFGA)

Undeclared channel refused + recorded (inner fetch never called); unlisted destination refused + recorded; declared destination permitted + recorded; suspended mission refused before any allowlist evaluation; stale-lease variant via injected now; constructor consistency rejection; guardedFetch end-to-end (permit forwards, refusal does not).

Gates: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 45 files / 372 tests, 0 skipped, against live OpenFGA; pnpm lint clean; make draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.txt kramdown-rfc OK + xml2rfc-txt OK.

Notes: evidence base fields the gate cannot know natively: authority_hash is an optional constructor input (the demo passes the mission claim's value; "unknown" otherwise) and action is recorded as egress:channel_class.

The Mission Containment follow-up the kernel PR named: the PDP join, the refresh-path conformance fix, and the demo trigger.
