pulls.body:
Closes #485.

Applies the `creation_request_id` idempotency pattern to the async-delegation token exchange, spec + code, one PR. A lost-response retry of the exchange can no longer mint a second live refresh-token family or consume a second derivation.

**Spec**
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-continuation.md` (`{#transport-async}`): `creation_request_id` REQUIRED on the async-delegation exchange (missing -> `invalid_request`), importing only the COMMON idempotency primitives from the expansion profile (key uniqueness, fingerprint comparison, reservation ownership, tombstone retention, revalidation) — a refresh-token family is not a Mission, so family delivery/recovery is defined here. Fingerprint members: `op` `async-delegation`, `iss`, `client`, `source` = the RESOLVED base Mission (never the raw token), `cnf` = the ACTING client's confirmation (this exchange deliberately re-binds the family to the acting key), `proposal` = the requested confined subset, `resource` = the target, `request_refresh_token`. Three operation states: reserved (before any side effect) -> family-created (family + single derivation count, committed atomically, family identity on the reservation) -> completed (response delivered). Recovery by state: reserved -> retryable in-progress; family-created -> RESUME delivery of the recorded family; completed -> stored response while the initial refresh token is unissued or unconsumed. Consumption PROVES delivery: once consumed, creation recovery is REFUSED with `invalid_grant` and the caller continues on the family's current refresh token — a rotating family is a single lineage (RFC 9700) and recovery never mints an independent sibling into it. Fingerprint mismatch -> `invalid_request`. Expansion normative, RFC 9700 informative.
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-expansion.md`: one clause in the creation_request_id definition acknowledging adoption by delegation-family-creating exchanges by reference, each under its own domain-separating `op` (continuation cited informatively).

**Code**
- `creation-idempotency.ts`: `CreationOp` gains `"async-delegation"`; `AsyncDelegationFingerprintInput` variant (same anchor `typ`); `advanceReserved` (family-created transition, atomic with caller accounting), `failReserved` (failed tombstone in place), `completeDelivered` (completed + delivery in one UPDATE).
- `delegation-family-store.ts`: `invalidate(grantId)` for a provisional family whose creation rolled back.
- `continuation-grant.ts` (`handleAsyncDelegationExchange`): REQUIRED id; fingerprint over parsed, verified inputs; lookup after client auth + possession, BEFORE the lifecycle/derivation gates; the reservation is acquired BEFORE any side effect (uniqueness = the concurrency funnel; the loser re-reads the winner); grant + family recorded, then the family-created transition commits atomically with the single `gateDerivation`; GateError rolls back, invalidates the provisional family, records a failed tombstone; `deliverAsyncDelegationFamily` mints the initial AT+RT and completes with the stored response (shared by first presentation and crash-resume); `recoverAsyncDelegation` revalidates (same client, recorded cnf, fingerprint) and recovers by state — including the post-consumption REFUSAL.

**Tests** (async-delegation.test.ts, +6 over baseline)
- lost-response retry: stored response verbatim, ONE family, count +1 once, recovered RT refreshes;
- A->B rotation then creation retry: REFUSED (`invalid_grant`, already-delivered); B stays the sole live head; no sibling, no recount;
- concurrent first presentations: exactly ONE family + one count; responses coherent (200) or retryable in-progress;
- crash simulation (family-created without completion): retry RESUMES delivery of the SAME family, no recount; subsequent post-consumption retry refuses;
- same id + different fingerprint -> `invalid_request`; missing id -> `invalid_request` with nothing created or counted;
- existing async fixtures (incl. aam-nightly + demo exhibit) carry the REQUIRED param.

**Gates** (re-run after the review round): `pnpm -C src typecheck` clean; `pnpm -C src test` 66 files / 600 tests passed, 0 skipped (OpenFGA up, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS); `pnpm -C src lint` exit 0; both drafts build (0 "Section ??"), `make lint` exit 0, no em-dashes, docnames `-latest`.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Review round applied in b924acf:

**1 (P1) Single-lineage recovery, no post-consumption re-mint.** Consumption of the initial refresh token proves delivery, so once it is consumed (or gone: expired, reuse-wiped) creation recovery is refused with `invalid_grant` ("the delegation was already delivered; continue with the family's current refresh token"). The fresh-RT/AT re-mint path is removed; the stored response is returned only while the initial refresh token is unissued or unconsumed. Spec rationale added: a rotating refresh-token family is a single lineage (RFC 9700); recovery MUST NOT mint an independent sibling refresh token into it. (`projectRarThroughEffective` is retained solely for the family-created RESUME path, where no token was ever issued and the initial delivery must not carry a since-contained capability.)

**2 (P1) Reservation before side effects.** `reserved -> family-created -> completed`: the durable `(client, creation_request_id)` reservation is acquired first (uniqueness is the concurrency funnel; a concurrent loser re-reads the winner — in-progress, resume, or stored response); the family grant is then created and its identity recorded on the reservation atomically with the single `gateDerivation` (`advanceReserved`, one kernel-db transaction); delivery marks completed with the response. Crash after family-created: the retry resumes delivery of the recorded family (never a second family). Derivation-gate rejection: the transition rolls back, the provisional family is invalidated (grant destroyed, family row terminal), and a failed tombstone replays the refusal.

**3 (P2) Spec ownership.** `{#transport-async}` now imports only the common idempotency primitives from expansion (key uniqueness, fingerprint comparison, reservation ownership, tombstones, revalidation) and defines refresh-family delivery and recovery itself: the three states with the crash-resume rule, stored-response-while-unconsumed, and consumed => delivered => refused. The "fresh refresh token within the same family" text is removed.

Tests: post-consumption retry now expects refusal with the rotated head as sole live lineage; added concurrent-first-presentations (ONE family + one count) and crash-resume (same family, no recount). Full gate re-run: typecheck clean, 66 files / 600 tests / 0 skipped, lint 0; both drafts rebuild clean (0 "Section ??", make lint 0, no em-dashes).

pulls.title: Expansion: recognize independent continuation; keep atomic replacement
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Rules #241 per the revised proposal on that issue (second-round review accepted in full).

**Retained**: atomic replacement as the only succession this document defines. The requirement is a single logical serialized commit (predecessor state check, successor creation and activation, `predecessor`/`successor` links, `superseded` transition, idempotency reservation), justified by the exactly-one lineage invariant: it is what keeps the Approver's consented word "replaces" true under concurrency, keeps supersession issuer-authoritative rather than client-asserted, and feeds the distinct `superseded` state downstream. The simple-base/experimental-atomic inversion is rejected, not deferred.

**Added**: a "Continuing Under an Independently Approved Mission" section recognizing the lightweight path as an operational pattern that is not expansion, succession, or replacement:
- properties derived from the independence of its two commits: both-active interval vs revoke-first availability gap; lifecycle as backstop when revocation fails or is omitted; ordinary token residuals, no rebinding; Child Mission terminal cascade with fresh child creation under the new Mission; ordinary harness stop behavior, no continuation handoff; no exactly-one guarantee, not grant-bound;
- `related_to` governance: issuer-recorded correlation metadata, no client request parameter (`mission_intent` is task-only), authenticated and authorized input, same-issuer resolution (cross-issuer needs a structured extension), anti-oracle handling for unauthorized/absent/unknown references, "related work only";
- `predecessor` reserved for replacement expansion (MUST NOT), and the pattern satisfies no successor-requiring profile — containment restoration in particular.

**Management companion (finding 4 follow-up from the issue review)**: the atomic-transition commit list now includes the validated `replacement_s256` for `superseded` terminations, so the recorded replacement is part of the same commit its reason names.

AAuth supersession is the binding-specific precedent for non-atomic replacement activation (analogous, not identical); cross-binding coherence keeps the lightweight pattern substrate-shaped and the atomic strengthening OAuth-bound.

Closes #241 when merged.

Validation: expansion and management render (xml2rfc exit 0), make lint passes, manifest checker 36 drafts no drift, git diff --check clean.

pulls.title: Mission Approval Governance: the Approval Governance Record as the 37th draft (#240)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes the amended ruling on #240 (approval authority as first-class governance state), incorporating all eight findings of the external review of the original proposal. **Posted for review; do not merge without explicit approval.**

**New companion: `draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance`** (Approval-time group, Advanced rung, stable dependencies only, ceremony-independent). Defines the **Approval Governance Record**, the reshaped successor of the deferred-approval companion's experimental Approval Decision Set:

- Members: `approval_event_id`; `mission` binding (`issuer`, `intent_hash`, `authority_hash`); `approval_policy` as `{id, version, digest}` with the referenced policy version or an immutable snapshot retained for the Mission's audit horizon (threshold/quorum/veto/SoD semantics live in the policy, summaries are advisory); `assertions[]` (id, principal, kind human/service/policy, decision including denials, time, authority/authentication reference); `evaluation` (decision, time, contributing assertion ids); `envelope` (issuer-signed JWS over the JCS bytes of the record with the envelope removed, five-step byte-equality verification, `typ`-pinned, unsupported formats rejected).
- Security core: every contributing assertion authenticated, bound to its approval event and Authority Set, and policy-authorized; denials and vetoes recorded; **exactly one assertion matches the accountable `approver`** (a policy-authority Approver satisfies it with a `policy` assertion per the approval-spectrum doctrine); the evaluated record commits **atomically with Mission activation and failure prevents activation**; committed records immutable; the two-phase framing is explicit (pre-commit the record is part of the approval decision, post-commit it is evidence).
- **Recording triggers** as observable predicates profiles cite: approver differs from subject; more than one contributing principal; a non-human assertion contributes; a threshold, veto, or SoD rule is evaluated; assertion validation requires authority standing outside the Mission record. Direct self-approval by one authenticated human stays the degenerate case.
- Boundaries: off tokens, protocol messages, and enforcement projections (the RFC 9396 boundary); ARAP action-time approval is a different layer; R5's single accountable approver unchanged.

**Consumer rewiring:**
- *Deferred-approval companion*: the Decision Set section becomes a pointer (same anchor) to the ceremony-independent record; conformance and security text follow; the document keeps its deferred-specific status and substrate posture.
- *MAS Enterprise Mission Authority Profile*: new **Approval governance** bullet requiring the record under the triggers, committed atomically, retained for the audit horizon.
- *Consent evidence*: `co_approvals`/`approval_authority` become a declared **deliberately partial presentation** (never "the projection"); new `approval_governance_digest` carries the AGR's record digest, verified during evidence integrity checking; `policy_version` renamed to `approval_policy_version` (disclosed breaking rename), ending the collision with the core's derivation-policy member and deleting the conflated possession rationale.
- *Audit profile*: evidence-type table gains the approval-governance row (`application/mission-approval-governance+json`, producer `issuer`).
- *Plumbing*: README catalog + adoption order, architecture document map, family manifest 36 → 37.

**Core untouched** per the published-core convention; the stale Single Accountable Approver pointer is filed as #499 for the next core revision batch.

Validation: all five touched drafts + the new draft build clean, lint 0, manifest checker 37 no drift, whitespace clean; zero "Decision Set" residuals outside the core; zero em-dashes.

Closes #240.


## Review round 2 (commit b289134)

Request-changes findings applied:

1. **Policy digest preimage is reproducible**: the issuance profile's integrity-anchor envelope with `typ` `mission-approval-policy` (domain separation), `iss` the Mission issuer (replay binding), and a `value` of the snapshot's `content_type` plus base64url content bytes, JCS-canonicalized; snapshot bytes and media type join the audit-horizon retention obligation.
2. **One byte sequence**: the **record digest** (JCS canonical bytes of the complete record, `envelope` included) is the single value audit registration hashes and `approval_governance_digest` equals; consent-evidence verification gains step 8 (retrieve, verify envelope and Mission binding, recompute, compare; mismatch is an integrity failure, unavailability within retention is an audit failure).
3. **Approved-only records**: `evaluation.decision` carries `approved` only; a denying evaluation creates no Mission and no committed record, dissent lives in retained negative assertions, and a wholly declined approval's surface is consent evidence's declined outcome.
4. **Testable agreement**: member-by-member mapping (each `co_approvals` entry corresponds to exactly one `human` assertion with equal principal/decision/time; omission permitted, fabrication or alteration an integrity failure; `service`/`policy` assertions never presented; consent `approver` equals the accountable assertion's principal; `approval_authority`/`approval_policy_version` MUST equal the AGR values when present). The AGR governs on any disagreement.

pulls.title: Expansion/management: second-round independent-continuation corrections
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #498, addressing a second-round review of the merged content: one blocking contradiction and three specification gaps.

## 1. `replacement_s256` requiredness (management, high)

The request field said MAY, the Person path said the PS SHOULD require it, and the atomic transition committed it unconditionally for `superseded`. Resolved in the strict direction: **`replacement_s256` is REQUIRED whenever `reason=superseded`**, for every caller class. A `superseded` request without it fails as a missing member with `invalid_request`; the uniform-failure rule now says *unresolvable* (referenced mission) rather than *absent*, removing the member-absence ambiguity. The Person-path same-approver verification stays SHOULD, unchanged in strength.

## 2. `related_to` creation-time and immutability rules (expansion)

The issuer MUST authorize and resolve the reference (own namespace) **before the new Mission's approval completes**, MUST set `related_to` **atomically when the Mission record is created**, and MUST NOT add or change it afterward. Late linking and mutable correlation metadata are out.

## 3. Anti-oracle behavior specified (expansion)

An unresolved or unauthorized reference is **never recorded**. Deployment policy chooses uniform rejection or silent omission (proceed without the relationship), applied consistently across requests; neither behavior discloses whether the referenced Mission exists.

## 4. Conformance and privacy coverage (expansion)

- Conformance now has two targets: the existing expansion-capable Mission Issuer, plus an optional **`related_to` correlation** target for an issuer that records the member without adjudicating expansion, defined by the enumerated {{independent-continuation}} obligations.
- New **Related-work correlation** privacy subsection: `related_to` correlates independently approved tasks like the `predecessor` chain correlates a succession, without the authority linkage; same audience-scoping guidance applies.

## Validation

Both drafts build (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc), `check-family-manifest` passes (36 drafts, no drift), `git diff --check` clean.

pulls.title: Clarify that authority_hash is not a subset proof
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

- distinguish the complete Authority Set commitment from an RS-local containment proof
- state normatively that a subset-only RS treats `authority_hash` as audit context, not enforcement input
- describe the complete security mechanism as approval-time commitment, correct AS projection, signed token issuance, and RS enforcement

This is the unconditional core-draft clarification identified in #501. It does not select or define an optional Authority Set retrieval or selective-proof mechanism.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `make SKIP_SED_CHECK=1 MD_PRE= draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.html`

The `MD_PRE` override avoids the repository's known BSD `sed` limitation during local rendering; CI uses GNU `sed` and exercises the normal build.

Addresses the core-draft clarification in #501; the optional local-verification design remains open.


## Review disclosure

The Resource Server Enforcement hunk upgrades previously descriptive language to conformance language: a Resource Server holding only a narrowed token MUST treat `mission.authority_hash` as an audit correlator, not an enforcement input, and MUST NOT treat it as a cryptographic subset proof. This is the one normative delta in the clarification, disclosed deliberately; the old text already asserted the property descriptively, and the upgrade forecloses the misread #501 identified.

Post-review tightening (second commit): the `mission` claim table entry returns to house style (the negative property lives normatively at Resource Server Enforcement, which the entry cites), and the authority-commitment paragraph separates the full-set holder's two operations (recompute the commitment to confirm the set, then apply the subset rule).

pulls.title: fix(core): reconcile substrate companion description with kernel refactor (#440)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Resolves #440.

The core described the substrate companion as "a substrate-neutral statement of the Mission model, generalizing it across non-OAuth authorization substrates". After the substrate's capability refactor (#428) and follow-ups (#438, #439), that inverts the actual relationship: the substrate is a standalone binding-neutral contextual-governance kernel, and this document's Mission model is its OAuth-native instantiation.

Two informative sites in `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md` only; no normative change, no reference reclassification (the substrate I-D stays informative).

1. Related-work paragraph (GNAP): the Mission model "is a candidate binding onto that substrate" becomes "is the OAuth-native instantiation of a binding-neutral contextual-governance kernel that admits a candidate binding onto that substrate; this document does not define one."

2. Companion-profiles paragraph: the sentence above is replaced with the issue's proposed wording: "A binding-neutral contextual-governance kernel, of which this document's Mission model is the OAuth-native instantiation, is specified separately and is out of scope for this document."

Verification:
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt` renders OK, 0 occurrences of "Section ??"
- `make lint` exit 0

pulls.title: Runtime: reconciliation ownership, non-active boundary, identifier survival
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes #315.

States the three boundary conditions the existing machinery implies at the intersection of reconciliation and termination. No new mechanism, no new evidence object.

## 1. Unknown outcomes get an owner and a deadline

The Enforcement Scope Statement already names the component responsible for orphaned-evidence and sequence-gap detection. That component's duty now includes **driving each unresolved outcome to committed or failed within the reconciliation window**, and its alerting obligation covers any outcome still unknown at the deadline. The owner is the already-declared component; the deadline is the already-declared window.

## 2. Reconciliation resolves, never executes

Once the Mission is non-active, reconciliation MAY resolve an in-flight outcome to committed or failed and MUST NOT admit a new effect under that Mission. The line is drawn without touching the TTL-first permit design: an action already executing follows the existing run-to-completion rule, and executing-PEP reverification still needs no Mission-state re-check.

## 3. Identifier state survives termination

Consumed and reserved decision identifiers and idempotency claims persist across Mission lifecycle transitions for at least the reconciliation window and any declared tombstone horizon. Termination does not erase them, so a post-termination retry resolves against the recorded claim rather than double-executing.

## 4. Failure-mode table row

One row for the non-active-with-unresolved-outcome case, so a reviewer working the timeout-after-the-permit scenario finds the rule where they would look.

## Validation

kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc build OK, `check-family-manifest` passes (36 drafts, no drift), `git diff --check` clean.

pulls.title: Runtime: evidence determines outcomes; indeterminate claims stay non-reusable
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Second-round corrections to the #315 boundary text merged in #505: two high findings and one structural one, all confirmed against the cited family texts.

## 1. Evidence, never the deadline, determines the result

The merged text required driving each unresolved outcome to "committed or failed," which could force a falsely synthesized terminal record for a genuinely indeterminate distributed outcome, enabling unsafe retry or compensation. It also used orchestration vocabulary where Execution Evidence vocabulary belongs. Now: the declared component MUST actively reconcile each unresolved outcome within the window (query the resource, match evidence) and records the outcome the evidence establishes (`completed`, `failed`, or `suppressed`); an outcome it cannot establish **stays undetermined-outcome**, is escalated under the declared alerting obligation, and is never synthesized into a terminal result. This matches the runtime-evidence orphan classification and orchestration's rule that `unknown` remains unknown.

## 2. Unresolved claims never become reusable through time alone

Retention "for at least the reconciliation window" plus the claim table's expired-past-horizon-treated-as-new row could re-authorize a still-indeterminate effect after a long suspension. Now: when the window closes on an undetermined outcome, the claim converts to a **non-reusable indeterminate tombstone**, retained for at least the declared idempotency horizon and released only by an evidence-recorded operational resolution, never by expiry into a fresh claim. The claim table gains an `indeterminate` row (`duplicate_suppressed`, terminal; resolution is operational, never a new permit), and the expired row states an indeterminate tombstone does not expire into it.

## 3. Failure-mode table keeps its actors

The added row assigned bookkeeping work to the reconciliation component inside a table whose conformance scope is "a PDP or PEP MUST behave as follows." The row is removed; the rule lives in the reconciliation section, and the existing `Mission not active` row now carries the pointer: "Refuse; work already initiated reconciles under the evidence section, never re-executes."

The positive rule from #505 is unchanged: after a Mission becomes non-active, reconciliation may record the outcome of work already initiated and must not admit a new effect under that Mission.

## Validation

kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc build OK, `check-family-manifest` passes (37 drafts, no drift), `git diff --check` clean.

pulls.title: feat(506): Mission Intent Submission envelope + Intent Submission Evidence intake (code)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## #506 CODE cluster — Mission Intent Submission envelope

Implements the code half of the #506 design lock (rev-2 + orchestrator decisions), coordinated with SPEC PR #509 (member names, `submission_evidence` record member, fingerprint `evidence` member, error codes). Includes the review-round fixes: two-stage evidence types, end-to-end verified-fact propagation, and non-empty `evidence`.

### Error-code contract (aligned with #509)
- `invalid_request`: envelope STRUCTURAL failures — bare old shape, unknown envelope member, entry not an object / no `type`, EMPTY `evidence` array, count/size bounds.
- `invalid_mission_intent_evidence` (core-registered, `InvalidMissionIntentEvidence`): evidence-type dispatch failures — unsupported `type` (every presented type on the SHIPPED registry, which is empty), an entry failing its type's stage-1 schema or stage-2 verification, and a policy-REQUIRED type absent (anti-downgrade).

### Two-stage evidence types (`kernel/intent.ts`)
- `IntentSubmissionEvidenceType` = `{ validate(entry): void; verify(input): Promise<Record<string, JsonValue>> }`:
  - Stage 1 `validate`: SYNCHRONOUS structural parsing at envelope parse (closed per-type schema, after non-empty/count/size bounds) — so the creation-fingerprint input is shape-valid.
  - Stage 2 `verify`: ASYNC, receives `IntentSubmissionEvidenceVerifyInput` = `{ entry, intentHash (provisional), issuer, presenter { clientId, cnf? }, now, requestContext? }` and returns the NORMALIZED recordable facts (the nested `facts` object). `verifyIntentSubmissionEvidence` wraps each fact as `{ type, artifact_hash (anchor typ mission-intent-evidence over the entry as presented), verified_at, facts }`; ALL failures map to `invalid_mission_intent_evidence`.
- Registration API: `registerIntentSubmissionEvidenceType` / `unregisterIntentSubmissionEvidenceType`; `INTENT_SUBMISSION_EVIDENCE_TYPES` stays the readonly view and ships EMPTY (tests register fixtures locally).
- Anti-downgrade hook: `requiredEvidenceTypesFor(opts, client)` = global `requiredIntentEvidenceTypes` (buildAuthorizationServer/AdapterOptions) ∪ the client's registered `required_intent_evidence_types` metadata (new extraClientMetadata property); resolved BEFORE derivation on every carrier; a required type absent refuses; success without evidence never satisfies a requirement.

### End-to-end fact propagation (per creation flow)
- **PAR/interactive**: stage 2 runs at PAR push (refuses bad evidence early), re-runs from the interaction's immutable pushed params at approval RENDER (facts are input to `renderApprovalPage` — new "Verified intent provenance" section, normalized facts, never raw artifacts; ready for the spec cluster's rendering-commitment digest) and at `decide()` (same TOCTOU rule as proposal re-derivation) whose facts land via `kernel.approve({ submissionEvidence })`.
- **Template dispatch**: verified in `handleMissionDispatchGrant` (presenter = authenticated dispatcher), landed via `DispatchInput.submissionEvidence` -> instance record.
- **Child creation**: verified in `handleChildCreationExchange` AFTER the idempotency recovery lookup, landed via `CreateChildInput.submissionEvidence` -> child record.
- **Expansion incl. deferred**: verified at INITIATION after the recovery lookup; facts persisted on the deferral row (`submission_evidence_json`, new column) across the window; redemption passes them to `createExpansion` (`ExpansionInput.submissionEvidence`) -> successor record. Redemption does NOT re-verify freshness.
- **Recovery ordering (both exchanges)**: the completed-operation recovery lookup PRECEDES stage-2 re-verification — an artifact that expired after completion cannot break recovery; a FRESH operation still verifies.
- Presenter conjunction inputs: exchanges pass `{ clientId, cnf: { jkt } }`; PAR/dispatch pass the authenticated client.

### Tests (67 files / 632 tests, all green)
- `test/submission-envelope.test.ts` (23): envelope parse + anchor stability; stage-1 rules incl. registered-type closed schema and EMPTY-array refusal (flipped per review); stage-2 unit coverage (verifier ctx, fact normalization, failure mapping, required-absent anti-downgrade); END-TO-END: test evidence type via PAR -> "Verified intent provenance" rendered -> approve -> record `submission_evidence` carries the verifier-returned facts (request-derived, `bound_intent_hash` === recorded `intent_hash`), anchors unchanged; wire anti-downgrade on a second AS with global required types (absent => `invalid_mission_intent_evidence`, present => 201); fingerprint mismatch on evidence change.
- `test/creation-idempotency.test.ts`: recovery-before-reverification ordering (completed child recovers with an expired artifact; fresh creation_request_id refuses).
- `test/expansion-endpoint.test.ts`: deferred-window persistence (facts verified at initiation land on the successor; window expiry does not re-verify; failing artifact at initiation refuses before the deferral opens).
- All wire `mission_intent` fixtures across 12 test files + demo/exhibit re-plumbed to the envelope (first round).

### Gate (full, re-run after review fixes)
- OpenFGA v1.18.1 SERVING; running container's CA in `certs/` + `src/certs/` (gitignored); `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` at process start.
- `pnpm -C src typecheck`: clean.
- `pnpm -C src test`: **67 files passed, 632 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `pnpm -C src lint`: exit 0 (two pre-existing biome config infos).

No draft/PLAN/SPEC_VERSIONS edits; no merges. Refs #506.

pulls.title: feat(core+companions): Mission Intent Submission envelope + Intent Submission Evidence hook (#506)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Implements the SPEC cluster of #506 per the rev-2 issue body and the design lock (baseline provenance commitment; "Intent Submission Evidence" naming; Intent Admission profile deferred).

## FOR THE CODE CLUSTER: envelope member names + error codes

**Envelope** (the `mission_intent` parameter VALUE, everywhere the parameter or its equivalent claim/member appears):

- Top level closed to exactly: **`intent`** (REQUIRED, the semantic Mission Intent object) and **`evidence`** (OPTIONAL, non-empty array of typed entries).
- Every evidence entry: JSON object with REQUIRED **`type`** (collision-resistant name); the owning type spec defines all other members. No generic members exist.
- `intent_hash` commits exactly the `intent` object, never the envelope or `evidence`.

**Error codes:**

- **`invalid_request`**: envelope structural failures. Unknown envelope top-level member; the old bare-Intent shape (its `goal` etc. are unknown envelope members); `evidence` entry not a JSON object or missing `type`; envelope/intent/evidence size + count bounds exceeded; verification-cost bound exceeded.
- **`invalid_mission_intent_evidence`** (NEW, IANA OAuth Extensions Error registration in core): entry whose `type` the AS does not support; entry failing its type's validation/verification (including presenter `client_id`/`cnf` mismatch and intent_hash mismatch); a policy-required evidence type absent from the submission.
- MAS equivalent: **`invalid_intent_evidence`** (new row in the MAS error table); envelope structural failures map to the existing `invalid_mission_intent`.
- With no evidence types registered this cycle, EVERY presented entry is unknown => refused. That is the correct shipped state.

**Record member:** `submission_evidence` (OPTIONAL array on the Mission Record): each element carries exactly `type`, `artifact_hash` (integrity anchor, `typ` `mission-intent-evidence`, over the entry as presented), `verified_at`, and a NESTED **`facts`** object holding the type-owned verified output facts (no collisions with the common members). Elements preserve the submission's `evidence` order (one canonical form). Record-trusted provenance metadata, outside all anchors (not on the `mission` claim).

**Review round (547ebc6):** (1) `evidence`, when present, MUST be non-empty; an empty array `[]` is refused `invalid_request` (omission expresses absence). (2) Rendering commitment covers provenance: consent-evidence gains `submission_provenance_hash` (anchor `typ` `mission-submission-provenance` over the `submission_evidence` array, JCS+SHA-256), covered by `consent_rendering_hash`; raw artifacts stay out of the disclosure. (3) Idempotent recovery: completed-operation recovery returns the recorded outcome without re-verifying evidence freshness. (4) All three MAS examples wrapped in the envelope.

**Fingerprint:** the D69 creation fingerprint (expansion + child creation) gains **`evidence`** (the parsed array, when present); `intent` is now the semantic `intent` object of the envelope. Same `creation_request_id` with different evidence => fingerprint mismatch => `invalid_request`.

## Per-draft changes

- **core** `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`: Submission-envelope definition at `mission_intent` ({#submission-via-par}), closed-top-levels + bounded-size rules extended, envelope example; new section **Intent Submission Evidence** ({#intent-submission-evidence}) with the full rule set (reject-never-ignore; type owns members; policy-input-never-authority; required-evidence anti-downgrade resolved before derivation; evidence binds one exact `intent_hash` across shaping/revision; presenter conjunction; verification-cost bounds; 8-step processing order; fingerprint cross-ref; naming contrast with emitted Evidence incl. the audit companion's Mission Evidence Base); `submission_evidence` record member with the HONEST baseline statement (record-trust, not verifiable association; the anchor `typ` extension point named as where a future provenance_hash would live); terminology entries; extensibility bullet; conformance bullet; privacy line (evidence artifacts can carry personal data); IANA: `mission_intent` ref updated + `invalid_mission_intent_evidence` registered; e2e example wrapped in the envelope; Document History breaking-change entry (carriage-breaking, **anchor-stable**: committed values, recorded anchors, test vectors unchanged).
- **expansion**: `mission_intent` param = the envelope; fingerprint `intent` re-scoped to the semantic object + new `evidence` member; `related_to` "task-only" phrasing corrected; example shows `{"intent":{...}}`.
- **child-delegation**: `mission_intent` param = the envelope (one sentence); example updated.

pulls.title: Core: free-text Intent members never carry machine semantics into derivation
pulls.author: mcguinness

Executes #313's approved recommendation with all four reviewer amendments, on explicit go-ahead per the published-core convention. Two edit sites, 23 inserted lines, no new members and no new mechanism.

**Site 1, `constraints` member**: "These inform derivation and consent rendering" (the draft's only "inform derivation" occurrence, and the sentence the external review flagged) becomes: disclosure and audit context, rendered to the Approver beside the derived Authority Set, never parsed by the AS for machine semantics, pointing at the derivation boundary.

**Site 2, {{authorization-derivation}}**, after the existing "describe and bound the task but grant no authority" paragraph, the reviewer's normative core with the amendments applied:

- **Uniform prose class** (amendment 3): `goal`, `constraints`, and `success_criteria` together; `success_criteria`'s existing member-level MUST NOT is untouched and now has the section-level rule beside it.
- **Scoped MUST NOT** (amendment 1): binds in the narrowing and template modes this profile defines; a deployment deriving from prose does so under the existing generative local-policy carve-out, outside both conforming modes for that step. The carve-out text itself is unchanged.
- **Both carrier surfaces** (amendment 2): the top-level `authorization_details` proposal with Common Constraints, type-specific constraints, and understood collision-resistant deployment extensions; or the Intent's `controls` plus the template mapping keyed on `purpose`/`resources`, stated as a lookup over structured values yielding structured candidate entries.
- **No rule-author-reads-prose framing** (amendment 4): execution-time mapping is lookup only; the human consistency check is the Approver reading the rendered prose beside the derived Authority Set, stated as never a machine enforcement mechanism.

D67 carriage is respected throughout (the proposal rides top-level `authorization_details`; no `proposed_authority` references). The generative-provenance question stays a follow-on per the issue's open question 3; #309 restates the boundary in the companion guidance and is tracked there.

Validation: core renders, lint 0, manifest checker 37 no drift, whitespace clean.

Closes #313.

## Review round 2 (commit 3449ab4)

Request-changes findings applied; the PR now spans the core plus the two companions so the family never publishes the rule beside guidance teaching its violation.

1. **Universal boundary, one strength everywhere**: the MUST NOT is no longer mode-scoped; the AS never parses `goal`, `constraints`, or `success_criteria` for machine semantics, period. The generative local-policy extension becomes model assistance over structured inputs and loses "from the Intent's free text"; NL-to-structure is the shaper's job before admission (core now cites the shaping companion informatively). The `constraints` member, the boundary paragraph, and the "constrain what the AS MAY derive" sentence all state the same rule at the same strength, with the structured/prose split explicit (structured members constrain mechanically; prose members bound through the Approver's refusal; none widens).

The canonicalization test vector is untouched (hashing only, no derived set beside it).

pulls.title: Core: name the three authority sources and the subject-representation discipline
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes #316, implementing the recommendation recorded on the issue. Core-only, no new members, no wire or IANA change.

## What it adds

**New Overview subsection `Authority Sources`** beside the Principal Model, naming the three sources: **user-delegated** (a delegating person's own authority), **service-owned** (a workload's own provisioned authority), **organizational** (explicitly governed policy with a named accountable owner). The source axis is explicitly composed with, not conflated with, `approval_basis`: the source names whose authority the approval draws on, the basis records how drawing on it was activated, and any source may activate through `direct` or a companion standing-consent basis.

**The subject-representation discipline**, uniform across sources:

- the accountable principal is `approver` (= `approval_basis.consent_principal`), never inferred from the token `sub`;
- `sub` carries a delegating person only in the user-delegated source; a service-owned or organizational Mission MUST record the workload or organizational principal as `subject` and MUST NOT record a human principal in its place (the service-account-wearing-a-Mission anti-pattern), with the injective mapping of the approval event unchanged, so the principal denotes itself and impersonates nobody;
- the actor model is invariant: `client_id` names the Agent, delegates ride `act`.

**Three light supporting touches**: the Subject terminology entry admits the workload/organizational principal; Applicability states the machine-to-machine exclusion is the credential-lifetime-equals-task-lifetime equality, not the absence of a human (a workload's durable multi-step task is in scope as a service-owned Mission), with "durable, user-approved task" widened to "durable, approved task" for consistency; approval event step 2 gains one sentence that a workload or organizational Subject changes nothing about establishment or mapping.

## Open-question dispositions (from the issue)

1. **Vocabulary**: kept the title "Authority Sources" with the composition sentence distinguishing it from `approval_basis`; avoided the word "ceiling" in the service-owned definition since core already uses it for authority-proposal ceilings.
2. **Applicability clarification**: included here; it is the sentence most likely to be misread today.
3. **No new terminology entry** for organizational principal; the subsection's usage plus the widened Subject entry suffice.
4. **Disjoint from #499**: the Single Accountable Approver section is untouched.

## Validation

kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc build OK, `check-family-manifest` passes (37 drafts, no drift), `git diff --check` clean.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Second-round review applied in 1b3a8cc. The reviewer posed the fork: explanatory-only taxonomy, or normative with recorded provenance. Resolved **normative**: the explanatory model would delete the anti-borrowing MUST that is #316's entire payload, and the issue's no-new-members non-goal was conditional on existing members carrying the distinction, which the review showed they cannot (neither `subject` {iss,sub} nor `approval_basis.type` records whose authority; the axes compose).

- **P1 source-never-bounds**: new approval step 3: establish the source from trusted configuration or authenticated governance state (never client assertion); verify the Approver may activate it; verify the derived Authority Set lies within it; fail closed. Activation authority explicitly distinct from personal possession.
- **P1 not-recorded**: new immutable `authority_source` record member (`type`, plus `policy` {id, version, digest} for `organizational`, reusing the Approval Governance shape). Provenance like `approval_basis`: outside both anchors, never on access tokens. Rendering identifies the source; a pre-decision source change forces re-evaluation and re-render.
- **P1 architecture contradiction**: the Approver-ceiling element is now the established authority-source ceiling; approval activates authority the source already holds and grants nothing beyond it.
- **P2 sub semantics**: the workload or organizational principal MUST be an authorization subject the AS recognizes as a resource owner in its own right (RFC 9068), not merely the task's beneficiary. Issuance-grant PAR carriage scoped to user-delegated Missions; service-owned and organizational grants redeem directly.
- **P2 sweep**: applicability rewritten so ordinary M2M credentials are an instance of the lifetime-equality exclusion, not a categorical peer; Agent definition now acts "for the Mission's Subject".

All three drafts build; manifest and whitespace checks pass.

pulls.title: Core: a Mission never carries a third-party data subject's consent
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes #344's approved recommendation with all five review amendments, on explicit go-ahead per the published-core convention. One new Privacy Considerations subsection (`{#third-party-data-subjects}`, between Intent Retention and Record Access, beside the personal-data-sink paragraph it extends) plus one forward pointer from the `goal` member. 39 inserted lines; no new role, member, or mechanism.

The amendments as landed:

1. **Enforcement boundary, not a deployment location**: the resource domain's disclosure policy MUST be satisfied in its own lane, wherever the deployment evaluates it (RS, gateway, PDP, or an AS acting for the domain), and access MUST be refused while required evidence is absent or invalid. Nothing requires the RS process itself to gather claims.
2. **No legal conclusions**: approval is not *by itself* evidence of a data subject's consent or other required legal basis; whether a basis is required and what satisfies it is deployment and legal policy outside the protocol. The "processes under its own legal basis" framing is gone.
3. **Generic examples**: "claims gathering, a resource-domain consent artifact." No UMA reference.
4. **All four surfaces in minimization**: Intent prose (`goal`, `constraints`), `proposed_authority` identifiers, record concentration ({{record-access}}), and the unsalted anchors' confirmation channel; resource-scoped or pseudonymous references SHOULD be used, with opacity named as minimization, not anonymity.
5. **No Non-Goals duplication**: one normative home in Privacy Considerations, one short forward pointer from the `goal` definition, nothing else.

Also per the review: the anchors stay unsalted (the confirmation channel argues for minimization, not for salting reproducible commitments), and the erasure-record pointer states it records an erasure, neither performing one nor overriding retention law.

Validation: core renders, lint 0, manifest checker 37 no drift, whitespace clean. Applied on current main (post-#508/#509 envelope carriage; no interaction, the record members and `goal` definition are unchanged by that move).

Closes #344.

## Review round 2 (commit 2564c5f)

1. **Consent vs evidence of consent (P1)**: the absolute prohibition conflicted with the merged Intent Submission Evidence model, whose record member retains verified facts about "an admission or consent decision." The rule now distinguishes: Mission approval and Mission authority MUST NOT be treated as the data subject's consent, while the record MAY retain a verified consent reference as `submission_evidence`, provenance and policy input only, validated independently by the resource domain under its own authoritative disclosure policy. Three-lane discipline preserved: evidence never becomes authority or bypasses resource-policy re-evaluation.
2. **Open surface inventory (P2)**: the minimization rule now covers every Intent, proposal, authority, and recorded-evidence member with the named fields as examples: prose members (`goal`, `constraints`, `success_criteria`), `purpose`, `resources`, deployment-defined `controls`, type-owned proposal members, derived Authority Set entries that reach tokens, and `submission_evidence` facts including a consent reference.
3. **Erasure precondition (P2)**: the transparency-side pointer now applies where the approval-event evidence was registered under the audit profile, and explicitly leaves the operational Mission record and its audit-horizon retention floor untouched.

pulls.title: Core/runtime: commitment-mechanism underpinnings (I-JSON, hash agility, digest species)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes #284, implementing the recommendation recorded on the issue. Core + runtime in one PR; no anchor recomputation, no breaking changes, no new endpoints or registries.

## Core: new Commitment Mechanisms section (beside Canonicalization Rules)

**Digest species taxonomy.** The family commits to bytes in three ways, now named so every commitment site classifies itself: **envelope anchors** (the domain-separated, issuer-bound envelope), **canonical-object digests** (JCS over a normalized object, no envelope, e.g. `parameter_digest`), **raw-octet digests** (exact octets, no canonicalization, e.g. `artifact_digest`). Prefix/agility rules bind all three; I-JSON binds the two JSON species; the envelope and `typ` discipline binds envelope anchors alone.

**I-JSON.** Every committed JSON value and envelope MUST satisfy RFC 7493; the **party computing or verifying** a commitment rejects non-conformant input before canonicalization (duplicate members, numbers JCS cannot serialize exactly, invalid Unicode). This closes all three gaps behind finding 1: actor scope (the old duty bound only "the AS"), value scope (the number rule covered only Common Constraint values), and strings (previously unaddressed). RFC 8785 security considerations inherited; the Common Constraints decimal-string convention stays as the stricter overlay.

**Hash agility, stated once.** The algorithm prefix is the agility mechanism: `sha-256` is MTI and the only algorithm defined; a new algorithm enters only via a new prefix defined by a referencing specification, names drawn from the RFC 6920 Named Information registry (name source only, keeping the family's registry-free posture and base64url form); verifiers MUST reject unrecognized prefixes and MUST NOT treat them as `sha-256`. The rule's object is broadened from "an integrity anchor" to **every prefixed digest defined by a document citing the section**, so `parameter_digest`, `artifact_digest`, and companion anchors inherit by reference instead of the current 4-of-24 restatement pattern. "Algorithm agility is future work" is gone; an informative dual-anchor transition sketch replaces it.

## Runtime

- `parameter_digest` self-classifies as a canonical-object digest inheriting I-JSON and prefix rejection from the core statement (one sentence, no second canonicalization).
- Operation Profiles MUST fix **at least one digest test vector per operation** (normalized parameter object + digest), so PDP/PEP normalization drift surfaces at profile adoption rather than as a fail-closed outage (finding 3).

## Open-question dispositions (from the issue)

1. RFC 6920 as **name source only** (recommended option adopted).
2. Raw-bytes digest option for `parameter_digest`: **not adopted** — it changes the TOCTOU story (the executing PEP recomputes over normalized parameters, not relayed bytes); the raw-octet species exists for artifacts, and an Operation Profile remains the seam if a deployment ever needs it.
3. Common Constraints numeric rule **kept as the stricter overlay** with one cross-reference.
4. `artifact_digest`: the species taxonomy itself states the I-JSON exemption (binds JSON species only); no work-products edit.
5. Existing test vectors verified I-JSON conformant (plain ASCII, small integers) — the new MUST changes no published anchor value.

Companion tidy-ups (consent-evidence wording, mandate/work-products restatement conversion) deliberately deferred to ride future edits per the sketch.

## Validation

Both drafts build (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc), `check-family-manifest` passes (37 drafts, no drift), `git diff --check` clean.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Review round applied in 5e8e43a; all four findings taken, 17 files.

**1 (blocking, transition sketch)**: deleted. Replaced by the future-algorithm contract: a specification introducing a new prefix MUST define the carrier and schema of any parallel commitment, the equivalence binding to the same object, producer behavior, verifier selection/downgrade behavior when recognition sets differ, and the transition procedure. The section now also states plainly that every current carrier holds a single prefixed string.

**2 (blocking, numeric rule)**: restated as the actual input domain: no duplicate member names; string data valid Unicode, free of I-JSON-prohibited surrogate/noncharacter code points, preserved unchanged; number data representable as a finite IEEE 754 binary64 ({{RFC8785}} s3.1). Added the data-model sentence: the commitment is over the parsed I-JSON data value, not the source lexeme's spelling or excess precision; profiles needing exact decimal or large-integer semantics use strings or a stricter domain, as Common Constraints already does.

**3 (major, honest scope)**: took option 1, the full companion pass, grep-derived and agent-surveyed across all 37 drafts. Every family defining site now classifies its digests and imports the section normatively: runtime (`parameter_digest`, `mission-policy-view`), runtime-evidence (three canonical-object digests), authzen (canonical projections), orchestration (`mission-unwind-plan`), audit (`entries_digest` envelope + `token_digest` raw-octet), approval-governance (policy digest envelope + record digest canonical-object), capability-binding (`source_digest` canonical-object + `catalog_digest` raw-octet), harness (`scope_statement_digest` raw-octet), discovery (two raw-octet + `ceiling_entry_digest` canonical-object), shaping (`input_digest` + `mission-shaping-evidence` envelope), consent-evidence (two envelope anchors + `template_hash` raw-octet, with its 'algorithm agility is future work' text removed), template (`mission-template`), progressive (`mission-authority-ceiling`), work-products (`artifact_digest` raw-octet + `provenance_digest` envelope, local prefix restatement converted to a reference), expansion (`mission-creation-fingerprint`), authority-server (`token_sha256` documented as deliberately unprefixed, algorithm fixed by member name). The core's binding sentence now reads: rules bind a digest when its defining specification classifies it and imports the section. Non-definers (mandate, metering, containment, attenuation, cross-domain, uma, issuance-grant, approval-revision, status, child-delegation) confirmed as echoes and left untouched; mandate's verifier step already defers to the issuance profile.

**4 (major, vectors)**: each vector now carries the pre-normalization input, the exact normalized value, the exact JCS UTF-8 serialization (or unambiguous byte representation), and the prefixed digest; at least one vector MUST exercise a normalization rule that materially changes the input; and at least one conformance case MUST present changed parameters that fail the digest match.

**Minor**: envelope-anchor bullet now says 'commitments produced with companion-defined `typ` values'.

One pre-existing issue surfaced by the survey, out of scope here: `template_hash` names two different constructions — the template draft's envelope anchor over the Mission Template object, and consent-evidence's raw-octet digest over the disclosure template's content bytes. Flagging for a rename in one of them; happy to file it.

All 17 touched drafts build, family manifest (37 drafts) and whitespace checks pass.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Layering correction in the latest commit, per review discussion: the commitment rule's neutral home is now the **substrate**, not the issuance profile.

- The substrate's Approved Context commitment checklist gains a **Default Commitment Construction** subsection: the three species, the `{typ, iss, value}` envelope shape, prefixed encoding with `sha-256` MTI, the I-JSON input domain, prefix agility with the no-downgrade MUST, and the future-algorithm contract. Adopting it is one way to satisfy the checklist; bindings with native commitments (AAuth's `mission_s256`, a content address) remain free to use their own.
- The ten ceremony-independent `mission-*` companions now import the substrate's default construction rather than "the issuance profile's commitment mechanisms" — no non-OAuth draft depends on issuance for the rule.
- The core keeps its section unchanged as the self-contained OAuth instantiation (its no-companion-dependency bar forbids importing) with one informative sentence declaring the alignment; the OAuth-layer drafts (template, progressive, consent-evidence, work-products, expansion) keep pointing at the core.

12 drafts rebuilt clean; manifest (37) and whitespace checks pass.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Round-3 review applied in 3e549e3; all six findings taken, plus the merge conflict resolved.

**1 (P1, parse-time duplicates)**: the duplicate rule now binds the parser, not the canonicalizer: externally received JSON destined for commitment MUST pass through a duplicate-detecting parser, and an object carrying duplicate member names is rejected at parse time, before the parsed data model exists (core bullet + canonicalization rule + substrate). The parsed-data-value rule remains for numeric spelling and rounding.

**2 (P1, `template_hash` de-collision)**: consent-evidence's member is renamed **`rendering_template_digest`**, with an explicit statement that it commits the rendering template, never a consented object; the Mission Template's envelope anchor rides in `source_hashes` as the committed anchor of a non-Mission approval (now stated in the `source_hashes` definition). The template profile's audit linkage now matches the envelope anchor, recomputed from the stored Mission Template object, against `source_hashes`, naming the rendering digest as a different object. The disclosure vector was recomputed: the JCS implementation was first validated by reproducing the published `sha-256:dUuA6io...` byte-for-byte, then the renamed disclosure yields `sha-256:y-XRrRqSKkeR6mjgXKqcM2DW8FMOwrjOqzZwjb1rNqY`, propagated to the canonical-bytes block and the approval-revision example.

**3 (P1, envelope precision)**: the substrate envelope is a closed JSON object carrying exactly three members and no others: `typ` (string, collision-resistant because a namespace the defining specification controls qualifies it), `iss` (string, value specified by the defining commitment), `value` (the committed JSON value).

**4 (P2, taxonomy scope)**: the taxonomy is scoped to the default prefixed construction; native and member-named digest constructions are explicitly permitted outside it (stating their own algorithm identification and agility), and raw-octet digest is redefined over an exact, specification-defined octet sequence, covering both whole artifacts and UTF-8-encoded scalar values (audit's `jti` case). MAS `token_sha256` is reworded as a member-named construction.

**5 (P2, `iss` semantics)**: the substrate now says `iss` is a namespace binding that domain-separates commitments across issuing authorities and does not authenticate the commitment producer, which stays a signature or evidence property.

**6 (P2, references)**: RFC 4648 added as a normative reference in core and substrate, cited at the encoding steps; RFC 6920 promoted to normative in both.

**Integration**: main merged (the family is now 38 drafts); the expansion conflict resolved keeping both the envelope-anchor classification and #519's hash-domain sentence.

Seven drafts rebuilt clean; manifest (38) and whitespace checks pass.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review against `25c3cbb..9c403ea`, current `main`, the family digest sites, and RFCs 7493/8785/6920. CI is green and the core taxonomy is useful, but I do **not** think this is merge-ready yet. There are three substantive specification gaps and one conformance gap.

## 1. Blocking: remove the generic parallel-commitment transition sketch

Lines 2320–2326 reintroduce the exact mechanism the accepted #284 review said not to define:

> During an algorithm transition a record MAY carry parallel commitments ...

No current carrier has a location or schema for a second commitment. The text does not define which two fields assert equivalence, how both are integrity-bound to the same object, whether an old implementation ignores or rejects the new field, or how selection works when verifier recognition sets differ. “Reject if any recognized commitment mismatches” is not safe generic behavior when the document has not defined which additional values are legitimate commitments rather than injected or unrelated values.

This also contradicts “no breaking changes”: every existing anchor is a singular string, and the Mission Record has no generic commitment collection.

Delete this paragraph. Retain only the future-algorithm contract: the specification defining a new prefix MUST define its carrier/schema, the binding that proves old and new values commit to the same object, producer behavior, verifier selection/downgrade behavior, and transition procedure. That gives real agility without inventing an unusable wire form.

## 2. Blocking: make the I-JSON/JCS numeric rule precise

Lines 2298–2303 require rejection of:

> numbers outside the range JCS serializes exactly

That is not a defined RFC 7493 or RFC 8785 test. RFC 8785 §3.1 requires number **data** presented to JCS to be expressible as IEEE 754 binary64. JCS then deterministically serializes that parsed binary64 value. It does not promise that every source decimal lexeme is preserved without rounding: RFC 8785 itself demonstrates `333333333.33333329` being serialized as `333333333.3333333`. Conversely, ordinary values such as `0.1` are not exactly representable as a real number in binary64 but are valid JCS inputs. RFC 7493’s avoidance of excess magnitude/precision is a `SHOULD NOT`, not the proposed undefined MUST.

Specify the actual input-domain rule instead:

- objects have no duplicate member names;
- string data is valid Unicode, has no surrogate/noncharacter code points prohibited by I-JSON, and is preserved unchanged;
- number data supplied to JCS is representable as a finite IEEE 754 binary64 value; and
- a profile requiring exact decimal or large-integer semantics uses a string or defines a stricter numeric domain (as Common Constraints already does).

Also distinguish the received JSON text from the parsed data model. Duplicate names and source-number precision can be erased by an ordinary parser; if the protocol intends to reject a source lexeme that would lose application-significant precision, it must require a parser/validation step capable of detecting that loss and define the comparison. Otherwise say explicitly that the commitment is over the parsed I-JSON data value, not its original numeric spelling.

## 3. Major: the claimed family-wide taxonomy is not actually adopted family-wide

Lines 2279–2281 say every family commitment classifies itself, and lines 2316–2318 say the shared rules bind documents that cite this section. This PR classifies only core anchors and Runtime `parameter_digest`.

Existing definitions remain outside or conflict with the new rule. For example:

- Consent Evidence still says `algorithm agility is future work` for `consent_rendering_hash`;
- Work Products defines `artifact_digest` and its own prefix behavior but neither classifies it as raw-octet nor imports this section;
- other canonical/raw digest sites (`provenance_digest`, source/policy-view/content/token/entries digests, and runtime-evidence digest variants) do not explicitly classify/import the new rules.

Therefore the new text cannot truthfully claim that all three species or “every commitment” inherit it. A generic citation to the core document is also not a deterministic normative import of this section.

Choose one of two coherent scopes:

1. perform a grep-derived companion pass that classifies each prefixed Mission digest, normatively imports this section, and removes conflicting agility text; or
2. make this explicitly opt-in: the rules apply only when a digest’s defining specification classifies it and normatively imports this section, and narrow the family-wide claims until companions adopt it.

The first option better closes #284. It can be mechanical and does not require recomputing any digest.

## 4. Major: the Operation Profile vector requirement is too weak to detect normalization drift

Lines 1745–1748 require only a normalized object and digest. A trivial vector can satisfy that requirement without exercising any normalization rule, and a consumer must reimplement both JCS and the profile’s normalization before it can tell which layer disagreed.

Require each vector to include:

- the operation input before normalization;
- the exact normalized parameter value;
- the exact JCS UTF-8 serialization, or an unambiguous byte representation such as UTF-8 hex; and
- the resulting prefixed digest.

At least one vector per Operation Profile needs a case where its normalization rules materially change the input—default insertion, omitted optional field, set-like array treatment, URI/string handling, or another operation-specific rule. Add a mismatch/changed-parameter case to conformance tests. This is the part that turns the vector into protection against PDP/PEP drift rather than merely another digest literal.

## Minor wording

The envelope-anchor bullet should say “commitments produced with companion-defined `typ` values,” not place the `typ` values themselves in the list of anchors.

## Disposition

**Changes requested in substance.** Keep the three-species taxonomy, MTI `sha-256`, RFC 6920 registry as a name source only, unknown-prefix rejection, raw-body exclusion, and the stricter Common Constraints overlay. Remove the generic dual-anchor sketch, correct the numeric input rule, make taxonomy adoption scope honest, and strengthen the required vectors. No anchor recomputation or new endpoint/registry is needed.

pulls.title: Core: RS-local subset verification is a deliberate non-goal (#501)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Planned as one hygiene PR for #344 + #501; on branching it turned out #344 (Third-Party Data Subjects) already landed on main via #514 and the issue is closed, so this PR carries only the remaining #501 work. Both changes are informative; no schema or protocol change.

## #501: RS-local verification of narrowed projections

Per the issue's analysis, with the review round's precision fixes (undefined, not impossible):

- **Consent Binding**: the flat Authority Set commitment defines no selective inclusion-proof mechanism; recomputation needs the full set, and the baseline defines neither a retrieval surface nor a proof format for less. Retrieval is a privacy and authorization burden (introspection minimization keeps other audiences' entries out of token introspection; a distinct control-plane surface needs authorization at least that strong), not an architectural prohibition. A selective proof composes generic inclusion proofs with the type-specific subset test, so it is future-profile territory with privacy, commitment, and trust-bootstrap requirements. Threat model split: a same-root proof adds nothing against an issuer malicious at approval time (which can approve and commit arbitrary authority), but does cover projection implementation errors, record corruption after an independently anchored approval commitment, and post-approval signing-key compromise under external pinning. Baseline path for independent assurance stays out-of-band full-set provisioning plus the rs-enforcement recomputation.
- **Resource Server Enforcement**: a worked narrowed-token contrast against the two-entry test-vector Authority Set (`journal-entries.write`, `max_amount` tightened from 500.00 to 250.00 USD): what the subset-only RS verifies, why it cannot recompute `authority_hash`, and how a full-set holder verifies containment relative to the authenticated committed set, including the provenance a deployment provisions (set, Mission id and issuer binding, expected hash, authenticated approval-time source) so a compromised issuer cannot substitute a replacement set's hash.

Build clean (0 unresolved section refs), `make lint` clean.

Closes #501.

pulls.title: Runtime evidence: name the evidence property set as one citable anchor
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes #343, implementing the recommendation recorded on the issue.

One informative section, `Evidence Properties {#evidence-properties}`, in the schema companion, placed between Retention and Extension Members: a lead sentence naming the four-property cluster and a four-row table pointing each property at its existing mechanism.

- **Parameter-bound**: `parameter_digest` on Decision Evidence, the authorized/effective pair on Execution Evidence, action-bound approval's dynamic linking.
- **Key-isolated**: emitter-published signing keys bound to scope and audience; the agent-inaccessible placement holds only under the runtime profile's custody rules, stated conditionally so base conformance is not overclaimed.
- **Session-independent**: verification anchored in published key sets with retired-key retention; no step consults a live session, so a record verifies whether the carrying session is active, expired, or absent.
- **Third-party-verifiable**: one row, two tiers, mirroring the existing honesty scoping: scoped independent verification against the Enforcement Scope Statement's published keys here, durable third-party verifiability via the audit profile where adopted.

Open-question dispositions (from the issue): home is runtime-evidence (these are record properties; runtime's Named Enforcement Claims are deployment claims, the wrong genus); single third-party-verifiable term with two-tier wording rather than two rows; `third-party-verifiable` not `non-repudiable` (containment already uses the latter for approver disclosure). No pointer sentence in runtime.md, keeping the change one-file as the sketch allowed.

No new normative words, no new evidence object, no schema or conformance change. Terms are defined in place; the WG threads are not cited in the spec.

## Validation

kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc build OK, zero unresolved "Section ??" references, `check-family-manifest` passes (38 drafts, no drift), `git diff --check` clean.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Review applied in 41f2183; all four findings taken in the direction the review specified.

**1 (blocking, key-isolated)**: resolved with the second option: the row now states the gap honestly. Base = origin and integrity only; the condition column says **none in the current profiles**, that no requirement places the evidence-signing private key outside the agent's runtime, and that custody governs the confirmation key, a different key; the non-proof column: the agent's runtime could not access the signing key or emit under the emitter's identity. Nothing is inferred from `cnf` custody. The mechanism gap is now owned by follow-up issue #521 (evidence-signing-key custody as a runtime custody/claims condition), so `Closes #343` stands per the accepted disposition.

**2 (parameter-bound)**: decision-time not execution-time; "digest of the parameters evaluated" (covers denies); the recompute clause states how the link to parameters is established; human-rendering binding moved to the condition column (action-bound approval required and used, rendering derived from the same normalized parameters by a trusted component, dynamic link verifies); non-proof: human understanding, and that the action occurred (outcome record = emitter's signed assertion).

**3 (session-independent)**: reworded to the suggested form: a verifier can verify a retained record without a live session and without possession or validity of the carrying credential; the compromised-key exception is preserved in the same cell; non-proof: validity at decision or execution time, current Mission state.

**4 (audit tier)**: the durable tier now requires retained or configured producer **and** Transparency Service trust anchors, a Receipt, and the evidence bytes, verifying without contacting either operator; cross-domain adds the independent-operator condition; non-proof: producer-key trust, assertion truth, feed completeness.

**Table shape**: the four-column form from the accepted #343 review, verbatim column names; the lead now names "a property vocabulary ... and the conditions under which the records support each property" and calls the table a conditional capability map. The footer caveats are gone because the columns carry them.

Build, manifest (38 drafts), and whitespace checks pass.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review against `759df3c..cdad7b6`, current `main`, #343's accepted review, and the normative Runtime Evidence/Audit mechanisms. The one-anchor section is the right shape and CI is green, but this wording is **not merge-ready**: the compact three-column table recreates the exact capability conflation the issue review asked the table to prevent.

## 1. Blocking: the cited custody mechanism does not establish evidence-key isolation

The `Key-isolated` row says custody places “key material with the mediating PEP, inaccessible to the agent.” Runtime `{#custody}` is specifically custody of the Mission-bound credential's sender-constraint (`cnf`) private key. It does not govern the JWS private key used to sign Decision, Execution, or Refusal Evidence.

Runtime Evidence requires each emitter to sign and publish the corresponding verification key, and it binds that public key to emitter/scope/audience. That establishes origin and integrity. Nowhere does it require the **evidence-signing private key** to be generated or held outside the agent runtime, prevent the agent from invoking it on arbitrary records, or attest its isolation. Even the agent-compromise-resistant claim speaks to `cnf` custody and PEP path placement, not evidence-signing-key custody.

Consequently, base conformance does not supply `key-isolated`, and the current conditional citation still does not close the gap. Choose one honest resolution:

- add an actual requirement/claim condition that the evidence-signing private keys for the relevant PDP/PEP/executor are generated, held, and usable only in components outside the agent's control, with the emitter/path scope declared; or
- state that key isolation is an additional deployment property not provided by the current profiles, and keep #343 (or a focused follow-up) open until a mechanism owns it.

Do not infer isolation of one key from custody of another.

## 2. Major: “parameter-bound” conflates record integrity, execution evidence, and human rendering

The row currently says “Evidence produced at execution and cryptographically bound to the authorized parameters.” Three corrections are needed:

- Decision Evidence is produced at the PDP decision, not at execution. It also records denies, for which there are evaluated parameters but no “authorized parameters.”
- The JWS authenticates a record containing `parameter_digest`; recomputing the digest over the normalized parameters establishes the link to those parameters. Merely seeing the digest does not reveal or independently prove which parameters produced it.
- Binding to **human-rendered** parameters exists only when action-bound approval is actually required and used, the rendering is derived from the same normalized parameter object/digest by a trusted component, and its freshness/dynamic link verifies. Action-bound approval is not base evidence conformance.

The base property should therefore say: a verified Decision Evidence record authenticates the digest of the parameters evaluated; linked Execution Evidence authenticates the authorized/effective pair and exposes equality or deviation. A separate condition states when that digest is also bound to what a human approved. It does not prove the human understood the rendering or that the action occurred—the outcome record is the emitter's signed assertion.

## 3. Major: session-independent verification is not verification *of* session state or authorization validity

“A record verifies whether that session is active, expired, or absent” is ambiguous and reads as if the record verifies the session's state. The mechanism proves only that evidence signature verification does not use a live session or carrying credential as its trust anchor. It does not establish that the session/credential was valid at decision or execution time, that the Mission remains active now, or that the recorded action was authorized correctly. Those are record contents and linked policy/state evidence, not consequences of session-independent signature verification.

Use wording such as: “A verifier can verify the retained record without a live session or possession/validity of the credential that carried the action.” Then put the non-proof alongside it. Also preserve the compromised-key exception: retired keys remain resolvable, while evidence after a declared compromise time is unverifiable.

## 4. Major: the audit tier still requires trust anchors

The `Third-party-verifiable` row says durable verification “for a party without [access to the Enforcement Scope Statement's published keys] rides the audit profile.” Audit does not eliminate producer-key authorization. Its offline verification algorithm still requires:

1. the producing component's trust anchor;
2. the Transparency Service's retained/configured verification key;
3. the Receipt/inclusion proof; and
4. retrievable evidence bytes to check the committed digest.

The transparency profile removes dependence on the producer's **live logs/service** and proves registration/inclusion at a committed time. It does not make an unknown producer key trusted, prove the signed assertion true, or prove feed completeness. Replace “without that access” with the actual stronger tier: a party with retained/configured producer and Transparency Service trust anchors can verify offline without contacting either operator, where a Receipt and evidence are retained. Cross-domain verifiability additionally requires the audit profile's independent-operator condition (or its compensating second service).

## Required table shape

The accepted #343 review explicitly recommended:

**Property / What the base evidence proves / Additional mechanism or condition / What it does not prove**

This PR reduced that to **Property / Mechanism / Where** and pushed only two caveats into a footer. That is why parameter-to-human binding, evidence-key isolation, session validity, and transparency trust assumptions disappeared. Please use the four-column form—or equivalent prose with the same four distinctions—and change the lead from “the records ... carry” to “the property vocabulary and the conditions under which these records support it.”

## Disposition

**Changes requested in substance.** Keep the section in `runtime-evidence`, keep it informative, retain `third-party-verifiable` rather than `non-repudiable`, and keep one row with scoped/durable tiers. Correct the three proof boundaries above and either define evidence-signing-key isolation or state that it remains a gap. The latter point is the only one that may require normative follow-up; informative wording cannot manufacture a missing property.

pulls.title: IANA registry strategy: one family-wide namespace story (#170)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes #170's approved plan as revised by its fresh review, one PR across the core and seven companions. **Posted for review; do not merge without explicit approval.**

**Core**: the extensibility taxonomy names the three postures (registry-backed, pre-drafted where the namespace is defined and **requested by the eventual defining RFC**, never activated at adoption; specification-defined with a named promotion path under the document series' change controller, retiring the family's one "author-coordinated" phrase; collision-resistant deployment names, never registered), plus the typed-artifact rule: wire-crossing artifacts get `application/mission-*` media types with RFC 6838 templates at definition time, JOSE `typ` is the registered type, and commitment-envelope `typ`s are hash domains, deliberately not media types. The **Mission Lifecycle States registry** is pre-drafted with minimal stable columns; the only-`active`-derives invariant lives in the governing text and the DE instructions, and a registration cannot redefine it. Seven seed rows verified against defining texts (and cross-checked against the signals draft's own enumeration): `active`/`revoked`/`expired` (core), `suspended`/`completed` (status), `superseded` (expansion), `cascaded` (child-delegation; a lifecycle state, distinct from cascade modes).
