A parameter binding alone is neither form; the evaluation-identifier dereference rule now requires yielding one of the two forms complete.

pulls.title: MAS: Mission-bound issuance is the high-consequence floor (#237 ruling, part B of the MAS-join pair)
pulls.author: mcguinness

pulls.title: Substrate Statements: supplied/not-supplied migration under the ACC native-binding rule (#554)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes #554 under its review's seven-point disposition, not the original eight-document sweep.

**1. The Authorized Context Correlation native-binding rule, resolved** (`8cae49aa`). The definition's own closing sentence decides it: the capability is required exactly where one authority did not itself bind all required facts, so the inverse is now stated in the definition — a binding whose single authority natively binds all facts in scope does not supply it; nothing independently established remains to join, and its Statement says `not supplied` with that reason. GNAP already said this; the substrate's OAuth Statement row flips to match, and the informative crosswalk stops crediting native bindings — leaving the MAS join/Join Assertion machinery as the genuine supplier. This is also consistent with the transaction-authorization profile's own consumption declaration and the worked composition's gateway-as-joining-authority framing.

**2-4. Only the three provider Statements migrate, semantically audited** (`1d9805f2`). AAuth, MAS, and UMA move to the five-column `supplied`/`not supplied` format with the missing eighth row added under the resolved rule (MAS `supplied` — with the mapping contract as association policy, `mission_mismatch` as failure behavior, the party-not-issuance ceiling, and the join-spoofing substitution note; AAuth and UMA `not supplied` — native binding). The consumer tables are untouched (see 7). The review's three audits are applied rather than mechanically converted:
- MAS Monotonic Derivation narrows to the native child-creation derivation point; PDP evaluation is enforcement, never derivation. Its Credential-Bound activates on the Join Assertion with party-correlation fact semantics; mapping-join-only deployments are outside the row.
- UMA State-Observable activates on authenticated per-use introspection or Mission Status; a self-contained RPT validated only to its `exp` is not observation.
- AAuth Credential-Bound activates on the PS-asserted/federated modes carrying and validating `mission_s256`; identity-based and resource-managed paths stay outside.

**Item 4 placement call**: AAuth State-Observable keeps Management as an activation condition of the base Statement — no Statement extension in the management draft, which depends on neither Substrate nor the binding.

**5. Partial collapse recorded** (`7fb6da94`): the worked-composition note now states that the AAuth lifecycle and Management-conditioned state rows are the binding's published Statement, while the payment-policy adapter and gateway correlation join remain deployment-local provider claims. The `family-manifest` records the aauth→aauth-management dependency the citation already implied.

**6. Structural tripwire** (`71768b57`, `a2bbf379`): `scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs` validates every registered Statement (exactly the canonical eight capabilities in order, binary claims, activation on every supplied row, populated scope/limitations cells as the temporal/failure structural proxy, dash discipline on not-supplied rows), plus two repo-wide tripwires: retired vocabulary in any draft table fails (the five consumer tables carry an allowlist annotated with #620 until their migration), and an unregistered "…substrate capabilities" table fails. Wiring note: the push token lacks `workflow` scope, so instead of editing the workflow file the check chains from `check-family-manifest.mjs`, which CI already runs — identical coverage; move it to an explicit workflow step at your convenience.

**7. Consumer tables split off**: #620 filed for the five consumption tables (`required` / `required when` / `not consumed`), coupled to the validator's allowlist so the tripwire tightens automatically when it lands.

Closes #554

pulls.title: Discharge: the terminal_when funnel, endpoint, signals gate, and 21 rows tested (#287 residual)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Implements the discharge mechanism end to end — the #287 residual: the spec landed in PRs #530/#543 and no code path existed (D92's own record). Eight commits.

## The build

- **Kernel funnel** (`901849c3`): `terminal_when` becomes an implemented Common Constraint (closed `{event_type, discharge_policy?}` wire shape, since condition identity is byte equality of the canonical form; children inherit it under the subset rule). `discharge()` mirrors `contain()`'s metadata-only commit: the latch is keyed by `entry_digest` (`mission-authority-entry` anchor over the immutable entry), which *is* the equivalence class — byte-identical entries discharge together as one transition and one version increment. `effectiveAuthoritySet` filters discharged entries before the containment rewrite, so derivation gating, introspection, and Status visibility all updated for free per #569's single composition point.
- **Idempotency, two identities** (`8bbded15`): a whole-endpoint `LifecycleResponseStore` (nonce → stored signed response verbatim; divergent retry → `invalid_request`) and a `DischargeEventStore` keyed by the five-part tuple with the assertion fingerprint, written inside the latch transaction. A fresh-nonce retry of the same assertion returns a freshly signed envelope carrying the stored outcome and the *original* versions; a divergent re-assertion is `conflict`; the same `event_id` against a different target is an independent assertion.
- **The endpoint** (`fb96a4f0`): `discharge` as the fifth lifecycle operation. A minimal scope model lands on the service-token auth (`serviceTokenPrincipals`: token → principal + scopes; the dev token keeps both scopes so nothing breaks): `mission_discharge` is distinct, and `mission_lifecycle` does not imply it. The anti-oracle contract is exact: all six refusal classes are one `not_found` (reasons recorded issuer-side only), the normative validation order runs selector existence → condition membership → target authorization → terminal acknowledgement, and the endpoint's 404 vocabulary is aligned to `not_found` throughout (the status route had drifted to `unknown_mission`). `discharge_policy` selectors are resolved fail-closed at every entry-introduction point: an unconfigured selector cannot enter a record at approval or child creation. `evidence_ref` is never dereferenced (the test proves it with a fetch spy) and never authorization input.
- **Signals** (`d1039495`): a discharge commit passes `authority_changed: true` explicitly (per the `LifecycleCommit` constraint comment), and `MissionSignalEmitter` gains the `mission_capabilities_supported` gate: an event whose only narrowing signal is `authority_changed` is withheld from streams that have not declared it; containment-carrying events follow containment's existing rules. One ambiguity rule for review: the gate keys on a `containment_version` *advance*, and with no cursor only `containment_version === 1` counts — a higher first-seen value is ambiguous and a gate resolves ambiguity by withholding.
- **PDP** (`3684a106`): the policy view carries the discharge delta, and a discharged entry refuses at the point of use (`authority_discharged`) even while the Mission stays active.
- **Tests + ledger** (`5a0872a0`, `069f9888`): 46 new tests (966 total); the concurrency row races two discharges with distinct nonces *and* distinct event_ids so neither idempotency store serializes them (one `discharged`, one `already_discharged`, one increment); `child-propagation` is exercised through real child derivation against a discharged parent entry.

## Row outcomes (24)

21 `tested`. Two honest holds, one unchanged:
- `status.discharge.policy-resolution-on-condition-entry` — `partial`: implemented and tested at both entry-introduction points, but the row's declared surface is `lifecycle-endpoint` while the observable is a derivation refusal, so no mapping can satisfy level+surface; the note also records the one unimplemented clause (persisting the resolved mapping id/version against the exact `condition_digest`; resolution is live at each discharge instead). Both look like row-metadata questions for you rather than build gaps.
- `signals.discharge.authority-changed-rematerialize` — stays `partial` for its original reason (detection is built and now driven end-to-end by a real discharge commit; no consumer in this repo performs the actual Status refetch).

## Extra: `--collect` clean repo-wide (`c0a4b08d`)

The six standing `authzen.response-context.*` `--collect` findings (flagged on #616/#617) are root-caused and fixed: `evaluate.test.ts`'s describe is aliased through the FGA-gating `d()` idiom and the mappings stored leaf-only names, which the static checker's leaf matching was blind to. Full vitest names restored; first fully clean `--collect` run.

## Flagged, not fixed

- Pre-existing tag defect from #617: `@spec status#effective-authority-set` in `kernel/derive.ts` names an anchor that does not exist in the status draft (it is the single remaining outstanding line in the spec-versions report). Left for a ruling since it is outside this change.

Refs #287, #288 (status-surface risk), #543, #530.

## Gate

`pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` clean; `node scripts/check-spec-versions.mjs` OK (all new anchors declared); **966/966 tests, 0 skipped (89 files)** with OpenFGA live; conformance manifest OK in default **and `--collect`** modes (490 requirements: 122 tested, 43 partial, 325 todo); SPEC_VERSIONS rows updated with the discharge anchors and components.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All seven findings addressed in `8cfb1e32`.

**1 (P0) — service-token prototype bypass.** The registry is now a null-prototype dictionary and the lookup requires `Object.hasOwn` — belt and suspenders, so neither an inherited name nor a future refactor of either half reopens it. The regression test presents `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, and `hasOwnProperty` against both the lifecycle route and the `/templates` admin plane; all four get 401 and nothing latches.

**2 (P1) — Signals gate restart inference.** Took the "explicit discriminator from the kernel" option: `LifecycleCommit` gains `containment_advanced`, stamped by the one funnel that advances `containment_version` (`contain()`, which always advances it on commit), and the emitter's gate reads exactly that — `authority_changed` without `containment_advanced` is a discharge commit, gated on the declared capability. The `emittedContainmentVersion` cursor is deleted outright. The discriminator is internal: the SET builder does not copy it to the wire. Fresh-emitter tests prove both of your failure modes fixed: a discharge on a previously contained Mission (unchanged `containment_version: 1`, first commit the emitter ever sees) stays gated from the undeclared consumer, and a genuine containment first observed at version 5 is delivered to it.

**3 (P1) — mapping pinning.** `insertRecord` — the single record-creation funnel, so child creation, expansion, and template dispatch are all covered — now binds each condition's resolved mapping to its exact `entry_digest` + `condition_digest` in the same transaction as the record (new `DischargeMappingPinStore`), retaining identifier, version, *and content*. Discharge target authorization reads the pin and never the live policy; a missing pin fails closed into the anti-oracle `not_found` collapse under a new issuer-side reason `unpinned_mapping`. The test does exactly your scenario: policy version 1 names principal A, the record is approved, the policy is edited to version 2 naming principal B — B is refused, A still discharges, and the pin still reads `mapping_version: "1"`.

**4 (P1) — `terminal_noop` idempotency.** It now records through the standalone event store before returning, mirroring `already_discharged` one screen below (which already did). Kernel and HTTP tests cover both cases: a fresh-nonce replay of the same tuple + fingerprint returns the stored outcome with the original versions, and the same tuple under a different fingerprint is `conflict` (409).

**5 (P1) — atomic-commit overclaim.** Marked `partial` with the gap named precisely: the single-process transactional funnel (latch + increment + dedup row + in-transaction lifecycle commit) is proven; durable propagation under interrupted delivery is not — in-memory store, best-effort delivery with retry/dead-letter deferred, no multi-connection recovery test. The note states the flip condition (transactional persistent outbox + interrupted-delivery recovery test). Tally: 121 tested / 44 partial / 325 todo.

**6 (P2) — `authority_discharged` owner.** Status's `{#runtime}` section now defines it: a family-coordinated denial-reason under the AuthZEN binding's extension rule, carried in the decision response's `context.reason` and the evidence `denial_reason`, distinct from containment (trust withdrawn) and out-of-authority (never approved), unrecognized-means-deny per the binding's own rule. AuthZEN itself needed no edit — its extension rule is the hook, and Status already cites it informatively, so the reference graph is unchanged (which matters: main's manifest now drift-checks it).

**7 (P2) — wire validation.** Digests: exactly `sha-256:` + 43 base64url characters. `observed_at`: strict RFC 3339 shape gated before `Date.parse`. A valid-JSON non-object body (`null`, array, scalar) parses to an empty member set and refuses — the member-access 500 is gone; note the refusal is the endpoint's own `not_found` vocabulary (no operation resolves), which the test pins. The nonce bound is now documented in Status `{#idempotency}` (1–255 characters, longer/empty/non-string malformed with no echo) rather than being an undocumented implementation limit. Negative endpoint tests for every case.

Verification: full suite 863 passed / 110 env-gated skips (the docker-gated suites; CI runs them with services up); conformance validator green at 490 requirements (121/44/325) with the Status spec digest re-audited (no existing row text affected); SPEC_VERSIONS clean; the Status draft builds through kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc.

pulls.title: README: the curated landing page; catalog and dependencies extracted; verb-first navigation
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes the README review under its own editorial rule: **the README explains the system once; the Architecture defines it citably; the manifest inventories it exhaustively.** Five commits.

## The new README (`f227a882`)

157 lines, ~1,140 words (from 1,389 lines / ~10,300). The eight-section structure as proposed: the problem and the standardization ask up front, with the RAR boundary sentence verbatim and the **issuance profile** naming anchor preserved; four start-here routes; the verb spine as primary navigation; one binding decision; one assurance table with the per-path claims rule beneath it; the by-verb capability note; status with the four canonical links; ~30 lines of repository use.

**One deliberate deviation from the proposal**: the verb table uses the Architecture's **ten canonical verbs** (`{#layers}`: Propose, Approve and Record, Govern, Enforce Each Action, Run and Wind Down, Delegate, Project, Continue, Prove, Analyze), not the proposed eleven. The proposal's "Issue" and "Operate" rows and the old README's "contain"/"dispatch" lines regrouped the spine; the family rule is that presentation overlays the verb spine and never regroups it, and the README table must match the citable form. Issuance mechanics live under Approve and Record (the bindings) with Govern carrying Management; the delegate-vs-project teaching sentence survives beneath the table. The old README's 12-verb diagram had already drifted from the Architecture; this restores agreement.

## The machinery (`d0df9113`, `0c2ba4f6`, `eb0672b2`, `a7fae6bb`)

- **Manifest metadata**: every draft carries `verbs` (from the canonical ten), a real one-sentence `summary` (eight authored fresh where the catalog's first sentence was a bare maturity word), and `pull_when` (from the old adoption matrix). Top-level `verbs` enum and `packages` (issuance-baseline, runtime-enforced, governed-agent, and transaction-assurance completing the old fourth profile row). Retired: `presentation_zones`/`presentation_tracks`/`adoption_rungs` and the per-draft fields — verified consumed by nothing but the checker (the reader-editions build takes its lists from the Makefile).
- **DRAFTS.md**: the exhaustive catalog — a generated index table (title/maturity/verbs/summary, freshness-checked in CI, never rewritten silently) over the full catalog prose moved byte-identical from the README.
- **DEPENDENCIES.md**: the dependency report moved verbatim, with its one dangling cross-reference ("steps 1 through 3", which pointed at the retired adoption order) repaired.
- **Checker rewrite**: the seven README-structure checks (adoption order, presentation enums, adoption-map table, the four menu checks) are gone with their helpers; the catalog check now targets DRAFTS.md; new checks validate `verbs`/`summary`/`pull_when`/`packages`, DRAFTS.md index freshness, and exactly two things about the README — it links the two reports, and every backticked `draft-*` token is a manifest slug. Every new check was proved non-vacuous by perturbation.

## Notes for review

- `notes/adoption-plan.md` still describes the retired taxonomies (nothing reads it; left for a separate pass).
- `adoption_alias` (3 drafts) lost its only reader and is now unvalidated data; kept.
- The generated index follows manifest order (runtime-evidence precedes runtime); reordering the manifest reorders the index if wanted.
- `.github/workflows/ghpages.yml`'s paths-ignore doesn't list DRAFTS.md/DEPENDENCIES.md, so edits to them trigger an (idempotent, wasteful) editor's-copy rebuild — a one-line workflow edit I can't push without `workflow` scope.

## Validation

family-manifest (with the chained Statement check), drafts-index freshness, and conformance manifest all green; the moved catalog and dependency prose are byte-identical to their README sources; DRAFTS.md carries all 41.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All six findings addressed in `ea591e3f`.

**1 (P1) — adoption closure via `deps`.** `deps` is gone. Each draft now carries two typed edge sets, and the truth source is the drafts themselves: **`requires`** is the draft's normative in-family reference set, *extracted from the draft's own front matter*, and the only edges that close transitively for adoption; **`references`** is the full in-family citation graph and pulls in nothing. The checker's new `typed-edges` rule validates shape (real slugs, no self-edges or duplicates, `requires ⊆ references`) and, decisively, **drift**: every draft's `requires` must equal the normative `I-D.draft-mcguinness-*` set in its front matter, in both directions. So Security Model's wide reference list lands in `references` where it belongs, and the core's `requires` is empty — its self-containment rule, now machine-visible. The extraction also surfaced 25 drafts whose old `deps` under-recorded actual references; the union is preserved in `references`.

**2 (P1) — the packages taxonomy.** Removed. The top-level object is now **`reference_stacks`**: a transcription of the Architecture's own four cumulative stacks (`{#reference-architecture}`) — protocol-core, reference-security-architecture, recommended-agent-architecture, high-assurance-architecture — with the two alternatives modeled explicitly: `binding_one_of` (the five issuer bindings; substrate conformance is carried by the binding, per the object's `$comment`) and `freshness_one_of` (Status, Signals, or `core:token-introspection` — Status is no longer hard-required). The high-assurance stack adds `claims`, not documents, matching the Architecture's text. The checker pins the four stack names exactly — adding a fifth or renaming one fails CI — and the `$comment` records that the Architecture is authoritative and its five *packages* are deliberately not restated. README language updated accordingly.

**3 (P1) — the duplicated conformance checklist.** The bullet list is gone. The section now states the minimum outcome in two sentences and links the core's [Conformance section](https://mcguinness.github.io/mission-bound-authorization/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.html#name-conformance) (anchor verified against the built page) as the authoritative checklist, explicitly naming the distinct client and RS obligations as living there. The what-the-core-does-not-protect list stays: it is a threat-scope statement, not a conformance surface.

**4 (P1) — Cross-Organizational Delegation.** Now `["delegate", "project"]` in the manifest, shown under both verbs in the README table, and the delegate/project distinction paragraph gains a sentence saying multi-verb classification is expected, with this document as the example. DRAFTS.md's generated row picked up the change.

**5 (P2) — custody.** "held by the party that approved it" → "recorded and retained by the Mission control point," which also now agrees with the control-plane paragraph below it.

**6 (P2) — generated-index guardrails.** `renderIndex` escapes pipes and collapses newlines in every manifest-sourced cell (`escapeCell`, shared by generate and `--check` so freshness stays consistent), and the checker validates every `#go.<slug>.html` target in **both** README.md and DRAFTS.md against manifest slugs — the README rule count is now three, and the README's own description of it updated to match.

Every new check was proved non-vacuous by perturbation: dropped `requires` edge, phantom `requires` edge, subset violation, mistyped go-link, bogus stack slug, and renamed stack all fail; a pipe-and-newline summary renders escaped. Full gate green (family-manifest + chained Statement check, drafts-index freshness, conformance manifest).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
A fresh-eyes review round (three independent reviewers over machinery, spec fidelity, and newcomer reading, findings verified against the sources), applied in `ff07856c`.

**Fixed before merge:**
- **The minimal-implementation sentence now names the constitutive gates.** It read "state-gated issuance with revocation by Mission," omitting the subset rule — one of the three gates without which the core says an implementation "conforms to no role." Now: "issuance bounded by the subset rule and gated on Mission state (revocation by Mission is the kill switch)."
- **DRAFTS.md's MAS catalog prose caught up with the merged #619 floor.** The prose moved byte-identical from the old README still said "No Mission-bound tokens and no issuance gating; runtime enforcement over every consequential path is required" — contradicting both the README's binding row and `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server` itself. It now states the floor: a path claiming the Enterprise profile's high-consequence credential property MUST use Mission-bound issuance.
- **The `group` validation regression is closed.** The rewrite had left `groups` and every draft's `group` completely unvalidated (main checked them via the deleted adoption map). New check (o): enum validation plus placement — every draft must be named under its group's `###` section in DRAFTS.md's catalog, restoring the placement semantics the adoption map used to carry.
- **`generated_note` no longer documents the retired `packages` field.**

**Precision and disclosure:**
- Baseline Issuance's kill-switch row is now conditioned ("where the binding issues Mission-bound credentials"), matching the Architecture's hedge — under standalone MAS there is no issuance gate to kill. The High-Assurance row uses the Architecture's two named claims verbatim (agent-compromise-resistant enforcement, trifecta containment). "Validated in CI" became "structurally validated in CI," and the `reference_stacks` `$comment` now records the two places the transcription resolves ambiguity in the Architecture's prose (`runtime-evidence` in `adds`; `binding_one_of` generalizing the "OAuth realization" sentence).
- Reader fixes: RAR, PEP/PDP, MAS, and Person Server get first-use expansions in the README; RPT/PCT in the UMA catalog entry; DEPENDENCIES.md gains the shorthand-to-DRAFTS.md mapping note and loses its two over-long lines; off-path execution is attributed to the runtime layer alone, per the cited core section.

**Checker hardening:** duplicate slugs/files and malformed entries rejected up front (one clean finding instead of a crash mid-run); `title` validated; `maintenance_classes` gets the same enum validation as `verbs`; the stacks' `contains` chain checked for a single root, self-reference, and cycles; a malformed `references` no longer masks the `requires` drift check on the same draft; the go-link regex is imported from the generator so the two can't drift; `spliceIndex` fails loudly when the generated-index markers are duplicated (previously a bad merge would ship a stale duplicate block while `--check` reported "current").

Everything the reviewers verified clean stayed clean: all editor's-copy links 1:1 against the live site, verb table exactly the Architecture's ten, the manifest rewrite lost nothing. All new checks perturbation-proved (eight tampering scenarios, each fails; restored gate green).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All five findings addressed across `ff07856c` (which the review predates — it already resolved several sub-items) and `89597e08` (the adoption-model rework).

**1 (P1) — `requires` modeled the wrong relationship.** Agreed, and the fix separates the two graphs completely:
- **`normative_references`** and **`references`** are now purely the citation graph: extracted from each draft's front matter, drift-checked bidirectionally in CI, and explicitly carrying no adoption semantics. Making `references` exact extraction (instead of a union with the old hand-authored `deps`) dropped precisely the three phantom Substrate edges you found — discovery, issuance-grant, progressive.
- **`adoption_requires`** is authored, not inferred: 120 edges were classified from quoted in-draft evidence (every edge examined at its citation sites; "not implementable alone" and unhedged conformance MUSTs read as unconditional, hosting/option hedges as conditional, terminology imports as reference-only), then validated as a subset of the draft's normative references — an unconditional deployment dependency must at least be normatively cited. Only these edges close transitively.
- **`requires_when`** records the conditional edges, each naming its activator (binding, option, or composition); targets must be cited by the draft.

Your counterexamples are the acceptance test: runtime now closes to {runtime, substrate} — core introspection needs no Status and no Cross-Domain; AuthZEN closes to {authzen, runtime, runtime-evidence, substrate}, with core/Status/Cross-Domain conditional; Audit closes to 3 drafts, not 20; the AAuth binding closes to {aauth, substrate} with no OAuth core; Security Model closes to itself.

**2 (P1) — the stacks pretended binding-neutrality.** Took your second option: `reference_stacks` now transcribes what the Architecture actually defines — the OAuth realization ("the OAuth realization of Baseline Issuance"), with the root stack's `binding` pinned to the core. The binding decision stays in the README's binding table, and the `$comment` records how other bindings relate: standalone MAS has no issuance gate unless the Issuance Grant is composed, AAuth reports native capabilities with the Person Server's contextual gate as its per-action analogue, UMA/GNAP are sketches. The README stacks paragraph says the same in prose. (The Baseline Issuance row's missing qualification was already fixed in `ff07856c`: "where the binding issues Mission-bound credentials.")

**3 (P2) — CI vs claims.** Both directions tightened. The checker now enforces more of the semantics: self-reference/cycles/single-root on the `contains` chain (`ff07856c`), the Runtime-Enforced stack must declare `freshness_one_of`, each stack's `architecture_name` is tripwired against the Architecture's text (a rename upstream fails CI), and the full citation graph — normative *and* informative — is drift-checked both ways, which is what caught and killed the Substrate drift. What remains genuinely editorial (whether the stack membership matches the Architecture's prose semantics) is stated as such in the README ("structurally validated in CI; fidelity to the Architecture's prose is an editorial obligation", `ff07856c`).

**4 (P2) — competing adoption authorities.** The top-level `$comment` no longer claims "package membership" (now: typed reference and adoption edges, OAuth reference stacks), `generated_note` was fixed in `ff07856c`, and `notes/adoption-plan.md` is marked **superseded** by the shipped storefront with the retirement of its zones/tracks/rungs recorded, kept for provenance.

**5 (P2) — status wording.** The Status section now reads: the core is a published Internet-Draft on the IETF Datatracker; the companions are editor's copies in this repository; and stable/experimental/sketch/guide are this repository's own labels, not IETF statuses.

All new checks perturbation-proved (eight scenarios: un-cited adoption edge, empty condition, uncited conditional target, phantom and missing references, unpinned root binding, missing freshness alternatives, architecture rename tripwire — each fails CI; restored gate green). Full local gate green including the chained Statement check and index freshness.

pulls.title: README iteration: the question, the wire, and the adjacency map
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes the post-merge README review feedback as one reviewable change.

**Overview rewrite** (six deltas): the question stated as a question (every deployment can answer whether a token is valid; none can answer whether the work it serves is still approved); one clause of incident scene; the family invariant promoted to the record paragraph (authority derived from the approved task, never asserted by a client or inferred by a model); the kill switch carries its honesty bound at first mention (stops new issuance everywhere at once, outstanding tokens run to their own expiry); the boundary paragraph now defends against all three arrival misreadings in parallel construction (RAR / agent identity / policy engines, each kept, each given what it lacked); em-dash asides and the tokens-possessing-a-boundary grammar fixed.

**Ranked items 1-6, all applied**: assurance section slimmed to the adoption decision (manifest plumbing moved to Repository use); typed-edges model explained once; Substrate Requirements relocated to the binding section it belongs to; the agent-runtime Start-here row; voice nits; the size-objection sentence in the ask (the suite's size is evidence of thinking, not the ask).

**Additions, verified before writing**: the wire exhibit is the core's own example claim, exactly three members (the suggested `expires_at` member does not exist on the claim and was dropped); the six-row composes-with table's relationships each check against the family's own positioning; Running code promotes src/, SPEC_VERSIONS, DEMO, and the conformance manifest to a section of their own.

**Deliberately omitted**: the community gap-catalog line. No such citation target exists anywhere in this repository, and per the family's citation-hygiene rule an unverifiable it-is-public claim does not ship; one sentence can land later with a live link.

Also flagged upstream, not addressed here: the handbook sync gap (41 documents / 5 bindings vs the handbook's 34 / 4) accrues for a batched round once the current burst settles.

Validation: family-manifest checker (all three README rules), chained Statement check, and drafts-index freshness all green; 267 lines.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All five findings applied in `a3b64ac6` — each a wording correction that pulls the page back inside the residuals the drafts themselves document.

**1 (P1) — revocation scope.** The kill-switch sentence now says exactly what the architecture guarantees: "Issuance and issuer-mediated derivation are gated on the Mission's current state: revocation stops the Mission Issuer from minting or deriving further authority, while already materialized credentials and downstream grants run only to their own lifetimes unless state-aware runtime enforcement cuts off their use sooner." That is the core's materialized-capability residual verbatim in spirit — redeemed projection grants and offline attenuation children included — and it keeps runtime enforcement's reason to exist in the same breath.

**2 (P1) — anchors as detectability.** Now: "…commits both as `intent_hash` and `authority_hash`, making later alteration detectable to a verifier that retains or can independently establish those commitments." No impossibility claim, no implied faithful-rendering guarantee.

**3 (P2) — the universalized opening.** Replaced with the token-scoped form: "A conventional access token can establish what access it authorizes; the token alone cannot establish whether the task it serves is still approved." And "end it everywhere at once" is gone — the incident clause now closes on "how to wind it down," which is also the family's own verb.

**4 (P2) — layer collapses.** Policy engines "consume the task, authority, and lifecycle context a Mission-aware decision consumes" instead of deciding "against the record"; the Token Exchange row is narrowed to AS-mediated delegation and continuation with offline attenuation explicitly outside it; "Cross-App Access (XAA), via ID-JAG"; "Security Event Tokens (RFC 8417) / OpenID Shared Signals Framework."

**5 (P2) — conformance scope.** "Maps each inventoried requirement in its audited specification set to tested, partial, or todo coverage" — the audited-set qualifier carries the 11-of-41 reality without restating counts that will drift.

Structure untouched; family-manifest checker (all three README rules) and the chained Statement check green.

pulls.title: Core batch: goal_lang + i18n (#534), standing-consent approved_at + recency (#580), substrate Statement pointer (#551)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The core batch on explicit go-ahead: three issues, one reviewable PR against the editor's draft, one commit (`8a33f65f`).

**#534 — `goal_lang` and Internationalization Considerations.** An OPTIONAL BCP 47 language tag (RFC 5646, added as a normative reference) on the Mission Intent, declaring the language of the Intent's human-readable prose (`goal`, `constraints`, `success_criteria`). Design points from the issue resolved as follows: it sits inside the committed Intent, so `intent_hash` covers it automatically (the test proves two Intents differing only in `goal_lang` commit to different hashes); the new `{#i18n}` section states the three honesty rules — the declaration is syntactic only (well-formedness validated at submission acceptance, refused `invalid_request`; never a verified property of the text), rendering follows `{#consent-binding}` unchanged with translation recording left to Consent Evidence's one-locale-one-disclosure-one-hash rule (`goal_lang` declares the source's language, never what was rendered), and Authority Set entries deliberately gain no language-tagged display fields (localizing how authority is explained is the approval surface's duty, never a property of the committed set). Implementation: the member joins the closed Intent top level with well-formedness validation (2–8 alpha primary or `x`/`i` singleton, 1–8 alphanumeric subtags, the RFC 5646 §4.4.1 35-character support floor as the acceptance bound).

**#580 — the standing-consent human-approval instant.** `approval_basis.approved_at`, REQUIRED for every standing-consent `type` and absent for `direct` (whose approval event carries its own instant): the instant the accountable human approved the exact consented root that `root_commitment` commits — the template version, the drawdown policy version — not the activation instant. The activating issuer MUST verify it against retained, authenticated state for that exact version and MUST NOT accept it as the activating request's own uncorroborated assertion — the same verification discipline #575 landed for the AGR `policy` assertion's `approved_at`, cross-referenced to Approval Governance's Policy-Approval Recency as the AGR-path analogue. Recency: deployments MAY declare maximum standing-consent ages per consequence class; where a ceiling is declared, activation past it MUST be refused. Scoped deliberately per the issue: this PR is the core component only; the companion follow-through (template, child-delegation, progressive carrying and verifying the member) stays tracked on #580 — recommend keeping #580 open, re-scoped to the companions, or closing it against a fresh companion-scoped issue on merge.

**#551 — the substrate Statement pointer.** One informative paragraph at the end of Conformance: the binding's Mission Substrate Statement is published in the substrate companion's family appendix (`{#oauth-statement}`, landed with the Statement-migration arc, so the blocker is cleared); it restates this document, adds no requirement, and the core remains self-contained. The substrate was already an informative reference in the core's front matter, so the citation graph — which main now drift-checks — is unchanged.

**Ledger**: three new rows — `core.intent.goal-lang-well-formed` (tested, name verified under `--collect`), and `approved_at` verification plus recency-ceiling refusal as honest `todo`s under the new `core.standing-consent` capability (nothing in `src` implements a standing-consent basis with the member yet). Core spec digest re-audited. Tally 493 requirements (122 tested / 44 partial / 327 todo).

**Gates**: core draft clean through kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc; full suite 864 passed / 110 env-gated skips; conformance, family-manifest + chained Statement check, and SPEC_VERSIONS green; `--collect`'s 78 findings are all pre-existing environment-gated suites, none from this change. Document History carries all three by-touch entries under -01.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All six findings addressed across two commits per your provenance discipline: `cf8727d1` (spec + code + tests) and `2333cc8c` (the ledger, pinning the first).

**1 (P1) — real BCP 47.** The regex is gone; `isWellFormedBcp47` is a faithful RFC 5646 §2.1 implementation: langtag structure (language with extlang, script, region, variants, extensions, private use), the privateuse-only form, and the fixed grandfathered lists — plus the no-duplicate-singleton and no-duplicate-variant rules. All five of your invalid examples refuse (`x`, `i-foo`, `de-419-DE`, `en-a`/`en-x`, `ar-a-aaa-b-bbb-a-ccc`), and the tests carry them verbatim alongside grandfathered accepts (`i-klingon`, `art-lojban`) and multi-variant/duplicate-variant cases. The 35-character misreading is corrected in both directions: no length cap exists beyond the Intent's own size bound, and the valid 39-character `en-Latn-US-variant-a-extended-x-private` is an accepting test case.

**2 (P1) — the recency contract is core-normative.** The abbreviated rule became four normative rules in the core itself, no import-by-reference: the evaluation instant is the atomic Mission-creation commit (the same commit that re-checks effective expiry; deferred/relocated flows inherit at their own commit), and recency is issuance-time eligibility only — later ceiling changes or elapsed time never retroactively terminate an active Mission; `approved_at` is bounded by the evaluation instant plus a declared bounded skew, future-dated values refused; per-class ceilings select the strictest across every consequence class from the derived Authority Set and the Intent's consumption `controls`; and the ceilings and skew allowance are versioned, retained policy identified by the record's `policy_version` (a mutable out-of-band statement MUST NOT serve), so the decision reproduces from retained state. The AGR cross-reference remains, now as the analogue it is rather than the definition.

**3 (P1) — the family lands in one batch.** Template, child-delegation, and progressive each define `approved_at` for their basis type in this PR, and the implementation aligns in the same commit: the TypeScript basis shapes carry it REQUIRED, template dispatch reads it from the retained template record (the consent instant of the exact `template_version`), and child creation from the retained parent record — never from the request. Your `root_commitment` question is ruled with one principle: **`approved_at` follows the root's own approval provenance.** Both child-delegation root forms were consented at the parent's approval event (an entry-carried `child_creation_policy` reference rides the committed entry that approval covered); a deployment that separately versions and re-approves the referenced policy's content as its own standing consent carries that version's human-approval instant, verified from its retained governance record. Both basis round-trip tests pin the recorded value to the retained-state source.

**4 (P2) — capability split.** `core.standing-consent-recency` is its own declared capability; the refusal row is gated on it, since a deployment can run standing consent without declaring any ceiling.

**5 (P2) — provenance pinned.** `source.specs["draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md"].revision` now names `cf8727d1` (the commit whose text the rows were audited against) with the matching digest, and the SPEC_VERSIONS rows for the core's authorization-server surfaces and the child-delegation kernel are re-pinned to `cf8727d` (2026-08-21). Committed as the second commit so the pin can name the first.

**6 (P3) — the registered error is asserted.** Every malformed case asserts `IntentError.code === "invalid_request"` individually, and a new Submission-envelope intake test covers the PAR-path funnel with the same assertion.

**Also, one repair riding along (flagged per the #615 precedent):** this round's full-suite run surfaced a pre-existing time bomb on main — the discharge replay test hardcodes `observed_at: "2026-08-20T11:59:00Z"` while its HTTP harness runs on the real clock, so the endpoint's ±24h skew window expired at 2026-08-21 and the suite now fails everywhere, including on clean main (reproduced on a detached checkout). The instant is now clock-relative. Without this, every CI `test` run from today fails regardless of branch.

Gates: full suite 865 passed / 110 env-gated skips; all four drafts build clean; conformance at 493 (122 tested / 45 partial / 326 todo), family-manifest + chained Statement check, SPEC_VERSIONS, and `--collect` (unchanged 78 pre-existing env-gated findings) all green.

pulls.title: README front door: argue before navigating
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes the persuasion-layer review: the first half now makes the case a skeptical OAuth reader needs before meeting the family, and the reference layer follows.

**The arc, as prescribed**: attack-resistant opening (an access token carries authority for a resource request; it does not, by itself, establish the approved task or its continued approval — the not-survivable absolutism is gone); the tagline elevated to the definition (identity answers who, entitlements what a principal may hold, a Mission what work was approved and whether it is still in force); the four-object model (Intent → Mission → Authority → Action, lifecycle vertical); proposal-vs-authoritative-derivation precision; the **One Mission, end to end** steel thread (the family's own Q3-payables example, six steps, ending on the audit question); **What a Mission is not** answering the grant objection head-on (outlives any one token, spans RSs and — through projection — ASs, creates subordinate authority, ends as one object at the control point, with the materialized-credential residual stated, not hidden) and consolidating the perimeter (RAR, workflow ids, Transaction Tokens, identity chains, policy engines); **The standards proposal** (retitled, two-thing surface in WG language); minimal implementation directly beneath it; **Start here** led by the three rings (Core / Runtime-enforced profile / Optional capabilities) as the dominant hierarchy, with verbs, bindings, and assurance as secondary navigation.

**Also applied**: composes-with closes on the design claim (adjacent layers, designed to compose, not a disprovable no-overlap absolute) with the Token Exchange row simplified; the High-Assurance row spells out both named claims in place (no click required to understand the top level); maturity's first use carries the not-IETF-status note; Mission-gates phrasing de-anthropomorphized throughout (Mission state as authoritative input to the gates).

**Three deliberate deviations, each with a reason**:
1. **The verb table keeps the Architecture's canonical ten**, not the proposed seven: the verb spine is the family's citable signature and presentation overlays it, never regroups it (the #623 round specifically restored ten-verb agreement). The catalog-creep complaint is met the other way: the two catalog-sized cells (Govern's eight, Approve-and-Record's four) are slimmed to headline mechanisms with counts, and the table now points to DRAFTS.md's Verbs column as the full verb-to-document map — preserving the verb-to-spec links added on request in #623.
2. **Maturity labels keep their names** with the first-use disclaimer instead of renaming: the label vocabulary is load-bearing across family-manifest.json's enum, DRAFTS.md's generated index, and the validators.
3. **Every new claim stays inside the honest-claims bounds** the #624 round locked in: the steel thread's suspension step says issuance and refresh stop at the issuer and a Runtime-Enforced deployment denies at the decision point; the grant paragraph carries the materialized-credential residual in the same sentence as the kill-switch property.

Validation: family-manifest checker (all three README rules), chained Statement check, and drafts-index freshness green. 370 lines.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All seven findings fixed in `fd1cc615`.

**1 (P1) — the duplicate.** Gone: the rewrite had added the moved copy without deleting the original below the rewrite boundary. One `## The minimal implementation` heading remains, in its new position under the standards proposal.

**2 (P1) — Authority is the Authority Set.** The four-object model now reads exactly as you suggested: "the approved, bounded Authority Set for the work; tokens, grants, projections, and delegations carry or derive subsets of it." The carriers no longer masquerade as the authority, which keeps the sits-above-grants-and-tokens claim coherent.

**3 (P1) — all three anchors.** The example's step 2 now commits all three, with each named for what it covers (`intent_hash` over the task, `proposal_hash` over what the agent asked for, `authority_hash` over what was granted) — the asked-vs-granted distinction stated exactly where the narrative earns it. The opening's commitment sentence names `proposal_hash` where a proposal was submitted, with the same distinction in a clause.

**4 (P1) — the Runtime ring is dependency-closed.** Substrate Requirements is now the ring's first entry ("the kernel contract the runtime documents consume"), matching the manifest's `adoption_requires` edges for runtime, runtime-evidence, and authzen. The each-ring-is-complete promise now holds.

**5 (P1) — the steelman.** The grant paragraph concedes the strong form up front: a grant, consent record, refresh family, or PDP record can be durable and lifecycle-bearing within one AS's administrative domain, and durability is not the difference. The difference claimed is the one the Architecture claims: the standardized approved-task object joining many grants, credentials, actors, and evidence producers — and, through projection, trust domains — with the materialized-credential residual still in the same sentence.

**6 (P2) — vocabulary.** "Independently selectable companion work with declared dependencies" in the standards proposal, and "each selectable on its own with its declared dependencies" in the rings. No more contradiction with the `adoption_requires` instructions below.

**7 (P2) — the complete claim shape.** Trifecta containment's parenthetical now carries the egress-channel enumeration and the pre-consented-destination carve-out, and a sentence under the table states the epistemics: both names are claims with proof obligations — the parentheses give their shape, and the Architecture's declared per-condition evidence and appraisal contract is what establishes them, never the wire alone.

Validators green (family-manifest's three README rules, chained Statement check, drafts-index freshness).

pulls.title: OAuth is one binding, part 1: reader surfaces
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
First of three PRs executing the layering ruling (the family is Mission-Bound Authorization, not Mission-Bound OAuth; OAuth = most deployed infrastructure, never more Mission-mature; no production Missions anywhere).

Built from a two-agent audit that classified every OAuth-privileging instance (CORE-VOCAB / LAYER-INVERSION / DEFAULT-BINDING / MATURITY-IMPLIES-DEPLOYMENT / STRUCTURAL, with LEGITIMATE instances fenced off — the published I-D's own title, oauth-mission-* companions being OAuth-lane by design, the reference implementation's substrate). Notable audit fact: the manifest's maturity **data** is already symmetric (OAuth, MAS, AAuth all `stable`); the privileging lived in prose and structure.

**This PR (reader surfaces)**: DRAFTS.md's 'The core' section retired and the peer section reordered kernel-first ('The substrate and the bindings'); the false 'Every other document builds on this one' corrected; README's opening de-OAuthed, ring 1 renamed 'The model and a binding', the steel thread labeled as the OAuth realization, the binding table led by the peers/infrastructure/maturity framing, the AAuth row stated in its own terms; DEPENDENCIES' singular 'the stable adoption path' pluralized with MAS and AAuth named; manifest group 'core' retired, `is_published_core` → `is_published_draft`, stacks $comment carries the infrastructure rationale. The canonical three-part framing sentence now exists in three places (proposal, binding table, DRAFTS disclaimer).

**Coming next**: part 2 — Architecture + Security Model (the '(the core)' shorthand and its ~40 cites, terms sourced from one binding, the entry-ramps 'upgrade path' waystation framing vs MAS's own 'peer binding, not a staging area', the reference-architecture infrastructure rationale, the security model's 'other bindings re-derive the deltas' contradiction). Part 3 — the six binding-neutral companions' 'this version's normative substrate' pattern, with conformance digests re-audited.

Validators green (family-manifest three README rules + group placement, chained Statement check, drafts-index freshness).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All five findings addressed: F1/F2/F4/F5 here in `006c65b9`, F3 (and F5's Architecture instance) on #628 in `9506fe77`, since the MAS lines live in that PR's scope.

**1 (P1) — the substrate joins the standardization surface.** The proposal is now three layers, stated as such: the informative **Architecture** (the model), the normative **Mission Substrate Requirements** (the binding-neutral kernel contract, publishing before or with any binding claiming conformance to it), and the **OAuth issuance binding** as the one complete binding for the most-deployed substrate. OAuth is no longer the model's de facto normative home.

**2 (P1) — ring 1 is dependency-closed per binding.** The ring now carries Architecture plus Substrate Requirements plus "one binding's dependency-closed adoption set from the peer table below (the manifest's `adoption_requires` edges name each binding's floor)". The OAuth binding's self-containment is stated as its own property — one document, a useful deployment by itself — with the peers declaring their own floors rather than inheriting a false completeness promise.

**3 (P1) — the MAS lines, on #628.** Part 3 of that PR had already recast "the strongest deployment" and "the stronger, stable binding" as the token-plane chokepoint; per this finding, `9506fe77` names the capability differences explicitly — "the two capabilities a joined deployment lacks (Mission-bound credentials and issuance gating)" — and calls the difference "a capability difference between the bindings rather than a maturity one," with no superlative left. The README's steel-thread label here also changed per your wording: the peers "realize the same kernel on their own substrates, each declaring its lifecycle capabilities in its Mission Substrate Statement."

**4 (P2) — publication metadata scales.** `is_published_draft` and its exactly-one validator invariant are gone (the invariant could not survive the substrate or a second binding reaching the Datatracker). Publication is now zero-or-more `datatracker_url` metadata, validated to name the draft's own slug; the 40 vestigial `false` flags are dropped (absent means unpublished). The stragglers are migrated: the manifest summary no longer says "The mandatory core" (generated index refreshed), and README Status reads "The OAuth binding is a published Internet-Draft."

**5 (P2) — the claim is scoped to evidence.** Every instance on these surfaces (proposal, binding table, both DRAFTS.md instances, the stacks `$comment`) and the Architecture's citable peer statement on #628 now reads "no production Mission deployment is known today," never the unbounded universal.

Validators green on both branches (family-manifest with the new datatracker_url rule, chained Statement check, drafts-index freshness; conformance with the MAS digest re-audited, no row text affected).

pulls.title: OAuth is one binding, parts 2+3: the Architecture, the Security Model, and the companions
pulls.author: mcguinness

**Part 2 (`d5a2b73a`) — the citable layering.** The Architecture gains the peer statement at the decomposition (bindings are peers; OAuth first-authored on the substrate with the most deployed infrastructure; a deployment fact, not a maturity ranking; no production Missions anywhere), and every one of its 45 'the core' usages now reads 'the OAuth binding'. The base reference stack is one issuer binding shown in its OAuth realization for infrastructure reasons (stack display names unchanged; the manifest tripwire holds); the actor chain and substrate section label their OAuth instantiations with ownership migrating to the substrate by touch; the entry ramps stop framing the MAS as a waystation (matching the MAS's own 'peer binding, not a staging area'); the document map corrects the oauth-mission and mission-substrate entries. **Part 3 (`ae2a8bf4`) — the companions.** 'This version's normative substrate' becomes 'this version's reference host' across runtime, authzen, harness, mandate (the phrase collided with the family's actual substrate and read OAuth as the assumed base); approval-governance opens on the Mission model's rule with minimal conformance reading 'conformant to its Mission binding'; the MAS's 'strongest deployment' and 'stronger, stable binding' become the structural fact (token-plane chokepoint) with 'not yet exercised in production deployment, like every mechanism in this family' stated plainly; UMA stops equating the Mission model with the OAuth document ('first specified in its OAuth binding'). Nine drafts clean through kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc; conformance digests re-audited for the three audited specs (runtime, authzen, authority-server) with no row text affected; family-manifest (architecture-map + stacks tripwire) and Statement checks green.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All six findings addressed in `58c7a857`. The organizing correction is the one your review implies: the first pass overcorrected from OAuth-privileged into false binding-neutrality; this round is OAuth-specific where the structure is OAuth's, kernel-scoped where it is the kernel's.

**1 (P1) — Mandate v1 is scoped.** Two native hosts (the OAuth binding and the MAS) plus UMA realizing the same AS surface — "UMA adds no third Mandate host." The AAuth bullet is gone, replaced by the honest scoping paragraph: this version's payload is defined over the OAuth-shaped record whose members those hosts record (the integrity anchors, `subject`, `client_id`, `policy_version`); AAuth commits approval through its own construction with no OAuth integrity anchors, so an AAuth Mandate is a distinct payload profile with its own verification rules, deliberately not defined by this version.

**2 (P1) — AGR's introduction is scoped.** "An authority-bearing binding of the Mission model records one accountable Approver…" with the OAuth binding cited as stating the rule "whose record members this document's binding rules consume." No kernel-level claim remains.

**3 (P1) — the Security Model splits kernel from capabilities.** Its analysis rests on the kernel every binding provides (reference and controller, only-active state space, governance gate, bounded reliance); the capability-conditioned entries (Structured Authority's representation-with-subset-rule, the anchor envelope, Credential-Bound) apply where the selected binding claims them in its Mission Substrate Statement, with the selected binding's own document as the normative owner of the cited surfaces, and a missing capability inherited as inapplicable, not a failure. The Status section now assigns enforcement obligations to the selected binding, with OAuth as the parenthetical instance.

**4 (P1) — the stack is explicitly the OAuth realization, and the peer statement is precise.** "Protocol core: the OAuth issuance binding alone, the realization these stacks are expressed in (chosen for OAuth 2.0's deployed infrastructure)… The stacks are this OAuth realization throughout; a peer binding realizes the levels per its own document, and peer standing does not imply identical rungs or capabilities." The peer statement now distinguishes the binding (OAuth) from the substrate (OAuth 2.0), and "exactly as on every other substrate" is gone — replaced by "peer standing implies neither identical capabilities nor identical adoption cost: AAuth, natively contextual, adds no new wire members."

**5 (P2) — the sweep is complete.** Zero `normative substrate` instances remain repo-wide (your grep will confirm): harness's body paragraph, orchestration, and audit read "reference host" with the substrate contract named; containment reads "base profile," correctly, being an OAuth-lane companion. The Architecture's core compounds are fixed: "The Mission lifecycle states," "defined by the OAuth binding or by a companion," "The OAuth binding states the same composition property," "The OAuth binding's Privacy Considerations." "Protocol core" remains as the intentional stack name.

**6 (P2) — MAS.** "…places the chokepoint at the token plane, **supplying** the two capabilities a joined deployment lacks…" and "like every mechanism in this family, **has no known production deployment**."

No front-matter reference changes anywhere, so the manifest's typed-edges graph is untouched; nine drafts build clean; MAS conformance digest re-audited with no row text affected; all validators green.

pulls.title: Layering audit: full-family alignment sweep
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The full-family audit you asked for, executed: three agents swept all 41 drafts and every prose surface against the layering rubric as refined through #627/#628, I adjudicated each finding, and this PR lands the fixes.

**Headline numbers**: ~60 residual 'the core' instances found and eliminated (the earlier sweep was pattern- and case-sensitive; 'The core' and line-wrapped instances survived it — this one is case-insensitive, wrap-aware, and grep-verified to zero, with sanctioned uses fenced: the published binding's adjectival self-descriptions and Document History, ordinary adjectival 'core', AuthZEN's own 'Core 1.0'). One vocabulary rule now holds everywhere: neutral documents and the substrate say **the OAuth binding**; OAuth-lane companions say **the issuance profile**. Both places that re-*defined* the retired alias (issuance-grant, discovery) no longer do.

**Structural findings fixed**: the one genuine R6 violation (issuance-grant's 'The core is the destination, not a competitor' — recast as within-lane grant retirement that ranks nothing); attenuation and management family-overclaims lane-scoped; AAM's top framing aligned with its own accurate Conformance section; capability-binding's digest encoding re-attributed to the substrate's default commitment construction per the #284 ruling; metering's acknowledgment names the family.

**Clean bills worth having on record**: all 41 manifest summaries and pull_when entries, README, DEMO, the notes files (properly historical), 11 of 19 OAuth-lane companions, and — importantly — the published OAuth binding itself: correct kernel attribution at all three substrate-relationship references, zero binding-ranking language, nothing needing a core edit.

**Deliberately left**: the core's Document History line (historical by the by-touch convention), SPEC_VERSIONS' changelog entry (same), PLAN.md's implementation-table cell (rides the next direct-to-main D-entry commit per the PLAN convention).

Verification: zero residuals by cross-line grep; all 41 drafts rebuild; one conformance row re-audited where the sweep touched its quoted clause; seven audited-spec digests bumped; every validator green (conformance 493 at 122/45/326, family-manifest + Statements, drafts-index, SPEC_VERSIONS).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All findings addressed in `1c942878`.

**1 (P1) — the substrate owns the commitment construction, completely.** Runtime Evidence's three attribution points all moved: the canonicalization sentence ("JCS canonicalization applies… under the substrate's default commitment construction"), the digest-encoding sentence, and the digest member's canonical-object/raw-octet classification — plus the matching conformance row, re-quoted. This completes the #284 ruling's application: mission-* documents import commitments from the substrate, never the issuance profile, and OAuth attribution survives only where the anchors themselves are OAuth's (the substrate's own worked test-vector pointer, now correctly named "The OAuth binding's Integrity Anchor Test Vectors").

**2 (P2) — the zero is now machine-owned, not claimed.** Every named residual is gone: the substrate's three "Core's / OAuth core's" instances and its disclosed-history sentence, the Architecture's "OAuth core" binding cell and two prose instances, DRAFTS' "single-domain core," and the payments operation profile's "the core's `max_amount` shape" (its tier column's "core" is the runtime profile's own enforcement-tier vocabulary and stays). And the structural fix you prescribed: **family-manifest check (p) retired-vocabulary** now scans every draft (except the OAuth binding's own document, whose adjectival self-descriptions and Document History are sanctioned), the reader surfaces, and the conformance manifest for `the core` / `OAuth core` / `Core's` — with adjectival followers allowed (evaluation, record, principle, enforcement tier) and exactly one explicit allowlist entry (a vitest test name recorded in a conformance row; renaming it means renaming the test).
