**Editorials**: Status compares completion to "baseline issuance and runtime enforcement" (capabilities, not a document); management reads "the OAuth lane's fleet-management surface"; child-delegation reads "the issuance profile's approval event."

Three audited-spec digests re-audited (runtime-evidence, substrate, status); touched drafts build clean; all validators green including the new tripwire running on every CI push from now on.

pulls.title: Architecture consolidation: order, nesting, and tables
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Executes the consolidation proposal as three gate-green commits, with two honest findings reported up front.

**What changed:**
1. **One Mission section, the spine promoted, the map added** — the Capability Envelope and A Mission's Life nest under The Mission (with the four-object framing stated once, matching the README's model); the Mission Verbs move from line 1,743 to directly after Non-Goals, so the citable skeleton appears before the reference material it organizes; the Ontology Contract nests under Mission Invariants; a Map of This Document follows the Introduction. Light dedupe only (the AAuth realization told once).
2. **The substrate primitives become one table** — six definition/home/consumers prose subsections collapse into a scannable four-column table in their OAuth realization, with the commitment-anchors-not-proofs warning kept as prose and an explicit anchor added to Approval Fidelity (the ontology contract cites its auto-slug). Kept whole as irreducible signature content: Token Classes, the Mission-Bound Credential, the Validity Model, the Binding Checklist, Error Surfaces.
3. **The Document Map becomes a map** — 41 definition-list entries convert to grouped Document|Role tables (246 → 112 lines), every role sentence preserved, DRAFTS.md pointed to as the full catalog.

**Two honest findings from doing the work:**
- The proposal estimated −33%; the real number is **3,426 → 3,245 (−5%)**. Reading every candidate cluster showed the assumed duplication mostly is not there: the Assurance Levels' proof obligations and test sets, the kill-switch composition table, the Prevention/Detection and Containment matrices, the conventional-stack steelman, and the Deployment Profile are each stated exactly once and earned their lines through this month's rulings. The document's real problems were **order** (the spine buried 1,300 lines deep), **nesting** (four top-level tellings of one object), and **prose where tables scan** — all fixed. Forcing further cuts would have violated the consolidate-structure-not-content discipline.
- The proposed per-section italic 'this section answers' lines were dropped: the sections already open with strong statement sentences, and the family's tight-prose rule counts that kind of meta-commentary as noise.

**Preserved and verified per commit**: all external couplings (the # Mission Document Map heading and all short forms, the four stack display names, {#layers}/{#reference-architecture}/{#packages}/{#binding-properties}/{#assurance-levels}, zero retired vocabulary under check (p)); kramdown+xml2rfc builds (which prove every internal anchor, including the auto-slug ones); family-manifest + Statement checks green on each commit.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All five findings addressed in `fb4bff1d`.

**1 (P1) — the AAuth arc is precise again.** The walkthrough tail restores the former exact statement — the Person Server governs the native Mission Context through propose, clarify, approve, and the mission log — and now names what it does not emulate in full: the AS's Authority Set, integrity anchors, PDP permits, Child Missions, and portable evidence, matching baseline AAuth's unclaimed capabilities exactly. My compression had traded precision for brevity; wrong trade.

**2 (P1) — the four dropped semantics are back, inside the cells.** "No semantic content" on the Mission Identifier; "an algorithm-prefixed encoding a verifier recognizes or rejects (unknown prefixes refuse; no downgrade)" on the anchor envelope; "harness pause, suppress, and terminate" (the queue-preserving behavior restored); and the subset rule "(derived or delegated authority is never broader)" with Common Constraints "(registered names with fixed subset and intersection rules)". The prose subsections stay retired.

**3 (P2) — the map agrees with the manifest, and structurally cannot drift again.** A new **Cross-domain projection and continuity** group carries cross-domain, cross-org delegation, and Continuation (with the external ICA transport riding informatively); AAM moved under **Architecture mappings** and work-products under **Security model**, both matching their manifest groups; and one misplacement was fixed at the *source* — metering's manifest group was `bindings-substrate` (an artifact of its old catalog position), now `runtime-enforcement`, with its DRAFTS.md block relocated to match, so all three surfaces agree semantically. Your "ideally" is implemented: checker (d) upgraded from short-form presence to **group agreement** — every draft must sit under the doc-map group its manifest group maps to via an explicit header map, with a found-under-instead diagnostic. Perturbation-proved: moving a row to the wrong group fails CI naming both groups.

**4 (P2) — the framings are qualified.** "The **authorization flow** separates four objects…" and "**Separately from the authorization flow's four objects** ({{the-mission}}), a deployment… governs three independently lifecycle-bearing objects." The sets read as the different taxonomies they are.

**5 (P3) — forward reference and map completeness.** The ontology opens with "The derivation boundary ({{derivation-boundary}}, later in this document) settles…", and the Map of This Document now covers the derivation boundary, the prevention-detection and containment matrices, and Mission Requirements.

All gates green: the build (proving every internal anchor), family-manifest with the new placement checks on both DRAFTS.md and the doc map, drafts-index freshness, conformance, and the retired-vocab tripwire.

pulls.title: Substrate contract: consolidation for readability and scanability
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Owner-directed revisit of the substrate contract for readability and scanability, from the six-move proposal delivered in session. Unlike the Architecture pass, the normative body here is irreducible by design: 83 conformance rows quote its sentences verbatim across 24 anchors, so the consolidation targets are the edges — currency, scan surfaces, nesting, and rendering.

**Commit 1 — the appendices become current.**
- **M1**: The Binding Mapping Guidance appendix predates the real Statements. Its illustrative 9×3 capability table covered three of the five peer bindings and restated, speculatively, what five normative CI-validated Statements now state authoritatively. The table is retired for a pointer to all five Statements (UMA and GNAP join the informative references, with the family-manifest reference edges synced), and the three prose mappings remain as named design poles that teach the mapping method: **broad-claims** (OAuth), **separation-and-join** (MAS), **private-context** (AAuth).
- **M4**: The OPTIONAL-roles relation table carried paragraph-length cells (the Delegation cell ran ~130 words) that mangle in text rendering. It is now a definition list preserving every clause. The retired "Core optional roles" / "Core OPTIONAL capability" / "Core delegation" vocabulary — which slipped check (p)'s regex because no "the" precedes it — becomes OAuth-binding vocabulary.
- **M6**: The ownership-migrates-by-touch rule regroups beside the scoped-precedence rule; it had dangled after the OAuth Statement as if it governed only that.

**Commit 2 — scan surfaces and nesting.**
- **M2**: Two additive index tables: the 9 kernel duties and the 8 optional capabilities, one line each, pointing at their sections. Pure scan surface; no pinned prose touched.
- **M3**: Default Commitment Construction — a MAY construction that commits "the Approved Context and any other artifact" and that family profiles import standalone (#284 ruling) — is promoted from two levels under one kernel duty to its own top-level section between the kernel and the capabilities. That also fixes a hygiene wart: a MAY construction no longer lives inside the everything-here-is-MUST kernel. The explicit `{#default-commitment}` anchor survives; the kernel duty gains a one-sentence pointer; "the duties above" becomes the explicit `{{approved-context}}` reference.

**Commit 3 — timeless prose (M5).** The Statement section narrated the retired `conditional` state's history. The four-facts insight is kept as the positive rule (an activation condition states separately what a specification defines, an implementation supports, a deployment enables, and where the property applies); the archaeology is dropped.

**Commit 4 — conformance digest.** Audit digest bumped, revision pinning the spec commit. Zero requirement-row changes: before editing, every `approved-context`, `default-commitment`, and `statement` row was checked against the planned edits — none quotes moved-or-reworded text, and no pinned anchor changes.

**Honest size report** (the D124 lesson, stated up front): source grows 1,261 → 1,325 lines. Content shrank (crosswalk table and archaeology deleted); the growth is the two index tables plus the definition list, which spends source lines to fix rendered readability. This was a currency-and-scanability pass, not a shrink, and the proposal said so.

**Guardrails observed**: the CI-pinned OAuth capability table (title, header, canonical 8 rows) is byte-identical; all 24 conformance anchors survive; all gates green (family-manifest, substrate-statements, conformance, drafts-index, retired-vocab) and the draft builds clean, proving every internal and new external reference.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All five points addressed in `a6b06042` (digest follow-up `6e6151e2`).

**1 (High) — the promoted construction is self-contained.** Adoption is now defined for any importing specification: "Any specification that defines a commitment, a Mission Substrate Binding or an importing profile alike, MAY satisfy the commitment duties of {{approved-context}}…" — and the second, surviving positional reference ("stating its own algorithm identification and agility behavior under the duties above") is now an explicit `{{approved-context}}` reference too, with "a binding with a native or member-named commitment" widened to "a specification". The two pinned conformance rows in this section are untouched.

**2 (Medium) — Person Server, throughout.** The appendix pole now reads "the Person Server (PS) controls approval and contextual decisions" (establishing the PS abbreviation the later "PS-issued" / "PS-local" wording resolves against). You caught more than you flagged: the Introduction had a second instance, line-wrapped as "An AAuth Policy / Server", invisible to single-line grep — fixed, and a corpus-wide wrapped-pattern sweep confirms no other residual in the family. The AAuth binding itself uses Person Server exclusively, so the substrate now matches its source.

**3 (Medium) — semantics owners, not the carrier.** "Registered authorization-detail types can supply Structured Authority: each type's semantics owner defines its operations, constraints, and comparison behavior, and Rich Authorization Requests are the carrier, not the semantics." This restores the deleted table's precision in the surviving prose.

**4 (Low) — conditional unguessability.** The index row now says "how unguessability is met where the reference is disclosed beyond the Controller", matching the normative rule's disclosure condition and its allowance for protected predictable namespaces.

**5 (terminology) — implementation roles.** "The OAuth binding's three OPTIONAL implementation roles, which its Conformance section names OPTIONAL capabilities…" — the rename you asked for, keeping traceability to the source section's own vocabulary so a reader landing in either document can join the two names.

Gates green: family-manifest, substrate-statements (the pinned OAuth capability table remains byte-identical), conformance (no row changes; digest bumped pinning the spec commit), and the draft builds clean.

pulls.title: OAuth binding: consolidation for readability and scanability
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Owner-directed revisit of the published OAuth binding, following the Architecture (D124) and substrate (D125) passes, from the six-move proposal delivered in session. The document's dominant growth artifact was **repetition with archaeology**: each amendment round left a local restatement of rules stated elsewhere, plus retired-design narratives in the main flow.

**Safety net first (commit 1).** Explicit anchors pinned on all 22 surviving auto-slugged headings — extracted from the generated XML, not guessed — so every published fragment identifier is preserved byte-for-byte and future retitles cannot silently break references. The 29 conformance-pinned quotes were mapped against every planned edit site before the pass ran: zero overlap, zero row changes.

**One home per rule + timeless prose (commit 2).**
- `client_id`'s registered meaning: canonical at `mission-bound-tokens` (issuance side) and `rs-enforcement` (consumption side); the ~50-line "Adopted Model" rejected-design narrative compressed to its design rationale under its kept `{#client-id-rebinding}` anchor, and the delegation/worked-example restatements trimmed to references.
- The submission trust rule (proposal, never authority) stated once in Submission via PAR; the Authority Proposal instance now defers to it.
- The RFC 7662 deviation justified once, in the introspection intro; the two downstream re-justifications became back-references.
- The prefix single-normalization rule owned by Resource Boundary Canonicalization; the runtime-boundary duplicate defers.
- "Mission Drift" deleted: it restated the Conformance gate summary, and even its SHOULD duplicated Issuance Gating's; Information Propagation re-anchored to `{{lifecycle}}`.
- Both "Earlier revisions of this document…" passages, "now"/"no longer" framing (6 sites), and "this version"/"v1 property" language removed; the Document History carries the record.
- Deliberately **kept** after inspection: the Agent/Approver double definitions (glossary vs. principal model serve different lookups), the disclosure-only per-member and block statements (member definition vs. AS-side enforcement rule), and the AS-asserted-subset-trust clause at its three sites (definition semantics, RS duty, mechanical rule).

**Structure (commit 3).** Three moves, each exploiting existing order:
- Introduction: five positioning subsections became **Why a New Object** + **Relationship to Adjacent Work**; the agent-identity subsection was fully redundant with the Introduction's own opening and folded in by reference.
- **Submission Processing Order** now closes the submission arc as its own section (it governs the whole envelope, not evidence alone).
- The commitment machinery (Integrity Anchors, Canonicalization Rules, Commitment Mechanisms) promoted out of the approval ceremony into a top-level **Integrity and Commitments** section — a pure heading insertion, since the three sections already sat contiguously; no block moved, no anchor changed.
- Security Considerations grouped into five themed clusters (**Commitment and Consent Integrity / Agent-Specific Threats / Enforcement Boundaries / Credentials and Delegation / Composition and Residual Authority**) by inserting group headings and demoting in place — the 16 flat sections were already in clustered order.

**Scan surfaces + currency (commit 4).** `mission_denial`'s three values as a definition list; a remediation-grains summary table; the prefix-matching ALLOW/DENY examples as a three-column table; and the end-to-end example now shows `mission_id` and `mission_expires_at` on the token response — the client surface Conformance requires, previously never illustrated. **Common Constraints deliberately stays prose**: its Subset/Intersection semantics are paragraph-length, and paragraph cells are the mangled-table anti-pattern the substrate pass (D125) just removed — the existing bullets already carry a fixed Name/Type/Subset/Intersection microformat.

**History + digest (commits 5–6).** A Document History `-01` entry records the pass as editorial with no normative change (every removed sentence restates a rule that remains stated at its home); the conformance audit digest pins the spec commit.

pulls.title: Architecture: correctness round from external review (precise gap, residual honesty, capability algebra, bundles-not-claims)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the deep external review of the Architecture document (reviewed at `b4e35419`), scoped per the owner's direction: **the 50% restructure is not adopted**; this is a correctness and honesty round within the document's existing structure. Rulings per finding:

**1 — Accepted.** The opening now states OAuth's baseline accurately (delegated authorization, tokens spanning requests, durable grants and consent records behind them) and the real gap in the reviewer's stronger form: no independently addressable, lifecycle-bearing approved-task object whose semantics persist across tokens, actors, audiences, and evidence.

**2 — Accepted, at every site.** The exact three-part rule replaces "only active permits reliance": only `active` permits new decisions and derivation; a state-aware consumer relies while it observes `active`; a state-unaware consumer retains the bounded materialized-credential residual. Expiry "closes the temporal bound by the clock alone, observing no revocation, suspension, completion, or containment"; a revocation *can* land inside a window, it just has no observation point that reaches the artifact first. R8 carries the same correction.

**3 — Accepted, and the manifest already knew.** The family manifest's `reference_stacks` `$comment` explicitly records that the Architecture's three-item sentence omits `mission-runtime-evidence` — the prose was the drifted side. The stack prose is now dependency-closed (runtime evidence named; substrate arriving by adoption closure as runtime and AuthZEN's normative kernel; Status the reference freshness choice), matching the manifest, with the Runtime-Enforced Documents line closed the same way. "Ratified" → "non-experimental family documents". The stale no-executable-rows claim now points at the conformance manifest **without volatile counts** — the reviewer's own citation (460/89/39) was already stale against current (493/122/45), which is exactly why numbers don't belong in this prose.

**4 — Accepted.** Requirements now mirror the substrate's capability algebra: Structured Authority and Monotonic Derivation are separate claims, the second requiring the first; Runtime-Enforced sits over a State-Observable source with a stated staleness bound; requirement 8 scales honestly (Decision Evidence always; *shown* needs Consent Evidence; *done* needs Execution Evidence for covered classes; the full join is reconstructible where those are adopted). R16: classified, suppressed/cancelled where possible, compensated where authorized, or escalated — irreversible and unknown outcomes remain. R18 separates the projection grant (authority) from the Mandate (grants nothing, verifiable facts).

**5 — Accepted.** Levels are **adoption bundles only** — never earned, claimed, or compared; the claims axis is the sole comparison surface, listed in the Deployment Profile beside residuals. "Full agent safety" is gone. "Compromise-resistant custody" is restored to the exact normative name **agent-compromise-resistant enforcement**.

**6 — Accepted, via honest claims.** The illustrative profile now declares `assurance_claims` (replacing the level label) and claims agent-compromise-resistant enforcement **but not trifecta containment** — which its memory/provider-context residual then honestly permits. `external_commitment` joins `action_bound_approval_classes`; `external_communication` moves out of the runtime classification list into the egress model (`exposure.egress_mediated`), matching runtime's actual class enum; execution-environment attestation is declared.

**7 — Accepted.** The digest loop is conditioned on a deployed semantic-binding mechanism, with the explicit statement that an ordinary registered type can carry stable semantics with neither digest. The evidence claim is corrected: the join makes the judgment *reconstructible*; a task-aware decision point can draw the history from trusted prior workflow state at decision time.

**8 — Accepted.** Entry ramps state the day-one work: Mission-creating clients change (PAR + `mission_intent` + lifecycle refusals); scope-only Resource Servers keep scope-grain enforcement only, per-entry constraints arriving via projection or PEP; the MAS row names approval integration, correlation, and the PEP/PDP join; the short mission keeps issuer-owned state and the issuance gate.

**9 — Partially accepted.** The five packages' false claim ("each belongs to one package") is corrected: the machine-checked document-map groups (D124's checker) are the maintained assignment, and the packages are the product architect's view, with drafts allowed to span packages. The wholesale spine replacement, catalog extraction, and verb demotion are **declined**: the verb spine is the family's signature view, the Document Map is machine-checked against the manifest as of D124, and the owner scoped this round against the 50% cut.

**10 — Accepted.** Security Considerations now name the seven composition-risk classes (stale state and materialized authority, unmediated paths, semantic-derivation trust, component compromise, context splicing and join ambiguity, false-but-correctly-signed evidence, correlation) with the Security Model carrying the full analysis; Privacy adds the cross-profile dataflow view (issuer concentration, evidence join, identifier travel) and the one-shape minimization rule.

**Smaller items**: token-class names attributed to the OAuth binding's Terminology; "full agent safety" removed; Baseline rung cell carries the outstanding-token residual; Runtime-Enforced rung cell defers reversal/compensation to the orchestration profile; Governed Agent cell says Consent Evidence binds each approval event. **Declined**: the A2A/AP2/ACP/MCP pointer — the design note is repo-internal and not a citable reference from an I-D under the family's citation-hygiene rules; the AAM companion carries the formal agent-architecture mapping, and formalizing the protocol matrix as a companion remains available if wanted.

**Also declined per standing reservations**: extracting the Deployment Profile JSON to a separate design note (the Deployment Profile's document-form is the parked #281 decision, deliberately reserved) and moving the minimum test sets to the manifest (they are the levels' earned test sets from prior rounds; the stale executable-rows sentence, the actual defect, is fixed).

Gates: build clean (all internal references), family-manifest (including the reference-stack name tripwire and doc-map group agreement), substrate-statements, drafts-index. The architecture carries no conformance rows or digest entry, so no manifest changes ride along.

comments.body:
All seven points addressed in `366e9ab0`.

**1 (High) — the example claims only what its evidence supports.** `agent-compromise-resistant enforcement` is removed from `assurance_claims`. Rather than importing a seven-condition evidence map into an illustrative shape (bloat, and a drift hazard against runtime's normative list), the lead-in now names exactly what a real claim requires — the runtime profile's per-condition evidence bindings (EAT profile and claim identifiers, measurements, appraisal policy, attester identity, freshness, signed approval configuration, rendering evidence, path-completeness audit) — and states that this shape's generic attestation reference is declaration input, not that proof. pulls.title: Consent evidence: register the +jws media type and structured syntax suffix (#536)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes #536.

The JWS protected `typ` `mission-consent-evidence+jws` is MUST-carried by the signing and verification steps, but only the `+json` variants were registered. The draft's typ-vs-payload distinction is **deliberate and preserved** (the typ names the secured representation; the payload identifier stays `application/mission-consent-evidence+json`, which the audit profile's `payload-preimage-content-type` carries) — so the fix is registration, not restructuring:

- `application/mission-consent-evidence+jws` registered beside its `+json` sibling;
- the Integrity and Verification section ties the short-form typ to the registered type per RFC 7515 §4.1.9, keeping the exact-match substitution defense intact;
- because `+jws` is **not** a registered structured syntax suffix, the document also requests that suffix registration (the same pattern by which `+jwt` entered the registry via the SET spec).

**Same-gap audit per the issue**: runtime-evidence (`evidence_envelope`) and approval-governance (record envelope) both use their registered `+json` media types as protected typ values — no gap there; consent-evidence was the only unregistered typ.

No conformance rows or digest entry exist for this file; build and all checkers green.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All three points addressed in `c7fa32ad` (digest follow-up `c383469a`).

**1 (P1) — the suffix request is gone.** You caught a knowledge-staleness error: IANA registered `+jws` on 2025-12-09, and my proposal was reasoning from the pre-registration world. The Structured Syntax Suffix Registry section is removed (a duplicate request RFC 6838 would have IANA reject), and both the IANA intro and the media-type text now say the registration uses the suffix already registered with IANA. The `application/mission-consent-evidence+jws` registration stays.

**2 (P1) — audit conclusion corrected; the siblings adopt the composed model.** My audit stopped at "typ values are registered" and missed that they were registered as *payload* types doing *complete-JWS* duty. Both siblings now carry the RFC 7515 §§4.1.9–4.1.10 pair exactly as you proposed:

- **Runtime evidence**: `typ: application/mission-runtime-evidence+jws` (one umbrella secured type, newly registered — five media types now) with `cty` naming the record kind through the existing four `+json` registrations. The cross-use rejection is restated over the pair ("reject a JWS whose protected `typ` is not the umbrella **or** whose protected `cty` is not the media type of the object it is verifying"), the refusal-record and receipt envelope rules state their `cty`, receipt verification checks both members, and the shared-shape paragraph's "sole authority for which kind a signature covers" now names `cty`. The conformance row `evidence.integrity.typ-rejects-cross-use` tracks the rewritten sentence (still todo; digest bumped pinning the spec commit).
- **Approval governance**: `typ: application/mission-approval-governance+jws` (newly registered) with `cty: application/mission-approval-governance+json`, exact-pair rejection.
- The audit profile's worked example shows the composed header. The payload-typed uses that correctly stay `+json`: the evidence *reference* descriptors' `type` member and `payload-preimage-content-type`, both of which name the record, not the JWS.

**3 (P2) — `Macintosh file type code(s): N/A`** on the `+jws` registration (and on the two new `+jws` registrations), matching `application/jose`; the `+json` payload registrations keep their existing TEXT convention.

pulls.title: Gateway PEP: Mission-Reference propagation on both carriages (#557)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Advances #557, part 1 (follow-up from #283: "spec-only closure would leave the identified implementer gap present in the reference stack").

**Scope after review**: this PR delivers the carriage (both transports), the credential-governs conflict rule with issuer authoritative end-to-end, and the refusal contract. The MAS Join consumption path, a gateway selecting a Mission for a credential that carries no mission claim, is the remaining #557 scope and keeps the issue open; no Join substrate exists in src yet.

**What landed** — the Mission Reference Propagation channel (`authority-server#reference-propagation`) wired through the reference stack's gateway PEP path:

- **Strict parsers in mission-core**: the `Mission-Reference` Structured Fields Dictionary (exactly `id`/`issuer` as Strings; duplicates rejected **before map collapse**; parameters, Inner Lists, non-String values, extra members, multi-line carriage, and over-cap lengths all malformed) and the MCP `_meta` key `com.karlmcguinness.mission/reference` (`mission_id`/`issuer` member names, same closure — with the honest note that JSON duplicate keys collapse in the SDK's parse upstream, so membership closure and types are the reachable checks on that carriage).
- **Both transports** parse their carriage and carry the result — malformedness preserved, never dropped — to the PEP as a request signal.
- **The PEP precondition** applies `reference-verification`: the credential-carried reference governs; a propagated reference naming a different Mission or issuer, or malformed carriage on this fully governed surface, refuses as **`mission_reference_conflict`** with a Refusal Record. Absent carriage leaves the credential-established path unchanged (rule 1's source exists here).
- **`TokenFacts.mission` now carries `issuer`** — the server read and dropped it before; the canonical `(issuer, mission_id)` pair is what conflicts compare, and claim validation now requires it.
- **Drive-by**: the dangling `@spec status#effective-authority-set` tag in `kernel/derive.ts` repoints to `status#conformance`, the section stating the single Effective-Authority-Set computation rule the docblock describes (the old anchor exists in no draft).

**Conformance**: five `mas.reference.*` rows flip todo → tested (their notes had pre-named this issue), citing 11 parser unit tests plus 8 new channel tests; `conflict-deny`'s row level corrects to `endpoint`. `mcp-unsupported-refusal` (needs a non-supporting build) and `no-cross-domain-forwarding` (intermediary duty) honestly stay todo. 493 rows at **127 tested** / 45 partial / 321 todo; `--collect` verifies every cited name.

**Verification**: 994/994 tests pass with the OpenFGA stack live (the new channel tests ride the same env gate as their files' existing tests); `tsc -b` clean. One local-env note: the gitignored `src/certs` pair was stale/mismatched and was regenerated locally — nothing in-repo changed.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All five findings addressed across `0616a3cd` (spec), the impl commit, and `bf105bae` (conformance); the PR body is reframed.

**1 (High) — partial scope, stated as such.** Confirmed: no Mission Join substrate exists in src, so implementing the MAS Join consumption path here would have meant building the join itself inside this PR. The PR now says "Advances #557, part 1" with the remaining scope named (a gateway selecting a Mission for a credential carrying no mission claim), and **#557 stays open**. What this PR does implement — the carriage on both transports and the credential-governs rule — is the spec's governing branch wherever a `mission` claim is present, which is every credential in this codebase today.

**2 (High) — issuer is authoritative end-to-end.** Three fixes: (a) strict claim parsing — `id`, `issuer`, and `authority_hash` must all be strings, so `issuer: {}` fails validation instead of passing truthiness (negative test: empty tool list, refused call); (b) the loaded view's issuer is compared against the credential's — a mismatch is reference sources disagreeing on the canonical `(issuer, id)` pair, refused as `mission_reference_conflict` (negative test added); (c) the PDP contract carries `issuer` in `context.mission` and its view-consistency check compares it, with every PDP and service fixture updated. 996/996 tests pass against live OpenFGA.

Note: this PR and #634 both touch runtime-evidence in disjoint sections; whichever merges second re-pins that digest on rebase.

**4 (Medium) — rows now honest.** `fail-closed-carriage` → **partial** (malformed arm tested; the missing/stripped-with-no-other-source arm is the open #557 scope). `conflict-deny` keeps tested *because the recorded-binding arm is now genuinely exercised* — the new view-issuer conflict test is its cross-component mapping alongside the endpoint conflicts.

pulls.title: Tri-doc review: hosted Statement reconciled, effective-active rule, stable discovery baseline, constraint binding
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the validated three-document review (against `3b647e27`) under owner scoping ("use judgment"). Rulings:

**P0 (Statement location) — resolved by reconciling the rule, not relocating.** The Statement hosting is deliberate family doctrine: the published OAuth binding takes no companion normative dependency, so its Statement lives in the substrate's family appendix. The contradiction the reviewer proved was real — the substrate's own MUST didn't admit the form it uses. Now it does: {{statement}} defines the **hosted form** (a binding that must stay free of normative dependencies on the substrate publishes its Statement through the family appendix, which carries it on the binding's behalf and satisfies the requirement); the hosting sentence states the actual rationale instead of the backwards-sounding one; the OAuth Conformance pointer explains both directions. The pinned conformance row tracks the rewritten sentence. *The reviewer's relocation alternative remains available if the owner prefers it — it would invert the core-stands-alone doctrine, so it is deliberately not taken here.*

**P1 effective-active** — the one-rule model the reviewer proposed, landed in core lifecycle verbatim in spirit: evaluate `expires_at` before relying on stored state on every state-dependent decision; effectively active = stored `active` AND now < `expires_at`; persistence and events may be lazy. This states what the implementation (`applyExpiry()` before every gate) already does.

**P1 RAR metadata** — `authorization_details_types_metadata_endpoint` drops to SHOULD-where-implemented; conformance no longer depends on an individual draft; RFC 9396's `authorization_details_types_supported` + out-of-band documentation is the stable baseline; the endpoint's semantics (key-set source of truth, the `mission_resource_access` schema entry) bind only where advertised. {{other-types}}' "supported" definition follows.

**P1 constraint binding** — the runtime Operation Profile MUST now bind each carried constraint to its authoritative operation input: extraction/normalization rule, units/currency with conversion prohibited by default, value-space comparison, fail-closed missing/malformed behavior, and a digest vector per binding. New manifest row (todo) records the duty; the `max_amount`→`amount_usd` mapping stops being implicit.

**P1 R3** — rewritten to the true invariant: client input selects and narrows derivation and can request gates, and never grants or widens authority by its own assertion.

**P2 Approver** — reserved for the consent principal in the OAuth lane (always `approval_basis.consent_principal`); policy adjudicates a standing-consent activation. The substrate's broader Approver definition is deliberately untouched.

**P2 introspection** — disclosure is member-scoped as well as caller-scoped: `derivations_remaining` and `proposal_hash` need their member's disclosure privilege; an RS audience gets the enforcement projection by default (the implementation already enforces this; the draft now requires it).

**Editorial** — the closed-top-level rationale names both extension seams (`controls` and `evidence`).

**Filed as decisions, not edited**: #636 (controls taxonomy: `acr`→`acr_values`/RFC 9470, `max_derivations` min-rule, `agent_deployment` relocation) and #637 (staged Mission Resource Access Profile split, plan-of-record with triggers, coordinated with #207). **Declined**: architecture deployment-JSON extraction (parked #281 reservation; the reviewer withdrew the latent-protocol claim). **Acknowledged withdrawals**: `requires_action_approval`/ARAP and the architecture-as-protocol claims.

Gates: all four touched drafts build; conformance 495 rows (statement row tracks the hosted-form sentence; new constraint-binding row born todo; three digests pinned to the spec commit); family-manifest and substrate-statements green.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All six findings addressed in `adfe7c1b` (spec+impl) and `bcdcfbdf` (conformance).

**1 (P1) — ownership resolved by your third model, sharpened.** The hosted Statement's conformance claim is now **the substrate's own claim** about the described specification: normative as substrate content, made and maintained there, with the described specification neither making the claim nor taking any requirement from it. Concretely: the `{{statement}}` rule now applies its MUST to "a specification that itself claims conformance," and defines the hosted Statement as this document's claim about a non-claiming specification; the hosted section's intro says "the conformance claim it embodies is this document's own… asserts, and maintains against the OAuth binding's text"; the crosswalk says four bindings publish their own Statements and this document publishes the hosted one describing OAuth; and OAuth's pointer attributes the claim to the substrate. This is your option (c) without giving up the checkable Statement: nothing claims "OAuth core conforms" *from OAuth's side*, the substrate claims and warrants it from its own, and the no-mutual-dependency rule stands with no tailored exception. (Options (a) and (b) remain available if the owner prefers a claim OAuth itself makes — (a) inverts the core-stands-alone doctrine, (b) mints a 42nd document — but neither is needed for coherence now.)

**2 (P1) — hosted Statement item 6 matches the rule this PR introduced**: stored `state` equal to `active` **with the decision time strictly before the record's effective `expires_at`**, lazy materialization allowed; the remainder of the item (unrecognized values non-active, authenticated transitions, refusal of issuance and derivation) unchanged.

**3 (P1) — implemented, not just described.** A named `budget` disclosure privilege now gates `derivations_remaining` in `introspectionProjection()`; `rs-payments` holds it; a new privilege-less `rs-payments-basic` principal (same audience) proves the negative in an endpoint test — the enforcement projection arrives without `derivations_remaining` or `proposal_hash`. The draft names "the ordinary audience-filtered enforcement projection defined above" instead of my incomplete parenthetical. My round-1 claim that the implementation "already does this" was wrong for the budget member — provenance was gated, budget was not — and this round closes it. 997/997 tests pass against live FGA.

**4 (P1) — validation layered per RFC 9396 §5**: every entry validates against its type's **documented definition**; where a machine-readable schema is advertised or established out of band, the entry MUST *also* validate against that schema; the refusal rule names both layers. An advertised issuer without the optional schema endpoint is now fully covered.

**5 (P1) — constraint-evaluation fixtures required separately from digest vectors**: at least one permitting value, one beyond the bound, a missing and a malformed input, and an incomparable pair where the constraint admits one — with the `max_amount` worked set spelled out (mapping, exact-bound permit, over-bound refusal, absent amount, malformed decimal, mismatched currency).

**6 (P2) — bookkeeping**: the Statement row quotes the complete sentence; all three Operation Profile rows carry role `RS` (the two pre-existing misclassifications corrected together); `core.lifecycle.effective-active-before-reliance` exists (todo, with the flip condition named); `core.introspection.member-scoped-disclosure` exists (tested, citing the new budget test and the existing issuer-only-members test). 497 rows, digests re-pinned, `--collect` verifies every cited name.

Gates: three drafts build, family-manifest and substrate-statements green, `tsc -b` clean, 997/997 with the FGA stack live.

pulls.title: Tri-doc round 3: expansion activation race, Mapping Assessment, constraint semantics ownership
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Follow-up round on the merged #638, applying the reviewer's six remaining findings.

**1 (P1) — the expansion activation TOCTOU is closed.** `redeem()` now commits the expiry-aware predecessor re-check, successor creation, idempotency completion, and predecessor supersession as **one kernel-db transaction**; the handler mints only after that commit. A predecessor that stops being effectively active between check and commit rolls the whole activation back — no token, no successor row, no supersession (endpoint test: revoked-during-window now also proves the predecessor keeps its terminal state with no successor link). `supersedeOnRedemption` splits into the in-tx CAS (now expiry-aware, per the effective-active rule) and a post-commit finalize carrying the lifecycle hook and cascade; direct-driver callers keep working, hardened. The effectively-expired variant is covered structurally by the in-tx `applyExpiry` check; a clock-injection e2e remains future work (the builder has no injectable clock), stated in the row note. Per the reviewer, `core.lifecycle.effective-active-before-reliance` **stays todo** until all state-dependent paths are inventoried and boundary-tested.

**2 (P1) — third-party conformance is gone.** The construct is now a **Mapping Assessment**: the substrate's own normative assessment of a non-claiming specification's mapping, in the Statement's form. It is expressly *not* the described specification's conformance result — no such result exists unless a specification claims conformance itself. Section renamed (anchor kept), crosswalk, OAuth pointer, and the mandate's table cell follow. This is the reviewer's option (a); options (b)/(c) remain available if the owner wants OAuth to make the claim itself.

**3 (P1) — the constraint definition owns its semantics.** An Operation Profile maps authoritative inputs *into the constraint's own value domain* and MUST NOT override the constraint's syntax/subset/intersection/comparison/satisfaction semantics; conversion is never mapping — a converted evaluation composes a distinct registered constraint or profile fixing rate source, observation time, rounding, freshness, and evidence rules.

**4 (P2) — the worked example satisfies the MUST it sits beside**: the `amount_usd` → `{amount, currency}` binding declared, plus the five evaluation fixtures (exact-bound permit, over-bound refusal, absent, malformed decimal, mismatched-currency incomparable).

**5 (P2) — the stable baseline is a MUST**: an advertising AS MUST list `mission_resource_access` in `authorization_details_types_supported`; the schema endpoint stays optional; this specification, not out-of-band documentation, is the type's normative definition.

**6 (P2) — the inactive response is member-scoped too**: endpoint test proves a privilege-less principal's `active:false` composite carries neither `derivations_remaining` nor `proposal_hash` (`containment_version` rides ungated as enforcement-relevant state); the member-scoped-disclosure row cites it.

Gates: 998/998 with the OpenFGA stack live, `tsc -b` clean, four drafts build, family-manifest + substrate-statements green, conformance 497 rows with `--collect` verifying every cited name, digests pinned to the spec commit.

pulls.title: Round 4: durable activation outbox, one-way normative assessment reference
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Follow-up on the merged #639, applying the reviewer's five findings.

**1+2 (P1) — the event plane now shares the transaction's guarantees.** Direct emission is suppressed while the redemption transaction is open; the transaction writes a durable `lifecycle_outbox` job — successor activation event plus predecessor supersession finalize, both rebuilt from persisted rows — **atomically with the state it describes**, and the drain runs post-commit, idempotently replayable (at-least-once; consumers dedupe on the event tuple). A rolled-back activation can no longer leak an event that describes state which doesn't exist. The crash window between commit and finalize is recovered on the next poll: a committed operation is recognized by `(predecessor, approval_event_id)`, the outbox drained, the deferral marked redeemed, and the committed successor returned — **never converted to `access_denied`**. Test-proved by simulating the crash (resetting `redeemed` and the outbox after a successful redemption): the re-poll returns the *same* successor with the job drained. The in-transaction predecessor checks became read-only effective-active tests so suppressed emission can never swallow a materialized expiry event — lazy materialization stays with the ordinary gates, as the rule allows.

**3 (P1) — the reference model is coherent, your second option.** The substrate takes a **one-way normative reference** to the OAuth binding (the specification its Mapping Assessment is asserted against); OAuth's reverse pointer stays informative, so no cycle. The precedence rule states exactly that, and the open-ended "editor's-draft lineage" becomes the exact pin: the OAuth edition published from the same repository revision (the two revise and publish in lockstep), base single-domain mode, OPTIONAL capabilities as activation conditions. family-manifest typed edges follow.

**4 (P2)** — conversion belongs to the *new constraint's semantics owner*: "a distinct registered constraint type, whose defining specification or profile fixes … as that new constraint's own semantics."

**5 (P2)** — the inactive-introspection disclosure test is self-contained (its own capped, proposal-bearing Mission, revoked locally); the conformance row's recorded name now runs in isolation.

Gates: **999/999** with the OpenFGA stack live (the new crash-recovery test included), `tsc -b` clean, substrate + runtime build, family-manifest (typed edges with the new normative edge) + substrate-statements green, conformance 497 with `--collect` verifying every cited name, digests pinned to the spec commit.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All six points addressed in `af1782ed` (+ digest `6e37eabf`), with one deliberate scoping ruling.

**1 (P1) — scoped honestly, and the remainder is filed, not claimed.** You're right that my durability claim covered local callback invocation. The drain's docstring now states its actual scope — durable **local** finalization, at-least-once to the lifecycle hook — and expressly does not claim event-plane durability. Per-consumer delivery jobs / persisted signed SETs acknowledged at the Signals profile's durable boundary, plus the recurring dispatcher and multi-process claiming from your finding 3, are **issue #641**, with your design as its body. (Context that shaped this ruling: the store baseline is `:memory:` by decision D27, so cross-restart durability is the file-backed escape hatch's territory; the outbox contract is written for it without pretending the baseline exercises it.)

**2 (P1) — replays now redeliver the same event.** `enqueueExpansionFinalize` builds and persists **both immutable commit payloads inside the activation transaction**: the transaction's own `committed_at` and a stable `event_id` per event. The drain delivers the persisted payloads — never reconstructing from the current clock — and the Signals signer reuses `event_id` as the SET `jti` (the same-`jti` redelivery rule), so a replay is a redelivery, not a newly asserted event with a false later commit time. Byte-identical persisted-SET redelivery is the #641 half.

**3 (P1) — startup drain added** in `buildAuthorizationServer` (before traffic; a no-op on the `:memory:` baseline, meaningful for file-backed deployments). The recurring dispatcher and lease semantics are #641.

**4 (P1) — the crash window is now actually simulated.** A failpoint makes the drain throw immediately after the activation transaction commits. The test proves the window state (predecessor superseded, job pending with persisted payloads, deferral unredeemed), then recovers on the next poll and asserts: the **same successor**, the **persisted `event_id` and `committed_at`** delivered to the recorded lifecycle hook (not fresh values), and the job drained. The round-4 test remains as the replay-idempotence fixture. Honest residual: the child-bearing crash fixture and per-consumer redelivery assertions ride #641 — the cascade is invoked and state-guarded, but this round does not fixture a child through the window.

**5 (P2) — committed recovery precedes the deferral-code lifetime check**, guarded on `redeemed !== 1` so the handle stays single-use: a sufficiently delayed restart recovers the committed successor instead of reporting `expired_token`.

**6 (P2) — both details fixed**: "no **normative** dependency" (the informative pointer acknowledged, with the manifest's typed edges recording it); and the pin is readable off-repository — the assessment now points at the family conformance manifest's `source.specs` content digest for the assessed binding's exact bytes, alongside the lockstep statement.

Gates: **1000/1000** with the OpenFGA stack live (failpoint test included), `tsc -b` clean, substrate builds, family-manifest + substrate-statements + conformance (`--collect`) green, digest re-pinned.

pulls.title: Reader program (stack batch A): family Status skeleton, anchor pins, wedge/bridge promotion, assessment tripwire
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Batch A of the five-lens analysis stack rank (items 1-5, 9, 10, and the altitude notes from 13): the reader program. Everything here is mechanical or informative; no normative requirement changes. Batch B (normative-small) is stacked on this branch as a follow-up PR.

## What changed

**Family skeleton, checker-backed (stack item 5).** Every draft except the published OAuth binding now opens with a `# Status` section generated from the family manifest: its standing (stable / experimental / sketch / informative), the adoption trigger (`pull_when`), and its dependency closure (`adoption_requires`, by title). Checker (r) enforces presence; the OAuth binding is the one exemption (its standing lives in Introduction and Conformance). UMA and GNAP had the only nested Conventions sections in the family; both are un-nested to top level.

**Anchor stability over anchor uniformity (item 5, adjusted).** 13 Conventions headings had no explicit anchor. Each is now pinned to its own existing generated slug, so no published fragment changes. Checker (s) enforces anchor *presence* on Conventions headings; it deliberately does not enforce one uniform slug, because retrofitting `{#conventions}` onto the 9 documents that pinned a different slug earlier would break published fragments. The readability finding is honored as "links never depend on a generated slug".

**Mapping Assessment drift tripwire (item 4).** The substrate's OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment now carries `<!-- assessed-oauth-digest: ... -->`, the first 16 hex of the conformance manifest's content digest for the binding. Checker (t) fails whenever the binding's bytes change without the marker being re-pinned, so a core edit can no longer ship a silently stale normative assessment. Perturbation-proved (one flipped digit fails the check; restore passes).

**Wedge promotion (item 1).** The smallest-useful-conforming-deployment paragraph moves from ~line 4200 to the opening of the core's Conformance section. Text unchanged; it stays inside the `{#conformance}` anchor section, so the pinned conformance row that quotes it is unaffected.

**Ring rescope and bridge (items 2, 3).** README Ring 1 is now Architecture + one binding; the Substrate Requirements are explicitly "for binding authors and reviewers validating a mapping", which is what the Mapping Assessment doctrine already says. A one-paragraph "runtime ring in one breath" bridge sits under the rings so the Ring-2 vocabulary cliff has a rope. The verb spine gets one altitude sentence (a table of contents, not new machinery).

**Signposts and density (items 9, 10).** README points at the two easy-to-miss pieces (work-product commitments, swarm ladder). Core: Third-Party Data Subjects is split into three rule paragraphs plus a bulleted entry-surface list (every element preserved); the effective-ceiling section gains a numeric illustration (2 x 3 x 2 lineages, 120 vs the "10" the Approver saw). Runtime: a worked example of the staleness + permit + execution latency arithmetic (60 + 30 + 30 -> 120 s).

## Verification

- All 25 touched drafts build clean; drafts-index `--check` OK.
- `check-conformance-manifest`: 497 rows (127 tested / 46 partial / 324 todo), digests re-pinned two-commit style (content at 0330ddb0, revisions pinned in the follow-up commit).
- `check-family-manifest` (with new checks r/s/t) and `check-substrate-statements`: green; check (t) perturbation-proved.
- No normative sentence added or changed; the two restructured core passages (third-party list, paragraph splits) preserve every clause verbatim, and no conformance row pins either passage.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All six findings applied on this branch (round 2). Per finding:

**1 (P1, README substrate scope) — fixed as scoped.** The claim is now each binding's own declaration, not a family-wide promise: "whether an adopter also needs them is each binding's own declared adoption closure (the `adoption_requires` edges): the OAuth binding is self-contained and never requires them, while several peer bindings and the runtime documents pull the substrate in as a dependency." You were right that only the OAuth binding can carry the original sentence; AAuth/MAS/UMA/GNAP/Runtime/Runtime-Evidence/AuthZEN all list the substrate in `adoption_requires`, and their new Status blocks (finding 2) now say so per document.

**2 (P1, Status not manifest-synchronized) — rebuilt as demanded.** Every draft except the core now carries a delimited `family-status` block inside its Status section, generated from the manifest and exact-matched by check (r): `Maturity`/`Maintenance` (all five maintenance classes), `Adopt when` (pull_when verbatim), `Requires` (adoption_requires by title), and `Also requires, conditionally` (the full `requires_when` set, when/requires pairs by title). The 20 bespoke Status sections keep their prose outside the block (Cross-Domain's dependency-posture paragraphs are untouched, with the block appended); the 20 sections this PR introduced are now block-only, so there is no second manifest-derived prose surface to drift. Placement is validated (the block must sit between the `# Status` heading and the next top-level heading), and the exact-match failure message prints the expected block. Perturbation-proved.

**3 (P1, ceiling arithmetic) — replaced with model-supported variables.** The multiplicative "12 independently-rooted lineages" framing is gone. The illustration now uses the child-delegation profile's actual members: `max_children` 3 with `max_child_depth` 2 admits up to 12 descendant Missions (3 + 9), each with its own independent `max_derivations` (10 each -> up to 120 across the subtree while no single bound the Approver saw exceeds 10). Cross-domain projection is separated out explicitly: a projected grant preserves lineage rather than rooting a new Mission, and the Resource AS's local issuance is bounded by the grant's own lifetime and policy, not counted against the origin issuer's per-Mission derivation cap.

**4 (P2, 120-second double count) — corrected to the tight bound.** The example now derives 90 seconds (60s staleness + 30s execution) through the permit cap: a permit issued from a stale view expires no later than that view's valid-through, so nominal permit validity cannot be added after a full staleness window. One sentence keeps the general formula honest: the worst case above counts permit validity as its own term because an explicit lease end can leave a permit window beyond the staleness bound; under observation-time reporting the cap collapses that term.

**5 (P2, tripwire honesty) — now hashes the source directly, described as coupling.** Check (t) computes sha256 of `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md` itself (node:crypto) and compares the substrate marker against it; the conformance manifest is out of the loop, so re-pinning that file cannot satisfy the check by accident. Comments and failure text now call it what it is: a change-coupling tripwire that forces the marker to move in the same change that moves the binding, prompting a re-read — not proof the re-read happened.

**6 (P2, manifest reformat) — serialization restored.** `conformance-manifest.json` is rebuilt from origin/main's exact bytes with only the pin values substituted (content digests in the content commit, revisions in the follow-up pin commit). The diff against main is now the pins alone. The pin tooling does textual substitution going forward instead of re-serializing.

Note on blast radius: finding 2's block insertion touches all 40 non-core drafts, so every pinned spec's digest moved and the whole family rebuilt (all green). CI is running; digests re-pinned two-commit style as before.

pulls.title: Reader program (stack batch B): advertisement-time delegation boundary, reference-token carriage, template on-ramp
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Batch B of the stack rank (items 6, 7, 8, 14): the normative-small set. **Stacked on #643** (base is `fix/reader-program`); merge #643 first, then retarget this to `main`. One new MUST; everything else is naming an existing shape or moving structure.

## What changed

**Advertisement-time delegation boundary (item 6, the one new MUST).** The carried-as-approved rule already lived at derivation time in Other Types: a type with no subset relation the AS understands is never narrowed, delegated, or projected. What was missing is when an adopter *learns* that. The rule's home section now states: for every supported type, the AS MUST state, wherever it documents the type as supported, whether it enforces a subset relation for it; a type documented without one is thereby declared carried-as-approved, non-delegable and non-projectable. Discovery carries a pointer paragraph (one home, one pointer). This lands before the AuthZEN policy-entry lane invites exactly those types into Authority Sets at scale, which is the design-revisit lens's trigger.

*No conformance row*: the manifest's surface vocabulary is model-enumerated (par, introspection, derivation, ...) and this MUST binds a documentation surface, not a harness-observable endpoint; the precedent is template mode's "publishes its mapping space as deployment documentation", which likewise carries no row. Say the word if you'd rather extend the model's surface list instead.

**Reference-token deployments named first-class (item 7).** Most enterprise ASs issue opaque reference tokens, and the document previously framed introspection purely as a freshness overlay on a stateless JWT baseline. A new paragraph in the introspection section says what was implicit: token format is not a conformance surface; for an opaque token the introspection response is the claims carriage — RFC 9396's top-level `authorization_details` response member plus the `mission` member, under the existing caller-authorization and minimization rules — and an RS in such an estate satisfies its token-consumption obligations from the response alone. An opaque-token estate without introspection remains a scope-only deployment. All MAY/statement-of-sufficiency; no new requirement.

**Template mode as the no-RAR on-ramp (item 8).** The template-mode bullet now says plainly that it is the low-integration path: the client submits a Mission Intent and no `authorization_details` proposal at all, so an estate adopts Mission governance without teaching clients RAR authoring. Narrowing mode stays RECOMMENDED; nothing normative moved. README gains the matching adoption-table row ("Adopt without clients authoring RAR"). I'll drop a note on #220 that this is most of what it asked for, with packaging as the remainder.

**Overview order (item 14).** Authority Sources moved after Protocol Flow within the Overview: a first reader now reaches the wire flow before the source taxonomy. Pure block move, anchors and text unchanged.

**Tripwire, exercised.** These edits changed the binding's bytes, so checker (t) from #643 refused the tree until the substrate's `assessed-oauth-digest` was re-pinned — done after re-verifying the Mapping Assessment (the kernel mapping and capability table are untouched by these additions). First live proof the tripwire works as designed.

## Verification

- Core and substrate rebuild clean; drafts-index `--check` OK.
- `check-conformance-manifest` (497 rows), `check-family-manifest` (checks a-t), `check-substrate-statements`: all green; digests re-pinned two-commit style (content at 121dccc7).
- Document History carries the -01 bullet for the normative additions.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
All four findings applied (round 2). Per finding:

**1 (P1, opaque tokens permitted-but-unprofiled) — resolved with the explicit mode you outlined.** New subsection "Introspected Token Consumption" (`{#introspected-consumption}`) in the introspection section: an opaque Mission-bound token is profiled under this mode and only under it. Its floor: introspection REQUIRED of the issuing AS; an active response MUST carry, as introspection response members, the audience-filtered granted `authorization_details`, the `mission` member, `aud`, `cnf` where sender-constrained, and `act` where delegated — everything the JWT carriage requires, from the same issuance state. Authority and the `act` chain appear only on active responses; inactive responses stay within the existing limited RFC 7662 deviation (state facts, never authority). The RS MUST resolve through introspection before service, verify `active`/`aud`/`cnf`, enforce the response under the same rs-enforcement rules, and fail closed on introspection failure. The conflicting surfaces now cohere: the JWT-only paragraph in Mission-Bound Tokens points at the mode as the one profiled alternative (outside it, opaque stays unprofiled, standalone Mission Issuer remains the fallback); the RS section names the active response as the claims source; the section lead and the Conformance roles state the conditional REQUIRED (OPTIONAL is the JWT deployment's, not the opaque one's).

**2 (P1, template conflation) — conceded and renamed.** The claim that the Mission Template profile profiles the core mapping's publication/versioning was false; removed. The core mode is renamed **configured-mapping mode** (six sites, including the `purpose` lookup-key rule, the Mission Record `proposed_authority` note, and both -01 history bullets) — conveniently, the conformance manifest's own notes already used exactly this vocabulary ("Core configured-mapping mode, not the Mission Template companion"), so the spec now matches its ledger. The mode text states the boundary: every Mission it yields takes its own fresh approval; standing consent to a pre-approved ceiling with machine-speed dispatch is the separate, experimental Template profile. README: the no-RAR on-ramp row points only at configured-mapping mode; a separate "dispatch recurring work under standing consent" row carries the Template profile with its experimental status and Runtime + Consent Evidence dependencies stated.

**3 (P1, undeliverable discovery claim) — scoped to documentation, completed to both semantics.** The MUST now covers whether the AS understands the type's subset relation AND its delegation semantics (matching the existing carried-as-approved prerequisites: a type lacking either is non-delegable, non-projectable, never narrowed), and the text says plainly this is a deployment-documentation obligation — no metadata member or schema-endpoint field carries it, and no machine-readable per-type capability map is defined here. pulls.title: Txn authorization: post-merge review hardening (PR #558 findings)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the six findings from the post-merge review posted on PR #558 (https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/pull/558#issuecomment-5384282722), against the current hardened text.

## High — the cross-workflow double-mint race is closed

Carrier invariant 3 (at most one result per transaction instance, across every workflow) was discharged only per-workflow. The mint gate is now **`txn`-scoped**: before minting, the TAS consults its issuance record for the `txn` atomically; where any workflow already produced a result, it returns that result and MUST NOT mint a second token under a different `jti`. A second workflow admitted for one `txn` (a reissued challenge for one uncompleted operation) converges on the first result or refuses. The `exactly-one-issuance` conformance row is re-quoted onto the new wording, and a new `txn-scoped-mint-gate` row pins the atomic consult (tests ride the #540 implementation track).

## Medium

- **`containment`/`discharge` defined by citation**: Conventions now names both terms with their owning profiles; Mission Containment added as a normative reference (both drafts Experimental, so the maturity bound holds); family-manifest typed edges updated.
- **Interleaving pinned**: establishment steps 1-4 run inside redemption step 1's `subject_token` validation and MUST complete before redemption step 5 binds the approval to the pinned subject; establishment steps 5-6 run at completion before redemption step 7's fresh decision.
- **RFC 8725** cited at the token profile in the family's exact-validation + mutually-exclusive-rules substitution-defense formulation (the draft was the lone `+jwt`-registering holdout).

## Low / editorial

Named failure outcomes for a superseded Operation Profile version and for an Effective Authority Set narrowed since admission; the `act`-chain validation enumerated in redemption step 1 (the token's 'verified at redemption' claim now has its step); 'registered semantics' corrected to specification-defined; `venue.latest` fixed to the merged identity's slug; the 'local subject' straggler aligned to destination-local subject; the imported commitment-species vocabulary now used at `parameter_digest`.

## Validation

Draft builds (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc); conformance manifest green at 503 rows (spec-inventory digest bumped for the audited revision); family manifest green (41 drafts, typed edges); whitespace clean; zero em-dashes.

pulls.title: Signals: durable per-consumer delivery, recurring dispatcher, cascade-under-replay fixture (#641)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes the event-plane half of #641: the crash window between the kernel's lifecycle hook and SET delivery no longer loses events. The prior state (mapped before building): the emitter's `onCommit` scheduled async signing and returned, `emitOne` swallowed every failure in a bare `catch {}`, there was no dispatcher, no delivery state, and the manifest carried zero durability rows for the signals spec.

## What the emitter does now (`@mission/signals`)

**Durable journal in the commit hook.** `onCommit` synchronously inserts one `signal_outbox` job per (event, eligible consumer audience) — better-sqlite3 is synchronous, so the job exists before the hook returns — then kicks the dispatcher off the commit path. The outbox is the emitter's own `@mission/store` database (`:memory:` by default per D27, `store.file` escape hatch for real restart survival).

**Identity minted once, redelivery byte-identical.** The event identity is fixed at journal time: a commit replayed from the kernel's finalization outbox arrives with its persisted `event_id` and `UNIQUE(event_id, audience)` makes the replay re-enqueue nothing; a direct-funnel commit gets its identity minted once into the journaled payload. The signed SET is persisted before the first hand-off, so every retry — including one by a fresh emitter after a process restart — delivers the same `jti` and the same bytes, never a re-signed sibling assertion.

**Failures back off, never vanish.** A failed hand-off leaves the job pending with exponential backoff capped at `retry.capMs` (the draft's transmitter DoS bound); the job is never dropped. Zero registered sinks is not a vacuous success: an audience whose transport isn't wired yet keeps its jobs for the late-registered sink. `startDispatcher`/`stopDispatcher` add the recurring drive, and lease-based claiming (`leaseMs`) keeps concurrent dispatchers over a shared file store from double-delivering while letting a crashed claim holder's jobs recover at lease end. `drain()` keeps its barrier semantics for tests and shutdown.

## Tests (38 signals-package tests, full suite 1008 green)

New `durable-delivery.test.ts` (7): journal-and-redeliver with byte/jti identity asserted across attempts; restart recovery over a file store (a fresh emitter with no in-memory state delivers its predecessor's journaled event, byte-identical); kernel-replay dedup; the backoff cap held exactly (runnable at +cap, not at +cap−1); late sink registration; lease respected while live and recovered at lapse (the expansion-test failpoint pattern); autonomous redelivery via the dispatcher with no `drain()` call.

Plus the fixture the issue named: **cascade under replay** in `expansion-endpoint.test.ts` — a child-bearing predecessor exercised through the crash-window replay (deferral un-redeemed, outbox job un-done, re-poll). The already-cascaded child is skipped: same terminal state, same version, no re-emitted child commit; the replay redelivers only the persisted activation and supersession.

## Spec + conformance

The signals draft gains **Transmitter Delivery** (`{#delivery}` — which also makes the code's pre-existing `@spec signals#delivery` citations point at a real anchor): the transmitter MUST NOT lose a committed transition between commit and the delivery method's hand-off; redelivery reuses the event identity (same `jti`, and once signed the same bytes); the schedule is bounded per the existing DoS rule. It explicitly composes with, rather than replaces, the consumer-side staleness fallback. The Conformance producer bullet picks up the duty. Three rows (505 total, 130 tested): persist-until-acknowledged, same-event redelivery, bounded-retry — all `tested`, mapped to the new suite; `--collect` verified the names.

## Honest scope

Two things this PR does not claim, both now stated in the code comments where #641 was cited: durability on the `:memory:` baseline outlives the request, not the process (the `store.file` option is what makes restart survival real, and the restart test uses it); and the **kernel** finalization outbox's own recurring drive with multi-process claiming stays scoped behind a plumbed file-backed kernel store, which `KernelOptions` does not expose yet. If you want #641 kept open for that kernel-store remainder rather than closed by this PR, say so and I'll split it into a successor issue at merge time.

pulls.title: Migrate consumer capability-consumption tables to required/required-when vocabulary (#620)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #620

## What this does

Per the issue's ruled disposition (including the latest fresh-review comment, which controls and overrides the earlier session disposition on one point — see Deviation below), migrates all seven consumer capability-consumption tables (`| Capability | Consumption | Scope of consumption |`) from the retired `conditional`/bare-`consumed` vocabulary to the consumer vocabulary: `required`, `required when <condition>`, `not consumed`, `produced`, `required and produced`. Also generalizes `scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs` to detect and validate any such table by its header, replacing the temporary five-file allowlist.

An eighth table, `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence.md`, was already fully compliant (all rows `not consumed`); no edit needed there.

## Per-file row counts (12 cells migrated total)

| File | Rows converted | Capability |
|---|---|---|
| draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md | 2 | Credential-Bound, Structured Authority |
| draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md | 3 | State-Observable, Monotonic Derivation, Credential-Bound |
| draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md | 1 | Structured Authority |
| draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md | 1 | Structured Authority |
| draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md | 2 | State-Observable, Credential-Bound |
| draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.md | 1 | State-Observable |
| draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md | 2 | Structured Authority, State-Observable |

Only the Consumption cell changed in every row; Scope of consumption prose is untouched (terminology migration, not re-derivation).

## Judgment rows (compound/multi-clause conditions distilled to one phrase)

- **Harness / Structured Authority**: Scope text names three activities gated on the same underlying fact (tool-catalog/schema scoping, `authority_hash` recording, supersession continuity). Distilled condition: "required when an Authority Set is conveyed to the harness."
- **Metering / Structured Authority**: Scope text names two consumers (`call_class`, SHOULD-drawn; `exclusive`, which "consumes it even then"). Distilled condition, kept modality-neutral so the `exclusive` consumer doesn't read as optional: "required when a call class or an exclusive selector is drawn from the Authority Set's identifiers."

## Deviation from the issue's Scope line

The task scope description mentions reclassifying the three self-produced-evidence "Portable Evidence" rows (harness, orchestration, containment) to `produced`. That was the *first* session-disposition comment's recommendation. The issue's **latest** comment explicitly reverses this: producing an evidence-shaped object (Harness Evidence, the orchestration evidence envelope, Containment Evidence/Protected Event Receipt) is not the same as supplying the substrate's Portable Evidence capability (cross-administrative-boundary transfer + verification, canonicalization, integrity, ordering, retention, disclosure). All three documents delegate registration/cross-boundary composition to audit/transparency machinery they don't themselves define. Per that final ruling, these three rows are left as `not consumed`, unchanged. (This also means the total mechanical migration is 12 cells, not 9+3 with 3 semantic reclassifications as the earlier disposition sketched.)

## Checker change

`scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs`: removed `CONSUMER_TABLE_ALLOWLIST_620`. Consumer tables now self-register by header (the same table-discovery method the retired-vocabulary tripwire already used, which is what caught the two un-allowlisted tables in the first place: mandate.md and transaction-authorization.md). Each detected table is validated for: legal Consumption value (`required`, `required and produced`, `required when .+`, `not consumed`, `produced`), Capability name in the canonical eight (no completeness/order requirement, since consumer tables legitimately omit untouched capabilities), and non-empty Scope of consumption. Verified the regex against positive and negative cases (`conditional`, `consumed`, `not supported`, empty, and a truncated `required when` all correctly rejected).

## Conformance

- `node scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs`: clean — `5 Statements, 8 consumer tables validated`.
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: clean (502 requirements, no schema/stale-requirement/spec-inventory-drift failures).
- **source.specs pins**: only `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md` and `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md` had existing conformance-manifest rows/entries before this PR; both are re-pinned to the spec commit (revision + content_sha256 bumped). The other five edited drafts (harness, mandate, orchestration, metering, containment) carry **no** conformance-manifest rows at all, so per the manifest's own spec-inventory-drift rule ("an entry for a spec no row references" fails), they get no source.specs entry — there's nothing to pin. No stale-requirement re-anchoring was needed: none of the existing rows for runtime.md or transaction-authorization.md anchor into the `mission-substrate` section that holds the edited table.

## Commits

- `spec(consumer-tables): migrate to required/required-when/produced vocabulary`
- `ci: generalize consumer-table detection in check-substrate-statements.mjs`
- `conformance: pin source.specs revisions to e75c5b60 (#620)`

## MERGE-ORDER NOTE

Merge this before the #238 runtime regroup PR (`fix/238-*`). This PR overlaps `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md`, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.md`, and `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md` only in their capability-consumption table sections.
