pulls.title: spec(runtime,authzen): narrow the idempotency claim to Exact enforcement (#648)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #648.

## Summary

Implements the ruled disposition on #648 as amended by the fresh review against `2d63119a`: narrows D28's PDP-side idempotency claim rather than reversing it. Spec delta only; the claim-store implementation stays a follow-on.

## Changes

**`draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md`**
- The idempotency claim's atomic-claim paragraph ({{idempotency}}) now cites the metering companion's Exactness and Topology framework instead of restating stateful machinery. New requirements: the claim MUST run under the Exact enforcement profile only (never Bounded-consistency, matching the non-degradable shape of metering's `exclusive` latch), and a PDP or store that cannot reach its declared Exact domain MUST fail closed.
- "Before issuing a permit for a keyed action" is narrowed to the irreversible-action, external-commitment, and privileged-administration classes (the fresh review's refinement 1), so a core-tier reversible write's optional idempotency-key control no longer inherits the PDP claim duty.
- The Enforcement Scope Statement (#runtime-conformance) gains a new top-level bullet: the deployment MUST name the Exact claim domain per mediated action class or idempotency scope, not enumerate individual dynamic claims.
- Reversible-write completeness (the fresh review's refinement 2): a new closing paragraph in the Idempotency section states that the PDP makes no claim for a reversible consequential write's idempotency-key control, and the enforcing PEP/resource instead atomically reserves the key and retains the record for the declared non-high-consequence retention posture (the existing "outside those classes" reconciliation-window bullet), covering both concurrent and completed duplicates so the narrowing does not weaken the existing guarantee.

**`draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md`**
- The `idempotency_key` field's PDP-atomic-claim sentence gains the same class qualifier, with an explicit clause for the reversible-write case (PDP makes no claim; the PEP/resource deduplicates instead), so the wire semantics match the narrowed runtime text. Checked the `duplicate_suppressed`/`idempotency_conflict` denial-classification prose for drift: both already scope from the (already class-scoped) claim established earlier in the same field description, so no change was needed there.

**`conformance-manifest.json`**
- Re-pinned `source.specs` per the repo's established pattern (see `1fa0414c`/`074f38ec`): `content_sha256` bumped for the two edited spec files, `revision` bumped to this branch's content commit for every entry.

## Fresh-review amendments honored

- Refinement 1 (Exact-only, not a Exact/Bounded choice): implemented as above; ESS declares the domain per class/scope, not per dynamic claim; unreachable domain fails closed.
- Refinement 2 (reversible-write branch must stay complete): implemented as the closing paragraph; PEP/resource now carries an explicit atomic reserve + retention duty rather than an implied one.
- AS `creation-idempotency` store noted as precedent-not-drop-in: no implementation changes in this PR (spec delta only), so this observation carries forward to the follow-on that builds the claim store.

## Checks run

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: OK, 41 drafts, no drift. Metering is already an informative reference in `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md`'s front matter (used repeatedly elsewhere in the doc), so the added `{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-metering}}` citations are not a new edge; no manifest change needed.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 502 requirements (127 tested, 46 partial, 329 todo, 0 blocked), no stale-requirement findings. Verified none of the edited/added text overlaps any row's quoted `text` before editing; the only pre-fix failures were the expected `content_sha256` drift for the two edited files, resolved by the re-pin commit.

## Deliberately out of scope / deferred

- `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`: left alone. Its own convention (D25/D41) makes a pin bump deliberate and paired with the affected-module/test change list, which belongs to the follow-on implementation PR, not this spec-only change.
- `src/docs/CONFORMANCE.md` (S-6) and `src/PLAN.md` (D28/S-6 entries): left alone. This PR is the spec delta that unblocks the claim-store implementation; the implementation itself, and the bookkeeping that closes S-6, are the follow-on. `src/PLAN.md` is also off-limits to this PR by house rule (direct-to-main only).

Addressed on `697ae034`, pushed to this branch. Point by point:

**"No distinct rows or tests were added" / falsely green ledger.**
Fixed the root cause: added four new rows, all `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#idempotency`:

- `runtime.idempotency.claim-exact-enforcement-only` — MUST NOT apply the Bounded-consistency profile to the idempotency claim.
- `runtime.idempotency.exact-domain-unavailable-fail-closed` — MUST fail closed when the declared Exact domain is unreachable.
- `runtime.idempotency.ess-must-name-exact-claim-domain` — the ESS names the Exact claim domain per class/scope.
- `runtime.idempotency.reversible-write-pep-reserve-and-retain` — the PEP/resource atomic reserve + retention duty for the reversible-write case.

These are now visible in the outstanding report (`node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`), not silently absent. `check-conformance-manifest.mjs` and `check-family-manifest.mjs` both pass clean.

**"lowest-public-surface positive/negative tests," "Do not use the resource-consumption test as PDP coverage."**
Agreed on the second half without qualification: none of the four new rows cite `src/services/mcp-payments/test/transaction.test.ts` or any resource-consumption test. I did not add tests for three of the four rows, and want to flag that rather than let it pass quietly:

- `claim-exact-enforcement-only`, `exact-domain-unavailable-fail-closed`, and `reversible-write-pep-reserve-and-retain` are `coverage: "blocked"`, `blocked_by: "#648"`. I checked (`grep -rl idempotency src/services/pdp`, and the mcp-payments transaction/connector code): there is no PDP-side idempotency claim store and no reversible-write reservation store anywhere in this codebase today. A test for these rows would have to build that store first. That store is exactly what #648 (still open, "Impl: transaction-assurance idempotency claim states...") tracks, and what this PR's own scope statement and the prior fresh review on #648 both named as a deliberate follow-on — the fresh review specifically warned the AS's `creation-idempotency` store "is not a drop-in... Runtime requires the larger claim-state table and an indeterminate claim." I'd rather land that as its own reviewed PR against #648 than improvise a thin version of it here under review pressure. `blocked_by: "#648"` makes that dependency mechanical rather than a note only I can see — the outstanding report will keep surfacing these three until #648 closes with an implementation.
  
  If you'd rather I build the claim store and reservation store in this PR instead of deferring, say so and I'll scope that as new work (it's materially bigger than a spec-conformance PR — the existing `creation-idempotency.ts` precedent this needs to roughly match is ~250 lines of transactional store code, and this needs an equivalent for the PDP's Exact claim plus a second, separate one for the PEP/resource reversible-write reservation).
- `ess-must-name-exact-claim-domain` is `coverage: "todo"` (no `blocked_by`; not an #648 gap). This one isn't blocked on the claim-store implementation — it's blocked on the fact that no Enforcement Scope Statement artifact exists anywhere in this codebase to assert against, the identical, already-accepted gap its sibling row `runtime.conformance.no-claim-outside-declared-scope` records. I used that row's own justification rather than inventing a new one.

**Nonblocking hygiene (source.specs revision bumping).**
Fixed: reverted the nine untouched specs' `revision` back to `dc3f88f0` (their prior reviewed commit); only `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md` and `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md` — the two files whose bytes actually changed — advance to the commit that changed them.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of `19489e9c`: **changes requested before merge**.

The direction of the Exact/Bounded clarification is right, but the conformance ledger is currently falsely green. This PR adds or changes externally testable requirements for:

- Exact-only PDP claim topology and refusal when the Exact claim domain is unavailable;
- publication of the selected topology in the Enforcement Scope Statement; and
- an atomic, retained reservation path for reversible writes.

Those requirements appear in [Runtime](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/19489e9c4bf7808d9fefc089c6cc0b8f99129104/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2133-L2164) and [the reversible-write rule](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/19489e9c4bf7808d9fefc089c6cc0b8f99129104/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2239-L2251), but no distinct rows or tests were added.

The existing `runtime.idempotency.atomic-claim-and-linearizable-consumption` row does not cover the new PDP claim. It quotes the PEP rule that two replicas must not both consume one permit and maps to a resource-side transaction-token race test; it never exercises a PDP claim store, Exact-domain unavailability, or `idempotency_conflict`: [current row](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/19489e9c4bf7808d9fefc089c6cc0b8f99129104/conformance-manifest.json#L6177-L6203).

Please add separate manifest rows and lowest-public-surface positive/negative tests for the PDP Exact claim, unavailable-domain refusal, ESS declaration, and reversible-write reservation/retention. Do not use the resource-consumption test as PDP coverage. This is required by CONTRIBUTING's new/changed externally-testable requirement convention.

Nonblocking hygiene: the PR advances every `source.specs` revision even where the bytes did not change. Keeping untouched entries at their previous reviewed revision will reduce conflicts and preserve useful audit provenance.

pulls.title: spec(template,progressive,approval-governance): close the consumption-bound/AGR cross-reference gap
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #660

## What changed

Implements the ruled disposition on #660 as amended by the fresh review against `origin/main` at `2d63119a`.

- **template.md `{{prohibited-classes}}`**: softened the "this is the prohibited set the progressive profile holds back" sentence to scope it against progressive alone (dropping the implied comparison to the issuance profile's larger four-class high-risk classification), then added two paragraphs: the issuance profile's fourth high-risk class (a consumption bound) is already satisfied via the template's standing-consent `approval_basis` trace and metering's consent-integrity rendering; and a deployment that also adopts Approval Governance and records a Governance Record for a dispatched instance carrying a consumption bound MUST declare that profile's class-named exception admitting `kind: policy`, with the exact assertion mapping specified (`principal` = `approval_basis.consent_principal` = Mission `approver`; `kind: policy`; `authority.policy_id`/`authority.version` = `approval_basis.activation`'s `template_id`/`template_version`; `authority.approved_at` = `approval_basis.approved_at`; authenticated by the Mission Issuer's own retained template record). The Dispatcher (`approval_basis.activation_actor`) is explicitly not an assertion principal, since it triggers the Dispatch without asserting approval.
- **progressive.md `{{in-ceiling-expansion}}`**: the analogous pair of paragraphs for the `ceiling_drawdown` standing-consent basis (principal = the Approver who consented the ceiling; `authority.policy_id`/`version` = `approval_basis.activation`'s `policy_id`/`policy_version`; the requesting client is not an assertion principal).
- **approval-governance.md `{{boundaries}}`**: corrected (not merely expanded) the paragraph that previously claimed standing-consent bases "carry no equivalent human-approval instant" — that's no longer true now that `approval_basis.approved_at` is a core requirement both profiles populate. Names `template` and `ceiling_drawdown` explicitly, and describes the two recency paths (this document's `{{policy-approval-recency}}` ceiling vs. each profile's own maximum age — `review_cadence` for template, the ceiling review cadence for progressive) as analogous (both bound staleness against a retained human-approval instant) but distinct (they gate different things: counting an AGR assertion at evaluation vs. whether the dispatch/drawdown may happen at all).
- **family-manifest.json**: added the new informative reference edges in both directions (template/progressive → approval-governance; approval-governance → template/progressive; template → metering, since the new paragraph cites metering's consent-integrity rule), plus a `requires_when` entry on each of template/progressive for the AGR case, and regenerated the two profiles' Status-section `family-status` blocks to match.

## What the fresh review amended vs. the original disposition

The original disposition's sketch said the AGR linkage could be "closed by cross-reference" (cite approval-governance's existing exception mechanism and move on). The fresh review rejected that as insufficient: AGR requires exactly one assertion whose `principal` matches the Mission's accountable `approver`, and template/progressive keep a human `approver` while a Dispatcher/policy activates the instance, so the composition needed an actual field-by-field mapping, not just a citation. This PR specifies that mapping directly in template.md and progressive.md (bulleted, per the fresh review's request), derives `principal = approval_basis.consent_principal` from the issuance profile's `approver`/`consent_principal` equivalence plus AGR's own consent-evidence-relationship rule (rather than treating it as a free choice), and states plainly why the Dispatcher/requesting client is excluded as an assertion principal. It also corrects, rather than just expands, the Boundaries paragraph, since the fresh review flagged the existing text as now factually wrong.

One deviation worth flagging: the fresh review's language for the exception used "require," which this PR treats as a normative MUST scoped to the antecedent ("a deployment that ... records a Governance Record for a ... bound MUST declare that profile's class-named exception"). That reading turns the AGR dependency into a conditional deployment edge, which is why `requires_when` entries were added to the manifest (with the generated Status blocks updated accordingly) even though the disposition/review didn't explicitly ask for the manifest change — it followed from treating the requirement as a MUST rather than informative prose.

## Checks run

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — clean (`family-manifest check OK: 41 drafts, no drift detected.` / `substrate-statements check OK: 5 Statements validated.`) after adding the new reference edges, `requires_when` entries, and regenerating the two profiles' Status blocks (the checker prints the exact expected block text, pasted verbatim).
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean (`502 requirements (127 tested, 46 partial, 329 todo, 0 blocked)`). None of the three edited files (template, progressive, approval-governance) appear in `source.specs` — no conformance requirement row references them — so no `source.specs` pin (revision/content_sha256) needed updating for this change.
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-progressive.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.txt` — all build cleanly through kramdown-rfc/xml2rfc with no new warnings beyond the existing canned-bibxml-override notices.

No core (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`) edit, per the disposition; the substrate assessment digest tripwire is untouched.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed in `45b4a7bd`. Per-point resolution:

**1. Invalid standing-consent-to-AGR mapping (missing `decided_at`, retained record conflated with authentication).** Agreed this was broken as written, and took the review's own preferred fix rather than patching the mapping: extended `approval-governance.md` itself rather than fabricating a current-event assertion.

- `{{assertion-requirements}}`: a Mission rooted in a named standing-consent `approval_basis` now satisfies the accountable-approver rule *through that record itself* — `consent_principal` (equal to `approver`), `root_commitment`, `approved_at` — instead of through a contributing assertion. No assertion is minted in the name of the Dispatcher/requesting client or the Dispatch/drawdown policy, so there's no `decided_at` to fabricate and no "old record authenticates a new assertion" confusion.
- `{{policy-approval-recency}}`: the existing kind-default rule ("MUST be `kind: human` unless a committed, class-named exception admits `kind: policy`") is extended with a parallel sentence binding a Mission whose accountable-approver rule is satisfied via `approval_basis` the same way: the class-named exception is still required before an AGR may be recorded for such a Mission carrying a high-risk class, absent which the record and Mission MUST NOT be created.
- The Boundaries paragraph and the Consent Evidence Relationship rule (`approver` MUST equal the principal of the accountable assertion) are corrected to state the `approval_basis` carve-out explicitly, since there's no assertion to reference in this case.
- template.md/progressive.md's composition paragraphs are rewritten: the assertion-field bullet list is gone; each now says plainly that `approval_basis` satisfies the rule directly and that Approval Governance's own class-named-exception default still governs the consumption-bound class.

**2 & 3. Normative-vs-informative classification, and a new MUST with no conformance coverage.** These turned out to have one resolution once (1) was fixed correctly: with the mapping no longer forcing a fabricated `policy` assertion, template.md and progressive.md no longer need to state a MUST of their own — the operative requirement (the class-named exception, and atomic-commitment blocking activation without it) is entirely AGR's, already stated normatively inside `approval-governance.md`. So:

- Reversed my prior round's judgment call: dropped "MUST declare that profile's class-named exception" from both profiles' composition paragraphs, replacing it with a plain description of what AGR's own rule does. No BCP-14 keyword in either profile now depends on Approval Governance, so per the Reference Classification Convention it correctly stays an *informative* reference in both — no front-matter/`normative_references` change needed.
- Removed the `requires_when` manifest edges and the regenerated "Also requires, conditionally: Mission Approval Governance..." Status-block lines added last round, since there's no longer a conditional deployment MUST creating that edge.
- No new conformance rows added, per the review's second option: the class-named-exception requirement isn't a new externally-testable surface unique to template/progressive — it's AGR's own pre-existing rule (which itself currently has zero rows in `conformance-manifest.json`, consistent with the rest of that document) now correctly extended to cover the standing-consent case.

**Checks re-run after this round**: `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — clean (41 drafts, no drift; substrate-statements OK). `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean, unchanged at 502 requirements (127 tested, 46 partial, 329 todo, 0 blocked) — confirms no new externally-observable requirement was introduced. All three drafts (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.txt`, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-progressive.txt`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.txt`) build clean via `make`.

No dissent to register — all three points held up and are addressed as above.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of `3d3df896`: **changes requested before merge**.

There are three coupled issues.

1. The standing-consent mapping does not yet produce a valid current AGR policy assertion. Template maps the old human consent principal to `principal`, selects `kind: policy`, and treats the retained template record as authenticating the assertion: [Template mapping](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/3d3df89609a8fedf11c0e03ee8eb542b87c59419/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.md#L693-L718). Progressive mirrors this. But AGR requires each contributing assertion to be authenticated and bound to the current `approval_event_id` and current `authority_hash`; `decided_at` is the assertion instant, and an assertion from another event cannot be replayed: [AGR assertion rules](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/3d3df89609a8fedf11c0e03ee8eb542b87c59419/draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.md#L286-L319), [event binding](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/3d3df89609a8fedf11c0e03ee8eb542b87c59419/draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.md#L390-L416). The old consent record corroborates `authority.approved_at`; it does not authenticate a fresh policy assertion, and the mapping never defines `decided_at`.

   Please define a current-event policy assertion, including the actual asserting principal, `decision`, `decided_at`, authentication, and event/authority binding. If AGR's single-principal model cannot truthfully express “policy decided, human remains accountable,” extend AGR rather than labeling the human as the policy assertion principal.

2. Approval Governance is still informative in Template and Progressive even though the new conditional MUST requires its class-named exception and atomic-commitment rules. Under CONTRIBUTING, a conditional BCP 14 dependency is still normative. Move AGR into normative front matter and `normative_references` (retaining `requires_when`), or make the composition paragraph genuinely informative.

3. The new exception-declaration requirement is externally observable but has no conformance rows/tests. Add the rows, tests, and source pins, or avoid creating a new MUST where AGR already owns the operative requirement.

pulls.title: audit: demote Experimental normative refs to informative (Exit 1)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #662

## What changed

Applies the ruled disposition on #662 (Exit 1: apply CONTRIBUTING's maturity-bound remedy), as amended by the fresh review's precision (moving the three references to `informative` is necessary but not sufficient; the table itself has to stop reading as a normative catalog for companion-owned rows, and Discovery's real gap — no document fixing `application/mission-discovery-evidence+json` — has to close).

**`draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.md`**
- Front matter: moved `I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery`, `I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment`, and `I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-work-products` from `normative:` to `informative:`. These are the only three edges where a Standards-Track draft (audit, `category: std`) cited an Experimental draft as normative, per CONTRIBUTING's maturity bound.
- Evidence Types intro ({{evidence-types}}): reworded so the table is the normative definition only for the four evidence types audit itself defines and registers ({{iana}}); every other row is an informative catalog of properties the cited profile owns normatively. This applies uniformly to all companion-defined rows (not only the three exp ones), since that's what "the cited profile fixes those properties normatively" actually is for a Standards-Track companion too — only the front-matter classification differs by maturity.
- Reworked the "conditional normative down-reference" rationale paragraph, which borrowed CONTRIBUTING's conditional-reference language ("binds only a deployment that adopts X") without meeting the document's separate maturity bound in the same section. It now plainly states the citation is informative under the maturity bound and the registration duty sits with each cited profile.
- IANA Considerations' "defined elsewhere" list: added the Discovery Evidence media type, closing the one real content gap the review identified (Discovery Evidence was absent from this list even though the table used its media type as `payload-preimage-content-type`).

**`draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.md`**
- Added a `## Canonical Bytes {#discovery-evidence-canonical}` subsection (matching the pattern Containment and Child Delegation already use) fixing the Discovery Evidence object's canonical bytes and its `application/mission-discovery-evidence+json` type identifier as registered by this document.
- Added a full IANA media-type registration (RFC 6838 template, matching Containment/Work-Products/Child-Delegation's own registrations) for `application/mission-discovery-evidence+json`.
- Stated explicitly that the Discovery Adjudicator — always the Mission Issuer — is the authoritative producer of Discovery Evidence.
- The operational `typ` now reads as naming that registered media type, prefix omitted (RFC 7515), and the old "local-use identifier pending registration" language is removed: shipping both a real registration and a "pending registration" disclaimer for the same identifier would have left the document self-contradicting.

**`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md`**
- Fixed the Portable Evidence capability-consumption row, which said "an audit or transparency profile registers" the Containment Evidence / Protected Event Receipt canonical bytes and type identifiers. Containment already self-registers both media types in its own body ({{evidence-canonical}}, {{protected-event-receipt}}, and a full IANA registration) — this was a stale forward-pointer in the direction Exit 1 reverses.

## What I left alone (and why)

- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-work-products.md`: already self-hosts its canonical bytes, `payload-preimage-content-type`, and producer ({{binding-verification}}); no changes needed.
- Audit's Registration Policy section ({{registration-policy}}): its MUSTs (Work Product Binding producer resolution, `iss`-equality, key authorization) bind to properties — `mediator.id`/`mediator.role`/key material — not to any companion's schema, so they survive Exit 1 unchanged.
- Containment's other citation to audit ("mirroring the Child and Discovery Evidence registration conventions") was already accurate in direction; it becomes fully true once Discovery self-registers here, so it needed no edit.

## Checks run

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: clean (41 drafts, no drift). Removed the three slugs from audit's `normative_references` in `family-manifest.json`; `references` is unchanged since the citations still exist, just informatively.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: clean (502 requirements, same count as the pre-change baseline). **No `source.specs` pin update was needed or made**: none of `draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.md`, or `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md` appear in any conformance requirement row's `spec` field (verified by enumerating all `"spec":` values in `conformance-manifest.json` — only 11 files are tracked there, none of the three edited here), so there is nothing to bump and adding an untracked entry would itself fail the checker's spec-inventory-drift check.
- Built all three edited drafts (`make draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.txt`): all three build clean (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt OK). This catches anchor/reference-resolvability issues the two manifest checkers don't cover (new RFC 6838/7515 refs, the new `{#discovery-evidence-canonical}` anchor, forward cross-references).

## Deviation from the literal task scope

None from the fresh review's controlling comment. One clarification: the review says "Companion-defined rows therefore need to become an informative catalog of properties normatively owned by the cited profile" — I read this as the correct framing for the intro paragraph's prose uniformly across all companion rows (std and exp alike), since that's the accurate state of ownership regardless of maturity; only the front-matter reference classification (and therefore which citations render as normative vs. informative) differs by maturity. This does not touch `requires_when` or `adoption_requires` in `family-manifest.json`, which are validated against `references` (unchanged) and were already correct.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed in `821c995f`.

## Point 1: normative ownership leak survived the bibliography-tier move

Agreed, and fixed. The evidence-type rules ({{evidence-types}}, L473-487 in `5c17e87b`) still said "a producer MUST commit to the canonical bytes its defining profile names" — that BCP 14 requirement forced a conforming Audit producer to consult mission-discovery/oauth-mission-containment/oauth-mission-work-products regardless of which front-matter bucket the citation sat in, per CONTRIBUTING's own classification rule ("a draft lists a reference as normative when any BCP 14 requirement ... requires implementing or consulting it").

Reworked the paragraph:

- Audit is the normative "evidence-type registration" (canonical bytes + content-type + `typ` + producer) only for the four evidence types it itself defines and registers ({{iana}}).
- For every other row, that registration is the cited profile's own conformance duty, imposed there. Audit neither restates the duty nor requires consulting that profile's text to satisfy it — this document's own MUSTs stop there.
- The relying-party MUST (verify a record's `iss` is the authoritative producer, {{registration-policy}}) now explicitly draws its producer-authority input from the producer identifier Audit's own table records, never from the cited profile's text — it was already effectively self-contained (the table has always stated the producer role, and the role-to-key mapping in {{registration-policy}} is entirely Audit's own, over std references), but I made that self-containment explicit in the prose rather than leaving it implicit.

I checked every other citation to the three demoted drafts in Audit's body (the "media types are defined as follows" list, the reworked "conditional" rationale paragraph, the Work Product Binding producer-projection sentence, the Cross-Producer Correlation section) for the same pattern — none of them carry a MUST whose satisfaction requires reading the cited Experimental document; they're either descriptive citations or MUSTs stated entirely over Audit's own terms. So this was the one instance of the leak.

## Point 2: Document History

Added `# Document History {#document-history}` to both Audit and Discovery (their first, since only the OAuth binding carried one before this), each with one entry describing this PR's substantive changes and citing #662, per CONTRIBUTING's by-touch convention.

## Checks re-run

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: clean, no drift.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: clean, 502 requirements, unchanged from baseline. Confirmed again neither Audit, Discovery, nor Containment appear in any conformance row's `spec` field, so no `source.specs` pin applies to this round either.
- Rebuilt both edited drafts (`make draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.txt`): both kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt clean.

Pushed to `fix/662-audit-downrefs` (`821c995f`).

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of `5c17e87b`: **changes requested before merge**.

Discovery's self-hosted media-type and producer repair is sound, and demoting the three downrefs is directionally correct. However, Audit still retains the same normative ownership leak in its prose: a producer “MUST commit to the canonical bytes its defining profile names,” followed by normative producer-authority verification. See [the evidence-type rules](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/5c17e87bc634e8addfefd60faee4d144abf9a71f/draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.md#L473-L487) and [producer verification](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/5c17e87bc634e8addfefd60faee4d144abf9a71f/draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.md#L978-L984).

That BCP 14 rule still makes a conforming Audit producer consult the Experimental defining profile for Discovery, Containment, or Work Products. Changing the bibliography tier alone therefore does not implement Exit 1.

Please make Audit's normative rule self-contained over an adopted evidence-type registration: the registration supplies canonicalization/commitment metadata and producer-authority verification inputs, while each Experimental profile owns its own producer duties. Audit should not normatively say “its defining profile names.”

Process cleanup: Audit and Discovery are substantively revised but still lack the by-touch Document History section required by CONTRIBUTING.

pulls.title: spec(runtime): relocation-only regroup into Runtime Core / Named Assurance Extensions (#238)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #238

## Scope

Stage A of the three-PR staging from the issue thread's latest "Session disposition" / "Fresh review" comments: the **relocation-only** regroup of `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md` into a "Runtime Core" body and a "Named Assurance Extensions" grouping. Zero new normative statements, zero removed. The two open semantic items (ESS thinning, channel-integrity MUST) are explicitly **not** in this PR; they belong to the follow-on S5 normative-delta pass.

**Rebased onto main after #676/#677/#678 merged** (see PR comments for detail): those PRs landed status-tier front matter, consumer-vocabulary table wording, and idempotency-claim scoping edits on the same file. Per the coordinator, this was redone as a fresh reapplication of the relocation against the new base rather than a text-merge/mechanical rebase, to keep the zero-delta proof meaningful. Current head `2fec6a07`, rebased onto main `5d95a917`.

## What moved

**`# Runtime Core {#runtime-core}`** (new, inserted right after the trimmed Introduction, before `# Status: An Optional Profile`) gathers, in this order:
- `## The Runtime Contract {#runtime-contract}`
- `## Enforcement Invariants {#enforcement-invariants}`
- `## Mission Binding Establishment {#mission-binding}`
- `## Mission State and Freshness {#state-freshness}`
- `## Decision Output {#decision-output}`
- `## Decision Inputs {#decision-inputs}` (with its Authority/Capability Drift/Resource Policy/Parameters/Actor/Time/State/History children, unchanged)
- `## Parameter Digest {#parameter-digest}` (per the review round: it's an unconditional baseline dependency of Permit Binding, not an assurance extension)
- `## Permit Binding {#permit-binding}`
- `## Failure Modes {#failure-modes}` (demoted from a top-level `#` section to a `##` subsection)
- `## Required Decision Evidence {#required-decision-evidence}` (per the review round, as the last item; it had no anchor before, so one was added)

**`# Named Assurance Extensions {#named-assurance-extensions}`** (new, inserted right after the rump `# Parameter Binding and Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use` section, before `# Consumption Bounds Fail Closed`) gathers, in this order:
- `## Single-Use Identifiers {#single-use-identifiers}`
- `## Idempotency {#idempotency}` (now carrying the #678 scoping edits — the Exact-enforcement-domain and reversible-write paragraphs added since the original PR body)

Fresh review of `9c646571`: **changes requested before merge**.

The byte-level relocation proof is valid, but the resulting grouping does not match the approved Runtime Core boundary in #238.

First, Runtime Core says every decision and refusal leaves evidence, but Required Decision Evidence remains in a separate top-level section outside Core: [core contract](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9c6465712f061061f8570c495ae2675da89fdf89/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L352-L364), [stranded evidence section](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9c6465712f061061f8570c495ae2675da89fdf89/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2503-L2536). The absence of an existing anchor is bookkeeping, not a scope reason: add an anchor, relocate the subsection, and rekey its rows in this PR.

Second, `Parameter Digest` is placed under `Named Assurance Extensions`, while the Core permit-binding rule begins “Beyond the `parameter_digest`” and the draft unconditionally requires it for consequential writes and the high-consequence classes: [core permit binding](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9c6465712f061061f8570c495ae2675da89fdf89/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L884-L913), [parameter-digest requirements](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9c6465712f061061f8570c495ae2675da89fdf89/draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md#L2120-L2150). Labeling that baseline dependency an extension creates an election/downgrade ambiguity. Keep the baseline parameter-binding requirement in Core; only the additional Operation Profile, single-use, idempotency, and lease machinery belongs in the named transaction-assurance extension unless a real alternate core request-binding mechanism is normatively defined.

This can remain relocation-only; no requirement text needs to change, but the headings must contain the requirements the core already depends on.

pulls.title: Progressive/cross-domain: commitment and disclosure strength
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #667

## Changes

Implements the issue's **fresh review** amendment (which controls over the
earlier Session disposition sketch):

**progressive.md**
- `drawdown_policy`'s definition gains the same uncommitted-body flag and
  SHOULD-commit sentence template.md's `dispatch_policy` already carries:
  committing only the identifier under `ceiling_hash` leaves the policy body
  itself uncommitted, so a deployment SHOULD additionally anchor the body or
  disclose it under Consent Evidence.
- The Ceiling Review section no longer implies the cadence is
  anchor-committed. The fresh review rejected the original sketch's plan to
  add cadence to `approval_basis.activation`, since core states
  `approval_basis` is folded into neither `intent_hash` nor `authority_hash`
  — that would have been immutable issuer-trusted provenance, not
  anchor-detectable parity with template's `review_cadence`. Instead, the
  cadence is now framed explicitly as a recency ceiling on the
  `ceiling_drawdown` approval basis's `approved_at` (the kind of ceiling the
  issuance profile already permits a deployment to declare, made mandatory
  here rather than optional): recorded and reproducible, not anchored. To
  keep it reproducible in audit without touching `ceiling_hash`'s two-member
  preimage, the cadence in force MUST be a separately versioned declaration
  retained alongside the drawdown policy, and that version MUST be recorded
  with every policy-adjudicated drawdown. `ceiling_hash`'s two-member
  preimage and `ceiling_drawdown.activation`'s two-member shape are both
  unchanged.
- Audit Linkage and the Conformance section pick up the cadence-version
  retention requirement.

**cross-domain.md**
- Per-Domain Delegation Depth's disclosure is reshaped from a flat SHOULD to
  a conditional, interface-addressed MUST, mirroring child-delegation's
  `max_derivations` disclosure pattern, per the fresh review's direction (a
  flat SHOULD-to-MUST raise would have made cross-domain's rule stronger
  than the pattern it's supposed to match).
- The fresh review also caught an arithmetic bug in the original sketch:
  `max_depth` times domain count is only valid when the same `max_depth`
  applies to every domain, which isn't guaranteed since `max_depth` is a
  per-entry member. The disclosure now requires the sum of each distinct
  Resource AS domain's applicable `max_depth` (or a conservative per-domain
  maximum where a deployment doesn't track per-domain composition), and
  domains are counted by distinct Resource AS from the resource-to-AS
  mapping fixed at consent, never by raw resource count.

## Fresh-review amendments honored
Both amendments in the issue's latest comment are implemented as directed:
the cadence mechanism was redirected away from `approval_basis.activation`
to a recency-ceiling framing, and the cross-domain arithmetic was corrected
(sum/conservative-sum over distinct Resource AS domains, not `N × M`).

## Checks
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: OK, no drift (no new
  cross-document references were introduced by this change).
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 502 requirements
  unchanged. Neither progressive.md nor cross-domain.md currently has rows
  in `conformance-manifest.json` (they're not among the tracked
  `source.specs` entries), so no `source.specs` pin update applies to this
  PR; adding conformance rows for the new/strengthened cadence,
  policy-body, and disclosure requirements is called out by the fresh review
  as follow-on work, not included here.
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-progressive.txt` and
  `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.txt` both build clean
  (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt OK).

## Note
This PR touches `progressive.md` alongside PR `fix/660-consumption-bound-crossrefs`,
but in different sections (drawdown_policy/Ceiling Review/Audit
Linkage/Conformance here vs. that PR's consumption-bound cross-references).
Whichever merges second should rebase.

The cadence design currently has no interoperable serialization. The new text requires a distinct cadence version to be recorded with every drawdown and retained with every Mission record, but `ceiling_drawdown.activation` remains exactly `{policy_id, policy_version}`: [cadence requirement](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/830b6e3462420221bfb7b33c7ab51fd30edac784/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-progressive.md#L473-L486), [activation schema](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/830b6e3462420221bfb7b33c7ab51fd30edac784/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-progressive.md#L552-L568).

pulls.title: orchestration: re-gate mid-flight steps on containment/authority narrowing (#670)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #670

## Summary

Implements the fresh review's disposition on #670: orchestration's State-Change Behavior gains a third, independent trigger for authority narrowing at unchanged Mission state (the containment midflight seam), and metering gains one informative cross-reference clarifying that contain does not touch settlement.

## Changes

**draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md**
- New `## Authority-Narrowing Behavior {#authority-narrowing}` subsection under State-Change Behavior: on a `mission.lifecycle-change` event carrying `authority_changed` true at unchanged `state` ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-signals}}), the orchestrator rematerializes its Effective Authority Set and re-evaluates each pending step's concrete resource/action, resolving the step's authority basis via a fresh PDP evaluation or the step's Decision Evidence `authorizing_entry`/`entry_digest` (the unwind plan itself carries no authority binding).
- Reuses existing Orchestration Evidence enum values (`state_source: signal`, `mission_state: active`, `orchestration_decision` from the existing mapping) and the existing `not_dispatched`/`dispatched_not_committed`/`committed`/`unknown` in-flight classes. No new enum member, no new machinery.
- `step_id` on Orchestration Evidence is now REQUIRED when the record reports a re-evaluation under this trigger (was unconditionally OPTIONAL), so the per-step behavior is externally observable.
- One-clause repair to the Introduction so it no longer reads as an exhaustive non-active/staleness trigger list.
- Signals moves from an informative to a normative front-matter reference (its `authority_changed` discriminator is now normatively consumed), mirrored in `family-manifest.json`'s `normative_references` for orchestration. `references` was already correct (Signals was already cited informatively there).

**draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md**
- One informative cross-reference in Settlement by Evidence State: a contain transition is not settlement evidence, so an open reservation or duration lease still settles under the existing rules unchanged, and contain narrows only forward draw (a new reservation or a lease renewal) through the ordinary permit check against the narrowed Effective Authority Set. No new settlement state.
- Containment added as an informative front-matter reference, mirrored in `family-manifest.json`'s `references` for metering.

## Both execution notes from the fresh review, honored

1. **Third branch, correct ordering for already-dispatched work.** This is a sibling to the non-active/staleness sequence, not folded into it — the Mission stays `active`. A `not_dispatched` step now denied is suppressed or paused; a `dispatched_not_committed` step now denied follows its *existing* `in_flight_behavior` (re-gated, not additionally stopped — "stop and re-gate" had the wrong order for already-dispatched work); a `committed` step is never compensated merely because authority narrowed later.
2. **Per-step authority association, made interoperably decidable.** The signal carries no entry digest and the unwind-plan schema records only step/Mission/behavioral classifications, so the draft now requires either a fresh PDP evaluation of the concrete step, or a comparison against the step's Decision Evidence `authorizing_entry`/`entry_digest` ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}}).

## Checked, no change needed

- **management.md**: unchanged. The fresh review kept its existing dry-run-first analogy as-is; management does not claim to define `contain`.
- **containment.md**: unchanged. The fresh review is silent on it, and containment's own containment-plane text names no verb to repair. No reciprocal pointer added.
- Neither the five-row consumer table in orchestration.md nor the one in metering.md was touched (that's #620's vocabulary work).

## Bookkeeping (per the fresh review)

- Orchestration was not previously in `conformance-manifest.json`'s `source.specs` (zero rows referenced it). Added one row (`orchestration.state-change.authority-narrowing-regate`), coverage `todo`: `src/packages/orchestration/src/state-change.ts` implements only the non-active/staleness sequence today, no third-branch implementation exists yet. Added the `orchestrator` role (none of the existing roles — AS/client/RS/PDP/PEP/verifier/TAS/Controller/PRODUCER/RECEIPT-ISSUER/RECEIPT-VERIFIER — name this actor).
- metering.md's new sentence adds no requirement row: it restates that the existing settlement rules already govern contain, no new observable behavior.
- Considered, not added: a conditional `requires_when` edge from orchestration to Signals ("when Signals is the trigger source"), mirroring the existing Status entry. Left out because the fresh review's bookkeeping note asked only for front-matter/typed-edge (`normative_references`) changes; happy to add it if preferred.

## Checkers

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — clean (41 drafts, no drift).
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean (503 requirements: 127 tested, 46 partial, 330 todo, 0 blocked), new row appears correctly in the outstanding report (a bad anchor or paraphrased clause would have failed `stale-requirement`).
- Both `draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md` and `draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md` build cleanly via `make <name>.txt` (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc), no unresolved-reference warnings beyond the pre-existing canned-bibxml notices.
- `conformance-manifest.json`'s `source.specs["draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md"]` is pinned to this branch's final spec commit (e4f98f51) and its `content_sha256`, following the repo's `conformance: pin source.specs` commit pattern.

## Cross-PR note (#620 adjacency)

This PR and the #620 vocabulary work both touch `draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md` and `draft-mcguinness-mission-metering.md`, in different sections (their five-row consumer tables vs. this PR's State-Change Behavior / Settlement sections), so a plain rebase should be textually conflict-free. However: adding orchestration.md to `source.specs` here puts it under the `content_sha256` gate permanently. #620's capability-table edit to orchestration.md will change its bytes, so `check-conformance-manifest.mjs` will fail for #620 with a `spec-inventory-drift` finding even though there's no textual conflict — whichever of these two merges second must re-pin `source.specs["draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md"]` (revision + content_sha256), not just rebase.

Two are `tested` rather than `partial`: "committed is never compensated" and "step_id is required" are each fully decidable from the pure function/type alone (a `vi.fn` resolver spy asserted never called for the committed case; a throw-on-empty check for `step_id`), with no missing integration piece. The other two stay `partial` and say why in `observation.local`: the decision logic (suppress/pause; follow `in_flight_behavior`) is real and tested, but consuming a live `authority_changed` signal, calling Mission Status to rematerialize, and invoking a real PDP for the fresh per-step evaluation are integration concerns this dependency-free package takes as an injected predicate — nothing in this repo wires that end-to-end yet. That's the same disclosure pattern the existing `signals.discharge.authority-changed-rematerialize` row uses for its own detect-only gap, so I made it explicit here too rather than claiming more than the tests show.

Also covers "no-second-dispatch/no-double-commit" directly: a `committed` or `unknown` step never reaches the resolver at all (returned untouched before the predicate is called), so there's no code path in this function that can re-dispatch a denied step (`OrchestrationDecision` has no dispatch value) or act twice on a committed one. That's asserted with a spy, not just implied.

## 2. Missing `requires_when` edge for Signals

Added, parallel to the existing Status entry:

```json
{
  "when": "Signals is the authority-change trigger source",
  "requires": ["draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-signals"]
}
```

Regenerated orchestration.md's `family-status` block to match (mechanical, `check-family-manifest.mjs` names the exact expected text on mismatch).

Added `# Document History {#document-history}` to both orchestration.md and metering.md (neither had one before; per CONTRIBUTING's by-touch convention, this substantive revision is what triggers it), each with one entry describing this PR's normative change.

- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean (506 requirements: 129 tested, 48 partial, 329 todo, 0 blocked), including a `--collect` run against the live vitest runner (0 new findings beyond the 85 pre-existing, unrelated findings that are already on `main` and outside this PR's scope — verified by diffing `--collect` output against a `git stash` baseline).

- `source.specs["draft-mcguinness-mission-orchestration.md"]` re-pinned to `1d0cd5c6` (content unchanged since).
