pulls.title: Expansion/template: dispatch idempotency adoption with a complete binding
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #668

## Changes

Implements the issue's **fresh review** amendment (which controls over the
earlier Session disposition sketch): the review found the three-line
"adopt by reference" sketch insufficient because expansion's creation
idempotency apparatus is not parameter-neutral (it assumes a source Mission
resolved from `subject_token`, token-exchange-only fingerprint members, and
Mission-creation-shaped recovery), and asked for a complete, explicit
adopter binding instead.

**expansion.md**
- Widens the adoption clause's scope sentence per the review's own wording:
  "delegation-family-creating exchanges" becomes "a creation exchange
  explicitly profiled by an adopter, not only one that mints a Mission"
  (continuation's refresh-token family is already such a non-Mission
  adopter). Names the template profile's Dispatch as an adopter alongside
  continuation's async-delegation exchange.
- Adds `dispatch` to the operation fingerprint's `op` enumeration, with a
  note (per the advisor's flag on enumeration coherence) that an adopting
  profile declares its own value the same way continuation's exchange
  declares `async-delegation` in its own document, rather than expansion's
  `op` list being a closed registry.
- Generalizes the fingerprint's `source` member additively: the existing
  expansion/child-creation definition is untouched (byte-identical), and a
  new sentence covers an adopter with no source Mission or `subject_token`
  to resolve one from, binding `source` to its own profiled source
  authority instead (template's Dispatch binds it to the dispatched Mission
  Template's `id`, explicitly not a Mission ID).

**template.md**
- Replaces the prior "claim by assertion" sentence (which cited zero actual
  uses of `creation_request_id`, the fingerprint, the reservation, or
  recovery) with a complete adopter binding covering every item the fresh
  review enumerated:
  - identifier and reservation key: `(authenticated client,
    dispatch_event_id)`;
  - fingerprint domain: `op: dispatch`;
  - source binding: `template_id`, not pretending it's a Mission ID;
  - exact included fingerprint members (`iss`, `client`, `source`, `cnf`,
    `intent`, `evidence`, `proposal`) and the token-exchange-only members
    stated absent (`actor`, `child_actor`, `requested_token_type`,
    `cross_check`);
  - atomic reservation with every creation-side effect (instance
    derivation, `max_active`/`dispatch_rate` accounting, evidence
    emission);
  - retry revalidation of Dispatcher eligibility, recorded `cnf`, and
    applicable template/version state; and
  - recovery as delivery of the same Mission, including fresh-credential
    delivery after the original access token expires.
- The `dispatch_event_id` name is unchanged (already load-bearing
  elsewhere), and the Conformance bullet is updated to reflect the full
  adoption rather than a bare idempotency claim.

**continuation.md / child-delegation.md**
- Adds the mutual `max_derivations` cross-references the fresh review asked
  to land regardless of the idempotency disposition: continuation's
  derivation-counting rule (one count per distinct derivation, not per
  refresh within an async-delegation family) now points at child
  delegation's non-aggregate, per-Mission subtree warning, and vice versa.
  Neither counting rule itself changes; this narrows the same
  `max_derivations` counter from two angles with a link either way, per the
  issue's original disposition analysis (no such link existed before).

## Fresh-review amendment honored
The scope-sentence widening uses the review's own phrasing ("creation
exchanges explicitly profiled by adopters," generalized further here to
cover continuation's non-Mission case explicitly), and template.md's
Dispatch binding is the full explicit apparatus the review required
(identifier/reservation key, fingerprint domain, source binding, exact
included/absent members, atomic reservation, retry revalidation, and
recovery-as-delivery) rather than the original sketch's brief mention.

## Checks
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: OK, no drift. `family-manifest.json`'s
  `references` arrays for `continuation` and `child-delegation` are updated
  to match the new mutual front-matter references (both already carried
  each other's document informatively is false before this change; both do
  now).
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 502 requirements
  unchanged. None of expansion.md, template.md, continuation.md, or
  child-delegation.md's touched sections are referenced by an existing
  `conformance-manifest.json` row (only child-delegation.md's document is
  tracked at all elsewhere in the family conformance surface, and this
  change touches none of its existing quoted clauses), so no
  `source.specs` pin update applies.
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-expansion.txt`,
  `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.txt`,
  `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-continuation.txt`, and
  `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation.txt` all build clean
  (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt OK). One fixup during drafting: an initial
  `{{RFC8693}}` citation in template.md's new prose failed to build since
  RFC8693 isn't a declared reference there; reworded to plain prose instead
  of adding an unnecessary reference.

Not stacked on PR #682 (fix/667); this branch is based directly on main.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed all four points in `a2670af3` (four commits: normative-tier move, registration + retry fix, conformance rows, then a source.specs pin bump).

**1. Reference tier.** Moved `I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-expansion` from `informative:` to `normative:` in template.md's front matter (template is `category: exp`, expansion is `category: std`, so this doesn't violate the "Standards-Track never cites Experimental normatively" bound — it's the experimental draft depending on the stable one, which is fine). Added it to `family-manifest.json`'s `normative_references`/`adoption_requires` for template, regenerated the family-status block's `Requires:` line, and replaced the "informative sibling" framing in Relationship to Other Profiles with a paragraph stating the new normative dependency and what's adopted (fingerprint, reservation, revalidation, recovery-as-delivery).

**2. `dispatch_event_id` registration.** Took the "register it" branch rather than reusing `creation_request_id`, since the name is already load-bearing in `approval_basis.activation`, the `template` lineage member, and the grant parameter list (the issue's own analysis wanted the name kept). Added a proper "OAuth Parameters" registry entry (Name/Usage Location/Change Controller/Reference, matching the format expansion.md and child-delegation.md already use for their own parameters), with a sentence explaining why this is a distinct registration rather than a reuse of expansion's registered `creation_request_id`. Updated the "requests no further IANA action" sentence to count both registrations.

**3. Retry-revalidation bug.** This was a real defect: requiring "the template version originally checked is still applicable" before recovering *anything* contradicted template.md's own lifecycle rule (retirement stops new dispatch, never terminates an already-dispatched Mission). Split the rule by whether creation already committed: a **completed** operation is recovered by verifying recorded template identity/version/fingerprint, requester authorization/PoP, and that the created Mission remains `active` — current template applicability is never re-checked, so recovery survives later retirement. A **reserved/pending** operation (no Mission yet exists) is revalidated exactly as a fresh Dispatch, current applicability included.

**4a. Atomic-commit wording.** Replaced "evidence emission" in the atomic-commit list with: the Mission Issuer atomically commits the evidence record (or a durable outbox entry for it) with Mission creation, then delivers/publishes it idempotently afterward, since external emission can't generally join a datastore transaction.

**4b. Conformance rows/tests.** Unlike #682's companions, template.md's Dispatch *does* have real implementation (`src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/template.ts`, `test/template-dispatch-endpoint.test.ts`). Added three rows: `template.dispatch.idempotent-retry-returns-committed` (MUST, **partial** — genuinely tested by the existing "repeated dispatch_event_id is idempotent" test), `template.dispatch.fingerprint-mismatch-refusal` (MUST, todo), and `template.dispatch.completed-recovery-survives-retirement` (MUST, todo, the point-3 fix). Added `source.specs` for template.md (previously untracked) and a `template.dispatch` capability tag following the `cross-org.delegation` precedent.

Flagging honestly rather than overclaiming: the current implementation dedupes on `dispatch_event_id` via the issuance profile's `approval_event_id` mechanism, not the fingerprint object (`op: dispatch`, `source: template_id`, `cnf`, etc.) this PR's binding now specifies. That gap is noted in the partial row's `notes` field. Bringing the implementation in line with the fuller binding, and testing fingerprint-mismatch/retirement-survival, is real follow-up work I'm not doing in this docs PR — happy to file an issue for it if wanted.

Checks: `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` and `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` both clean (505 requirements, 127 tested/47 partial/331 todo/0 blocked). template.md builds clean via `make`.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of `ec672849`: **changes requested before merge**.

The full binding is much better than the earlier sketch, but four interoperability issues remain.

1. Template now normatively adopts Expansion's reservation, fingerprint, revalidation, retention, and recovery rules, yet Expansion remains informative in Template's front matter and absent from `normative_references`/`adoption_requires`: [reference tier](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/ec67284985991aab3f74c902b1774fbe390752ec/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.md#L58-L66), [normative adoption](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/ec67284985991aab3f74c902b1774fbe390752ec/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.md#L531-L589). Move it to the normative tier and update the typed manifest edges/status block.

2. `dispatch_event_id` is a distinct OAuth token-request parameter, but Template's IANA section registers only the grant URI and explicitly requests no further action. Expansion's registration of `creation_request_id` does not register this different name. Either register `dispatch_event_id` in OAuth Parameters or reuse the shared `creation_request_id` carrier with the domain-separated `op: dispatch` fingerprint.

3. A completed retry is incorrectly required to establish that the old template version is still applicable before recovering anything: [retry gate](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/ec67284985991aab3f74c902b1774fbe390752ec/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.md#L568-L574). Template lifecycle says retirement stops new dispatch but does not terminate already-dispatched Missions. Recovery is delivery of that existing Mission, so it must survive later template retirement. For a completed operation, verify the recorded template identity/version/fingerprint, requester authorization/PoP, and that the created Mission remains active; apply current template applicability only to a still-pending/reserved operation that has not committed creation.

4. The PR adds externally observable uniqueness, conflict, retry, recovery, accounting, retention, and no-repeat behavior but no conformance rows/tests. Add them. Also replace “evidence emission committed atomically” with a realizable transaction boundary: atomically commit the evidence record or durable outbox with Mission creation, then deliver/publish idempotently. External emission itself cannot generally participate in the datastore transaction.

pulls.title: impl(mission-join): join-capable MissionView, loadView keyed by canonical (issuer, id) (#557 stage A)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #557

## Scope (stage A, per the fresh review)

This is stage A of the three-stage sequence the issue's fresh review confirmed ("join-capable view, independently tested baseline resolver, then gateway integration"): the join-capable `MissionView` plus `loadView`'s canonical-key contract. Stage B (a baseline join resolver implementing rules 1, 3-6, 8 — including delegate narrowing and the three-bound intersection the review called out as missing from the original sketch) and stage C (`pep.ts` wiring for a no-`mission`-claim token, plus the baseline-specific conformance rows) are follow-ons, not touched here.

Concretely:

- **`MissionView` gets `subject: { iss, sub }` and `client_id: string`** (`services/pdp/src/policy-view.ts`) — the two fields Join rules 3-4 compare the joined credential against. No `mission_mismatch` `DenialReason` here: the review's own sketch puts that with the resolver (stage B), since deciding a join failure needs the resolver's join logic, not just the view shape.
- **`loadView` is keyed by the canonical `(issuer, id)` reference tuple**, not a bare `mission_id` (`PepDeps.loadView` / `McpServerDeps.loadView` in `services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts` and `server.ts`, new exported `MissionReference` type). This is what "keying `loadView` by canonical (issuer,id)" in the fresh review asks for: a same-id collision under a different issuer is now a load-time miss by contract, not something every call site has to separately catch.

## Safety verification (policy_view_id)

Verified directly, not just asserted: `policyViewId` (`services/pdp/src/policy-view.ts`) hashes a pinned commitment of exactly `mission_id`, `mission_version`, `authority_hash`, and `model_id` — never the whole `MissionView` object. Grepped the repo for any other view-digesting site (`canonicalize(view`, `computeAnchor(view`, `JSON.stringify(view`, `view_digest`) — none exists outside that one pinned commitment. Adding `subject`/`client_id` cannot perturb an existing pinned hash. This is now also a standing test (`services/pdp/test/policy-view.test.ts`, no live infra required): `policyViewId` is byte-identical for a view with and without the Join fields, and still moves when a pinned field (`mission_version`) changes, so the pin itself isn't a no-op.

## Fixture-trap avoided

`services/mcp-payments/test/{mcp-channel,mcp-http-channel}.test.ts` already cover the existing view-issuer post-load check in `enforceInner` ("a credential naming a different Mission issuer than the loaded view is refused with `mission_reference_conflict`", both arms). Under a naive re-keying, a test double that enforces issuer-matching inside `loadView` would return `undefined` for that same-id-different-issuer case, silently turning the refusal into `unknown_mission` instead. Every test double touched here matches on `ref.id` alone (preserving current behavior); only the demo stack's real kernel-backed `loadView` (`demo/src/stack.ts`) enforces the issuer match for real, since nothing exercises that path today.

Every fixture's `subject`/`client_id` addition sources real data: the demo stack and the authorization-server e2e tests pull `fresh.subject`/`fresh.client_id` straight off the kernel's Mission Record (which already carries both, unconditionally — see `services/authorization-server/src/kernel/types.ts`); `packages/mission-signals/test/signals.test.ts` captures them once from the `kernel.approve()` return, alongside its other Mission-claim fields; plain unit fixtures mirror the `sub`/`clientId` the same test's `TokenFacts` already uses. Nothing is invented.

## Tests run

- `pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc --build`, whole workspace): clean.
- `pnpm vitest run services/pdp services/mcp-payments services/authorization-server services/agent services/access-request packages/mission-signals evals`: **717 passed, 120 skipped** (live-OpenFGA-gated suites auto-skip in this sandbox; same skip set as before this change), 0 failed.
- `pnpm test` (full workspace): **880 passed, 120 skipped**, 0 failed.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 502 requirements (127 tested, 46 partial, 329 todo, 0 blocked) — unchanged from baseline; no manifest rows added in this stage, per the review's direction that baseline-join rows land with the resolver/gateway PRs.

## Follow-ons (named, not in this PR)

- **Stage B**: a baseline join resolver (rules 1, 3-6, 8), `mission_mismatch` added to `DenialReason`, delegate narrowing (rule 5), and the three-bound intersection (rule 8) the review flagged as missing from the original two-PR sketch.
- **Stage C**: `pep.ts` wiring — a discriminated ordinary/Mission-bound credential-facts model or dedicated MAS-mode entry point (not a bare branch at the top of `enforceInner`, per the review), plus the baseline-specific conformance-manifest rows and their fixtures.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed in `9a7bd997`. Point-by-point:

**1. "The contract is not enforced at the consuming boundary" (`toolsList()`, `reverifyList()`).** Confirmed as real, not hypothetical — added `loadCheckedView(loadView, ref)` (`services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts`, exported), which verifies both `loaded.view.id` and `loaded.view.issuer` against the requested tuple and treats any mismatch as a miss. `McpPaymentsServer.toolsList` and `Pep.reverifyList` now resolve `loadView` through it.

`Pep.enforceInner` is deliberately left calling `deps.loadView` directly, unchanged. It needs to distinguish "no Mission" (`unknown_mission`) from "wrong issuer" (`mission_reference_conflict`) for its own refusal taxonomy — `loadCheckedView`'s undefined-on-mismatch contract would collapse that distinction and turn the existing `mission_reference_conflict` tests into `unknown_mission` failures. This is the one place a full "centralize checked loading" would have cost something, so I went with the second option the review offered (verify at every consumer) rather than force enforceInner through the same helper.

**2. "Ordinary fixtures should implement the canonical tuple contract; keep a deliberately nonconforming loader only in the negative boundary test."** Done. Upgraded every other `loadView` fixture touched in stage A (evals' `loadHarnessView`, the authorization-server e2e tests, `access-request`, `agent`, and the rest of `mcp-payments`'s tests) to check both `id` and `issuer`, sourcing the issuer from the same real record/view each fixture already had. Only `mcp-channel.test.ts` and `mcp-http-channel.test.ts` keep the `id`-only loader — now with an explicit comment explaining it's the deliberate exception, since their tests exist specifically to exercise `enforceInner`'s own issuer check rather than have a stricter loader absorb the mismatch first.

**3. "Add a same-ID/different-issuer test proving tools enumeration returns nothing and revalidation cannot consume the wrong view."** Added `services/mcp-payments/test/loaded-view-contract.test.ts` (pure unit test, no live infra, never skips): a nonconforming `id`-only loader hands back a real Mission's view to a credential naming that Mission's ID under a different issuer.
- `toolsList()` asserts `[]`, not the real Mission's tool catalog.
- `reverifyList()` asserts `false` against an `expectedDigest` deliberately crafted to match what the wrongly-returned view's own entry *would* produce — so the test only passes if the refusal comes from the loaded-view check itself, not an incidental digest mismatch.

I didn't just trust this test — I temporarily reverted both `loadCheckedView` call sites, reran it, and confirmed both assertions fail exactly as expected (`toolsList` leaks the two real-Mission tools; `reverifyList` returns `true`), then restored the fix and confirmed both pass again.

**4. Integration note on #686.** Noted — not something I can act on from this branch. Flagging back: this PR is ready for merge on your side; #686 will need to rebase onto the new `loadView({id, issuer})` signature and `loadCheckedView` and rerun typecheck/tests afterward.

**Test results (this round):**
- `pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc --build`, whole workspace): clean.
- `pnpm vitest run services/pdp services/mcp-payments services/authorization-server services/agent services/access-request packages/mission-signals evals`: **719 passed, 120 skipped** (unchanged skip set, live-OpenFGA-gated), 0 failed.
- `pnpm test` (full workspace): **884 passed, 120 skipped**, 0 failed.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 502 requirements (127 tested, 46 partial, 329 todo, 0 blocked) — unchanged.

No disputes — the review's read of the gap and its two-option fix were both right; I picked the "verify at every consumer" option over full centralization for the reason in point 1 above.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of `9e264415`: **changes requested before merge**.

The join-capable view and canonical `(issuer, id)` loader signature are the right stage-A shape, but the contract is not enforced at the consuming boundary. `Pep.enforceInner` checks the returned issuer after loading, while `toolsList()` and `reverifyList()` trust whatever the injected loader returns. In particular, `toolsList()` immediately exposes the returned view's authority-derived tool set: [unchecked lookup](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9e264415e10b50091946148cf4fc835065b8fe2a/src/services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts#L555-L563).

This is not hypothetical: the PR deliberately leaves repository test/eval loaders matching only `ref.id` so existing issuer-conflict tests retain their old classification. With one of those loaders, a credential carrying the same Mission ID under a different issuer can obtain the other Mission's tool catalog. The later action path refuses, but least-exposure has already failed.

Please centralize checked loading, or verify both `loaded.view.id` and `loaded.view.issuer` against the requested tuple at every consumer, including `toolsList()` and `reverifyList()`. Then add a same-ID/different-issuer test proving tools enumeration returns nothing and revalidation cannot consume the wrong view. Ordinary fixtures should implement the canonical tuple contract; keep a deliberately nonconforming loader only in the negative boundary test.

Integration note: #686 shares `pep.ts`/`server.ts` and was authored against the old string loader. Merge this first, then require #686 to rebase and rerun workspace typecheck/tests.

pulls.title: Cross-domain Origin Principal: PDP dual-axis primitive (#539 stage A)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #539

## Stage A scope (as the fresh review defined it)

The fresh review against `2d63119a` rejected the original session disposition's PR A as an incomplete vertical slice and set a revised sequence:

1. Shared mapping/entitlement contracts plus the complete PEP/PDP AuthZEN vertical slice.
2. Apply those contracts to both Cross-Org exchange and the ID-JAG RAS path.
3. Integration/privacy completion.

This PR is stage 1 only. It does **not** touch `services/authorization-server/src/adapters/cross-org-grant.ts` or `services/ras/src/index.ts` — those are stage 2, in the same wave, per the review ("Fixing only RAS leaves another profile entry point violating the same dual-axis requirements... Cross-Org must be repaired in the same implementation wave").

## What this PR builds

**`packages/mission-core/src/origin-principal.ts`** (new): `OriginPrincipal`, `PrincipalMappingObservation`/`PrincipalMappingResolver`, `EntitlementObservation`/`EntitlementResolver` — the two "separate fail-closed mapping and current-entitlement resolver contracts" the review required, placed in `@mission/core` (not `@mission/pdp`) so stage 2 can reuse them without a new dependency on the PDP package.

**`services/pdp/src/evaluate.ts`**: `EvaluationRequest.subject` grows `properties.iss` (the authenticated local subject's issuer — the representational gap the review flagged: "the current evaluation request cannot represent an issuer-qualified local subject"); `context.mission` grows `subject`; `DenialReason` grows `principal_mapping_failed`. New step 4a implements AuthZEN rule 10: resolves `context.mission.subject` via the injected `principalMapping` resolver, requires equality with `(subject.properties.iss, subject.id)`, then resolves current entitlement via the injected `entitlement` resolver against its own `entitlementStalenessBoundSeconds` (kept separate from `stalenessBoundSeconds`, per "Mission-state freshness and entitlement freshness are separate declarations and MUST NOT be collapsed into one timestamp"). Any failed/missing/ambiguous/stale result at either step denies `principal_mapping_failed`; a permit or later denial that passed the mapping step carries the `principal_mapping` evidence object. Runs before the authority-entry match (WHO gates WHAT).

This is the **PDP-authoritative default placement** ("The PDP is authoritative for the mapping in the default placement") — both resolvers are injected dependencies the PDP calls directly, the same idiom as the existing `fga: Fga` dependency, keeping the PDP's "pure function of injected dependencies" architecture. The alternative deployment configuration described in the same spec paragraph (mapping placed at the PEP, conveyed as a structured, integrity-protected observation the PDP verifies) is **not implemented** — see the conformance-manifest note below.

A throwing resolver (network/store failure) propagates as an exception rather than being caught and turned into a denial, matching the existing `fga.checkWithContext` precedent (also uncaught). Flagging this explicitly since the "failed... result" language could be read to cover it; out of stage A scope.

**`services/mcp-payments/src/server.ts`**: all four `TokenFacts`-construction sites (`validateToken`, `validateMissionToken`, `verifyTransactionCredential`, `validateAttenuationChain`) now carry `mission.subject` through when the verified claim has one, and add `iss` (this resource's own verified issuer — a resource-wide constant, not read from the token). `validateToken`/`validateMissionToken` now parse the mission claim with `@mission/core`'s `readTxnMissionClaim` (which already validates the closed `{iss,sub}` shape), replacing an inline check that only read `id`/`issuer`/`authority_hash` and silently dropped `subject`.

**`services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts`**: envelope construction populates `subject.properties.iss` and `context.mission.subject` only from verified `TokenFacts`, never from the per-request tool arguments a client controls. `PepDeps` grows `principalMapping`/`entitlement`/`entitlementStalenessBoundSeconds`, forwarded to the PDP's `EvaluateOptions` unchanged.

## Tests

- `services/pdp/test/evaluate-origin-principal.test.ts` (16 tests): the dual-axis rule's fail-closed matrix -- unconfigured resolvers, missing/stale/mismatched mapping, missing/negative/stale entitlement (including a future-dated `observed_at`, see fix below), the unconfigured-bound case, step ordering vs. the authority-entry match, and both boundary controls.
- `services/mcp-payments/test/origin-principal.test.ts` (6 tests): envelope construction only from verified `TokenFacts` (including a negative test where `args` attempts to smuggle a different origin principal), `subject.properties.iss` presence/omission, and end-to-end permit/deny through `Pep.enforce()` with the resolvers wired via `PepDeps`.

All existing tests pass unchanged (902 passed, 120 skipped -- the pre-existing OpenFGA-gated set; this sandbox has no OpenFGA/docker reachable). `pnpm -r typecheck` is clean workspace-wide.

## Self-review fix folded in

`fix(pdp): entitlement freshness must reject a future-dated observed_at` -- the entitlement freshness check initially only compared `age <= bound`, the exact shape GAP 3 (#612) already fixed for `context.freshness`: a future-dated `observed_at` yields a negative age that trivially satisfies any bound. Fixed to require `age >= -skewToleranceMs` too, mirroring `context.freshness`'s own check; two tests added (denies beyond skew, permits within skew).

## Conformance manifest

`node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` passes: 502 requirements, 127 tested, 49 partial (+3), 326 todo (-3), 0 blocked.

- `authzen.pdp-request.subject-shape-and-issuer-presence` -> **partial**: `subject.properties.iss` presence-when-known/omission-when-unknown tested; `subject.type`'s default-to-user is not (this PEP never sets it, relying on the wire-level AuthZEN default).
- `authzen.context-mission.origin-principal-only-from-verified-source` -> **partial**, deliberately not `tested`: the controlling review comment says "before claiming either AuthZEN row closed," tying this row to the one below. The mcp-payments PEP envelope path is fully covered by two tests, but Cross-Org and ID-JAG RAS still drop `mission.subject` and land in stage 2.
- `authzen.pdp-request.origin-principal-mapping-required` -> **partial**: the shared `principal_mapping_failed` classification and evidence-binding behavior the row's `observation.normative` also states is covered (PDP-authoritative placement); the row's own quoted MUST clause is the *other* deployment configuration (PEP-placed structured observation), not implemented.

`--collect` (stricter, validates full vitest names against the runner) reports 85 pre-existing findings, all OpenFGA-gated tests this sandbox can't collect without a live OpenFGA/docker -- none reference my new files. Worth CI re-running with OpenFGA up to independently confirm the five new test-name mappings collect cleanly.

No spec (`.md`) files touched.

## Follow-on stages (not in this PR)

- **Stage B**: apply the same `PrincipalMappingResolver`/`EntitlementResolver` contracts to `cross-org-grant.ts` (replace the static `.find` mapping and ceiling-only axis) and `ras/index.ts` (add `mission.subject` to the destructure, mapping-policy lookup before minting, `invalid_grant` on missing/ambiguous mapping). Sequenced after #650 per the review (`client_id` vs `mission.subject` are independent fields on one mint call, so not blocked by it, but #650 is already `decide`-labeled and touches the same mint block).
- **Stage C**: integration/privacy completion -- the 11-scenario fixture suite, `principal_mapping` evidence wired into `evidence.record()` with a protected-reference/digest convention (owned by the evidence profile, not invented here), and the txn-authorization mapping-revalidation/foreign-issuer-registry partials the manifest already flags.

comments.body:
Addressed both points, pushed as `a8d536e0..c7d2ab4a`.

## 1. Exceptions from either injected resolver escape `evaluate()`

Fixed in `e0021212`. Both `opts.principalMapping.resolve()` and `opts.entitlement.resolve()` are now wrapped in try/catch; a throw normalizes to the same `undefined` result the missing/ambiguous/disabled cases already produce, so it falls straight into the existing fail-closed logic -- no new branch needed. Restructured the mapping check's control flow (`if (mappingResult === undefined) return deny(...)` as its own guard, before computing `mappingEstablished`) so the exception-normalized `undefined` narrows cleanly for TypeScript too, now that the variable has to be a mutable `let`.

Two new tests in `services/pdp/test/evaluate-origin-principal.test.ts`: a throwing `principalMapping` resolver denies `principal_mapping_failed` (18 tests total in that file now, up from 16); a throwing `entitlement` resolver likewise denies, and -- since the mapping step had already succeeded before the entitlement resolver was even called -- the resulting refusal still carries the `principal_mapping` evidence object, exercising the same "denial after the mapping step still binds evidence" path the existing entitlement-failure tests cover.

## 2. Decision Evidence drops `principal_mapping` entirely

Fixed in `88eb4882` + `d7f6bcf7`. Two parts:

- **New anchor typ** (`88eb4882`): the runtime-evidence privacy rule names the digest form explicitly by typ (`mission-origin-subject`), so `packages/mission-core/src/anchors.ts` registers `MISSION_ORIGIN_SUBJECT_TYP` and reuses the existing `computeAnchor`/`verifyAnchor` -- no new digest mechanism invented, just the family anchor idiom applied under the typ the spec already names.
- **Evidence write** (`d7f6bcf7`): `DecisionEvidence.principal_mapping` (new, optional) mirrors the PDP's five sub-members, but `origin`/`local` are protected references (`computeAnchor(MISSION_ORIGIN_SUBJECT_TYP, view.issuer, {iss,sub})`), never the raw pair the ephemeral PDP decision context carries. `Pep.enforceInner` computes both references once and attaches them to every `evidence.record({kind: "decision", ...})` call where the PDP context carried `principal_mapping` -- so a permit AND a later-step denial that still passed the mapping check (e.g. an entitlement-caused `principal_mapping_failed`) both retain it; a request not claiming the profile never does.

Three new tests in `services/mcp-payments/test/origin-principal.test.ts` (9 total now, up from 6): a permit's persisted record has protected, independently-reproducible digest references (`verifyAnchor` round-trips) and the raw `sub`/`iss` values are confirmed absent anywhere in the record's JSON serialization; an entitlement-caused denial's persisted record still carries the full `principal_mapping` object; a non-profile request's persisted record never carries it at all.

**Disclosure obligation** (the same privacy rule's MUST-disclose clause for the deterministic-digest form): added to `evidence.ts`'s `principal_mapping` field doc comment, at the point a deployment reading this code would actually see it -- states plainly that this is dictionary-attackable correlation infrastructure over a small enumerable population, not concealment. Not machine-tested (it's a documentation obligation), so the corresponding manifest row (`evidence.privacy.protected-subject-reference-should-and-disclose-limitation`) is marked `partial`, not `tested` -- see the ledger commit for the split.

`c7d2ab4a` flips `evidence.extensions.principal-mapping-required-submembers` to `tested` (all five sub-members present-or-entirely-absent, proven) and `evidence.privacy.protected-subject-reference-should-and-disclose-limitation` to `partial` (protection tested, disclosure documented but not test-gated). `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` passes: 502 requirements, 128 tested, 50 partial, 324 todo, 0 blocked.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of `a8d536e0`: **changes requested before merge**.

The dual-axis ordering and separate entitlement-freshness bound are sound, but two fail-closed/evidence requirements remain incomplete.

1. Exceptions from either injected resolver escape `evaluate()` instead of becoming the profile's required `principal_mapping_failed` decision: [resolver calls](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/a8d536e0b5dcd7e16fa64eb8cd584c0d601949ce/src/services/pdp/src/evaluate.ts#L354-L409). A network/store failure is a failed mapping or entitlement result, not a different authorization outcome. Catch both resolver failures, normalize them to the registered denial, and test both throwing cases. This also ensures the denial follows the ordinary evidence path rather than becoming an unclassified transport exception.

2. The PDP response carries `principal_mapping`, but the PEP's retained Decision Evidence copies only decision metadata, denial, entry digest, evaluation id, and the ordinary Mission/action fields; it drops the mapping completely: [evidence write](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/a8d536e0b5dcd7e16fa64eb8cd584c0d601949ce/src/services/mcp-payments/src/pep.ts#L664-L683). That contradicts the requirement that decisions evaluating this profile record the composed mapping object. Extend the evidence contract/store, apply the runtime-evidence protected-reference rule rather than retaining raw identities by default, and test the persisted record for both permit and entitlement-caused denial.

The manifest may honestly remain `partial` until the PEP-placed alternative and the other entry points land, but the PDP-authoritative path implemented here should be internally conforming rather than knowingly leaving exceptions and its required evidence outside the slice.

Integration note: rebase this PR after #685. The branches auto-merge today, but #686's new fixtures still use `loadView(string)` and omit #685's required MissionView join fields, so the combined tree does not satisfy the new contract without edits and a fresh workspace test run.

pulls.title: Editorial: architecture and security-model density pass
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Scope

Editorial-only density and cross-doc dedup pass on the informational plane: `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md` and `draft-mcguinness-mission-security-model.md`. Both were consolidated recently (D124/D127); this pass respects that structure and targets paragraph density, front-loading, and the cluster-specific dedups called out below. No normative content, mechanism, heading, or anchor changed.

## Two honest findings, reported rather than silently resolved

**1. The brief's second architecture dedup target is the work-product reading, not "materialized-capability residual."** The brief named two composition-property restatements in architecture with an explicit "the profile is normative" deferral. Grepping the file for that deferral's actual sentence (`"...is the normative text this passage tracks."`) turns up exactly two hits, both in the Invariants section, both opening with "Read on the artifact plane" / "Read under composition": the non-transitive work-product (artifact-plane) reading, and the aggregate-ceiling (composition) reading. Both are tightened below. "Materialized-capability residual" as a literal restated concept with that deferral pattern does not exist elsewhere in the file (it only appears as terse, already-minimal table-cell citations in the Composed Kill-Switch Reality and Containment Matrix tables, which are left untouched per the adversary/family-checklist protection rule). Treating the brief's label as pointing at the work-product paragraph rather than manufacturing new content to match the label.

**2. Mandate's "issuer-key-compromise analysis" is not actually restated multiple times in security-model.** Grepped for `mandate`, `signing.key`, `compromised key`, `rotation`, `forge`, `backdated`, `existence proof` across the whole file: 3 total `mandate` mentions (none about keys), zero hits on the rest. What *does* exist is a small echo, not a restatement of Mandate's specific mechanics: the Authorization Server trusted-base entry says "This is the strongest trust assumption in the suite" (line ~452), and the Documenting section separately said "since the model's strongest assumption reduces to those keys" (line ~1214), the same idea in different words. Fix applied: dropped the Documenting-section echo (it already cross-references `{{trusted-base}}`), and gave the Authorization Server entry an explicit citation to `I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate`, the document that owns the deeper issuer-key-compromise mechanics (forged self-consistent Mandates, rotation not bounding exposure, audit-registration as the bound), so the trusted-base entry is now the one properly-cited home for that concern. Did not import Mandate's mechanics into security-model, since that would add content on a density pass rather than dedup it.

## Dedups performed

- **Architecture, Invariants section**: the artifact-plane (work-products/non-transitive handoff) and aggregate-ceiling (composition) restatements each tightened to a summary sentence plus citation, keeping the "that section, not this summary, is the normative text this passage tracks" deferral verbatim in structure.
- **Security-model, Trusted Base / Ten Residuals**: kept the Transparency Service entry in `{{trusted-base}}` as the one full statement of single-service equivocation; compressed the "Ten Residuals" list's restatement to a one-line pointer at that entry (`{{trusted-base}}`, `I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-audit`). Left the Adversary Model's own "Audit tampered..." row residual untouched (it's already a terse, non-duplicative one-line residual consistent with every other row in that table, and rubric 4 protects adversary-table rows/mitigations/residuals from being dropped).
- **Security-model, Authorization Server / Documenting**: removed the "strongest assumption reduces to those keys" echo from Documenting (kept its existing `{{trusted-base}}` pointer); added an explicit `I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate` citation to the Authorization Server trusted-base entry.

**Observed, not touched**: architecture's "Worked Composition" section (`{{worked-composition}}`) restates the same work-product/quarantine idea a third time with no deferral clause and a different section job (deployment-pattern framing vs. invariant reading). Left alone, consistent with D126's precedent of deliberately keeping duplications that serve distinct sections after inspection.

## Density pass (paragraph splits, front-loading, no content cut)

- Architecture: `{{capability-envelope}}` (What Approval Commits paragraph, 3 ideas -> 3 paragraphs), `{{validity-model}}` (freshness-dial paragraph, ~9 sentences/4 ideas -> 4 paragraphs; the frozen `MAY provide` sentence kept byte-identical), `{{assurance-levels}}` intro (2 ideas -> 2 paragraphs), `{{containment}}` (Containment Matrix prose, 3 ideas -> 3 paragraphs).
- Security-model: `{{guarantees}}` ("What the Model Does and Does Not Guarantee") had two long trailing paragraphs split into four, front-loaded; light in-place tightening of the MAS trusted-base entry (merged two sentences via colon, no content removed).

No em-dashes existed before this pass and none were introduced (`grep "—"` and `grep " -- "` both empty before and after).

## Mandatory proof: BCP-14 sentence diff (empty)

Method: `/tmp/bcp14_extract.py` strips YAML front matter and fenced (`~~~`/```) code blocks, normalizes all whitespace to single spaces, splits on sentence boundaries, and keeps only sentences containing an **uppercase** BCP-14 keyword (`MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHALL`, `SHALL NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, `REQUIRED`, `RECOMMENDED`, `MAY`, `OPTIONAL`), matched as whole words. Lowercase must/should/etc. are excluded by design: both documents' Conventions sections state that lowercase modal words carry ordinary English meaning, not a requirement, so counting them would flag dozens of non-normative sentences. Sets are compared as sorted multisets.

architecture (before, 3 flagged sentences) vs. architecture (after, 3 flagged sentences): **diff exit 0, empty**
security-model (before, 1 flagged block) vs. security-model (after, 1 flagged block): **diff exit 0, empty**

(The security-model file's one flagged block is the whole OWASP Agentic Threat Coverage table, swept in as one blob by the extractor's naive sentence splitter because of a mid-cell "SHOULD"; that table was not touched by this pass, so it is byte-identical before and after.)

## Lines before/after

| File | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md | 3376 | 3403 | +27 |
| draft-mcguinness-mission-security-model.md | 1362 | 1385 | +23 |

Growth is paragraph-break whitespace plus the new Document History sections (neither file had one), not new prose; the dedup edits are a net reduction in prose bytes, spent back on readability per D124/D125 precedent.

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`: OK, 41 drafts, no drift; substrate-statements OK.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK (519 requirements). Neither `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md` nor `draft-mcguinness-mission-security-model.md` appears in `source.specs` (grepped the manifest's pinned-file list directly), so neither is conformance-pinned and no re-pin was needed.
- `make draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-security-model.txt`: both `kramdown-rfc` and `xml2rfc-txt` stages OK for both files.
- No heading or `{#anchor}` renamed (`git diff` shows zero `+#`/`-#` lines); Mission Document Map section untouched.
- Document History added to both files (neither previously had one), each with one entry describing this pass, following the plain-bullet convention used in `draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.md`.

Not merging; base is `main`.

reviews.author: mcguinness
reviews.body:
Fresh review of exact head `9e6887ce` against `main` (`99265045`): **one correction is needed before merge.**

The composition rewrite at [`draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md:1180`](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/9e6887ce5b1b4c945db7ddbb826bbf1865f76a54/draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md#L1180-L1189) collapses two independent facts into “depth resets at each hop and generation independently of its parent.” The prior text separately said:

1. delegation depth resets at each cross-domain hop and child generation; and
2. a Child Mission's own derivation cap is independent of its parent's.

The new wording makes parent independence modify `depth` and drops the second fact entirely. That distinction is material to the aggregate-ceiling warning: the OAuth core's “Composition and the Effective Ceiling” discussion separately composes delegation depth / child generations with **derivations summed across the child subtree**. Please retain a compact second clause, for example: “Delegation depth resets at each cross-domain hop and child generation, and each Child Mission enforces its own derivation cap independently of its parent's.”

The artifact-plane compression remains faithful to the normative core rule, and the security-model edits—including the Mandate example and per-service transparency pointer—are sound.

## Summary

**1. BCP-14-keyword sentence multiset diff (pristine `99265045` vs. final), per file.**

mandate.md              :  93 ->  93 keyword sentences, diff EMPTY

The wording after the label is byte-identical; a `- **Label.** ` prefix was added.

**2. `{{...}}` cross-reference token multiset diff, per file -- all four empty.**

```

authority-server.md  : 73 distinct tokens, diff vs. pristine EMPTY

**3. All three node checkers clean**, plus two more run as a bonus:

```

  -> substrate-statements check OK: 5 Statements, 8 consumer tables validated.

(cd src && node scripts/check-spec-versions.mjs)
  -> SPEC_VERSIONS check OK (53 rows, ...); output byte-identical to the pre-edit baseline.

node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs

node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs

node scripts/check-external-pins.mjs    -> OK: structural validation passed.
node scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs  -> OK: structural and registry cross-reference validation passed.
```

**4. Build clean, nested-list rendering spot-checked:**

```
make draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.txt \
     draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-issuance-grant.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.txt

```

The two structural (not just whitespace) edits are the nested-bullet conversion under "Mission-bound issuance for the high-consequence classes" (`#enterprise-profile`) and the 3-item Redemption Errors list (`#redemption-errors`). Both spot-checked in the rendered `.txt`: the nested sub-bullets render as indented list items under the parent (not flattened into run-on continuation prose), and the 3-item list renders as three separate bulleted paragraphs.

None of the four files carries a `# Document History` appendix, and per the repo's convention (a companion adds one only on its next *substantive* revision) none was added: this is a pure reflow, not a substantive revision.

pulls.title: core: specify the Mission-to-OAuth-grant cardinality (#700)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #700

## Summary

Rules the "Mission above N grants" vs "one grant binds one Mission" question from the 2026-08-24 architecture-shape review, per #700's session disposition (adopted in full): independent Mission object identified by `(issuer, id)`; Mission-to-binding `0..N`; binding-to-Mission exactly `1`; no multi-Mission grant or credential, ever.

Changes are concentrated in `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`, Section "Binding the Mission to the Grant" (`{{grant-binding}}`):

- A Mission is independent of any OAuth grant, identified globally by `(issuer, id)` (the standalone MAS is the standing proof).
- Defines the **Mission grant binding**: an AS-controlled, functional mapping from one Mission-bound grant lineage to exactly one Mission.
- Permits zero or more bindings per Mission (an authorization-code lineage, an additional refresh-token family a continuation transport establishes later, a Token Exchange derivation, a cross-domain local grant), each identifying exactly one Mission; the AS `MUST NOT` establish a second binding for an already-bound grant lineage and `MUST` refuse `invalid_grant` on an attempted rebind.
- States that a Child Mission or expansion successor gets a new identity and its own bindings, related to its origin by lineage (`parent`/`predecessor`), never by extending the origin's binding.
- States that a continuation handle or refresh-token family is credential/execution machinery rooted in one Mission, not the Mission itself.
- Clarifies that non-active state gates every bound derivation without implying revocation of an unrelated OAuth grant or recall of an unexpired access token absent a runtime state check.
- Names fleet cascade/enumeration as an issuer-side index kept distinct from the interoperable model (a companion Management profile MAY standardize its wire surface).
- Resolves the unredeemed-authorization-code `SHOULD revoke ... or allow it to expire` fork into one deployment policy applied consistently, with idempotent replay.
- Distinguishes a grant binding from a decision-time runtime join: the Mission Authority Server's Mission Join is a per-request, non-persistent association and `MUST NOT` be modeled as a grant binding.

Also: two new terminology entries (`Mission`, updated; `Mission Grant Binding`, new); two new informative references (Mission Continuation, Mission Management) added to front matter and to `family-manifest.json`'s typed edges; one Document History entry.

## Conformance

Six new rows under `{{grant-binding}}` in `conformance-manifest.json`, all born `todo`, covering the acceptance tests the review named:

- `core.grant-binding.multiple-bindings-per-mission` (two refresh families, one Mission)
- `core.grant-binding.rebind-rejected` (rebind refused `invalid_grant`)
- `core.grant-binding.token-exchange-preserves-mission` (Token Exchange preserves the one Mission)
- `core.grant-binding.cross-domain-destination-family` (destination-local grant, one Mission)
- `core.grant-binding.runtime-join-not-persistent-binding` (MAS/PDP join never becomes a binding)
- `core.grant-binding.termination-gates-every-binding` (termination gates every binding; residual access-token behavior per the existing stateless-baseline/state-observable framing)

`conformance-manifest.json`'s `content_sha256` is re-pinned for the core, and mechanically for the substrate (whose OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment carries an `assessed-oauth-digest` marker over the core's bytes; re-read against this diff, no kernel-mapping or capability claim changed, since the mapping's own "grant binding" language already matched this PR's definition).

## Deviations / findings

No companion contradictions were found in the Mission Authority Server, Cross-Domain, or Child Delegation documents, so none of them were edited:

- MAS's Mission Join already distinguishes a decision-time join from issuance ("that join establishes correlation, not that the AS issued the token under the Mission") and already allows one credential to join more than one Mission across requests.
- Cross-domain already fixes exactly one Mission Issuer per Mission, with the destination-local token preserving the `mission` claim unchanged.
- Child Delegation's `parent` member is already lineage/audit data that "does not grant authority."

This PR only makes those existing invariants explicit from the core's side via cross-reference; it does not restructure any companion document.

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean (525 requirements, 6 new `todo`)
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — clean (41 drafts, no drift)
- `node scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs` — clean
- `node scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs` — clean
- `node scripts/check-external-pins.mjs` — clean
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.txt` — clean

## Merge note

Touches core. Please merge **after** the `feat/637-resource-access-profile` PR; sections should be disjoint (that PR extracts `mission_resource_access` into a Resource Access Profile, this PR only touches "Binding the Mission to the Grant" and adjacent terminology/history), but rebase here if needed.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Reviewed head `7eb22842df70254f2eba0c6004ad93486382d2a7` against issue #700 and the current Core, Continuation, MAS, and Cross-Domain contracts.

**Disposition: request changes.** The cardinality ruling is right, but the new abstraction currently merges two different OAuth relations and therefore does not yet define a stable cardinality model.

## P1 — Separate grant-lineage bindings from derived-credential association

The definition is a mapping from a **grant lineage** to one Mission, but the next paragraph makes every Token Exchange derivation and a “cross-domain local grant” a separate binding, then extends the invariant to “a grant or credential” ([lines 2261–2291](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/7eb22842df70254f2eba0c6004ad93486382d2a7/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2261-L2291)). Those are not one OAuth object:

- a delegation Token Exchange normally emits an access token; that token is a derived credential, not a new authorization-grant lineage;
- a Token Exchange creates a new grant binding only when the result actually establishes reusable grant state, such as a new refresh-token family;
- Cross-Domain defines the origin-issued ID-JAG and destination-minted **local access tokens**. The Resource AS section does not define the “cross-domain local grant” named here; it validates the one-time grant and mints local access tokens ([Cross-Domain lines 651–710](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.md#L651-L710)).

This ambiguity changes what the issuer-side index contains and whether cardinality is per exchange, token, refresh family, or durable grant.

Please define two relations explicitly:

1. **Mission grant binding:** a persistent/redeemable authorization-grant lineage (authorization-code grant and its refresh family, a continuation-created refresh family, or another profile-defined reusable grant) resolves to exactly one Mission. One Mission has `0..N` such bindings.
2. **Mission-derived credential association:** every issued credential identifies exactly one Mission, but issuing an access token does not by itself create another persistent grant binding.

If Token Exchange returns a refresh token or otherwise establishes reusable authorization state, that new family is a binding; an access-token-only exchange is a derivation under the input binding. For Cross-Domain, say whether the consumed ID-JAG becomes durable destination authorization state. If it does, define that state in Cross-Domain; if it does not, the minted access tokens are credential associations only. Then align the new conformance rows and the fleet index with this split.

## P1 — The rebind refusal has no protocol trigger

The PR correctly says the AS alone establishes and resolves a binding and that the client never supplies or negotiates one ([lines 2263–2265](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/7eb22842df70254f2eba0c6004ad93486382d2a7/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2263-L2265)). It then requires `invalid_grant` for a derivation that “would resolve” an existing lineage to another Mission ([lines 2286–2291](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/7eb22842df70254f2eba0c6004ad93486382d2a7/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2286-L2291)), but no request input or operation can name that second Mission. The new black-box conformance observation consequently cannot be exercised from a protocol surface.

Keep “one binding MUST NOT be reassigned” as an AS storage invariant. Require `invalid_grant` only on a profile-defined operation whose authenticated inputs can actually conflict with the existing binding, and name that operation and conflict source. Otherwise an internal data-integrity fault should fail closed and be audited, but should not be specified as a client-visible rebind request that the protocol makes impossible.

## P2 — Tighten establishment timing

The text says the AS establishes the binding at approval to both the authorization code and “the refresh token issued from it” ([lines 2267–2276](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/7eb22842df70254f2eba0c6004ad93486382d2a7/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2267-L2276)). A refresh token does not exist until successful code redemption and is not necessarily issued. Bind the authorization grant at approval; when code redemption emits refresh state, require that refresh family to inherit the same binding atomically with issuance.

The Mission independence, `0..N`/exactly-one direction, join-not-binding distinction, successor handling, lifecycle gating, and deterministic unredeemed-code policy otherwise match #700 well.

All current-head CI checks shown on the PR are green (reader build, editor copy, and repository checks).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Pushed `3ced0bd5`, addressing the review point by point.

## P1 — Separate grant-lineage bindings from derived-credential association

Agreed, and confirmed against each cited companion rather than taken on faith:

- **Delegation Token Exchange** (Section "Delegation Within a Mission"): the request fixes `requested_token_type` to `access_token`, so an ordinary delegated exchange never returns a refresh token. It is now a **derivation under the input binding**, not a new binding: the issued token is a derived token whose `mission` claim identifies the same Mission the `subject_token`'s binding resolved to.
- **Continuation's async-delegation family-creating exchange** is the one Token Exchange shape that *does* establish reusable state (a new refresh-token family), so it remains a genuine new grant binding, rooted in the Mission its `subject_token` resolved to — matching the review's own P1 list.
- **Cross-Domain**: re-read Sections "Cross-Domain Projection" and "Validation at the Resource AS." The consumed cross-domain grant is explicitly single-use ("MUST reject a replayed cross-domain grant... refuse a second presentation") and "not refreshable," and the Resource AS mints only local **access tokens** — no local refresh mechanism or other durable destination-side state is defined anywhere in that document. So per your own fallback ("if it does not [become durable], the minted access tokens are credential associations only") — that's the case here. "Cross-domain local grant" is gone from core; the local token is now a derived-token credential association, and I did not invent new durable state in Cross-Domain to make the old framing true, since none exists.

New core text (`{{grant-binding}}`) now states the Mission grant binding is scoped to a **persistent, redeemable grant lineage** only (the authorization-code lineage and its refresh family, or another profile-defined reusable grant), separately from a **derived token's `mission` claim**, which every issued credential carries without creating a new binding.

**One more instance I found while fixing this, beyond what was flagged**: the "Child Mission / expansion successor" sentence claimed each "has its own bindings," but Expansion's Token Exchange (`requested_token_type = access_token`, no refresh token in the request or the worked example) means a successor's *initial* credential is ordinarily a derived token with no grant binding of its own until a later exchange establishes one. Tightened that sentence to say a successor's grant binding or derived token, whichever it has, is its own — not that it necessarily has a binding at creation. Flagging this since it's the same category of error you caught, just not one you named.

**Ripple this forced**: the substrate's OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment (`draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md`, "Delegation:" capability entry) described the delegated Token Exchange as itself "a grant binding at issuance" — precisely the conflation this point corrects, in a different document. Reworded to "associates... without itself establishing a new grant binding," cross-referencing the corrected core section. No capability claim changed (Authorized Context Correlation is still supplied the same way); `assessed-oauth-digest` and the manifest's `content_sha256` are re-pinned for both files.

## P1 — The rebind refusal has no protocol trigger

Correct, and I couldn't find a counterexample after checking every operation that resolves a Mission from client input: the authorization-code/refresh grant types resolve from the credential alone, ordinary Token Exchange resolves from `subject_token` alone, and Continuation's family-creation fingerprint takes `source` from `subject_token` resolution, never a client-asserted value. There is genuinely no wire input a client can present that would ask the AS to resolve an existing lineage to a *different* Mission.

Took your first option: the no-reassignment property is now stated as an AS storage invariant ("this is an AS storage property rather than a client-visible refusal... treats the condition as a data-integrity fault: it fails closed... and audits the event, rather than surfacing an ordinary authorization outcome"), not an `invalid_grant`-producing client request.

For the conformance row, rather than drop the acceptance test entirely, I replaced it with the protocol-observable consequence: `core.grant-binding.lineage-resolves-stable-mission` — "The AS MUST resolve a bound grant lineage to the same Mission on every derivation performed against it." That's exercisable (drive repeated refreshes/derivations against one lineage, confirm the `mission` claim never drifts) without requiring an impossible client input. `core.grant-binding.rebind-rejected` is removed.

I also cross-referenced the one place a client-supplied identifier *is* checked against a resolved value: Expansion's `predecessor` parameter (non-authoritative cross-check, refused `invalid_grant` on mismatch). I was careful to frame this as a genuinely different thing — it protects which Mission a *new successor* is created from, not reassignment of an *existing* binding — so it doesn't quietly become "the operation" for this rule by association.

## P2 — Tighten establishment timing

Fixed as suggested: the AS now binds the Mission to the authorization code at approval; the text no longer treats the refresh token as existing simultaneously. Where redemption succeeds and emits a refresh-token family, that family "inherits the code's binding atomically with its issuance, extending the same Mission grant binding rather than starting a second one."

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean (525 requirements, same count: one row removed, one added)
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`, `check-substrate-statements.mjs`, `check-bundle-manifest.mjs`, `check-external-pins.mjs` — all clean
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.txt` — clean

No disputes — all three points held up under re-verification against the actual companion mechanics, and fixing them surfaced one more instance (the successor-binding overclaim) of the same underlying issue.

pulls.title: Refresh MCP pin to 2026-07-28 (#533)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #533

## Adoption review

The ruling required a scoped adoption review of the MCP 2026-07-28 diff (the statelessness redesign and the removed initialize/notifications/initialized handshake, both SEP-2575) against every family surface citing MCP, before the mechanical pin refresh. Swept the whole draft corpus for `{{MCP`; four reference keys cite MCP itself (a fifth, COAZ, is an AuthZEN artifact and out of scope here). A changes-requested review (see below) additionally required reconciling the implementation's own MCP traceability rows in `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`, which the original issue also named.

| Citing surface | Reference key | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission` tool-modeling section | `{{MCP}}` | **Unchanged** | Its claim that authorizing a tool's name "lines up with MCP filtering its tool list by the caller's granted authority" holds on direct text, not inference: `server/tools.mdx` (2026-07-28, same commit) states the `tools/list` result "MUST NOT vary per-connection" but "MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request... since credentials are per-request input, not connection state." The new `cacheScope: "private"` value corroborates this. Already pinned to 2026-07-28 in front matter; only the `notes/external-pins.json` registry entry was missing. |
| `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server` MCP Carriage section | `{{MCP-META}}` | **Prose-updated (pin only)** | The `_meta` reserved-prefix claim (`com.karlmcguinness.mission/reference` is outside MCP's reserved namespace) holds on more explicit textual footing: 2026-07-28 states the rule precisely (reserved only when the second label is `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp`). Front-matter target and date bumped from the retired 2025-11-25 track to 2026-07-28. Separately reviewed and deliberately left as-is: "absent negotiated or configured propagation support" - the removed handshake was one negotiation mechanism, but the sentence never named it, and per-request `clientCapabilities`/`extensions`/`server/discover` still satisfy "negotiated... support." |
| `draft-mcguinness-mission-capability-binding` MCP tool-object extraction rule | none (cites only the unversioned `MCP-REGISTRY` catalog example) | **Unchanged** | Confirmed directly against `server/tools.mdx`: `CacheableResult`'s `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` sit on the `tools/list` envelope, not the per-tool object, so `source_digest` over the extracted single-tool definition is unaffected. No version-pinned MCP citation here to refresh. |
| `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain` EMA citation | `{{MCP-EMA}}` | **Unchanged** | Enterprise-Managed Authorization now declares via per-request `clientCapabilities.extensions` (consistent with statelessness); the ID-JAG carriage claim it supports is untouched. Unversioned extension URL (`ext-auth` repo), not part of the base-protocol pin this ruling covers. |
| `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness` "MCP sessions" mention | none | **Unchanged, no citation** | Illustrative, non-normative list of cacheable harness state; not a reference-key citation, so out of scope of "the MCP pin." Remains accurate for the many deployed MCP servers still on pre-2026-07-28 revisions. |
| `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture`, `-shaping`, `-runtime` generic "an MCP tool/server" mentions | none | **Unchanged, no citation** | Format-agnostic illustrative examples, not tied to a protocol revision. |
| `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`: MCP EMA row, "MCP authorization profile" spike-pin row, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` row | none (implementation traceability, not a draft citation) | **Explicit older-version disposition recorded** | See "Implementation disposition" below. |

No delta broke a load-bearing draft claim, so no draft-level rework was triggered.

## Implementation disposition (src/), added after review

[Review](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/pull/711#issuecomment-5401346233): the family/draft citation pin advanced to 2026-07-28, but `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`'s implementation rows (MCP EMA, the "MCP authorization profile" spike pin, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `1.29.0`) still named 2025-11-25 with no disposition distinguishing the two pins. Correct: the original issue named `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md` and "any src assumptions" from the start; this was a real gap in the initial sweep, not just extra scope.

Resolution: **kept `src/` on the 2025-11-25 wire track** (did not adopt 2026-07-28 in the implementation) and recorded an explicit, verified compatibility disposition rather than leaving the split unexplained:

- Annotated all three `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md` rows with a pointer to the disposition.
- Appended a dated Notes entry (`src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`) recording: (a) the two pins are independent by design (citation pin = what the drafts describe; traceability pin = what the code speaks on the wire); (b) a verified compatibility check against the two named deltas, scoped to what this implementation actually does with MCP.
- **Verified, not assumed:** fetched the published `sdk-1.29.0` tarball and confirmed `dist/esm/types.js` sets `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'` (`SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` back through `2024-10-07`, nothing at `2026-07-28`); this replaces an initial inference drawn only from `src/spikes/SPIKE-REPORT.md`'s historical pairing. Read `services/mcp-payments/src/mcp-transport.ts` and `mcp-http-transport.ts` directly: both transports' `ListToolsRequestSchema`/`CallToolRequestSchema` handlers, and the HTTP transport's `authenticate()` DPoP middleware, derive `TokenFacts` fresh from that request's own `_meta` or `Authorization`/`DPoP` headers on every call, with no session-keyed cache between requests (the `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` does mint an SDK-level `Mcp-Session-Id`, but authorization does not read or key off it). So this implementation's authorization path already matches 2026-07-28's statelessness rule in substance; nothing the PEP relies on for authorization needs to change under that delta. What would need rework on an actual SDK/wire upgrade (the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake, new required per-request `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/*` fields, `resultType`, `server/discover`) is unimplemented protocol surface today, not a broken claim.
- **Decision:** defer the SDK/wire upgrade as separate follow-up work rather than fold a runtime migration into this pin-refresh PR (reworking both transports' handshake assumptions and re-verifying DPoP/Mission-credential carriage against the new per-request fields is implementation work, not a documentation change). `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0` exists on npm but its wire-version compatibility was not evaluated here. Not yet filed as its own tracked issue.

**`src/PLAN.md` constraint, disclosed rather than omitted:** the review also named `src/PLAN.md` lines (D38, the delivery-policy note) as still saying 2025-11-25. I did not touch `src/PLAN.md`: house convention routes it through direct commits to main, never a PR, and my own instructions forbid it here. Those PLAN.md lines remain accurate under this disposition (the implementation genuinely is still on 2025-11-25); the disposition itself lives in `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md`, which is the file this checker (`check-spec-versions.mjs`) and the traceability convention actually govern. If the owner wants the same pointer in PLAN.md, that needs a direct commit outside this PR.

## The PR

- Established the `MCP` and `MCP-META` entries in `notes/external-pins.json` (`kind: "git"`, `modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol` at the commit the `2026-07-28` tag resolves to). Two entries, not one, because the two reference keys cite two different files at that commit (`basic/authorization/index.mdx` vs `basic/index.mdx`) - the registry's one-path-one-digest shape can't span both, matching the existing `AUTHZEN`/`AUTHZEN-OBL` precedent (same repo, different files, separate ids). Each entry's note discloses the adoption-review finding for its citing claim, per house precedent for disclosure notes.
- Bumped `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md`'s `MCP-META` front-matter target and date from `2025-11-25` to `2026-07-28`. No body prose changed; the anchored MCP Carriage section text is untouched, so no conformance row text moved.
- Re-pinned `conformance-manifest.json`'s `source.specs` entry for `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md` (`content_sha256` in the first commit, `revision` bumped to that commit's hash in a follow-up commit, matching the repo's established two-commit re-pin convention).
- Annotated three `src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md` rows and appended a verified compatibility-disposition Notes entry (see above). `src/PLAN.md` intentionally untouched.

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-external-pins.mjs` - OK
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` - OK (41 drafts, no drift)
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` - OK (519 requirements; unchanged coverage counts)
- `node scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs` - OK (structural and registry cross-reference validation passed)
- `node src/scripts/check-spec-versions.mjs` - OK (53 rows, STRICT_SPECS clean; unchanged outstanding-gap/omitted-key counts)
- `make draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.txt` - builds clean

## Deviations

`notes/external-pins.json` had no prior MCP entry at all (confirmed by inspection), so this establishes rather than literally "refreshes" the registry row; the front-matter pin in `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md` is what was actually stale at 2025-11-25, which this PR corrects. Beyond that, no deviation from the ruling's scope: the `src/` reconciliation above was a real gap the review correctly caught, not a scope dispute, and is now addressed within this PR's existing bounds (documentation/disposition only, no `src/PLAN.md`, no runtime migration).

pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Reconciles the three previously uncross-referenced accounts of what earns the term "Mission-bound" (#663):

- **architecture, Mission Binding Properties** (`{{binding-properties}}`) is now the definition: the `credential-mission-bound` property's six equivalence conditions.
- **architecture, Token Classes** (`{{token-classes}}`) now cross-references that definition, and names the Mission Substrate Statement capability claims (Lifecycle-Gated Authorization, Monotonic Derivation, Credential-Bound) as how a binding evidences it — this was already implicit in the existing text, now made explicit with a link.
- **core, Conformance** adds one informative pointer sentence naming its existing gates (approval anchors, subset rule, state-gated derivation) as the OAuth binding's discharge of the architecture's `credential-mission-bound` property. Core-stands-alone holds: the pointer is informative only, core's own gates remain authoritative, and no new normative dependency is added.

Document History entries added to both `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md` and `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md` (both already carry the appendix).

**Mechanical companion changes** (required to keep `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` and `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` green, not part of the ruling itself):
- `draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md`'s `assessed-oauth-digest` marker re-pinned to core's new content hash (the digest tripwire the Mapping Assessment carries; only the marker line changed).
- `conformance-manifest.json`'s `source.specs` re-pinned for exactly the two files whose bytes changed (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md`), scoped to those two entries only.

## Coordination note (architecture file)

Another branch (`fix/708-substrate-neutrality`, tracking #708/#704) is expected to rework the architecture's "the bindings are peers of one another" paragraph (`draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md`, the paragraph beginning "The bindings are peers of one another..." near the Peer Standing area). This PR's architecture edit is scoped entirely to the **Token Classes** section (`{{token-classes}}`) and does not touch that paragraph, so the two branches should rebase/merge cleanly against each other as disjoint paragraphs in the same file. Recommended merge order: land this PR first, or land `fix/708-substrate-neutrality` first — either order should be conflict-free given the disjoint edit regions; this PR does not depend on that one.

No "Fresh review" ruling comment exists on issue #663 (checked via REST, GraphQL, and the issue timeline — zero comments). The issue body's own closing "Ruling:" sentence is the controlling text, and it already states the reconciliation verbatim (property vector as definition, Substrate Statement as evidence, core's gates as discharge), so this PR executes that text directly.
