comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Reviewed head `0a983ed1b725e204a2900d3c9f74788230e6f3b4` against issue #663, the exact six-condition property vector, Core conformance, the Substrate capability claims, and the adopted #702 claim-minimization ruling.

**Disposition: request changes.** Cross-referencing the three accounts is the right repair, but the PR currently declares them equivalent without resolving two substantive differences.

## P1 — The Core does not yet discharge condition 6 as written

The authoritative vector now requires an “auditable derivation link” and names an Issuance Grant `jti`, a **native issuance record**, cross-domain provenance, or an equivalent artifact ([architecture lines 2696–2713](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/0a983ed1b725e204a2900d3c9f74788230e6f3b4/draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md#L2696-L2713)). Core conformance, however, requires the approval anchors, subset rule, and lifecycle gate; it does not require the issuer to retain a per-credential issuance record or other audit artifact ([Core lines 4052–4123](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/0a983ed1b725e204a2900d3c9f74788230e6f3b4/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L4052-L4123)). The only nearby token-level audit behavior is an RS `SHOULD` log Mission id and token `jti`, which is not an issuer conformance gate.

The new prose nevertheless says Core “states its own discharge” of the six-condition property ([architecture lines 1741–1748](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/0a983ed1b725e204a2900d3c9f74788230e6f3b4/draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md#L1741-L1748)). A cross-reference cannot create the missing obligation.

Choose one explicit resolution:

1. If the signed JWT itself is intended to be the “equivalently specified artifact,” say so in condition 6 and explain how its `jti`, Mission reference, and carried authority form the derivation link without requiring retained server-side history; or
2. require and define a native issuer derivation record, including its token/grant identifier, Mission reference, authority projection, ordering/integrity, and retention, and add it to Core conformance.

Until one is done, call the accounts related but not equivalent and do not make the vector the authoritative definition.

## P1 — The authoritative definition conflicts with adopted #702

Condition 2 says the credential establishes the recorded `authority_hash` ([architecture lines 2699–2703](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/0a983ed1b725e204a2900d3c9f74788230e6f3b4/draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md#L2699-L2703)). The adopted #702 disposition makes the baseline token Mission reference exactly `{id, issuer}` and keeps Authority Set commitments on record/evidence surfaces; a bare token-carried digest is explicitly withdrawn as the baseline ([#702 disposition](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/issues/702#issuecomment-5398823360)).

Making this vector the definition now would mean a post-#702 conforming Core token can no longer earn `credential-mission-bound`. Resolve that coordination before this PR freezes the term. The durable property should require the canonical Mission identity plus an issuer-authenticated derivation from approved authority. A commitment or selective proof can strengthen that in a named verification/audit profile; it should not be an identity-field requirement on every credential.

## P2 — Map claims to conditions instead of saying “capability claims” generically

The new paragraph says a binding's Mission Substrate Statement capability claims are how it evidences the property, but it does not state which claims prove which of the six conditions. The nearby Token Classes paragraph names Lifecycle-Gated Authorization, Monotonic Derivation, and Credential-Bound, while the six-condition vector additionally depends on trusted issuer/controller, subject/client/actor context, lifetime, and the disputed audit link.

Add a compact condition-to-obligation mapping. In particular, distinguish `Credential-Bound`'s selectable fact semantics (which can be correlation-only under the Substrate contract) from the stronger `credential-mission-bound` architecture property. Otherwise a reader can still enter through the Substrate Statement and overread a generic capability claim—the ambiguity #663 was meant to close.

Editorially, call the numbered items “conditions,” not “six equivalence properties”; the table defines one property by six conditions.

Current-head reader and repository checks pass. The checks list also retains an older failed editor-copy run, followed by a passing rerun; I found no current-head build blocker.

comments.body:
Addressed in 692a2564. Per-point response:

**P1 — Core does not yet discharge condition 6 as written.**
Resolved by option 1 (name the artifact explicitly), refined: condition 6 now names the OAuth binding's **Mission Record** as the discharging artifact, not a bare "native issuance record" pointer or the token itself. The Mission Record is:
- REQUIRED and durable ("A Mission is the durable record created at the approval event," core `{{mission-record}}`),
- created at the same approval event Core's Mission Issuer conformance already requires (`{{approval-event}}`, `{{mission-record}}` cited together in the conformance bullet list), and
- retained under a MUST-level audit-horizon obligation ("the record MUST be retained for the audit horizon," core `{{mission-record}}`).

So this isn't a new Core obligation, it's a precise pointer to an existing one. The architecture text now states the mapping explicitly: "the same approval event's Mission Record, retained for the audit horizon, discharges condition 6." I did not add a new native issuer derivation record (option 2), since that would be new normative surface in Core beyond #663's cross-referencing scope.

**P1 — Conflict with adopted #702.**
Agreed and fixed directly: condition 2 is now Mission identity only, `{mission.issuer, mission.id}`, with an explicit note that this is "an identity condition only, never a token-carried Authority Set commitment." `authority_hash` no longer appears in condition 2. It's repositioned into condition 6 as an optional local-verifiability strengthener ("A token-carried Authority Set commitment, where a binding supplies one, strengthens this condition's local verifiability... it is never itself the Mission-identity requirement of condition 2, and its absence does not fail this condition where the issuer-retained record is otherwise reachable") — matching your framing exactly: "canonical Mission identity plus an issuer-authenticated derivation from approved authority... a commitment... can strengthen that... it should not be an identity-field requirement." A post-#702 conforming Core token (bare `{id, issuer}`, no `authority_hash`) can still earn `credential-mission-bound` under this text, since the Mission Record (server-side, per #702's own ruling: "the Authority Set commitment stays on the record") remains the derivation-link artifact regardless of what the token itself carries.

**P2 — Map claims to conditions.**
Added: condition 3 -> Monotonic Derivation, condition 5's active-state gate -> Lifecycle-Gated Authorization, conditions 1 and 4 -> issuer trust configuration and the credential's own subject/`client_id`/actor claims (not a Statement capability row at all), condition 6 -> the OAuth binding's Mission Record (Core-specific) or the other named artifacts (binding-general). Credential-Bound is called out specifically: its correlation-only fact semantics (Substrate `{{credential-bound}}`) "by itself evidences neither the derivation-link condition (6) nor the authority-projection condition (3)," and "a Credential-Bound claim alone, whatever semantics it selects, never by itself evidences `credential-mission-bound`."

**P2 — Editorial: "conditions" not "properties."**
Done, including the pre-existing "fails properties 3, 5, and 6" cross-reference, now "fails conditions 3, 5, and 6."

**Self-caught bug, disclosed:** my first attempt at the condition-to-Core-gate mapping cited Core's own local anchors (`{{approval-event}}`, `{{subset}}`, `{{lifecycle}}`) from inside architecture.md, where those anchors don't exist (they're Core-only headings) — a dangling cross-reference that a strict build would flag. Caught it before pushing by rebuilding architecture.md and checking the output for anchor-resolution issues; fixed by citing `{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission}}` once at the end of the sentence instead, matching this document's existing house style (no cross-doc anchor citations anywhere else in the family).

Checkers and build re-verified clean after this commit: `check-family-manifest.mjs`, `check-conformance-manifest.mjs`, `check-external-pins.mjs`, `check-bundle-manifest.mjs` all OK; `make draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.txt` builds clean with no anchor-resolution warnings. Core (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`) is untouched in this round, so its existing informative pointer and the prior commit's `source.specs`/`assessed-oauth-digest` re-pins stand unchanged.

pulls.title: README: verbs as the public front door, one link to the catalog
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #709.

## Ruling recap

#709's owner ruling (2026-08-24): verbs become the README's public front door; duplicate adoption tables are removed, not re-labeled; the full zone/track/group/package matrix moves behind one generated, linked catalog. Merge gate: a one-path walkthrough (verb, binding, minimum package, one link to the catalog), demonstrated before/after. Adoption-map validators in `check-family-manifest.mjs` move with the structure; the verb table keeps its per-mechanism spec links; manifest group/package metadata stays, no longer a peer entry point.

## The one-path walkthrough

**Before** (README.md at HEAD `59b958e5`): a reader choosing how to adopt the family had to triage **six** competing entry points before reaching a document list, several restating the same thing under a different axis:

1. "Start here" — three rings (model+binding / runtime-enforced / optional capabilities)
2. "You want to..." — an outcome table (7 rows, overlapping the verb table below it)
3. "The architecture, in verbs" — the verb table (the one the ruling wants kept)
4. "Choose a binding" — the binding table (the one the ruling wants kept)
5. "Choose an assurance outcome" — the four Mission Assurance Levels, restated from the Architecture
6. "Add capabilities by verb" — a closing paragraph pointing back at the verb table and `DRAFTS.md`

`DRAFTS.md` was linked three separate times across these sections (lines 202, 280, 340 at HEAD), diluting "one link out."

**After**, in `README.md`'s new "Find your path" section:

1. **Choose a verb** — the same 10-row verb table, unchanged, per-mechanism spec links intact (e.g. "Enforce Each Action" still links Runtime, AuthZEN, Transaction Authorization, Capability Binding).
2. **Choose a binding** — the same 4-row binding table, unchanged (OAuth AS / Standalone MAS / AAuth / UMA+GNAP).
3. **See the minimum package** — new, generated:
   ```
   | Binding | Minimum package |
   | Mission-Bound Authorization for OAuth 2.0 | 1 document: itself alone |
   | Mission Authority Server | 4 documents: Mission Substrate Requirements + Mission-Bound Authorization for OAuth 2.0 + Mission Status and Lifecycle for OAuth 2.0 + Mission Authority Server |
   | Mission Context Binding for AAuth | 2 documents: Mission Substrate Requirements + Mission Context Binding for AAuth |
   | Mission-Bound Authorization for UMA 2.0 | 2 documents: Mission Substrate Requirements + Mission-Bound Authorization for UMA 2.0 |
   | Mission-Bound Authorization for GNAP | 2 documents: Mission Substrate Requirements + Mission-Bound Authorization for GNAP |
   ```
   Example path: reader picks **Enforce Each Action** -> picks **OAuth AS** -> sees "1 document: itself alone" -> clicks through.
4. **Go to the catalog** — exactly one link, to `DRAFTS.md`, carrying forward the two easy-to-miss pointers (work-product commitment model, swarm ladder) and the Mission Handbook link.

Line count: README.md 410 -> 356 lines (net removal, not a relabeling).

## What moved vs. what was deleted

Nothing normative left the corpus:
- The four Mission Assurance Levels and their two named claims (agent-compromise-resistant enforcement, trifecta containment) are already defined in full, with proof obligations, in `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md` `{#assurance-levels}` (lines 2345-2557); the README table was a compressed duplicate. The "never the wire alone" epistemics point survives in substance in the Architecture's Deployment Profile section (`{#deployment-profile}`, `residual_risks`, lines 2829-2841).
- The four cumulative reference stacks are unchanged in `family-manifest.json`'s `reference_stacks` and validated by check (g), independent of this PR.
- Manifest `group`/`package` metadata is untouched; `family-manifest.json` has zero diff in this PR.
- The "You want to..." table's rows are all subsumed by the verb table (e.g. "Build a PEP or PDP" == "Enforce Each Action"; "Review threats and trust" == "Analyze").

Reachable via the "Analyze" verb row -> Architecture, or via the one catalog link -> `DRAFTS.md` -> Architecture entry.

## Validator-migration summary

**The interlock premise needs a correction, not a silent pass.** I checked `check-family-manifest.mjs` at HEAD before writing anything: check (m)'s own header says *"README's structure is otherwise unvalidated: it is curated prose"* (three generic rules: links `DRAFTS.md`/`DEPENDENCIES.md`, backticked `draft-*` tokens are real slugs, editor's-copy links are real slugs), and check (o)'s comment already describes "the placement semantics **the retired README adoption map** used to carry" as living in `DRAFTS.md`'s group sections. There was no "adoption order," "adoption-map matrix," or "menu prose claims" validator left at HEAD to move. So this PR is a **net addition** of machine-checking, not a relocation of an existing one, flagging this explicitly since a reviewer holding the task text could otherwise read the PR as having skipped the interlock.

What I did add, because this PR introduces the first generated content inside README.md itself:

- **New check (u) `binding-packages`** in `check-family-manifest.mjs`: the README's "Minimum package" block must exactly match what the manifest computes (same shape as check (l) for `DRAFTS.md`'s index), and every slug in `BINDING_SLUGS` must be a real manifest draft.
- **`BINDING_SLUGS` is derived, not a second hardcoded list.** It's `check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s `REGISTRY.map(e => e.slug)`, the family's own definition of "binding" is exactly "has published a Mission Substrate Statement capability table," and that file's existing tripwires already fail CI the moment a table appears anywhere in the corpus unregistered. A sixth binding cannot land without this list picking it up.
- `check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s `REGISTRY` is now `export`ed and its validation body is wrapped in a guarded `main()` (same pattern as `generate-drafts-index.mjs`) so importing `REGISTRY` has no side effect; direct invocation (`node scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs`, and the subprocess chain from `check-family-manifest.mjs`) is behavior-identical (verified: same "5 Statements, 8 consumer tables validated" output before and after).
- `generate-drafts-index.mjs` gained `adoptionClosure()` (transitive closure over `adoption_requires`, cycle-detecting), `renderBindingPackages()`/`spliceBindingPackages()`/`validateBindingPackages()`, and now regenerates/checks **two** marker blocks (`DRAFTS.md`'s index, README's binding-packages), reusing a generalized `spliceMarkedBlock()` helper.
- Corrected two stale comments and one stale doc line rather than leaving them wrong: check (m)'s "structure is otherwise unvalidated" now names the one exception; `generate-drafts-index.mjs`'s header now says it manages two files; README's own "Repository use" section (which describes the checker's rules to readers) now lists four rules instead of three and mentions the new block. Script is not renamed (CI and the `check-family-manifest.mjs` import reference it by name).

**Mutation tests run** (each applied then reverted via `diff`-verified restore, repo left clean):
1. Hand-edited one cell of the generated README block ("1 document" -> "2 documents") -> `check-family-manifest.mjs` failed with `[binding-packages] README.md's generated binding-packages block is stale`.
2. Pointed one `REGISTRY` entry's `slug` at a nonexistent draft -> failed with `[binding-packages] BINDING_SLUGS ... names "draft-mcguinness-mission-gnap-does-not-exist", which is not a family-manifest.json draft slug`.
3. Added an unregistered `{: title="Rogue Mission substrate capabilities"}` line to a random draft -> `check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s pre-existing tripwire failed with `[statement-unregistered]`, confirming a 6th binding can't silently bypass `BINDING_SLUGS`.

All green after each revert: `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`, `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` (519 requirements, unchanged), `node scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs --check`.

## One deliberate structural note

The "Find your path" section uses one `##` heading with four `###` substeps, the first H2/H3 nesting in this README (every other section is flat `##`). Chosen deliberately so the four-step structure the acceptance test names is visually literal, not just a claim in prose; flagging it as a design call rather than a silent deviation.

## Deviations from the literal task text

- The task's "extend `scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs` ... rather than hand-writing tables" is implemented as a **new** marker-delimited block inside `README.md` (not inside `DRAFTS.md`), because the acceptance test requires the minimum package to be visible on the README path before the one link out, not one hop further in.
- `BINDING_SLUGS` lives in `generate-drafts-index.mjs` but is sourced from `check-substrate-statements.mjs`, a file the task didn't name. This was a deliberate choice over a second hardcoded list, made after finding that registry already exists as the family's authoritative "what is a binding" source.

## Not in scope / out of scope confirmed

- No changes to `family-manifest.json` (presentation only, per the ruling).
- No changes to `src/PLAN.md`.
- No merge to `main`; independent of the other draft PRs in this wave, no merge-order constraint.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Review of `fb62b3217a8bff361583d8781df2a5f1de4ba4a3` against base `59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f` and the owner ruling on #709.

**Disposition: changes requested.** The verb table is the right survivor and the generated adoption-closure code is sound on the current manifest, but the resulting README still does not meet the ruling's “public front door / one short path / one catalog link” reader test.

### P1 — The verbs are still halfway through the README, not the front door

`Find your path` begins at [line 186](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/fb62b3217a8bff361583d8781df2a5f1de4ba4a3/README.md#L186-L200) of a 356-line README. A new reader must first traverse the four-object model, token claim, end-to-end walkthrough, exclusions, standards proposal, minimal implementation, and adjacent-protocol table. That is still a long conceptual funnel before the supposedly primary navigation.

Move the verb path immediately after the short Mission definition (roughly after current line 21, or after one compact model paragraph). The detailed walkthrough, non-goals, standardization story, and composition material can follow the path or move behind the catalog/Architecture links. This preserves the distinctive verbs while making them the actual first adoption choice.

### P1 — There are still two links presenting `DRAFTS.md` as the complete catalog

Step 4 gives the intended single catalog exit at [lines 271–283](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/fb62b3217a8bff361583d8781df2a5f1de4ba4a3/README.md#L271-L283), but Status repeats `DRAFTS.md — the complete document catalog` at [lines 297–309](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/fb62b3217a8bff361583d8781df2a5f1de4ba4a3/README.md#L297-L309). That fails the owner ruling's one-link exit literally and recreates a second navigation cluster immediately below the new path.

Keep the Step 4 catalog link and make Status purely status (Datatracker/current maturity caveat), or fold the dependency/conformance/manifest operational links under Repository use without repeating the catalog.

### P2 — The linked catalog does not expose the full adoption organization claimed by the ruling

The generated `DRAFTS.md` index still contains only `Document / Maturity / Verbs / Summary / Pull this in when` ([generator lines 70–86](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/fb62b3217a8bff361583d8781df2a5f1de4ba4a3/scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs#L70-L86)). Group placement remains in hand-authored headings, and the generated catalog does not show package/reference-stack organization. If #709's “full zone/track/group/package matrix behind one generated catalog” is still the acceptance rule, either add the relevant generated grouping/package view to `DRAFTS.md`, or amend the wording to the narrower result this PR actually delivers: a generated exhaustive document index plus a generated README binding closure.

Validation performed: `generate-drafts-index.mjs --check` passes; `check-conformance-manifest.mjs` passes (519 requirements); the binding closures match `adoption_requires`, including cycle/unknown-slug failure behavior. `check-family-manifest.mjs` reached only the expected archive-snapshot limitation because the isolated review tree lacks the historic bundle commit, not a PR finding.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Pushed `338cdc88` addressing every point in the review. Per-point resolution below, then the updated walkthrough.

## P1 — "verbs are still halfway through the README"

**Fixed by relocation, not by cutting content.** `## Find your path` now starts at line 36, immediately after the title, the two-paragraph Mission definition, and the four-object list (lines 3-34: the "one compact model paragraph" the review offered as the cut point, extended slightly to include the object list because the verb table's "The question" column leans on those four terms — Intent/Mission/Authority/Action). Nothing was deleted: the derivation/revocation paragraph, the "delegated-authority layer" framing, and the wire-claim JSON example (previously unheaded body text between the object list and "One Mission, end to end") now sit under a new `## The mechanics` heading, positioned after the path. The walkthrough, non-goals, standardization story, minimal-implementation, and composition table all keep their original relative order, just after the path instead of before it.

New order: title → model (34 lines) → **Find your path** → The mechanics → One Mission, end to end → What a Mission is not → The standards proposal → The minimal implementation → Composes with what you already run → Running code → Status → Repository use.

## P1 — "two links presenting DRAFTS.md as the complete catalog"

**Fixed.** `## Status` is now purely status: the Datatracker sentence and the maturity-vocabulary note, no bullet list, no `DRAFTS.md` link. `DEPENDENCIES.md`, `conformance-manifest.json`, and `family-manifest.json` moved to `## Repository use` as "operational references," explicitly framed as not the catalog. I also caught and fixed a second-order version of the same bug during self-review: my first draft of that Repository-use paragraph said "the catalog is one link away, see step 4" but then linkified `DRAFTS.md` again in the same sentence — technically a second `href` to the same target even while the prose disclaimed it. Fixed to a plain, unlinked `` `DRAFTS.md` `` mention. Verified: `grep -oE "\]\(DRAFTS\.md\)" README.md | wc -l` → `1`.

## P2 — "the linked catalog does not expose the full adoption organization"

**Fixed with generated content, per the first option offered, not the wording amendment.** Two additions, both computed from `family-manifest.json`, both freshness-checked in CI (never hand-typed, can't drift):

1. **Group**: `generate-drafts-index.mjs`'s main index gains a `Group` column. The section-title map (`GROUP_SECTION_TITLES`) used to render it is now the *same* map `check-family-manifest.mjs`'s check (o) uses to verify DRAFTS.md's `###` sections — moved to the generator and imported by the checker, so the two can no longer name a group differently.
2. **Reference stacks (assurance levels)**: a new generated table in `DRAFTS.md`, "## Reference stacks," computed by walking each stack's `contains`/`adds` chain in `family-manifest.json`'s `reference_stacks` object into a cumulative document list per level (Baseline Issuance: 1 doc; Runtime-Enforced: 4; Governed Agent: 6; High-Assurance Agent: 6, same set as Governed Agent since it adds no new documents, only named claims). New check (v) `catalog-stacks` validates it against the manifest, same shape as (l) and (u).

**Dispute, narrow**: I did not add a *package* view, and I'm flagging that as a disagreement rather than a silent gap. `family-manifest.json`'s own comment and this repo's pre-existing (untouched by this PR) Repository-use paragraph both state the Architecture's five packages are "not restated here," predating #709. That's a standing editorial decision about a different axis (the Architecture's own orthogonal decomposition of *itself*, not a document-selection axis), not something #709's ruling asked this PR to reverse. I surfaced it explicitly in both `DRAFTS.md`'s new section intro and README's Step 4 ("deliberately not restated anywhere in this repository") instead of quietly matching the original overclaim or quietly expanding scope. If the ruling intended packages in scope too, that's a call for the owner, not something I should decide unilaterally mid-review-response.

"Zone/track": these aren't present in `family-manifest.json`'s current schema at all (only `groups`, `verbs`, `maintenance_classes`, `reference_stacks`, `drafts`) — nothing to expose because there's nothing there to lose. Noting this so it doesn't read as an unaddressed gap.

## Updated walkthrough

**Before this round** (verb path at old line 186 of 356): a reader hit six sections of conceptual/positioning prose — the four-object model, the wire-claim JSON, the "One Mission, end to end" worked example, "What a Mission is not," "The standards proposal," "The minimal implementation," and the composition table — before reaching any navigation at all. `DRAFTS.md` was linked twice (Step 4, and Status).

**After this round**: line 36 of 374, right after:
```
## Find your path

One path, four steps: choose a verb, choose a binding, see the
minimum document package that binding needs, then go to the complete
catalog for everything else. Nothing below duplicates anything
above it.
```
Concrete path, same example as before: reader picks **Enforce Each Action** (step 1) → **OAuth AS** (step 2) → sees:
```
| Mission-Bound Authorization for OAuth 2.0 | 1 document: itself alone |
```
(step 3, unchanged, still generated from `adoption_requires`) → step 4's one link, `DRAFTS.md`, which (new this round) itself now shows, generated: every document's `Group` in the main index, and a "Reference stacks" table mapping Baseline Issuance → 1 doc, Runtime-Enforced → 4, Governed Agent → 6, High-Assurance Agent → 6.

`grep -oE "\]\(DRAFTS\.md\)" README.md | wc -l` → **1**. Total `DRAFTS.md` link count across the whole page (Status excluded, it no longer mentions the file): **1**.

## Validation

```
node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs        # OK: 41 drafts, no drift (checks a-v, including new (v))
node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs   # OK: 519 requirements, unchanged
node scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs --check # OK: DRAFTS.md's two blocks + README's one block, current
```

Mutation-tested this round: corrupted one cell of the new reference-stacks table → check (v) failed as `[catalog-stacks] DRAFTS.md's generated reference-stacks block is stale`; corrupted one Group-column cell in the main index → failed as `[drafts-index] DRAFTS.md's generated index block is stale`. Both reverted, repo verified clean, both re-runs green.

No `family-manifest.json` or `src/PLAN.md` changes (confirmed via `git diff --stat` against both, empty).

Rebased `docs/709-verbs-front-door` onto latest `main` (`a6093315`, which includes PR #718's 42nd draft, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access`) and force-pushed (`338cdc88` → `a875c341`, `--force-with-lease` verified against the actual remote SHA before pushing).

pulls.title: cross-domain: destination-local client_id identifies the redeeming client (S-12)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #650

## Summary

Applies the S-12 ruling (owner comment, 2026-08-24, property-level MUST):
the destination-local credential MUST identify the redeeming destination
client per the destination's own conventions (`client_id` where RFC
9068-style JWT local tokens are used); origin identity travels exclusively
via the Origin Principal members, never as the local client identity.

- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.md`: restated the Resource
  AS's local-token client identification (Validation at the Resource AS)
  as this property-level requirement, naming `client_id` as the RFC 9068
  case, and cross-referenced the Origin Principal profile's `mission.subject`
  as the exclusive carrier of origin identity. Document History entry added.
- `src/services/ras`: `RasConfig` gains a required `localClientId` (the
  RAS's own client registration; it has no separate client-authentication
  model, per the accepted S-12 deviation). `redeem()` stamps it as the
  minted local token's `client_id`, composed alongside the existing
  `mission`/`authorization_details`/`cnf` claims without touching the
  `mission` destructure #539 stage-B will extend. The ID-JAG grant's own
  `client_id` claim (the originating agent, ID-JAG §3.1) is never copied
  into this slot -- confirmed by tracing `cnf.jkt`/`presenterJkt`, which is
  the same DPoP key as the grant's, so a key-derived value would have
  smuggled origin identity back in; a fixed destination-local config value
  is the correct namespace.
- `src/config/topology.json` + `packages/demo-data`: added `rasLocalClientId`
  to the typed topology, wired into the demo stack and all five
  `ResourceAuthorizationServer` constructions (1 demo, 4 tests).
- Tests: a dedicated positive/negative test in
  `services/mcp-saas/test/cross-domain.test.ts` (client_id equals the
  destination's registration; never the grant's client_id or the presenter
  key), plus client_id assertions added to the existing end-to-end
  continuation redemption test in
  `services/authorization-server/test/continuation-grant.test.ts`.
- Conformance: new `conformance-manifest.json` row
  `cross-domain.resource-as.client-id-identifies-redeemer` (tested, mapped
  to both new/updated tests); `source.specs` re-pinned. `SPEC_VERSIONS.md`
  cross-domain row re-pinned (`dc7a897` -> `15810598`) with the fix named
  in Surfaces and the new test file added to Tests.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --build` -- clean, no errors
- [x] `pnpm vitest run services/mcp-saas/test/cross-domain.test.ts services/authorization-server/test/continuation-grant.test.ts` -- 23 passed
- [x] `pnpm vitest run` (full workspace) -- 929 passed, 120 skipped (pre-existing skips), 0 failed
- [x] `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` -- OK, 520 requirements (133 tested, 53 partial, 331 todo, 3 blocked); `--collect` shows only pre-existing, unrelated failures (verified identical set present on the pre-change baseline)

## Deviations / notes

- No client-authentication model was added at the RAS (the accepted S-12
  deviation, "a full fix needs a client-registration model at the RAS,"
  stays as-is). The owner's ruling scoped this to the property-level MUST,
  not full client authentication, so `localClientId` is a fixed
  destination-local config value rather than a per-client registry lookup.
  This is a truthful minimal registration for a demo with exactly one
  redeeming client; it does not yet distinguish multiple destination
  clients.
- `src/PLAN.md` untouched per standing instruction; its S-12 entry (line
  ~1337) is now stale and should be updated by whoever's turn it is to
  touch that file next.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review of head `c37dd584` against base `59b958e5`.

**Disposition: changes requested. The specification change is sound, but the implementation and conformance claim do not yet satisfy it.**

### P1 — `localClientId` is asserted, not authenticated

The new normative text requires the local token to identify “the party that authenticated at redemption.” The RAS still has no destination-client authentication or registration binding. `redeem(idJag, presenterJkt)` checks only that `presenterJkt` equals the origin-issued grant's `cnf.jkt`; it then stamps one global `cfg.localClientId` into every local token. Nothing proves that this key belongs to that destination-local client, and a trusted origin AS can issue a valid grant to any presenter key while the destination token will still call it `ledgercloud-ras-redeemer`.

This is not merely an acknowledged demo limitation: it contradicts the property the new `MUST` states and makes the new conformance row's `coverage: tested` false. The tests prove only that a configured constant was copied and that it differs from two origin values; they never authenticate a destination client or bind the output identifier to the authenticated principal.

Please use one of these shapes:

1. authenticate the destination client at redemption and pass the resulting destination-local principal into minting; or
2. for the deliberately single-client demo, configure a registration that binds `localClientId` to an accepted client credential/key and verify that binding during redemption.

Then add negatives showing that a different authenticated destination client/key cannot receive a token naming the configured client, and that a valid origin grant plus its PoP key is insufficient to select or impersonate the destination-local identity. If the implementation remains constant-only for now, mark the conformance row `partial` and describe the missing authentication seam rather than claiming this `MUST` is tested.

### P2 — Keep the origin-carriage sentence precisely scoped

The added sentence says origin identity travels “only” through `mission.subject`, but the base ID-JAG still carries origin-side `client_id` before redemption, and the Origin Principal profile is optional. What is true here is narrower: origin principal identity, **when the Origin Principal profile is claimed**, is conveyed to the local token/consumer through `mission.subject`; the ID-JAG's origin `client_id` must never be reinterpreted as the destination-local `client_id`. Please condition the sentence accordingly so it does not imply that the base profile always carries `mission.subject` or that no origin identity exists elsewhere on the grant.

Once the authenticated-principal binding and conformance status are corrected, the destination/origin namespace separation itself is the right rule.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed both points on `fix/650-redeeming-client-identity` (commits `d8c5b459`, `9536447a`).

## P1 — `localClientId` was asserted, not authenticated

Agreed in full; this was a real gap, not a style nit. Fixed by actually authenticating the redeeming client rather than stamping a constant:

- `src/services/ras`: `RasConfig.localClientId` (a config constant) is replaced by `registeredClients`, a `jkt -> client_id` table that IS this RAS's client registration (the same shape as `private_key_jwt` or DPoP-bound client credentials). `redeem()` looks up the proven presenter `jkt` in this table *after* sender-constraint verification and *before* `jti` consumption, and throws a new `RasError("invalid_client", ...)` on a miss. A valid, sender-constrained origin grant is no longer sufficient on its own to select or impersonate a destination-local identity: the RAS's own registration decides, independent of anything the origin AS asserted. A `registerClient()` method onboards a client whose key is generated after RAS construction, which this demo needs since the agent's DPoP key is generated per session (`exhibit.ts` now calls it once the key exists, before any redemption; every test's setup does the same).
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.md`: added an explicit Resource AS requirement (new bullet, Validation at the Resource AS) to authenticate the redeeming client at redemption and refuse `invalid_client` on failure, stating plainly that the grant's sender-constraint alone does not satisfy it. The `client_id` bullet now grounds in "the client identity established by that authentication" rather than an unauthenticated redemption party. Conformance section gained the matching bullet.
- Negatives added, both in `services/mcp-saas/test/cross-domain.test.ts`:
  - an unregistered presenter key, presented with a perfectly valid, sender-constrained origin grant, is refused `invalid_client`;
  - two distinct *registered* destination clients (two keys, two `registerClient()` entries) each redeem their own grants and each receive their own `client_id`, never the other's and never the grant's origin `client_id`.
- `conformance-manifest.json`: split the one row into two, matching the two distinct MUSTs (`cross-domain.resource-as.authenticates-redeeming-client`, new; `cross-domain.resource-as.client-id-identifies-redeemer`, updated). Both `coverage: tested`, mapped to the tests above. This is now an honest `tested` claim, not a copied-constant one.

## P2 — origin-carriage sentence over-scoped

Agreed. Reworded: it no longer claims origin identity travels "only" through `mission.subject` unconditionally. Now:
- conditioned on the Origin Principal profile being claimed ("Where the Origin Principal profile is claimed, that approved agent's origin principal is instead conveyed to the local token through `mission.subject`; otherwise the approved agent remains recoverable only at the originating AS..."), and
- separately, unconditionally, under any profile: "the cross-domain grant's own `client_id` claim MUST NOT be reinterpreted as this local identifier."

This drops the implication that the base profile always carries `mission.subject` or that no origin identity exists elsewhere on the grant, while keeping the one thing that's true under every profile: the grant's own `client_id` never becomes the local one.

## Test results (full branch state, head `9536447a`)

- `pnpm exec tsc --build`: clean, no errors
- `pnpm vitest run services/mcp-saas/test/cross-domain.test.ts services/authorization-server/test/continuation-grant.test.ts`: 25 passed (23 prior + 2 new negatives)
- `pnpm vitest run` (full workspace): 931 passed, 120 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 521 requirements (134 tested, 53 partial, 331 todo, 3 blocked)
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs --collect`: 85 findings, identical set to the pre-change baseline (verified by re-running on the base commit); none reference this PR's two rows or test files
- `node src/scripts/check-spec-versions.mjs`: OK, STRICT_SPECS clean
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.txt`: builds clean (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc-txt both OK)

No disputes; both points were correct as raised. Ready for another pass.

pulls.title: discovery: state the harness taint-duty degradation as a conformance note (#664)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Executes #664's ruling. The issue posed a choice: raise the harness's taint floor conditionally for discovery-adopting deployments, or have discovery state the degradation explicitly as a conformance note. This PR implements the **conformance-note** option, in `draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.md`'s Security Considerations, right after the existing "Injection-driven discovery" residual bullet.

## Why the conformance-note option

I verified whether `draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md` already has a conditional-upgrade mechanism keyed to discovery adoption that the other option could just reuse. It does have a conditional-upgrade mechanism — the opt-in PDP-enforced taint path (`{{decision-api-composition}}`), which carries real MUSTs — but it's gated on the deployment's Enforcement Scope Statement declaring PDP-enforced taint, not on whether the deployment adopts discovery. There is no existing "discovery-adopted" signal in harness's own conformance structure, so raising harness's floor conditionally on discovery adoption would require inventing a new cross-draft coupling: harness's conformance bar depending on whether a separate document is adopted. That is exactly the kind of coupling the family avoids elsewhere (core-stands-alone / no cross-draft normative dependencies; substrate's standalone-adoptable-kernel posture).

The conformance-note option keeps each draft's bar self-contained: discovery already has the MUST-level fail-safe ("MUST treat a missing, stale, or unverifiable taint state as tainted"), and the new note simply makes visible what was previously implicit — that a conforming harness meeting only its SHOULD-level duties still satisfies discovery's adjudication, at the cost of routing more encounters to a human (or refusing them) than a MUST-level harness would. No new requirement is added on either document; harness.md is untouched.

`draft-mcguinness-mission-harness.md` has no Document History appendix yet (confirmed: no `# Document History` heading), so no entry was added there per the "appendix added by touch" convention; discovery's existing appendix got the new entry.

## Deviation note

No "Fresh review" ruling comment exists on issue #664 (checked via REST, GraphQL, and the issue timeline — zero comments). The issue body poses the choice but does not resolve it. This PR makes and documents that call rather than inventing a ruling comment that doesn't exist; the reasoning above is the basis for picking the conformance-note option.

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — OK (41 drafts, no drift)
- [x] `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — OK (519 requirements, no drift; no new row needed since no new externally testable requirement is added)
- [x] `node scripts/check-external-pins.mjs` — OK
- [x] `node scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs` — OK
- [x] `make draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.txt` — builds clean
- [x] No em-dashes introduced; house style (timeless prose) followed
- [x] Independent branch from `main`, not stacked on the #663 PR

Refs #664

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fresh review of head `9ccbaddc` against base `59b958e5`.

**Disposition: no architectural blocker; one precision fix is needed before merge.** The selected #664 option is legitimate: Discovery can own and disclose the degradation without making Harness conformance depend normatively on adopting a separate profile.

### P2 — The note overstates what a conforming SHOULD-level harness supplies

“A harness meeting only the SHOULD-level duties still supplies a taint state this document's adjudication accepts” is not guaranteed. A `SHOULD` may be omitted for a documented valid reason, and the two cited duties have different effects:

- absent or coarse provenance can produce a coarse session-level taint state, or no trustworthy state; Discovery handles the latter as tainted and routes/refuses;
- the harness's SHOULD-level egress response is an execution control, not the source or authenticity of Discovery's taint input.

Please state the degradation in terms of the actual cases instead: a trustworthy but coarse report increases human routing; a missing, stale, or unverifiable report is treated as tainted and also routes/refuses; this note does not strengthen the harness's post-binding egress enforcement. That avoids implying that every conforming harness necessarily emits an acceptable report, and it keeps Discovery's safe default separate from the residual risk of a harness that does not implement the SHOULD-level egress response.

Suggested replacement for the final four sentences:

> A deployment whose harness supplies only coarse session-level taint can still satisfy this profile, but more encounters route to a human or are refused. A missing, stale, or unverifiable report is treated as tainted under the rule above; it is not an untainted report. This profile does not strengthen the harness's separate SHOULD-level post-binding egress response. The degradation is therefore explicit: less precise taint information reduces policy binding, while weaker harness egress enforcement remains a separately disclosed residual.

No new conformance row is needed if this remains explanatory text and introduces no new requirement.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed in b6846843. Precision fix per the review, adopting your suggested replacement text almost verbatim:

**P2 — Overstates what a conforming SHOULD-level harness necessarily supplies.**

Replaced the flagged sentences. The note now states the two cases separately instead of one blanket "a harness meeting only the SHOULD-level duties still supplies a taint state this document's adjudication accepts" claim:

- "A deployment whose harness supplies only coarse session-level taint can still satisfy this profile, but more encounters route to a human or are refused." (trustworthy-but-coarse case)
- "A missing, stale, or unverifiable report is treated as tainted under the rule above; it is not an untainted report." (the existing MUST-level fail-safe, unchanged, restated for clarity)
- "This profile does not strengthen the harness's separate SHOULD-level post-binding egress response." (the residual you called out: harness's own execution-control duty is not what this note is about)
- "The degradation is therefore explicit: less precise taint information reduces policy binding, while weaker harness egress enforcement remains a separately disclosed residual."

I kept one lead-in sentence ("The harness's duties to track parameter-level provenance and to gate egress on tainted content are SHOULD-level, outside its opt-in PDP-enforced taint path") to preserve the paragraph's opening context established in the prior commit; it makes no strength claim on its own and isn't part of what was flagged.

Also updated the matching Document History bullet, which had the same overstatement.

Re-verified: `make draft-mcguinness-mission-discovery.txt` builds clean; `check-family-manifest.mjs`, `check-conformance-manifest.mjs`, `check-external-pins.mjs`, `check-bundle-manifest.mjs` all OK. Still explanatory text only, no new conformance row, per your note that none is needed as long as it stays that way.

pulls.title: core: three-role approval model, adjudication object (#701)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #701

## Summary

Implements the session disposition on #701 (the three-role model superseding the earlier two-role proposal): `consent_principal` (accountability root), `activation_actor` (who/what triggered the instance), and a new discriminated `adjudication` object (what decided the instance).

- `approval_basis.adjudication` (REQUIRED): a discriminated object with `kind` (`human`, `policy`, or `agr`).
  - `kind: human` (the `direct` default): no further members; the deciding human is `consent_principal`.
  - `kind: policy`: names the deciding policy/workflow's `id` and `version`, plus an OPTIONAL `evidence` reference.
  - `kind: agr`: no further members; the Approval Governance Record retained under the Mission's `approval_event_id` carries the decision, including any multi-assertion set, never flattened into one principal.
- New **Role Mapping** table (`{{role-mapping}}`) covering direct approval, relocated human approval, Template dispatch, policy drawdown, and AGR-backed approval, with direct as the degenerate one-human case that does not define the model.
- Top-level `approver` is now DEPRECATED as a compatibility alias for `approval_basis.consent_principal` (normatively equal to it); its removal is parked to the #705 breaking-change window, not this PR.
- `activation_actor`'s trigger/requester meaning is unchanged.
- Verified the principal-model vs. record contradiction the review flagged (Overview's Principal Model text vs. the record's human-accountable invariant) was already resolved on `main`; added a forward cross-reference to `adjudication` instead of re-deriving the fix.
- The human-root invariant (every source traces to an accountable human) is retained unchanged.
- One-line cross-references added to `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.md` (activation_actor is never the instance's adjudicator) and `draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.md` (this record backs `adjudication.kind: agr`); their construction algorithms are otherwise untouched.
- `draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md`'s OAuth Mapping Assessment `assessed-oauth-digest` marker re-pinned (mechanical; re-read the assessment, no claim it makes is affected).
- `conformance-manifest.json`: four new `todo` rows for the adjudication rules, `source.specs` re-pinned for the three edited spec files that already carry rows.
- Document History entry added to core.

## Deviations from a literal reading of the brief

- Item 5 ("reconcile the principal-model contradiction") was already fixed on `main` by an intervening editorial pass before this branch was cut; this PR only adds a cross-reference there rather than re-doing the fix.
- Companions beyond `template.md`/`approval-governance.md` (e.g. `child-delegation.md`'s `policy_drawdown`, `uma.md`, `gnap.md`) are not updated to emit `adjudication` in this PR, per the explicit "core-centered... surgical only" scope. Core states the general MUST for companion profiles; propagation to each companion's construction algorithm is left for follow-up. Flagging this so it isn't lost.
- `feat/637-resource-access-profile` does not exist yet (issue #637 is open, unstarted), so there is nothing to rebase onto now; this note preserves the requested merge-after ordering for whenever that branch lands.

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — OK (523 requirements, incl. 4 new `todo`)
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — OK (41 drafts, no drift)
- `node scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs` — OK
- `node scripts/check-external-pins.mjs` — OK
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.txt draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.txt` — all build clean

## Note

Touches core (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`). Please merge this **after** `feat/637-resource-access-profile` lands, rebasing if needed.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Reviewed head `4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217` against the adopted three-role ruling in #701 and the Core, Template, Child Delegation, Approval Governance, and GNAP construction paths.

**Disposition: request changes.** The three-role split is correct, but making `approval_basis.adjudication` REQUIRED before all Mission constructors emit it makes the family internally nonconformant.

## P1 — Propagate the REQUIRED member atomically

Core now requires `approval_basis.adjudication` on every Mission ([lines 2664–2688](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2664-L2688)) and requires each standing-consent profile to populate it ([lines 2715–2723](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2715-L2723)). But the companion constructors still enumerate complete `approval_basis` objects without the new member:

- Template dispatch lists `type`, `consent_principal`, `activation`, `activation_actor`, and `root_commitment`, but no `adjudication` ([Template lines 475–500](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-template.md#L475-L500)); its conformance list is likewise incomplete.
- Child Delegation constructs both `direct` and `policy_drawdown` bases without the member ([Child Delegation lines 1019–1051](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation.md#L1019-L1051)).
- GNAP calls out the complete standing basis as “type, consent principal, root commitment, activation, and activation actor,” which becomes false after this change ([GNAP lines 628–637](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f/draft-mcguinness-mission-gnap.md#L628-L637)).

The PR body explicitly leaves this propagation for follow-up, but a follow-up is too late for a new REQUIRED record member. Either update every normative constructor, example, conformance list, and implementation path in this PR, or introduce the member as optional during a defined migration and make it required only when the family-wide cut lands.

For Template, specify the exact mapping: `adjudication.policy` should name the recorded Dispatch Policy `id` and `version`; the Template identity/version and `template_hash` already belong to activation/root provenance. The role table currently says it names the template and version while also saying the Dispatch Policy adjudicated ([Core lines 2837–2843](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2837-L2843)), leaving two possible values for one field.

## P1 — Do not use the lifecycle-state compatibility rule for an adjudication discriminator

`adjudication.kind` is said to be subject to the forward-compatibility rule of the lifecycle section ([lines 2670–2672](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2670-L2672)). That rule is specifically “only exact `active` permits reliance; every other state is non-active.” It does not define how an immutable provenance object handles an unknown discriminator. Applying it here is undefined and risks readers treating an unknown adjudication kind as a lifecycle denial.

Give this union its own rule. For example: preserve unknown kinds on an otherwise valid Mission record, do not infer an adjudicator from them, and reject them only on a profile operation that requires recognized adjudication semantics. The existing `approval_basis.type` reference to the lifecycle rule has the same category error and can be corrected in this touch.

## P2 — Keep the discriminator semantic and make evidence a typed seam

`human` and `policy` describe decision mechanisms, while `agr` describes where richer governance evidence is stored. The AGR itself contains assertions plus an evaluation; it is not the deciding actor. Making `agr` override either semantic kind loses whether the recorded evaluation was human- or policy-adjudicated. Prefer either:

- a semantic discriminator plus an optional typed governance-record reference; or
- a record-reference discriminator whose name makes clear that detailed adjudication is delegated to that record.

Also, `policy.evidence` is currently an untyped “reference ... shaped by the policy or companion profile that owns it” ([lines 2678–2682](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4210f4223007929a23e810f81060de76285e7217/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2678-L2682)). That is an open-ended grab-bag inside what is presented as a discriminated Core schema. Define a typed reference (`type` plus profile-owned members and collision rules), reuse a family evidence-reference type, or omit it from Core and let the owning companion add its declared extension.

The separation of `consent_principal`, `activation_actor`, and adjudication, plus deprecating rather than immediately removing `approver`, is otherwise the right architecture.

All current-head CI checks shown on the PR are green (reader build, editor copy, and repository checks).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Addressed at 3a9b79fa. Per point:

## P1 — Propagate the REQUIRED member atomically

Went with your second option: `approval_basis.adjudication` is now **OPTIONAL**, not REQUIRED, with an explicit migration path — a future breaking-change window (the same one already tracked for the `approver` alias's removal) MAY promote it to REQUIRED once every Mission-creating profile populates it.

While auditing every constructor to decide this, I found a **fourth** one neither of us had named: `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-progressive`'s `ceiling_drawdown` basis also builds a complete `approval_basis` without `adjudication`. UMA, MAS (authority-server), Expansion, and Deferred Approval do *not* construct `approval_basis` at all — they either don't touch it or ride the ordinary `direct` case, so nothing to fix there. That fourth constructor is additional evidence full propagation in one PR was the wrong call: even the reviewed enumeration was incomplete, so "update every constructor" wasn't actually a bounded task.

Template's exact mapping: `adjudication.policy` names the Dispatch Policy's `id`/`version` (`dispatch_policy`, already carried in the dispatched Mission's `template` lineage member), never the Template's own `id`/`template_version`. Fixed the Role Mapping table row, which previously named both. Added a Ceiling drawdown row too (`policy_id`/`policy_version` from `activation`).

gnap.md's "complete `approval_basis`" enumeration now lists `adjudication` as the OPTIONAL member alongside the REQUIRED ones — this was worth fixing regardless of REQUIRED-vs-OPTIONAL, since an enumeration claiming completeness while omitting a real member is inaccurate either way.

## P1 — Don't use the lifecycle-state compatibility rule for an adjudication discriminator

Fixed. `approval_basis.type` and `adjudication.kind` now share their own unknown-value rule: an unrecognized value is preserved unchanged as opaque provenance, a consumer MUST NOT infer or fabricate the standing behind it, and MUST refuse only a profile operation that itself needs recognized adjudication semantics. Stated once at `type`'s definition, explicitly distinguished from the Mission Lifecycle state rule, and `kind` cross-references it.

I did **not** extend this to `authority_source.type`, which carries the identical `{{lifecycle}}` citation. You named `approval_basis.type` and `adjudication.kind`; fixing a third, uninvited field in a changes-requested round felt like scope creep rather than a courtesy. Flagging it here as observed-and-scoped-out — happy to take it in a follow-up if you'd rather it ride along.

## P2 — Keep the discriminator semantic and make evidence a typed seam

Took your first option. `kind` is now `human` or `policy` only — semantic, never a storage location. Added an independent `governance_record` boolean: `true` when an Approval Governance Record backs the decision. When `true`, `kind` MUST equal *that record's own accountable assertion's kind* (human or policy) rather than being fixed by `type` — the accountable assertion is unique by approval-governance.md's own assertion requirements, so this derivation is total and well-defined. This directly fixes the original defect: a `direct` Mission whose AGR accountable assertion is `kind: policy` under the recency exception now correctly reports `kind: policy`, not a flattened `agr`.

One dispute: you asked for a "typed governance-record reference." I made it a bare boolean instead, deliberately. The record is already joined by this Mission's own `approval_event_id` — a second reference would duplicate that join key, which is exactly the kind of untyped-pointer surface I removed from `evidence` two paragraphs later for the same reason. If you want an actual reference object (even an empty extensible one) rather than a flag, say so and I'll add it; I don't think it earns its keep given the join already exists, but I recognize "reference" was specifically asked for and a boolean isn't one.

Dropped `policy.evidence` entirely from Core, per your third option — a companion profile that wants a typed evidence artifact for its policy decision adds its own extension member under the existing collision-resistant-naming rule instead of Core inventing an untyped grab-bag.

## Mechanical

- Rebuilt the corrected Role Mapping table (Template + Ceiling drawdown rows), Principal Model cross-reference, Single Accountable Approver section, and Document History entry to match.
- `draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md`'s `assessed-oauth-digest` marker re-read and re-pinned again (no assessed claim touches these fields).
- `conformance-manifest.json`: reworked the four adjudication rows to match the new shape, added a fifth for the unknown-value rule, re-pinned `source.specs` for core and substrate. All still `todo`.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`, `check-family-manifest.mjs`, `check-bundle-manifest.mjs`, `check-external-pins.mjs` all pass. All five touched drafts build clean via `make`.

pulls.title: substrate: remove the normative OAuth dependency (#708)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Executes ruled issue #708 (gated on #704's ruling, adopted): removes the substrate's normative OAuth dependency so `AAuth -> Substrate` carries no onward normative edge. AAuth's own `normative_references` in family-manifest.json name only the substrate (verified), so this closes the chain the review flagged.

**Placement chosen for the OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment: relocated into the OAuth binding's own back matter** (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`, new `{#oauth-statement}` appendix), not demoted in place. The substrate hosting a binding-specific discharge, even labeled informative, was still the substantive complaint; relocating lets the substrate's Statement-format definition ({{statement}}) stay fully binding-agnostic (no specific binding named as example beyond a parenthetical pointer) while the OAuth binding asserts its own mapping onto the substrate's kernel, informatively citing the substrate exactly as it already did. Concretely:

1. **Assessment relocated.** `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md` gains an `# OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment {#oauth-statement}` appendix: the binding's own self-assessment against the substrate's kernel/capabilities, normative as the binding's own content, taking no normative dependency on the substrate (its reference stays informative, matching the substrate's reference back). The substrate's Conformance-section pointer paragraph was replaced accordingly.
2. **Family vocabulary bridge is informative.** `# Mission-Bound Authorization Family Use {#family}` in the substrate is informative throughout (previously "normative for family, informative for others").
3. **Front matter re-tiered.** `I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission` moved from `normative:` to `informative:` in the substrate's front matter; `family-manifest.json`'s substrate entry now has an empty `normative_references` (the reference remains in `references`, since the substrate's kernel intro, Default Commitment Construction, and family appendix still informatively cite it).
4. **Neutral test vector added.** The substrate's Default Commitment Construction section now carries its own byte-level envelope-anchor worked example (JCS + SHA-256, generic field names, wrapped-for-layout caveat matching the OAuth binding's own vector section's phrasing), independent of the OAuth binding's `intent_hash`/`authority_hash` vectors, which remain as an additional informative example.
5. **83-row sweep: 0 rows re-anchored, 4 notes retargeted.** None of the substrate's 83 conformance-manifest.json rows anchor into `{{family}}`, `{{oauth-statement}}`, or `{{crosswalk}}` (all anchor kernel/capability sections untouched by this change). Four rows' `notes` fields cited `{{mission-substrate#oauth-statement}}` by item number (items 2, 4, 9 x2) as descriptive grounding; retargeted to `{{oauth-mission#oauth-statement}}` since the item numbering carried over unchanged. `mandate.md`'s Portable Evidence consumption row, which named "the substrate's OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment," was reworded to "the OAuth binding's own Mapping Assessment" with its citation moved to `I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission` (already an informative reference there).

**Interlocks moved with the content, both updated:**
- `scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs`'s Mapping Assessment change-coupling tripwire now reads the `assessed-substrate-digest` marker from the OAuth binding and hashes the substrate (reversed from the prior `assessed-oauth-digest` marker read from the substrate, hashing the binding).
- `scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s Statement registry now points the "OAuth Mission binding capability table" entry at `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`; the substrate's own exemption from the five-column-header self-registration rule (already granted for its "Mission Substrate Statement" heading, since it hosts the format's own non-normative illustrative skeleton) was extended to that same rule so the skeleton doesn't need registering as if it were a binding's Statement.

**Trade-off worth flagging for the owner:** the tripwire's coupling changed shape, not just direction. Previously, editing the OAuth binding's text forced a re-read of the (substrate-hosted) assessment on the next family-manifest check. Now a self-hosted assessment can't digest-pin its own subject, so editing the binding's own prose doesn't by itself trip this particular tripwire. What still catches drift: the binding is in `conformance-manifest.json`'s `source.specs`, so any byte change to it fails `check-conformance-manifest` until someone deliberately re-reviews and re-pins (this produced the two `spec-inventory-drift` findings during this PR, resolved by the pin commits). The substrate-side coupling (assessment tracks substrate changes) is unchanged in kind, just re-pointed.

Also worth naming: the relocated appendix is core's own normative-as-own-content text built on substrate vocabulary (Mission Reference, Controller, Approved Context, etc.) that core cites only informatively — the same posture the substrate used before, now mirrored on the other side. It carries the same non-claim language ("makes no substrate-conformance claim... takes no requirement from the substrate") the substrate's own format definition requires of any Mapping Assessment.

## #704-ruling rider + #663 (Refs both)

Checked #663's thread first per instruction: its ruling (embedded in the issue body, no separate ruling comment) calls for cross-referencing three previously-independent accounts of what earns "Mission-bound" — the architecture's Token Classes, the architecture's Mission Binding Properties equivalence vector, and the core's Conformance gates — designating the property vector as the definition, the Mission Substrate Statement as how a binding evidences it, and the core's gates as the OAuth binding's discharge. This overlaps the #704 rider's own target text (the architecture's Token Classes section, adjacent to the peer-sentence reword), so both are executed together in `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md` and `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`:

- The architecture's blanket "the bindings are peers of one another" sentence (Introduction) now names two axes — deployment topology and data-model independence — and classifies the Mission Authority Server using the ruling's exact wording: "a normative standalone-controller protocol binding over the OAuth Mission data model: a peer deployment topology, but not an independent substrate model," since it normatively imports the OAuth Mission record and issuance profile. AAuth is named as the binding that demonstrates model independence.
- Token Classes now cites `{{binding-properties}}`'s `credential-mission-bound` equivalence as the definition of "Mission-bound," keeps the existing "a binding earns it through... its Mission Substrate Statement" as the evidencing mechanism, and adds that the OAuth binding's Conformance gates are that binding's discharge of the definition.
- Mission Binding Properties' `credential-mission-bound` paragraph now states it is the family's authoritative definition and cross-references Token Classes and the OAuth binding's gates.
- The OAuth binding's Conformance section gates paragraph now cites the architecture's `credential-mission-bound` definition as what these gates discharge.

Document History entries added to substrate, architecture, and core (core touched for the relocated assessment and this cross-referencing, so it gets one too, consistent with by-touch convention).

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` (chains `check-substrate-statements.mjs`): OK, no drift, 5 Statements / 8 consumer tables.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs`: OK, 519 requirements, no schema/anchor/stale-requirement/spec-inventory-drift findings.
- `node scripts/check-external-pins.mjs`: OK.
- `node scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs`: OK (pins a historic commit; unaffected by this branch).
- `make draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.txt`: all OK.
- Grepped the whole tree (excluding `.git`) for the retired `assessed-oauth-digest` marker name and for stale prose in `DEPENDENCIES.md`, `README.md`, `DRAFTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/`: the only remaining hit is `src/PLAN.md`'s D133 historical log entry, an accurate-at-the-time record left untouched per the no-touch rule on that file.

## Deviations from the literal issue text

- Chose relocation over in-place demotion for the assessment (see placement rationale above); the issue offered both as valid.
- `check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s registry line was retargeted rather than gaining a second entry for the substrate's illustrative skeleton table, to avoid overstating the Statement count or over-constraining a deliberately abbreviated illustration.

## Merge order

Merge **after** `feat/637-resource-access-profile`: as of this PR that branch has not yet been opened (issue #637 is still open, "ready for the execution PR wave on go-ahead" per its own thread), so there is nothing to rebase onto yet. Both will touch core/substrate adjacency; rebase this branch once #637's execution PR lands if conflicts arise.

Refs #708 #704 #663

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Review of `4041d73399a02d482114d6ecc7056c1d3695c63b` against base `59b958e566443ca8e0fc68e6f263414b6dfa191f` and issues #708/#704/#663.

**Disposition: changes requested.** The mechanical edge reversal is clean, the neutral commitment vector recomputes exactly, and the manifests/checkers point in the intended direction. One normative-layering contradiction remains, plus one consequence for the family definition.

### P0 — The relocated appendix cannot be both normative and only informatively dependent on the contract it applies

The new appendix says it is [normative as OAuth-binding content](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4041d73399a02d482114d6ecc7056c1d3695c63b/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L5754-L5764), while its terms, nine-element format, capability vocabulary, activation semantics, and validity rules come from the Substrate's normative Mapping Assessment contract. The Substrate expressly says a Mapping Assessment is in the Statement's form and that either form has MUST-level requirements ([Substrate lines 940–953](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4041d73399a02d482114d6ecc7056c1d3695c63b/draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md#L940-L953)). Calling the citation informative does not remove a reference needed to understand and maintain normative claims.

This creates the exact choice #708 was meant to resolve:

- If the appendix is a non-conformance crosswalk/self-assessment, make the entire appendix explicitly **informative**. The OAuth binding's existing conformance gates remain its normative requirements, and the digest tripwire can still force review when the Substrate changes.
- If the table and mapping are intended as normative OAuth capability claims governed by the Substrate format, the Substrate is a normative reference, recreating the onward edge.

I recommend the first option. It preserves `AAuth → Substrate` with no onward normative edge and accurately describes what a Mapping Assessment can establish.

### P1 — The family definition now requires a Statement that OAuth deliberately does not publish

Architecture now says a binding earns “Mission-bound” through capability claims in its [Mission Substrate Statement](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4041d73399a02d482114d6ecc7056c1d3695c63b/draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md#L1746-L1753). But this PR deliberately makes the OAuth appendix a **Mapping Assessment**, says it is not a conformance result, and says OAuth publishes no Statement. The checker nevertheless puts the assessment table in the same undifferentiated [`REGISTRY`](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/4041d73399a02d482114d6ecc7056c1d3695c63b/scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs#L51-L57).

Please make the architecture precise: the property vector is the definition; a conforming binding evidences it through a Statement, while the legacy/unclaiming OAuth binding is assessed through the informative Mapping Assessment and normatively discharges it through its own Conformance gates. Renaming the checker registry to cover “Statements and Assessments,” or tagging the entry kind, would keep the automation from erasing that distinction.

Validation performed: dependency/front-matter and manifest directions inspected; all 83 Substrate rows checked for moved anchors by the conformance validator; `check-conformance-manifest.mjs` passes (519 requirements); the new canonical byte string independently produces `sha-256:R5C5cMDxLzhle5Xac-V9qCKN4q8wSVAvbgiv3PYEzzI`. The family checker reached only the expected archive-snapshot limitation (`source_repository_commit` unavailable without the full Git object store), not a PR finding.
