pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #637 #645 #698

## Summary

Splits `mission_resource_access` (an RFC 9396 `authorization_details` type previously defined inline in the OAuth binding) into its own companion Internet-Draft, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md`. The OAuth binding becomes type-agnostic; it also gains the type-agnostic scope-projection issuance algorithm (#698) and a MUST three-capability (narrowing/delegation/projection) declaration per supported `authorization_details` type (#645). The new profile owns `mission_resource_access`'s concrete subset/intersection algebra, delegation policy, Common Constraints registry, and its own Scope Projection safety conditions and Transformation Capabilities declaration.

**12 commits, 15 files changed (+1586/-771). New file: `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md` (914 lines).**

## 1. Three-bucket MUST inventory

### Relocated verbatim (moved, not duplicated — 0 old-home occurrences, 1 new-home occurrence, verified by grep)

| Content | Old anchor (core) | New anchor (profile) |
|---|---|---|
| Type member definitions (`type`, `resource`, `resource_match`, `actions`, `constraints`, `delegation` incl. `max_depth`/`allowed_delegates`) | inline in `{#authorization-derivation}` | `{#resource-access-type}` |
| Subset Rule's 3 comparison items, the RFC 3986 prefix-normalization paragraph, the flat-comparison paragraph, the delegation-invariant paragraph | `{#subset}` | `{#subset}` (profile's own) |
| Full Common Constraints section (9 constraints, value-syntax/subset/intersection fixes, decimal-string grammar, numeric-range rule) | `{#common-constraints}` | `{#common-constraints}` |
| "Matching `allowed_delegates`" + AS-authentication + `sub`-non-portability paragraphs | inline in Delegation Within a Mission | `{#delegate-eligibility}` |
| Modeling Tools and Function Calls (full section, MCP/tool-call mapping) | `{#tools}` | `{#tools}` |
| IANA: the type registration note | `{#type-registration}` | `{#type-registration}` |
| IANA: Common Constraints Registry (table + registration policy) | `{#iana-common-constraints}` | `{#iana-common-constraints}` |
| **Resource Boundary Canonicalization** (full security subsection: RFC 3986 normalization threat vectors, worked prefix-matching table) — **not in the original 27-edit plan; found during a post-implementation audit** | `{#resource-boundary-canonicalization}` (deleted from core) | `{#resource-boundary-canonicalization}` |

Verified with paired greps (`grep -c <distinctive phrase> core.md profile.md` for each block): every relocated block reports `0` in core, `1` in the profile.

### Generalized in place (pre-existing normative sentences whose scope widened; NOT 1:1 relocation)

From the original plan (C4, C5, C12, C16, C20/C22, C23 — **flagged: this one weakens a MUST** from "list `mission_resource_access`" to "list at least one AS-supported type", a deliberate scope change per #637's ruling —, C24, C25): the Authority Set derivation sentence, the Intent-bounding rule, the three-capability widening (two capabilities → three, new normative breadth per #645), the per-entry-enforcement restatement, the two discovery MUSTs, the schema-endpoint MUST, the minimum-deployment note, and the Mission Issuer surfaces bullet.

Found beyond the plan during the post-implementation audit (the checkers cannot see prose semantics or cross-document attribution, only anchors/digests/quoted-clause presence):

- Core's canonicalization section: "the only normalization this document defines" claim, now false — restated as "this document defines no such normalization itself; where a type defines one, as `mission_resource_access` does...".
- Core's Resource Server Enforcement bullet and the Enforcement Boundaries pointer paragraph: both cited the local `{{subset}}` anchor for the RFC 3986 normalization detail that moved to the profile; both re-pointed.
- Core's `mission_bound_authorization_supported` metadata description: named `mission_resource_access` derivation specifically; generalized to "derivation of `authorization_details` entries of its supported types".
- `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md`: the "authority only narrows" invariant, the resource-owned-meaning boundary paragraph, the Common Constraints mechanism's "Home" line, and the Authority Set representation row of the substrate-primitives table — all attributed `mission_resource_access`/Common Constraints to "the OAuth binding" where it's now the profile's.
- `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md`: the Structured Authority capability row's "Scope and defining sections" cell.
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-status.md`: the completion capability's normative-dependency paragraph, the "Relationship to the Issuance Profile" section, the `terminal_when` Common Constraint definition and both of its IANA registration passages, the Conventions term list, and the introspection `authorization_details` shape citation. Gains `I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access` as a new normative reference (its `terminal_when` registration depends on that registry) and a `requires_when` conditional adoption edge, since the completion capability is independently optional.
- `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence.md`: each document's Conventions term list attributed `mission_resource_access` to the issuance profile.
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain.md`: IANA Considerations claimed the type was "registered by the issuance profile".
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md`: the Conventions term list and the transaction challenge's `authorization_details` claim definition.
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-work-products.md`: a passing Status-section mention (fixed by dropping the false attribution rather than adding a new citation, since the reference was incidental).

### New normative content

- Core's type-agnostic Scope Projection section (`{#scope-projection}`): the semantic subset condition, the 6-step issuance algorithm, and the fail-closed rule (#698).
- Core's three-independent-capability declaration MUST and the `mission_transformation_capabilities` carrier shape (#645).
- The profile's own concrete Scope Projection safety conditions (3 numbered tests: exact resource match under the mapping, actions match without aggregation, every carried constraint independently enforced).
- The profile's Transformation Capabilities declaration section (stating `narrowing`/`delegation`/`projection` all `true` for a full implementation).

## 2. Forced cross-reference rewrites

Every relocated passage's references were re-targeted: a reference to core machinery stayed a same-document anchor in the profile only where the profile itself restates it (`{{subset}}` — the profile has its own Subset Rule heading with the same anchor id); a reference to core-only machinery became an informative citation (`{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission}}`, e.g. the Resource Server enforcement duty, the token `aud` derivation rule, anchor computation); a reference to the type's own concept became a local profile anchor (`{{authorization-derivation}}` → `{{resource-access-type}}` for `prefix`-entry mentions); `{{delegation-constraints}}` stayed a cross-document citation to core (delegation *policy application* is core's, the concrete `delegation` member shape is the profile's own `{{delegate-eligibility}}`); `{{protected-resource-metadata}}` and `{{integrity-anchors}}`/`{{canonicalization}}` stayed cross-document citations to core (both mechanisms are core's, untouched). No relocated passage retained a bare local-anchor reference to content that no longer lives in its own document.

## 3. Document History entries added

**Core** (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`, under `-01`):
> Mission Resource Access Profile split (#637, #645, #698): the `mission_resource_access` type definition, its resource and action matching, generic constraints, the Common Constraints registry, the delegation member and matching rules, the subset and intersection algebra, and the Resource Boundary Canonicalization security analysis relocated to the Mission Resource Access Profile ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access}}); this document keeps type-agnostic commitment, the approved-set metadata requirement, and derivation gating ({{authorization-derivation}}, {{other-types}}, {{discovery}}). Adds the type-agnostic scope-projection rule and issuance algorithm ({{scope-projection}}) and the machine-readable per-type transformation-capability declaration (`mission_transformation_capabilities`, {{other-types}}); sweeps every scope-only claim that assumed a lossy projection was always available (the Intent enforcement table, Resource Server Enforcement, and the minimum-deployment note).

**Architecture** (`draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md`):
> Non-goal reworded (#637): "a new authority format, or a new grant protocol" narrowed to "a new grant protocol," naming the OAuth binding's Mission Resource Access Profile as the family's one cross-resource `authorization_details` type, since RFC 9396 leaves type semantics to the type and the family now defines one. Document Map gains the profile's row under "The substrate and the bindings."

**New draft** (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md`, `-00`):
> Initial version: `mission_resource_access`, its resource and action matching, generic constraints, the Common Constraints registry, the delegation policy and delegate-matching rules, the subset and intersection algebra, and the Resource Boundary Canonicalization security analysis, relocated without change from {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission}}, where they were previously defined inline (#637). Adds this type's concrete Scope Projection safety conditions and issuance-algorithm interlock (#698), and its Transformation Capabilities declaration for the issuance profile's machine-readable per-type capability map (#645).

## 4. **MERGE FIRST among core-touching PRs in this wave.**

## 5. Deviations from the plan

- **The Resource Boundary Canonicalization security subsection was not in the plan's 27-edit list.** A post-implementation audit (prompted by advisor review) found core still carried a full `mission_resource_access`-specific security analysis (RFC 3986 normalization threat vectors + worked prefix-matching table) under Security Considerations, citing the now-relocated `{{subset}}` normalization detail. Relocated it to the new profile's Security Considerations; left a short type-agnostic pointer in core.
- **Family-wide attribution sweep, not in the plan.** The plan's edit list covered core and architecture only. A broader audit (grep for `mission_resource_access` and "Common Constraints" across every draft) found the same defect — a passage attributing `mission_resource_access`'s definition, or the Common Constraints registry, to "the issuance profile" — in `mission-authority-server.md`, `mission-authzen.md`, `mission-runtime-evidence.md`, `oauth-mission-status.md`, `oauth-mission-cross-domain.md`, `oauth-mission-transaction-authorization.md`, and `oauth-mission-work-products.md`. All fixed, each gaining the new profile as a front-matter reference (normative where the document's own wire protocol requires the type, informative where the mention is explanatory) with `family-manifest.json` updated to match.
- **No `source.specs` entry was added for the new draft in `conformance-manifest.json`**, despite the plan's Step 6 instructing one. `check-conformance-manifest.mjs` enforces bidirectional consistency between `source.specs` keys and requirement rows' `"spec"` values (lines 108/112 of the checker); no requirement row (the seven new ones or the two re-anchored ones) names the new file as `"spec"` — they're all anchored in core, since `{#scope-projection}` is core's own section. Adding an entry would have failed the checker's "entry with no referencing row" check.
- **`draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md` was never in `source.specs`** (zero requirement rows reference it), so the plan's instruction to recompute its digest had no target — nothing to do there.
- **`draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md` needed an unplanned fix and two re-pins.** Its OAuth Binding Mapping Assessment (`{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission}}`'s Statement) had a Structured Authority capability row citing "the Common Constraints" as part of the OAuth binding's own scope; updated to attribute them to the profile. The `assessed-oauth-digest` tripwire (which pins a hash of core's bytes) then required two re-pins, once after the initial core edit and once after the Resource Boundary Canonicalization relocation.
- **C8/C12 adaptation:** the plan's quoted section boundaries for the type-member-definition block and the `{#other-types}` rewrite both undercounted the actual file content by one paragraph or block each (a coincidental drift, not a deliberate change). C8's "Example Authority Set" intro fix (C9) was folded into the same edit. C12's actual `{#other-types}` section included a non-normative Cedar/`mission_resource_access` composition example the plan's quoted text omitted; kept it in place (unmodified) rather than deleting it, since C8/C9 explicitly established that concrete `mission_resource_access` examples stay in core.
- Every `content_sha256`/`revision` pair in `conformance-manifest.json` was computed by `shasum -a 256` and `git log -1 --format=%H -- <file>` against actually-committed bytes, never guessed; each was recomputed a second (and in core's case, third) time after later commits touched the same file.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — clean (42 drafts, no drift).
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean (526 requirements: 132 tested, 53 partial, 338 todo, 3 blocked).
- `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.txt/.html`, `make draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt`, `make draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.txt` — all build clean (only pre-existing, unrelated network-fetch warnings for external individual-draft bibxml).
- Every companion file touched in the deviations above was independently rebuilt (`make <name>.txt`) to confirm no kramdown-rfc/xml2rfc syntax errors.

## Review response (round 2)

Addresses https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/pull/718#issuecomment-5401337954 (changes requested).

### Additional relocation (core → profile)

- Resource Server enforcement duties (exact/prefix `resource` matching, `actions` matching, per-entry `constraints` enforcement and its fail-closed/no-disclosure-only rules) — core's `{#rs-enforcement}` bullets → profile's new `{#rs-enforcement}` section.
- `mission_constraints_supported` protected-resource metadata member, definition and IANA registration — core's `{#protected-resource-metadata}` / `{#oauth-protected-resource-metadata-registration}` → profile's new sections of the same names.

### Additional generalization in place

- Core's `{#rs-enforcement}` closing sentence ("A `constraints` member narrows authority...") and the `constraint_unrecognized` denial-reason description both hardcoded `constraints`; both generalized to "type-defined constraint"/"type-defined member or constraint" (same defect class as the review's P1 finding, found during the sweep it prompted).
- Core's `{#delegation-constraints}` opening sentence still said "the entry's optional `delegation` member"; generalized to "a type-defined delegation policy," matching the already-generic "Per-entry enforcement" paragraph below it.
- Three cross-references inside the profile itself (the `constraints`-fail-closed bullet under the type definition, the decimal-value fail-closed sentence in Common Constraints, and the Resource Boundary Canonicalization lead paragraph) still pointed at core's now-relocated Resource Server duty (`{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission}}`); re-pointed to the profile's own new `{{rs-enforcement}}`/`{{protected-resource-metadata}}` anchors, since that's now where the duty is actually defined.
- Core's non-normative "which party enforces each bound" table (in the Intent-controls discussion) had two cells citing `{{rs-enforcement}}` as the section that enforces `resource`/`actions`/`constraints`; after the relocation that section no longer names those members at all, so the citation was stale. Re-pointed both cells to the profile (`{{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access}}`, alongside `{{rs-enforcement}}`), keeping the member names as the illustrative example the table already uses. Found on a second self-review pass over every remaining `{{rs-enforcement}}` citation in core, checking each for a member-specific claim that section no longer makes; the other ~15 citations remain accurate (they cite the general RS-enforces-the-token duty, `client_id`, `authority_hash` recomputation, or the `mission` claim, none of which moved).
- Core's `-01` Document History entry for the original split named the relocated type definition, matching, constraints, registry, delegation rules, subset/intersection algebra, and Resource Boundary Canonicalization, but not this round's two further relocations (the Resource Server's `resource`/`actions`/`constraints` enforcement duties and the `mission_constraints_supported` member, including its IANA registration). Extended the same bullet to name both, since an IANA-registry-affecting relocation belongs in the changelog that already enumerates the others.

### Corrected (not relocated, not new): the profile's Conformance section

Previously conflated Authorization Server and Resource Server duties under one list. Now split by role, per the review: AS validates the type, declares all three Transformation Capabilities, and implements subset/intersection, delegate eligibility, or the three projection conditions only for capabilities it declares `true`; RS implements only `{#rs-enforcement}`'s matching/enforcement/fail-closed duties and is not measured against issuer-only machinery.

### Conformance ledger

Added `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md` to `conformance-manifest.json`'s `source.specs` (previously absent, per the review's third finding) and 13 new requirement rows covering schema validation, the four RS enforcement duties, Common Constraints intersection, delegate-eligibility authentication, the three Scope Projection safety conditions, the Transformation Capabilities declaration's undeclared-fallback, and RS role-independence. All `coverage: "todo"` — no fabricated test coverage. Total requirement rows: 526 → 539. Also re-pinned core's updated `source.specs` entry, and `draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate.md`'s (its `assessed-oauth-digest` Mapping Assessment tripwire and `source.specs` entry both moved, since core's Resource Server contract text changed; the Mapping Assessment's own claims needed no substantive edit, since it already spoke type-agnostically and named none of the relocated prose).

### Verification

- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` — clean (42 drafts, no drift; includes the `assessed-oauth-digest` re-pin).
- `node scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs` — clean (5 Statements, 8 consumer tables validated); no row text needed re-review.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — clean, 539 requirements (132 tested, 53 partial, 351 todo, 3 blocked).

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Reviewed commit [`c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587`](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/commit/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587).

The architectural direction is right: the approved set is now type-agnostic, the concrete `mission_resource_access` algebra has a plausible document home, and the core scope-projection rule implements #698's semantic-subset/fail-closed ruling. I found three issues to resolve before merge.

### P1 — the core still normatively interprets `mission_resource_access`

The split stops at the AS derivation boundary. Core says it defines no authorization-details type, but its generic Resource Server contract still requires every RS to interpret entries through the `resource`, `actions`, `constraints`, and `resource_match: prefix` members: [core lines 2885–2917](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L2885-L2917). Those are this new profile's semantics, not RFC 9396 or type-agnostic Mission semantics. A Cedar or payment type need not have any of those members.

The same leak remains on discovery: core still defines and registers the flat `mission_constraints_supported` protected-resource member ([definition](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L3961-L3968), [IANA registration](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L4837-L4841)), while the new type profile consumes that member for its own constraint keys ([profile lines 216–223](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md#L216-L223)). A flat list is not meaningful for unrelated RAR types and can collide where two types reuse a member name with different semantics.

Move the `resource`/`actions`/prefix/constraint enforcement bullets and `mission_constraints_supported` definition plus registration into the Resource Access Profile. Core should require an RS to evaluate each applicable entry according to that entry type's specification and fail closed when it does not implement that type. If core retains a cross-type constraint-discovery surface, make it a per-type map rather than a flat key array. Also generalize the opening sentence of Delegation Constraints, which still says every entry is governed by an optional `delegation` member before the later paragraph correctly switches to type-defined policy ([lines 3607–3644](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md#L3607-L3644)).

### P1 — the new profile's conformance contract assigns AS duties to Resource Servers

The conformance section says a conforming “Authorization Server or Resource Server” implements the subset/intersection algebra, delegate-eligibility test, and Transformation Capabilities declaration ([profile lines 704–716](https://github.com/mcguinness/mission-bound-authorization/blob/c8150667aab8175ce5af31331de7edf779bac587/draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md#L704-L716)). An RS neither publishes the AS's transformation declaration nor needs intersection/delegate-issuance machinery merely to enforce a carried entry. Conversely, the list does not explicitly enumerate the RS's actual request-matching and constraint-enforcement duties.

Split conformance by role:

- AS: validate the type; declare all three capabilities; implement subset/intersection when claiming `narrowing`, delegate eligibility when claiming `delegation`, and the per-target tests when claiming `projection`.
- RS: perform exact/prefix resource matching, action-family matching, and every carried constraint; fail closed on unsupported members/keys and canonicalization mismatch.

That also makes partial implementation precise instead of making an RS appear nonconforming for not implementing issuer transformations.

### P1 — the new normative document is absent from the conformance ledger

No requirement row names `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.md`, so it has no `source.specs` pin and no drift protection. The seven new rows cover core's generic projection algorithm, but none covers this profile's three concrete projection tests, its capability declaration, or its relocated AS/RS requirements. The PR explanation notes that adding a source entry alone would fail because no row references it; that is evidence the missing rows are the problem, not a reason to leave the profile untracked.

Add rows for at least the profile-owned normative surfaces introduced or made independently conformable by this split: schema validation, resource/action/constraint enforcement, subset/intersection, delegation eligibility, the three projection conditions, capability declaration, and role-specific fail-closed behavior. Then add the profile to `source.specs`. This is also what makes #637's 1:1 MUST-inventory rule durable after the PR merges.

Verification performed on the reviewed SHA:

- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-resource-access.txt` and `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.txt` — build successfully; only the repository's existing offline external-reference warnings appeared.
- `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` — passes (526 rows), while confirming zero rows reference the new profile.
- GitHub `check` and reader-edition jobs — passing at review time.

**Disposition: changes requested.** The document boundary is the right one, but core is not yet type-agnostic at enforcement/discovery, and the new profile does not yet have a correct or traceable conformance contract.

pulls.title: runtime-evidence: Mission Evidence Envelope, payload-type registry, and Intent Admission
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Defines the #282 committed-evidence envelope, per the 2026-08-24
architecture-shape finding (P1 #10) that reopened it, and lands #512's
ruling that Intent Admission is the registry's first payload type.

- **Mission Evidence Envelope** (`type`, `id`, `mission {id, issuer}`,
  `emitter`, `occurred_at`, `sequence`, `related`, `payload`,
  `evidence_envelope`): a generic wrapper a future evidence kind
  registers into instead of repeating this document's per-kind
  member-and-media-type shape. Reuses the existing `evidence_envelope`
  JWS-over-JCS procedure and the OAuth binding's integrity-anchor and
  commitment-mechanism conventions; defines two new media types
  (`application/mission-evidence+json`, `+jws`) shared by every
  registered payload type, never one per type.
- **Mission Evidence Payload Type Registry**: Specification-Required /
  Designated-Expert, modeled on the Mission Lifecycle States registry.
  Registration requires a collision-resistant `type` name, a closed
  `payload` schema, a verification procedure, and a producer. Domain
  separation is preserved (the #282 review's tradeoff constraint):
  `type` is inside the signed bytes, a verifier dispatches to exactly
  one registration before interpreting `payload`, and a schema/procedure
  change is a new `type`, never a silent revision. A dedicated Domain
  Separation section states why this is narrower than the single
  universal `typ` list the family previously declined. The existing
  Decision Evidence, Execution Evidence, Refusal Record, and Mission
  Receipt objects are unchanged and are **not** migrated onto this
  envelope here.
- **Intent Admission Evidence**, the registry's first payload type and
  the first consumer of the core's Intent Submission Evidence hook
  (#506, shipped with an empty type registry): the inbound Intent
  Admission Assertion (closed entry/claim schema, verification
  procedure covering issuer trust, `aud`, freshness, `jti` replay,
  `intent_hash` equality, presenter conjunction, status, and the
  no-lineage-carry default) and the emitted `mission-intent-admission`
  payload type (producer: the AS; payload = `intent_hash`, the Mission
  Record's own `submission_evidence` array restated verbatim, and
  `disposition`). The payload's `submission_evidence` member is
  designed to be exactly the normalized input #699's approval-context
  manifest investigation needs, without this document defining that
  commitment itself.
- One paragraph stating SD-JWT Mandates and SCITT Receipts stay
  outside this registry (selective disclosure and transparency-service
  commitment are properties a generic JSON `payload` wrapper can't
  preserve).

## Placement

Hosted as new sections in `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence.md`
rather than a new companion draft:

- The envelope reuses runtime-evidence's `evidence_envelope`
  JWS-over-JCS byte-equality procedure verbatim (by citation, not
  duplication). A new companion would have to either duplicate that
  procedure or awkwardly stretch `application/mission-runtime-evidence+jws`
  across an AS-emitted admission record.
- Precedent already stretches this document past pure PDP/PEP runtime
  evidence: the Mission Receipt's producer is a "receipt issuer key,"
  not a PDP or PEP.
- CONTRIBUTING's Consolidation Policy reserves reconsidering the
  runtime/evidence document boundary for WG adoption / publication
  planning; this PR adds sections, it doesn't touch that boundary.
- #512 said "a thin rider beside it at most; no standalone draft" for
  Intent Admission; a new companion draft would have added
  family-manifest/DRAFTS.md/README/reader-edition wiring and a
  maturity/maintenance class this scoped PR has no basis to set.

All new content is new top-level/nested sections (Mission Evidence
Envelope, Intent Admission Evidence, and additive subsections in
Conformance/Security/Privacy/IANA/Document History). No existing
Decision/Execution/Refusal/Receipt member definitions were touched, to
avoid colliding with the parallel Wave-2 runtime/authzen restructure
(which this PR's title notes is **not** touching runtime-evidence's
record schemas).

## Scope (deliberately bounded)

This PR defines the envelope, the registry, and the one pilot payload
type. It does **not** migrate the existing 29 `application/mission-*`
media types onto this envelope — that's explicit follow-on work for a
separate PR per type family (runtime evidence, consent evidence,
harness/egress, containment, audit, etc.), each judged on whether
migrating buys anything over its current registration.

## Conformance / build

- 16 new conformance-manifest.json rows (born `todo`), ids prefixed
  `evidence.mission-evidence-envelope.*` and `evidence.intent-admission.*`.
- `source.specs` re-pinned for `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence.md`
  in a follow-up commit, matching the family's re-pin convention (one
  commit for content, a second for the digest/revision).
- `family-manifest.json`: added the new informative
  `draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate` reference edge (cited in the new
  Specialized Containers paragraph).
- `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` and
  `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` both exit 0.
- `make draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence.txt` builds clean.

## Deviation (found, not scope-creep)

While re-validating conformance-manifest.json for the re-pin, found a
**pre-existing** structural bug unrelated to this PR: a missing `},{`
object boundary between two rows (`cross-domain.resource-as.client-id-identifies-redeemer`
and `resource-access.type.prefix-query-fragment-refused`) had silently
merged them under JSON's last-key-wins duplicate-key semantics,
discarding the first row (a `tested` row with real test mappings) from
every parse, including the checker's own — so CI was silently blind to
it. Fixed as a 2-line mechanical brace insertion in the first content
commit; verified round-trip (552 `"id":` occurrences before the fix
matched only 551 parsed rows; 552/552 after).

## Merge order

Fourth in Wave 2, after the runtime/authzen restructure. If
runtime-evidence.md moved under this branch, rebase over it; this PR
only adds new sections and should not conflict with a restructure that
leaves runtime.md/authzen.md's own record schemas alone.

Refs #282 #512 #506 #699

pulls.title: family-manifest: maturity vocabulary migration to role + spec_maturity axes (#707)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #707

## Merge-order note

**LAST in Wave 2, by design.** Built against `main` @ `30982cda` (post #717, #712, #720). Every other Wave-2 PR moves rows or adds a 43rd draft; this migration is kept mechanical (manifest field rename + generator/checker extensions + a full regeneration pass) specifically so a rebase onto a moved-row tree is cheap. Expect to rebase at least once; each rebase needs a fresh `conformance-manifest.json` re-pin (see "Re-pin mechanics" below), the same way `3081038a`/`75b8a5bf` re-pinned after earlier Wave-1 rebases.

## What this does

Migrates `family-manifest.json`'s single `maturity` field into the two axes the #707 review named as conflated:

- **`role`**: `core` (the substrate kernel, alone), `adapter-binding` (a binding of the Mission model to a wire protocol), `companion` (a profile/extension built on a binding or the kernel), `guide` (an informational document with no protocol interface to mature). Derived and structurally validated (`roleFor()` in `scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs`, new checks (w)): `core` is `draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate` alone; `adapter-binding` is exactly `check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s Statement/Assessment registry (5 slugs); `guide` is exactly the 3 `category: info` documents; `companion` is the remaining 33.
- **`spec_maturity`**: `candidate` | `experimental` | `sketch` | `not_applicable`, gated by the five criteria from the ruling (complete requirement inventory; no internal contradiction or open `decide` issue on the claimed interface; a named interop floor with representative evidence *where evidence is claimed*; examples/vectors and a clean build; disclosed unstable external dependencies) — **never a raw coverage percentage**, per the ruling's own text ("Do not gate candidate status on a raw percentage... Show it beside maturity rather than encoding it into the same word").

`category` (front matter's `std`/`exp`/`info`) already carries standards category/status and needed no new field. Implementation/conformance is derived from `conformance-manifest.json` per spec at generation time and rendered as a new `Implementation:` line in every draft's family-status block, beside `Spec maturity:`, never folded into it.

## Why 23 of 24 "stable" drafts became `candidate` (not a rubber stamp)

The review's opening line was blunt: "23 documents marked stable against a ledger reporting 132 tested / 53 partial / 331 todo / 3 blocked reads as overstatement." A reviewer should expect that finding to demote most of them. It doesn't, and here's why, in the ruling's own terms: the adopted remedy for that overstatement is the **rename** (`stable` → `candidate`, a word that stops claiming production stability) **plus** conformance displayed beside it **plus** the five criteria — explicitly **not** demotion by coverage percentage. 26 of 42 documents (most of the family) carry zero rows in the audited conformance ledger; that's disclosed honestly in the new `Implementation:` line ("not yet in the conformance ledger") rather than punished in the maturity word, because the ledger tracks what the reference implementation has undertaken, not specification quality — encoding that into `spec_maturity` would be exactly "using implementation incompleteness as a proxy for protocol quality," which the review named as the failure to avoid.

I did not rubber-stamp this. Concretely, for all 24:

- **Criterion 1** (requirement inventory): all 24 have a real Conformance section (checked structurally; two false negatives from a too-strict heading regex, `mission-runtime.md`'s "Enforcement Scope and Conformance" and `mission-substrate.md`'s "Mission Substrate Conformance", were manually verified present).
- **Criterion 2** (no contradiction / open `decide` issue on the interface): five open `decide` issues name currently-stable drafts (#662 audit, #653 child-delegation, #661 cross-domain, #664 harness, #238 runtime). I verified each against the current tree rather than trusting GitHub's open/closed metadata, and **all five are already resolved in-tree** (by earlier Wave-1/Wave-2 landings) despite the issues staying open — bookkeeping lag, not a live problem, and not mine to close. The one genuinely live self-contradiction is `oauth-mission-approval`'s own Status section.
- **Criterion 3** (named floor + representative evidence where claimed): all pass; where evidence is claimed it's real (spot-verified against `conformance-manifest.json`'s per-spec rows).
- **Criterion 4** (vectors + clean build): `make` builds all 42 documents clean. One deliberate judgment call, flagged for the owner to overrule: `aauth-mission-expiry` has zero `~~~` artwork blocks (no worked example at all) — I passed it on proportionality, since it's a one-member RFC 3339 format profile with a two-item Conformance checklist, not withheld pending a manufactured example.
- **Criterion 5** (disclosed unstable external deps): already structurally enforced by the existing `external-normative-ids` generated block (check (q)) and the `frozen-until-upstream-release` maintenance class; needed no new mechanism.

**The one gate failure**: `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-approval`. Its own "# Status" section already says "this profile is not yet a stable interface" because of its normative dependency on `draft-gerber-oauth-deferred-token-response`, an early, unratified individual I-D — this is the exact live contradiction the ruling named (manifest said `stable`, prose said not-yet-stable). Resolved by setting `spec_maturity: experimental`; the bespoke prose was already honest and needed no edit, only its generated family-status line changed.

**A negative-control worth naming**: `mission-mandate.md`'s Status section says "the artifact itself is not yet exercised in deployment... before relying on them," which is instability-*shaped* language. I did not fail it: its subject is deployment/implementation experience, not its own interface (its normative deps — JWS, JWT, SD-JWT — are explicitly stated as already ratified), so it stayed `candidate`. This sentence doubles as the negative mutation test for the new `candidate-honesty` validator (see below): the validator must fire on `oauth-mission-approval`'s self-referential claim and must **not** fire on mandate's deployment-experience disclosure. Both directions verified by mutation test (inject the failing phrase, confirm the checker catches it; inject a criterion-5-style external-dependency disclosure, confirm it does not; revert both, confirm clean).

**Deliberate exception, not an oversight**: DRAFTS.md's "the kernel contract first, then its five peer bindings" is spelled-out prose, left hand-written rather than converted to a marker block — it changes only when a new binding is authored (a rare, deliberately-reviewed event, already guarded by `check-substrate-statements.mjs`'s own tripwire against an unregistered capability table), and contorting that sentence into generated content for a number that changes roughly once a year wasn't worth the prose cost.

pulls.title: runtime: extract OAuth Adapter; rescope Core binding-neutral; authzen Decision Base + profiles
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #703 #238

## Summary

One coordinated restructuring per the #703 amended ruling and the #238 session disposition, executed as a single semantic rewrite (not two), in the order the ruling specified: finish the Runtime Core normative work, extract the OAuth adapter, then restructure AuthZEN.

1. **Runtime Core** (`draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md`) is rescoped to the binding-neutral semantic contract: established Mission reference/controller, effective-authority source, active predicate + freshness bound, subject/actor, action/resource/normalized parameters, local-policy intersection, authenticated permit/deny, execution boundary, fail-closed. OAuth claim/endpoint vocabulary (`authorization_details`, `mission_resource_access`, `sub`, `client_id`, `act`, `cnf`, `exp`, JWT/RFC 9068/RFC 6750/RFC 9728 mechanics) is named only in adapter cross-references, never as the operative vocabulary of a Core requirement.
2. **New**: `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-oauth.md` (Mission Runtime OAuth Adapter, the family's 43rd draft) carries Token Presentation and Validation, the `mission`/`act`/`cnf`/`aud` claim mapping, the `authorization_details`/`mission_resource_access` authority-entry mapping, Resource-Owner Class Floors via OAuth protected-resource metadata, and the OAuth IANA registration. It adds no enforcement invariant of its own.
3. **AuthZEN** (`draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md`) restructures into a **Decision Base** (sufficient for bare PEP/PDP decision interoperability) plus six named **feature profiles** — Transaction Assurance, Runtime Evidence, Obligations, ARAP, History, Batch — published as a dependency DAG with capability identifiers, each documented with the ruling's five-field template (prerequisites, producer/consumer roles, required members, behavior on absence, assurance claim). Runtime Evidence is no longer an unconditional adoption gate: the Conformance section's PEP/PDP checklists split into Decision Base MUSTs and a separate MUST list that applies only when the Runtime Evidence profile is claimed, closing the defect #703 named (a deployment could not previously claim bare decision interoperability without adopting the portable evidence schema).
4. **#238 residue**: the Enforcement Scope Statement thins from a flat twelve-item list to a five-item core declaration (mediated resources/actions/paths + PEP boundary, supported authority-entry types/evaluators, Mission-establishment mode, state source/staleness bound + PDP-unavailability posture, and a new **remote decision-channel trust mode** item) plus named-claim/capability-attached declarations for everything else (custody, transaction-assurance idempotency domains, evidence mechanism/retention/signing-key locations, EAT selections, outcome reconciliation). The PEP/PDP channel-integrity MUST — already present as an unconditional `runtime-enforced` row — relocates out of the OAuth-specific Token Validation section into a new binding-neutral Core subsection, `{{decision-channel}}`, with an explicit co-resident structural-satisfaction carve-out.
5. Baseline-vs-conditional per the ruling: channel authentication/integrity baseline for any non-co-resident PEP/PDP boundary; parameter/single-use binding baseline wherever the runtime profile already requires it by class (Transaction Assurance is the wire vehicle for that MUST, not a discretionary election); freshness required for Runtime-Enforced; no requester-side downgrade anywhere (selection is issuer/deployment policy plus authenticated capability negotiation only).

## MUST-inventory accounting (conformance-manifest.json)

Baseline: 122 rows anchored in `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md`, 78 in `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md` (200 total). Final: 119 in runtime, 5 in the new runtime-oauth, 80 in authzen (204 total; family total 551 → 555).

- **Relocated 1:1** (same id, new spec/anchor, text unchanged) — 5 rows, runtime.md → runtime-oauth.md: `token-validation.establish-validity-before-use`, `token-validation.audience-and-pop`, `token-validation.no-unverified-claims-and-missing-mission-refusal`, `classification.class-floor-metadata-not-lowered`, `classification.unknown-floor-value-high-consequence`.
- **Re-anchored within Core** (same id/spec, new anchor `decision-channel`, text genericized `token-derived` → `credential-derived`) — 2 rows: `token-validation.channel-integrity-and-token-forwarding`, `token-validation.minimize-claims-sent-should`.
- **Text changed, same id/spec/anchor** (OAuth vocabulary → abstract role, cross-reference retargeted to the adapter) — 10 rows: `classification.no-lowering-below-resource-floor`, `rs-profile.must-publish`, `rs-profile.no-claim-without-pep`, `decision-inputs.authority-entry-and-subset-required`, `decision-inputs.unknown-authorization-details-type-refusal`, `decision-inputs.actor-context-required-and-not-shortcut`, `decision-inputs.no-authority-expansion-via-actor`, `decision-inputs.mission-expires-at-refusal`, `decision-inputs.history-no-expand-authority`, `conformance.no-claim-outside-declared-scope`.
- **New rows** — 4: `runtime.decision-channel.no-unverified-credential-claims` and `runtime.conformance.remote-channel-trust-mode-declared` (Core, both unconditional `runtime-enforced`); `authzen.conformance.pep-checklist-runtime-evidence` and `authzen.conformance.pdp-checklist-runtime-evidence` (new capability `authzen.runtime-evidence`, `profiles: []` — the manifest-side proof the unconditional-adoption-gate defect is fixed).
- **Text changed in authzen's existing checklist rows** (base framing) — 2: `authzen.conformance.pep-checklist`, `authzen.conformance.pdp-checklist` (now "conforming to the Decision Base MUST:").
- Remaining 105 runtime rows and 76 authzen rows are untouched (same spec/anchor/text).
- `model.capabilities` gains `authzen.runtime-evidence`, `authzen.obligations`, `authzen.arap`, `authzen.batch`.
- `family-manifest.json`: new entry for the 43rd draft (`count` 42 → 43); runtime's OAuth `requires_when` bucket gains the adapter alongside the issuance profile; authzen's `adoption_requires` drops `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence` to a `requires_when` entry ("the deployment claims the Runtime Evidence feature profile, rather than the Decision Base alone").

Both `node scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs` and `node scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs` (which chains external-pins, bundle-manifest, and substrate-statements) exit 0 at every commit in this branch. `make` builds clean for all four touched/new drafts (runtime, runtime-oauth, authzen, architecture).

## Deviations from a literal reading of the ruling

- The ruling's "five-document shape" names Decision Base / Transaction Assurance / Runtime Evidence / Obligations / ARAP / History / Batch as if each might be its own document. Per explicit task scope, only **one** new draft is created (the OAuth adapter, the 43rd); the AuthZEN feature profiles are sections within the existing `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md`, not new files — physically reordering 2400 lines under new top-level headings would break every anchor for no reviewer value, so the restructuring is a new "Profiles and Capabilities" section plus corrected row/checklist attribution, not a file-level split.
- Most Obligations/ARAP/Batch rows were already fail-closed rules ("refuse what you don't understand/can't fulfill"), not adoption-forcing MUSTs, so they needed no re-gating — gating them would have been backwards (the trap of gating "you must fail closed" instead of "you must support this feature"). Only Runtime Evidence's conformance-checklist bullets were an actual unconditional-adoption-gate bug; those are the ones fixed.
- `mission_action_class_floors`' RFC 9728 registration and Resource-Owner Class Floors subsection moved to the adapter wholesale (per review), rather than staying in Core with only the literal word "OAuth" scrubbed.
- Did not touch `draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md`'s Mission Assurance Levels / `reference_stacks` object beyond adding the new draft to the Mission Document Map: the Architecture's own assurance-level document lists are a curated, stronger bundle than the mechanical `adoption_requires` closure and are not in scope for this restructuring.
- Spec-only change; no `src/` test changes. The conformance checker's existing test mappings for relocated/re-anchored rows were re-validated (still resolve) rather than needing updates, since no wire behavior changed — this is a relocation-plus-vocabulary-genericization pass, not a semantic change to any binding's wire format.

## Merge order

Wave 2, **THIRD**, after `feat/702-minimal-mission-claim`.

## Commits

1. `runtime: extract the OAuth Runtime Adapter; rescope Core to binding-neutral; thin the ESS`
2. `conformance: re-pin runtime and runtime-oauth source.specs digests`
3. `family: wire the 43rd draft, the Mission Runtime OAuth Adapter`
4. `conformance: re-pin runtime and runtime-oauth digests over the family-wiring commit`
5. `authzen: restructure into a Decision Base plus six named feature profiles`
6. `conformance: re-pin authzen digest over the Decision Base restructure`

pulls.title: Minimal mission claim: shrink baseline to {id, issuer}, profile-owned authority_hash (#702, #699)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Refs #702 #699

## Summary

Executes the ruled #702 migration: the baseline `mission` token claim shrinks to exactly `{id, issuer}`. `authority_hash` and `approval_basis.type` leave the baseline claim; `expires_at` becomes profile-scoped (a profile that mints a further credential downstream, or verifies remaining lifetime from retained state, MUST require it and error on absence — never a silent downgrade to the token's own `exp`). Companion profiles that need a stable per-token audit/lineage anchor reintroduce `authority_hash` as **their own** explicitly-required extension member, never inherited from the baseline.

Also incorporates #699's finding that the MAS Join Assertion carries `{id, issuer, authority_hash}` and belongs in the migration inventory (handled: MAS moves to present-then-check, `authority_hash` MAY still ride the assertion at the MAS's discretion).

Core additions:
- **Local Approved-Set Verification** (new named profile in `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`): authenticated complete-set retrieval + commitment recomputation + subset check, OR a typed selective-inclusion proof per carried entry, for a deployment that needs local verification of the approved set rather than merely its audit trail.
- `expires_at` profile-scoping rule (MUST-require-and-error, never silent downgrade).
- `Extensibility`'s claim-member stability list narrows from `{id, issuer, authority_hash}` to `{id, issuer}`.

## Per-use classification (migration inventory)

Every `authority_hash` use across the family's ~35 drafts was classified and, where the baseline shrink affected it, re-mechanized:

| Class | Disposition | Files |
|---|---|---|
| **Baseline claim** | Shrinks to `{id, issuer}`; `authority_hash`/`approval_basis` become introspection-disclosed only (member-scoped, "provenance" privilege); `expires_at` profile-scoped | `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md` |
| **Wire-consistency check (mix-up detection)** | Mandatory identity check narrows to `id`/`issuer`; a *present* `authority_hash` still gets strict equality; absence folds into the existing no-fail-on-optional-omission rule (mirrors `policy_view_id`) | `draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md` (PDP request), `draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime.md`, `draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server.md` (MAS High-Consequence Binding + Join Assertion, #699) |
| **Profile-owned lineage/audit anchor** | Companion profile explicitly REQUIRES `authority_hash` on its own extension member (never inherited) | `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-attenuation.md` (root token), `-cross-domain.md` (ID-JAG grant), `-cross-org-delegation.md` (Chain hops), `-issuance-grant.md` (grant object, also elevates `expires_at`), `draft-mcguinness-mission-mandate.md` (all 5 members REQUIRED), `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-consent-evidence.md` (Consent Evidence's `mission` binding) |
| **Producer-side audit/evidence record** | Out of scope: the producer already holds the full Mission record; the object never travels to a party that can't recompute the hash | `draft-mcguinness-mission-approval-governance.md` (AGR), `draft-mcguinness-mission-audit.md` (Decision Evidence example), `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation.md` (Child Evidence), `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-containment.md` (Containment Evidence, Protected Event Receipt), `draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-expansion.md` (Expansion Evidence; `predecessor` stays a bare mission-id string, never carried `authority_hash`) |
| **Record-level fact (unaffected)** | Describes the Mission Record member, not the claim | `-progressive.md`, `-resource-access.md`, `-signals.md`, `-template.md`, `mission-orchestration.md`, `mission-security-model.md`, `mission-shaping.md`, `mission-substrate.md`, `mission-capability-binding.md`, `mission-aauth.md` (already excluded it), `DRAFTS.md` |
| **OPTIONAL / issuer-discretion disclosure** | Already or newly OPTIONAL, disclosed at issuer/AS discretion | `-status.md`, `mission-harness.md`, `mission-runtime-evidence.md` (Decision/Refusal Evidence tier), `mission-gnap.md`, `mission-uma.md`, `mission-architecture.md`, `-approval.md`, `-approval-revision.md`, `mission-metering.md`, `README.md` |

## Implementation (`src/`)

- **`services/authorization-server/src/kernel/{types,kernel}.ts`**: `MissionClaim` → `{id, issuer}` baseline (others optional); `missionClaim()` returns exactly that. `introspectionProjection` (the caller-gated adapter surface) discloses `authority_hash`/`approval_basis.type` under the same `"provenance"` privilege `proposal_hash` already gates on. `introspectionMission` (ungated internal view) and `signedStatus` explicitly re-add `authority_hash` (unrestricted/discretionary surfaces).
- **`adapters/provider.ts`**: introspection's inbound-claim validator no longer requires `authority_hash` (typed-when-present); child-grant redemption's `authority_hash` cross-check becomes present-then-check (the assertion's `mission` claim no longer carries a top-level `authority_hash`; `mission.id` lookup + `client_id` match remain load-bearing).
- **`packages/mission-core/src/txn-authorization.ts`**: `TxnMissionClaim.authority_hash` optional; `readTxnMissionClaim()` parses it present-then-typecheck.
- **`services/mcp-payments/src/{evidence,pep,server}.ts`**: `TokenFacts`/`EvidenceBase` `authority_hash` optional; every construction site conditionally spreads it (Decision Evidence keeps it unconditional — sourced from the PEP's own resolved `MissionView`, never the wire).
- **`services/pdp/src/evaluate.ts`**: `context.mission.authority_hash` optional; view-consistency rule 1 narrows its mandatory check to `id`/`issuer`, treating `authority_hash` as present-then-check (like the pre-existing `policy_view_id`). `policy-view.ts` unaffected (PDP's own trusted, recomputed record).
- **`services/mcp-saas/src/index.ts`**: dropped a dead `authority_hash` type field the token-only enforcement path never read.
- **`cross-org-chain.ts`, `child-delegation.ts`, `expansion.ts`, `attenuation.ts`, `cross-domain.ts`**: confirmed already correctly scoped (each builds its own profile-owned lineage object directly; unaffected by the baseline shrink).

## Downgrade tests (ruling requirement)

- PDP: a baseline `{id, issuer}` `context.mission` (no `authority_hash`) **permits**; a supplied-but-wrong `authority_hash` still **denies** `view_inconsistent`; an id/issuer mismatch also denies (new, dedicated).
- Introspection endpoint: a crafted token with a bare `{id, issuer}` mission claim still introspects **active**; a present-but-empty-string `authority_hash` still fails closed (typed-when-present, not merely truthy).
- Cross-org-delegation: a structurally valid root carrying only the baseline `{id, issuer, subject}` — what a baseline consumer would accept — is **refused** by this profile's own verification, which requires `authority_hash` as its root-issuance lineage anchor.
- `kernel.test.ts` / `rar-carriage.test.ts` / `template.test.ts` / `child-delegation.test.ts` / `child-delegation-endpoint.test.ts` / `containment.test.ts` / `tracer.test.ts`: every fixture asserting the old 5-member claim shape corrected to `{id, issuer}` (plus each profile's own addition, e.g. `{id, issuer, parent}`); `approval_basis.type` disclosure moved to `introspectionProjection()` under the provenance privilege.

## Conformance manifest

- Re-pinned `source.specs` for every edited draft (core, authzen, runtime, runtime-evidence, authority-server, cross-org-delegation, cross-domain, status, issuance-grant).
- Renamed/split `authzen.pdp-request.consistency-view-id-and-authority-hash-equal` into `consistency-id-and-issuer-equal` (now **tested**) and the new `consistency-authority-hash-equal-when-present` (now **tested**).

pulls.title: Retire the controls taxonomy; normalize error/challenge mapping (#636, #706, #117)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Three related rulings, landed together because they touch the same Mission Intent surface:

- **#636**: retires the Mission Intent's `controls` object. `acr` becomes ordinary OAuth `acr_values`/`max_age` request carriage for the direct flow (new **Approver Authentication Strength** section: achieved acr/amr/auth_time is approval-time provenance, never an Intent member and never a derived-token claim). `max_derivations` splits into `requested_derivation_limit` (Intent, client-requested) and `derivation_limit` (Mission Record, AS-established), governed by a new **Derivation Issuance Policy** section: the effective limit is `min(deployment policy ceiling, requested value)`, established fresh at *every* Mission-creating approval event (direct, Child Mission, Template dispatch, Expansion), never inherited or copied verbatim. `agent_deployment` is removed with a forward pointer to a not-yet-defined Agent Deployment Binding profile — no replacement member exists today. `resources` → `target_resources`, `constraints` → `task_bounds`. The Intent's top level is now open to named, companion-defined members (how metering's five bounds and containment's extension point now attach).
- **#706**: a new **Error and Challenge Mapping** section is the normative endpoint × parameter × failure-stage matrix. `mission_denial` drops `step_up_required` in favor of RFC 9470's `insufficient_user_authentication` and the applicable Bearer/DPoP/mTLS `invalid_token` challenge. A well-formed Intent the AS cannot derive a valid Authority Set from now correctly distinguishes two cases that were conflated: `invalid_authorization_details` when the client submitted a proposal, `access_denied` when it did not (configured-mapping mode).
- **#117**: `exclusive` (metering) relocates out of `controls` alongside the other four bounds, explicitly marked EXPERIMENTAL/not-promoted at its own definition — a 2026-08 promotion assessment found every applicable gate not met. The relocation is not a promotion event.

## Wire-breaking changes (read this before merging)

These change what a real client observes, not just internal naming:

1. **`derivation_limit_exhausted`** (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-issuance-grant.md`) is a renamed *wire-facing error code* in that document's own protocol (was `max_derivations_exhausted`). Confirmed unmapped in `conformance-manifest.json` before renaming, but it's a real break for any implementer of that companion.
2. **`invalid_authorization_details` → `access_denied`** for configured-mapping-mode derivation refusals, in core, `shaping.md`, and `expansion.md`. A client that submits a bare Intent with no `authorization_details` and gets refused now sees `access_denied` instead of `invalid_authorization_details`.
3. **Expansion's `derivation_limit` is now established fresh** from the successor's own Intent (clamped by policy), reversing the prior implementation, which silently inherited the predecessor's value unchanged. That prior behavior was untested and undocumented — not a ruled decision I'm reversing, an oversight I found by cross-checking the new core section (a successor requesting a narrower limit than the predecessor previously got the *wider* inherited value, which directly violates "a client's request MAY only narrow, never widen"). New test in `expansion.test.ts` proves independence in both directions.
4. **The continuation ID-JAG's auto-rooted envelope no longer carries `acr`.** `rootMissionContinuation` (src/services/authorization-server/src/index.ts) previously synthesized `acr` from the approval event's satisfied class; that's exactly the RFC 9068-claim-repurposing pattern core now prohibits. It still carries `auth_time` (a legitimate root-authentication-event timestamp for the continuation chain, not disguised approval-context). `continuation-grant.test.ts`'s "approval-time rooting" test rewritten to assert the corrected behavior instead of a stale premise.

## The mission_error wire-carrier fix

Separately from the ruling text, found and fixed a real bug while implementing #706: `mission_error` (the SHOULD-level diagnostic alongside `invalid_grant`) never actually reached the client. oidc-provider 9.10's `InvalidGrant`/`err_out.js` copies only `error`/`error_description`/`scope`/`state` from a thrown error — any other member is silently dropped. Fixed via a `MissionGrantError` marker class plus a `grant.error` event listener that splices `mission_error` into the already-rendered response body.

This is **positively proven at the wire**, not just asserted: a new test in `tracer.test.ts` creates a Mission with `requested_derivation_limit: 1`, whose second derivation (a refresh, no lifecycle transition involved) is refused with `invalid_grant` + `mission_error: "derivations_exhausted"` — the first end-to-end evidence that a non-`undefined` value actually reaches the client.

`mission_revoked` and `mission_expired` remain **unproven at the wire in this demo specifically**: its own `/lifecycle` route destroys the underlying OAuth Grant on any terminal transition (a documented, pre-existing design choice — "revocation stops refresh" is satisfied structurally, via oidc-provider's own grant lookup, before `gateDerivation`/`MissionGrantError` ever runs). Both values are reachable in a deployment that gates purely on Mission state (a raw DB state change, or natural wall-clock expiry) — this is disclosed honestly in `conformance-manifest.json`'s `core.lifecycle.mission-error-diagnostic` row (`coverage: partial`), not papered over.

## Scope of the sweep

- **Core** (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission.md`): full rewrite of the affected sections plus regenerated test vectors, Document History entry.
- **~20 companion documents**, each checked for `controls.*`/`max_derivations`/`agent_deployment`, Intent-level `resources`/`constraints`, and the #706 error-code ambiguity, and fixed where it applied: architecture, authority-server, authzen, security-model, gnap, uma, approval, child-delegation, containment, expansion, issuance-grant, cross-domain, resource-access, approval-governance, continuation, shaping (the most substantially reshaped, since it exists to describe constructing an Intent), runtime, metering. Progressive, cross-org-delegation, and template were checked and needed no changes — every match found was an unrelated entry-level concept.
- **The whole `src/` workspace**: kernel/adapters rewritten (`kernel.ts`, `intent.ts`, `derive.ts`, `types.ts`, `template.ts`, `child-delegation.ts`, `expansion.ts`, `provider.ts`, `continuation-grant.ts`), plus the demo (`stack.ts`, `server.ts`, `exhibit.ts`, `agent-run.ts`) and the agent service's `shapeIntent`. ~55 test files across every workspace package updated to the new wire shape (kernel.test.ts/tracer.test.ts/anchors.test.ts by hand for the vector-pinned and manifest-mapped cases; the remaining ~42 files split across three parallel subagents with an identical, precise rename specification, each independently verified against `conformance-manifest.json` before touching any manifest-mapped test title).
- **`conformance-manifest.json`**: three stale rows re-anchored to the new spec text, two rows (`mission-error-diagnostic`, the new `derivation-issuance-policy` clamp row) updated with real test coverage, `source.specs` re-pinned for the 7 tracked docs whose content changed (revision = each document's own last-touching commit on this branch, not an arbitrary later one).
- **Deliberately unchanged**: `notes/`, `src/spikes/`, and `src/PLAN.md` still use the old names. These are informal/historical artifacts (PLAN.md is an append-only log per project convention), not part of the normative corpus — a grep will "find" them; they're not misses.
